## List deleted assistants

<a id="opIdget_deleted_assistants_public_assistants_deleted_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/deleted \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ai/assistants/deleted`

List the organization's soft-deleted assistants in the Recently Deleted list.

Each entry includes `deleted_at` and `permanently_deleted_at`, the point after which the assistant is erased automatically and can no longer be restored.

<h3 id="list-deleted-assistants-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|Page number to retrieve (1-based).|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "assistant_7f3c2a1b",
      "name": "Support Assistant",
      "created_at": "2025-08-14T09:24:11.000000Z",
      "model": "telnyx-gpt",
      "instructions": "You are a support assistant.",
      "deleted_at": "2026-10-02T00:46:15.245000Z",
      "permanently_deleted_at": "2026-11-01T00:46:15.245000Z"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total_pages": 1,
    "total_results": 1,
    "page_number": 1,
    "page_size": 20
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-deleted-assistants-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[PaginatedDeletedAssistantsResponse](#schemapaginateddeletedassistantsresponse)|

bearerAuth
</aside>

## Import assistants from external provider

<a id="opIdimport_assistants_public_assistants_import_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "elevenlabs",
    "api_key_ref": "string",
    "import_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /ai/assistants/import`

Import assistants from external providers. Any assistant that has already been imported will be overwritten with its latest version from the importing provider.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "provider": "elevenlabs",
  "api_key_ref": "string",
  "import_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="import-assistants-from-external-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[ImportAssistantsRequest](#schemaimportassistantsrequest)|true|none|
|» provider|body|string|true|The external provider to import assistants from.|
|» api_key_ref|body|string|true|Integration secret pointer that refers to the API key for the external provider. This should be an identifier for an integration secret created via /v2/integration_secrets.|
|» import_ids|body|[string]|false|Optional list of assistant IDs to import from the external provider. If not provided, all assistants will be imported.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» provider|elevenlabs|
|» provider|vapi|
|» provider|retell|

`POST /ai/assistants/tests`

Creates a comprehensive test configuration for evaluating AI assistant performance

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Customer Support Bot Test",
  "description": "string",
  "telnyx_conversation_channel": "web_chat",
  "destination": "+15551234567",
  "max_duration_seconds": 1,
  "test_suite": "string",
  "instructions": "Act as a frustrated customer who received a damaged product. Ask for a refund and escalate if not satisfied with the initial response.",
  "rubric": [
    {
      "criteria": "Assistant responds within 30 seconds",
      "name": "Response Time"
    },
    {
      "criteria": "Provides correct product information",
      "name": "Accuracy"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-assistant-test-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateAssistantTestRequest](#schemacreateassistanttestrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A descriptive name for the assistant test. This will be used to identify the test in the UI and reports.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional detailed description of what this test evaluates and its purpose. Helps team members understand the test's objectives.|
|» telnyx_conversation_channel|body|object|false|The communication channel through which the test will be conducted. Determines how the assistant will receive and respond to test messages.|
|» destination|body|string|true|The target destination for the test conversation. Format depends on the channel: phone number for SMS/voice, webhook URL for web chat, etc.|
|» max_duration_seconds|body|integer|false|Maximum duration in seconds that the test conversation should run before timing out. If not specified, uses system default timeout.|
|» test_suite|body|string|false|Optional test suite name to group related tests together. Useful for organizing tests by feature, team, or release cycle.|
|» instructions|body|string|true|Detailed instructions that define the test scenario and what the assistant should accomplish. This guides the test execution and evaluation.|
|» rubric|body|[object]|true|Evaluation criteria used to assess the assistant's performance. Each rubric item contains a name and specific criteria for evaluation.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Label for the evaluation criterion, e.g., Empathy, Accuracy, Clarity.|
|» » criteria|body|string|true|Specific guidance on how to assess the assistant’s performance for this rubric item.|

## Trigger a manual test run

<a id="opIdtrigger_test_run_public_assistants_tests__test_id__runs_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/tests/string/runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "destination_version_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
  }'
```

`POST /ai/assistants/tests/{test_id}/runs`

Initiates immediate execution of a specific assistant test

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destination_version_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

<h3 id="trigger-a-manual-test-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|test_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the test.|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[TriggerTestRunRequest](#schematriggertestrunrequest)|false|none|
|» destination_version_id|body|string|false|Optional assistant version ID to use for this test run. If provided, the version must exist or a 400 error will be returned. If not provided, test will run on main version|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "run_id": "987fcdeb-51a2-43d1-b456-426614174000",
  "test_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "status": "pending",
  "triggered_by": "cron",
  "completed_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "logs": "string",

  "test_suite_run_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "created_at": "2024-01-24T10:30:00Z",
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "detail_status": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
    {
      "code": "10036",
```

<h3 id="trigger-a-manual-test-run-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns the created test run with execution details and status|[TestRunResponse](#schematestrunresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request / Validation Failed (10015). Invalid, duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong Idempotency-Key headers are rejected by Edge with HTTP 400 and error code 10015.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (10036). Retry later with the same key and request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large. A request sent with an Idempotency-Key whose body exceeds the endpoint's Edge replay-protection limit (256 KB) is rejected before it reaches the service. Requests sent without the header are not subject to this limit.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error. Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different request body also returns 422 with error code 10027.|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable (10016), including unavailable Edge idempotency protection for a keyed request.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|

<h3 id="trigger-a-manual-test-run-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Idempotent-Replayed|boolean||Present with value `true` when Edge replayed a stored successful response for the supplied Idempotency-Key. Omitted for first-time requests and error responses.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}`

Updates the specified AI assistant's attributes and returns the updated assistant. The request can also control how the change is promoted across assistant versions. Every update saves a new version, and an assistant keeps at most 10 versions: once it has more, the oldest versions are permanently deleted, except the main version and any version referenced by a traffic distribution rule.

<h3 id="update-an-assistant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|body|body|[UpdateAssistantRequestWithPromotion](#schemaupdateassistantrequestwithpromotion)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» model|body|string|false|ID of the model to use when `external_llm` is not set. You can use the [Get models API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/openai-chat/get-available-models-openai-compatible) to see available models. If `external_llm` is provided, the assistant uses `external_llm` instead of this field. If neither `model` nor `external_llm` is provided, Telnyx applies the default model.|
|» instructions|body|string|false|System instructions for the assistant. These may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables)|
|» tools|body|[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)|false|Deprecated for new integrations. Inline tool definitions available to the assistant. Prefer `tool_ids` to attach shared tools created with the AI Tools endpoints. On update, a sent `tools` array fully replaces the assistant's inline tools; omit the field to leave the inline tools unchanged. Each tool type except `function`, `webhook`, and `client_side_tool` allows at most one instance per assistant, counted across inline `tools` and shared `tool_ids` combined — sending a duplicate of such a type returns HTTP 400 with error code 10015. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; when updating, omit those tools from the `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead.|
|» mcp_servers|body|[[AssistantMCPServer](#schemaassistantmcpserver)]|false|MCP servers attached to the assistant. Create MCP servers with `/ai/mcp_servers`, then reference them by `id` here.|
|» a2a_agents|body|[[AssistantA2AAgent](#schemaassistanta2aagent)]|false|A2A agents this assistant can delegate to. Tools are not stored here: at the start of every conversation each agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises, named `a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`. The following limits are not enforced when the assistant is saved, and anything past them is dropped when the conversation starts: 64 agents per assistant, 64 skills per card, 128 derived tools per assistant, and a 6 second budget for all card fetches combined. An agent whose card cannot be fetched costs the assistant that capability for the conversation; it does not fail the call. Omit this field to leave the assistant's agents unchanged; send an empty array to remove them all.|
|» tool_ids|body|[string]|false|IDs of shared tools to attach to the assistant. New integrations should prefer `tool_ids` over inline `tools`. On update, a sent `tool_ids` array fully replaces the assistant's attached shared tools; omit the field to leave them unchanged. Single-instance tool types are counted across inline `tools` and `tool_ids` combined, so attaching a shared tool of such a type when an instance already exists returns HTTP 400 with error code 10015.|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» greeting|body|string|false|Text that the assistant will use to start the conversation. This may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables). Use an empty string to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. Use the special value `<assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message>` to have the assistant generate the greeting based on the system instructions.|
|» llm_api_key_ref|body|string|false|This is only needed when using third-party inference providers selected by `model`. The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your LLM provider's API key. For bring-your-own endpoint authentication, use `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.|
|» external_llm|body|[ExternalLLMReq](#schemaexternalllmreq)|false|none|
|» fallback_config|body|[FallbackConfigReq](#schemafallbackconfigreq)|false|none|
|» voice_settings|body|[inference-embedding_VoiceSettings](#schemainference-embedding_voicesettings)|false|none|
|» avatar_settings|body|[AvatarSettingsRequest](#schemaavatarsettingsrequest) \| null|false|**Beta:** Replaces the assistant's avatar configuration. Omit this field to leave the current configuration unchanged, or set it to `null` to remove the configuration.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AvatarSettingsRequest](#schemaavatarsettingsrequest)|false|**Beta:** Telnyx avatar configuration accepted when creating or updating an assistant. Set `provider` to `telnyx`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» transcription|body|[TranscriptionSettings](#schematranscriptionsettings)|false|none|
|» telephony_settings|body|[TelephonySettings](#schematelephonysettings)|false|none|
|» messaging_settings|body|[MessagingSettings](#schemamessagingsettings)|false|none|
|» enabled_features|body|[[EnabledFeatures](#schemaenabledfeatures)]|false|none|
|» insight_settings|body|[InsightSettings](#schemainsightsettings)|false|none|
|» privacy_settings|body|[PrivacySettings](#schemaprivacysettings)|false|none|
|» dynamic_variables_webhook_url|body|string|false|If `dynamic_variables_webhook_url` is set, Telnyx sends a POST request to this URL at the start of the conversation to resolve dynamic variables. **Gotcha:** the webhook response must wrap variables under a top-level `dynamic_variables` object, e.g. `{"dynamic_variables": {"customer_name": "Jane"}}`. Returning a flat object will be ignored and variables will fall back to their defaults. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) for the full request/response format and timeout behavior.|
|» dynamic_variables_webhook_timeout_ms|body|integer|false|Timeout in milliseconds for the dynamic variables webhook. Must be between 1 and 10000 ms. If the webhook does not respond within this timeout, the call proceeds with default values. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables).|
|» dynamic_variables|body|object|false|Map of dynamic variables and their default values|
|» widget_settings|body|[WidgetSettings](#schemawidgetsettings)|false|Configuration settings for the assistant's web widget.|
|» interruption_settings|body|[inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings](#schemainference-embedding_interruptionsettings)|false|Settings for interruptions and how the assistant decides the user has finished speaking. These timings are most relevant when using non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn behavior is controlled by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` (`eot_threshold`, `eot_timeout_ms`, `eager_eot_threshold`).|
|» integrations|body|[[AssistantIntegration](#schemaassistantintegration)]|false|Connected integrations attached to the assistant. The catalog of available integrations is at `/ai/integrations`; the user's connected integrations are at `/ai/integrations/connections`. Each item references a catalog integration by `integration_id`.|
|» observability_settings|body|[ObservabilityReq](#schemaobservabilityreq)|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the assistant. Tags can also be managed with the assistant tag endpoints.|
|» version_name|body|string|false|Human-readable name for the assistant version.|
|» post_conversation_settings|body|[PostConversationSettingsReq](#schemapostconversationsettingsreq)|false|Configuration for post-conversation processing. When enabled, the assistant receives one additional LLM turn after the conversation ends, allowing it to execute final tool calls such as sending a summary or updating a record via webhook or function tools. Integration and MCP server tools are not available post-conversation; call-control tools (e.g. hangup, transfer) are also unavailable. Beta feature.|
|» delegation_settings|body|[DelegationSettings](#schemadelegationsettings)|false|Splits the conversation between a frontend model that talks to the caller and a backend model that does the work. On the GPT-Live route the frontend model cannot call tools at all — when it needs something done it raises a delegation and waits. On the chat completion route the frontend keeps a single `delegate` tool that returns immediately, so the conversation carries on while the backend works. Either way the backend's answer is spoken as commentary or kept as silent context, depending on `speak_results`. Beta feature.|
|» websocket_settings|body|[WebsocketSettings](#schemawebsocketsettings)|false|Streams conversation and telephony events to a WebSocket server you host, and accepts messages injected back into the conversation. Telnyx opens the connection as a client, once per conversation. Delivery is best effort throughout: while the connection is down events are dropped rather than queued, and no socket failure is ever allowed to affect the call. Beta feature.|
|» conversation_flow|body|[ConversationFlowReq](#schemaconversationflowreq)|false|Conversation flow as supplied by API clients (create / update).<br><br>A directed graph of `FlowNodeReq` connected by `FlowEdge`s. Validation<br>enforces unique node/edge IDs, that `start_node_id` references a real<br>node, and that every edge's endpoints reference real nodes.|
|» promote_to_main|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the assistant should be promoted to the main version. Defaults to true.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» enabled_features|telephony|
|» enabled_features|messaging|

> 200 Response

```json
{
```

## Delete an assistant

<a id="opIddelete_assistant_public_assistants__assistant_id__delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}`

Delete an AI Assistant by `assistant_id`.

By default this performs a soft delete: the assistant moves to the Recently Deleted list and stays restorable for 30 days, after which it is permanently deleted automatically. The assistant's versions and TeXML application are preserved during the retention window.

Pass `hard_delete=true` to skip the retention window and permanently delete the assistant immediately. A hard delete erases the assistant and all of its versions, and deletes its TeXML application unless phone numbers are still assigned to it. It does not delete conversations, recordings, shared tools the assistant referenced, or knowledge-base embeddings.

Deletion fails with `400` if other assistants reference this one through a handoff tool or a conversation-flow edge — remove those references first.

<h3 id="delete-an-assistant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|hard_delete|query|boolean|false|Permanently delete the assistant immediately instead of soft-deleting it to the Recently Deleted list, where it stays restorable for 30 days.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "assistant_7f3c2a1b",
  "object": "assistant.deleted",
  "deleted": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10015",
      "title": "Bad Request",
      "detail": "Cannot delete assistant assistant_7f3c2a1b. The following assistant(s) have handoff tools pointing to it: 'Billing Bot' (assistant_9c1d2e3f). Please remove these handoff tools before deleting."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-assistant-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[AssistantDeletedResponse](#schemaassistantdeletedresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request (code 10015). Another assistant depends on this one: a handoff tool points to it, or a conversation-flow edge hands off to it. The detail names the referencing assistants; remove those references and retry.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/canary-deploys`

Endpoint to create a canary deploy configuration for an assistant.

Creates a new canary deploy configuration with multiple version IDs and their traffic
percentages for A/B testing or gradual rollouts of assistant versions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "match": [
        {
          "attribute": "Attribute",
          "operator": "in",
          "values": [
            "string"
          ]
        }

        "version_id": "Version Id",

}
```

<h3 id="create-canary-deploy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CanaryDeployRequest](#schemacanarydeployrequest)|true|none|
|» rules|body|[[Rule-Input](#schemarule-input)]|false|none|

## Assistant Chat

<a id="opIdassistant_chat_public_assistants__assistant_id__chat_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/string/chat \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "content": "Tell me a joke about cats",
    "name": "Charlie",
    "conversation_id": "42b20469-1215-4a9a-8964-c36f66b406f4",
    "stream": false
  }'
```

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/chat`

This endpoint allows a client to send a chat message to a specific AI Assistant. The assistant processes the message and returns a relevant reply based on the current conversation context. Refer to the Conversation API to [create a conversation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/create-a-conversation), [filter existing conversations](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/list-conversations), [fetch messages for a conversation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/get-conversation-messages), and [manually add messages to a conversation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/create-message).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content": "Tell me a joke about cats",
  "name": "Charlie",
  "conversation_id": "42b20469-1215-4a9a-8964-c36f66b406f4",
  "stream": false
}
```

<h3 id="assistant-chat-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|body|body|[AssistantChatReq](#schemaassistantchatreq)|true|none|
|» content|body|string|true|The message content sent by the client to the assistant|
|» name|body|string|false|The optional display name of the user sending the message|
|» conversation_id|body|string|true|A unique identifier for the conversation thread, used to maintain context|
|» stream|body|boolean|false|When true, the response is streamed as Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`): `delta` events carry content fragments as they are generated, a final `done` event carries the full content plus `whatsapp_template`, and a terminal `error` event reports failures that happen after streaming started. When false (default), the response is a single JSON object.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "content": "Why did the cat sit on the computer? Because it wanted to keep an eye on the mouse!"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="assistant-chat-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[AssistantChatResponse](#schemaassistantchatresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request. The turn was refused before any message content was processed. For example, an assistant with `privacy_settings.in_transit_data_locality` enabled refuses a request that entered the platform outside the organization's data-locality region, or that this deployment cannot serve in that region; the response detail names the API hostname to send it to.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Assistant Sms Chat

<a id="opIdassistant_sms_chat_assistants__assistant_id__chat_sms_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/string/chat/sms \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from": "From",
    "to": "To",
    "text": "Text",
    "should_create_conversation": false
  }'
```

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/chat/sms`

Send an SMS message for an assistant. This endpoint: 
1. Validates the assistant exists and has messaging profile configured 
2. If should_create_conversation is true, creates a new conversation with metadata 
3. Sends the SMS message (If `text` is set, this will be sent. Otherwise, if this is the first message in the conversation and the assistant has a `greeting` configured, this will be sent. Otherwise the assistant will generate the text to send.) 
4. Updates conversation metadata if provided 
5. Returns the conversation ID

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from": "From",
  "to": "To",
  "text": "Text",
  "should_create_conversation": false
}
```

<h3 id="assistant-sms-chat-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[AssistantSmsChatReq](#schemaassistantsmschatreq)|true|none|
|» from|body|string|true|none|
|» to|body|string|true|none|
|» text|body|string|false|none|
|» conversation_metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| integer \| boolean|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» should_create_conversation|body|boolean|false|none|

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "Conversation Id"
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",

        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
      },

}
```

## Assistant WhatsApp Chat

<a id="opIdassistant_whatsapp_chat_assistants__assistant_id__chat_whatsapp_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/string/chat/whatsapp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from": "+13125550001",
    "to": "+13125550002",
    "content": "Send the login verification code 482913 to the customer.",
    "conversation_metadata": {
      "order_id": "A1"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/chat/whatsapp`

Start a WhatsApp conversation with a customer from the business side. This endpoint:
1. Validates that `from` is a WhatsApp number on your account whose messaging profile has this assistant configured
2. Creates a new `whatsapp_chat` conversation with the provided metadata
3. Asks the assistant to pick one of its approved WhatsApp templates and fill its variables from `content`
4. Sends the template from `from` to `to`
5. Returns the conversation ID and the message ID

When the customer replies, the reply is routed to the same conversation and the assistant answers within the 24-hour customer service window. The assistant needs a `whatsapp_template` tool with at least one approved template, data retention enabled and PII redaction disabled.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from": "+13125550001",
  "to": "+13125550002",
  "content": "Send the login verification code 482913 to the customer.",
  "conversation_metadata": {
    "order_id": "A1"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="assistant-whatsapp-chat-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant. Must be the assistant configured on the messaging profile of the `from` number.|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[AssistantWhatsappChatReq](#schemaassistantwhatsappchatreq)|true|none|
|» from|body|string|true|WhatsApp number on your account to send from, in E.164 format. Its messaging profile must have this assistant configured.|
|» to|body|string|true|Customer to message, as an E.164 phone number or a WhatsApp business-scoped user ID (BSUID).|
|» content|body|string|true|Instruction for the assistant, including the values for the template variables, e.g. `Send the login verification code 482913 to the customer.`|
|» conversation_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata stored on the conversation. Keys starting with `telnyx_` and the `assistant_id` key are reserved.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| integer \| boolean|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|

> Example responses

```json
}
```

|400|Bad Request|Bad Request. Missing required fields or a reserved `conversation_metadata` key, or the assistant is not the one configured on the messaging profile of `from` (10015). Invalid JSON (10023). A field of the wrong type, for example a non-string `from`, `to` or `content`, or a `conversation_metadata` value that is not a string, integer or boolean (10026). `from` is not a valid WhatsApp number on a messaging profile (40305). `to` is not a valid E.164 number or BSUID (40310). Invalid, duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong Idempotency-Key headers are rejected by Edge with HTTP 400 and error code 10015.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication Failed (10009). The API key is missing or invalid.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|

|404|Not Found|Not Found (10005). The assistant does not exist.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict. The messaging profile of `from` is disabled (40312), or a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (10036), in which case retry later with the same key and request.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large. A request sent with an Idempotency-Key whose body exceeds the endpoint's Edge replay-protection limit (256 KB) is rejected before it reaches the service. Requests sent without the header are not subject to this limit.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity (10027). The assistant did not return a WhatsApp template, or its privacy settings do not allow storing conversations. Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different request body also returns 422 with error code 10027.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable (10037). The assistant could not be looked up, the conversation could not be started, or the template could not be sent. Retry the request.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|

## Get a deleted assistant


`GET /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/deleted`

Retrieve a soft-deleted assistant from the Recently Deleted list by `assistant_id`, including its `deleted_at` and `permanently_deleted_at` timestamps. This is a read-only view; the assistant cannot be modified while it remains deleted.

<h3 id="get-a-deleted-assistant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|

```json
{
  "id": "assistant_7f3c2a1b",
  "name": "Support Assistant",
  "created_at": "2025-08-14T09:24:11.000000Z",
  "model": "telnyx-gpt",
  "instructions": "You are a support assistant.",
  "deleted_at": "2026-10-02T00:46:15.245000Z",
  "permanently_deleted_at": "2026-11-01T00:46:15.245000Z"
}
```

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],

      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Enhance Assistant Instructions

<a id="opIdenhance_assistant_instructions_public_assistants__assistant_id__instructions_enhance_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/string/instructions/enhance \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enhancement_prompt": "string",
    "instructions": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/instructions/enhance`

Enhance an assistant's instructions using an LLM. The endpoint reads the assistant's current instructions and tools, then streams back improved instructions as they are generated.

Optionally provide an `enhancement_prompt` to steer the changes (for example, "make the instructions more concise" or "add error handling guidance"). When omitted, the assistant's existing instructions are used as the basis for the enhancement.

The enhancement focuses on tool-calling reliability, clarity and precision, completeness and error handling, tool schema alignment, and conversation flow structure.

The response is streamed as `text/plain` using chunked transfer encoding; consume the body incrementally to render the enhanced instructions as they arrive.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enhancement_prompt": "string",
  "instructions": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="enhance-assistant-instructions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|body|body|[EnhanceInstructionsRequest](#schemaenhanceinstructionsrequest)|false|none|
|» enhancement_prompt|body|string \| null|false|Optional guidance describing how the instructions should be enhanced. When provided, the LLM applies these requested changes in addition to fixing any identified issues.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» instructions|body|string \| null|false|The instructions to enhance. When omitted, the assistant's existing instructions are used.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
Enhanced Instructions Stream
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="enhance-assistant-instructions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A stream of enhanced instruction text. The body is sent as `text/plain` using chunked transfer encoding.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Restore an assistant

<a id="opIdrestore_assistant_public_assistants__assistant_id__restore_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/string/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/restore`

Restore a soft-deleted assistant from the Recently Deleted list.

The assistant becomes fully active again with its versions and TeXML application as they were at deletion time. Restoring does not re-enable numbers or connections that were released separately after the deletion.

<h3 id="restore-an-assistant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|

```json
  "model": "telnyx-gpt",
  "instructions": "You are a support assistant."
}
```

`POST /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/scheduled_events`

Create a scheduled event for an assistant

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "telnyx_conversation_channel": "phone_call",
  "telnyx_end_user_target": "string",
  "telnyx_agent_target": "string",
  "scheduled_at_fixed_datetime": "2025-04-15T13:07:28.764Z",
  "text": "string",
  "conversation_metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "dynamic_variables": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "max_retries_client_errors": 0,
  "retry_interval_secs": 60,
  "call_settings": {
    "sip_region": "US"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-scheduled-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateScheduledEventRequest](#schemacreatescheduledeventrequest)|true|none|
|» telnyx_conversation_channel|body|[ConversationChannelType](#schemaconversationchanneltype)|true|none|
|» telnyx_end_user_target|body|string|true|The phone number, SIP URI, to schedule the call or text to.|
|» telnyx_agent_target|body|string|true|The phone number, SIP URI, to schedule the call or text from.|
|» scheduled_at_fixed_datetime|body|string(date-time)|true|The datetime at which the event should be scheduled. Formatted as ISO 8601.|
|» text|body|string|false|Required for sms scheduled events. The text to be sent to the end user.|
|» conversation_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata associated with the conversation. Telnyx provides several pieces of metadata, but customers can also add their own.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| integer \| boolean|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» dynamic_variables|body|object|false|A map of dynamic variable names to values. These variables can be referenced in the assistant's instructions and messages using {{variable_name}} syntax.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» max_retries_client_errors|body|integer|false|Configure number of retries on client errors: busy, no-answer, failed, canceled (caller hung up before the callee answered)|
|» retry_interval_secs|body|integer|false|none|
|» call_settings|body|[ScheduledCallSettings](#schemascheduledcallsettings)|false|Per-call telephony overrides applied when a scheduled phone-call event<br>dispatches. Phone-call events only. New per-call dispatch options should be<br>added here rather than as top-level event fields.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» telnyx_conversation_channel|phone_call|
|» telnyx_conversation_channel|sms_chat|

|201|Created|Successful Response|[ScheduledEventResponse](#schemascheduledeventresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request / Validation Failed (10015). Invalid, duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong Idempotency-Key headers are rejected by Edge with HTTP 400 and error code 10015.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (10036). Retry later with the same key and request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large. A request sent with an Idempotency-Key whose body exceeds the endpoint's Edge replay-protection limit (256 KB) is rejected before it reaches the service. Requests sent without the header are not subject to this limit.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error. Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different request body also returns 422 with error code 10027.|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable (10016), including unavailable Edge idempotency protection for a keyed request.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|

<h3 id="create-a-scheduled-event-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Idempotent-Replayed|boolean||Present with value `true` when Edge replayed a stored successful response for the supplied Idempotency-Key. Omitted for first-time requests and error responses.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Get all versions of an assistant

<a id="opIdget_assistant_versions_public_assistants__assistant_id__versions_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/assistants/string/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/versions`

Retrieves all versions of a specific assistant with complete configuration and metadata. An assistant keeps at most 10 versions, including the main version. When an update takes it past that limit, the oldest versions are permanently deleted. The main version and any version referenced by a traffic distribution rule are never deleted this way.

`GET /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/versions/{version_id}`

Retrieves a specific version of an assistant by assistant_id and version_id

<h3 id="get-a-specific-assistant-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|version_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the version.|
|include_mcp_servers|query|boolean|false|Whether to include MCP servers in the response.|

<h3 id="update-a-specific-assistant-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the assistant.|
|version_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the version.|
|body|body|[UpdateAssistantRequest](#schemaupdateassistantrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» model|body|string|false|ID of the model to use when `external_llm` is not set. You can use the [Get models API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/openai-chat/get-available-models-openai-compatible) to see available models. If `external_llm` is provided, the assistant uses `external_llm` instead of this field. If neither `model` nor `external_llm` is provided, Telnyx applies the default model.|
|» instructions|body|string|false|System instructions for the assistant. These may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables)|
|» tools|body|[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)|false|Deprecated for new integrations. Inline tool definitions available to the assistant. Prefer `tool_ids` to attach shared tools created with the AI Tools endpoints. On update, a sent `tools` array fully replaces the assistant's inline tools; omit the field to leave the inline tools unchanged. Each tool type except `function`, `webhook`, and `client_side_tool` allows at most one instance per assistant, counted across inline `tools` and shared `tool_ids` combined — sending a duplicate of such a type returns HTTP 400 with error code 10015. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; when updating, omit those tools from the `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead.|
|» mcp_servers|body|[[AssistantMCPServer](#schemaassistantmcpserver)]|false|MCP servers attached to the assistant. Create MCP servers with `/ai/mcp_servers`, then reference them by `id` here.|
|» a2a_agents|body|[[AssistantA2AAgent](#schemaassistanta2aagent)]|false|A2A agents this assistant can delegate to. Tools are not stored here: at the start of every conversation each agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises, named `a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`. The following limits are not enforced when the assistant is saved, and anything past them is dropped when the conversation starts: 64 agents per assistant, 64 skills per card, 128 derived tools per assistant, and a 6 second budget for all card fetches combined. An agent whose card cannot be fetched costs the assistant that capability for the conversation; it does not fail the call. Omit this field to leave the assistant's agents unchanged; send an empty array to remove them all.|
|» tool_ids|body|[string]|false|IDs of shared tools to attach to the assistant. New integrations should prefer `tool_ids` over inline `tools`. On update, a sent `tool_ids` array fully replaces the assistant's attached shared tools; omit the field to leave them unchanged. Single-instance tool types are counted across inline `tools` and `tool_ids` combined, so attaching a shared tool of such a type when an instance already exists returns HTTP 400 with error code 10015.|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» greeting|body|string|false|Text that the assistant will use to start the conversation. This may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables). Use an empty string to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. Use the special value `<assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message>` to have the assistant generate the greeting based on the system instructions.|
|» llm_api_key_ref|body|string|false|This is only needed when using third-party inference providers selected by `model`. The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your LLM provider's API key. For bring-your-own endpoint authentication, use `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.|
|» external_llm|body|[ExternalLLMReq](#schemaexternalllmreq)|false|none|
|» fallback_config|body|[FallbackConfigReq](#schemafallbackconfigreq)|false|none|
|» voice_settings|body|[inference-embedding_VoiceSettings](#schemainference-embedding_voicesettings)|false|none|
|» avatar_settings|body|[AvatarSettingsRequest](#schemaavatarsettingsrequest) \| null|false|**Beta:** Replaces the assistant's avatar configuration. Omit this field to leave the current configuration unchanged, or set it to `null` to remove the configuration.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AvatarSettingsRequest](#schemaavatarsettingsrequest)|false|**Beta:** Telnyx avatar configuration accepted when creating or updating an assistant. Set `provider` to `telnyx`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» transcription|body|[TranscriptionSettings](#schematranscriptionsettings)|false|none|
|» telephony_settings|body|[TelephonySettings](#schematelephonysettings)|false|none|
|» messaging_settings|body|[MessagingSettings](#schemamessagingsettings)|false|none|
|» enabled_features|body|[[EnabledFeatures](#schemaenabledfeatures)]|false|none|
|» insight_settings|body|[InsightSettings](#schemainsightsettings)|false|none|
|» privacy_settings|body|[PrivacySettings](#schemaprivacysettings)|false|none|
|» dynamic_variables_webhook_url|body|string|false|If `dynamic_variables_webhook_url` is set, Telnyx sends a POST request to this URL at the start of the conversation to resolve dynamic variables. **Gotcha:** the webhook response must wrap variables under a top-level `dynamic_variables` object, e.g. `{"dynamic_variables": {"customer_name": "Jane"}}`. Returning a flat object will be ignored and variables will fall back to their defaults. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) for the full request/response format and timeout behavior.|
|» dynamic_variables_webhook_timeout_ms|body|integer|false|Timeout in milliseconds for the dynamic variables webhook. Must be between 1 and 10000 ms. If the webhook does not respond within this timeout, the call proceeds with default values. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables).|
|» dynamic_variables|body|object|false|Map of dynamic variables and their default values|
|» widget_settings|body|[WidgetSettings](#schemawidgetsettings)|false|Configuration settings for the assistant's web widget.|
|» interruption_settings|body|[inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings](#schemainference-embedding_interruptionsettings)|false|Settings for interruptions and how the assistant decides the user has finished speaking. These timings are most relevant when using non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn behavior is controlled by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` (`eot_threshold`, `eot_timeout_ms`, `eager_eot_threshold`).|
|» integrations|body|[[AssistantIntegration](#schemaassistantintegration)]|false|Connected integrations attached to the assistant. The catalog of available integrations is at `/ai/integrations`; the user's connected integrations are at `/ai/integrations/connections`. Each item references a catalog integration by `integration_id`.|
|» observability_settings|body|[ObservabilityReq](#schemaobservabilityreq)|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the assistant. Tags can also be managed with the assistant tag endpoints.|
|» version_name|body|string|false|Human-readable name for the assistant version.|
|» post_conversation_settings|body|[PostConversationSettingsReq](#schemapostconversationsettingsreq)|false|Configuration for post-conversation processing. When enabled, the assistant receives one additional LLM turn after the conversation ends, allowing it to execute final tool calls such as sending a summary or updating a record via webhook or function tools. Integration and MCP server tools are not available post-conversation; call-control tools (e.g. hangup, transfer) are also unavailable. Beta feature.|
|» delegation_settings|body|[DelegationSettings](#schemadelegationsettings)|false|Splits the conversation between a frontend model that talks to the caller and a backend model that does the work. On the GPT-Live route the frontend model cannot call tools at all — when it needs something done it raises a delegation and waits. On the chat completion route the frontend keeps a single `delegate` tool that returns immediately, so the conversation carries on while the backend works. Either way the backend's answer is spoken as commentary or kept as silent context, depending on `speak_results`. Beta feature.|
|» websocket_settings|body|[WebsocketSettings](#schemawebsocketsettings)|false|Streams conversation and telephony events to a WebSocket server you host, and accepts messages injected back into the conversation. Telnyx opens the connection as a client, once per conversation. Delivery is best effort throughout: while the connection is down events are dropped rather than queued, and no socket failure is ever allowed to affect the call. Beta feature.|
|» conversation_flow|body|[ConversationFlowReq](#schemaconversationflowreq)|false|Conversation flow as supplied by API clients (create / update).<br><br>A directed graph of `FlowNodeReq` connected by `FlowEdge`s. Validation<br>enforces unique node/edge IDs, that `start_node_id` references a real<br>node, and that every edge's endpoints reference real nodes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» enabled_features|telephony|
|» enabled_features|messaging|


```bash
  "type": "string",
```

<h3 id="create-tool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateSharedToolRequest](#schemacreatesharedtoolrequest)|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» display_name|body|string|true|none|
|» function|body|object|false|none|
|» retrieval|body|object|false|none|
|» handoff|body|object|false|none|
|» invite|body|object|false|none|
|» webhook|body|object|false|none|
|» pay|body|[PayToolParams](#schemapaytoolparams)|false|none|
|» client_side_tool|body|object|false|none|
|» update_dynamic_variables|body|[UpdateDynamicVariablesToolParams](#schemaupdatedynamicvariablestoolparams)|false|Configuration for an update_dynamic_variables tool.|
|» vision|body|[VisionToolParams](#schemavisiontoolparams)|false|none|
|» timeout_ms|body|integer|false|none|

<h3 id="create-tool-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[SharedToolResponse](#schemasharedtoolresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request / Validation Failed (10015). Invalid, duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong Idempotency-Key headers are rejected by Edge with HTTP 400 and error code 10015.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (10036). Retry later with the same key and request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large. A request sent with an Idempotency-Key whose body exceeds the endpoint's Edge replay-protection limit (256 KB) is rejected before it reaches the service. Requests sent without the header are not subject to this limit.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error. Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different request body also returns 422 with error code 10027.|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable (10016), including unavailable Edge idempotency protection for a keyed request.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|

<h3 id="create-tool-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|false|none|none|

`GET /ai/avatars`

Returns a paginated list of the Telnyx stock avatars and custom avatars available to the authenticated organization. Custom avatars owned by other organizations are never returned. The `image_url` value is suitable for displaying a thumbnail and may be refreshed by listing or retrieving the avatar again. `suggested_voice_id` recommends a compatible Telnyx voice for stock avatars and is an empty string for custom avatars; it does not change an AI Assistant's voice automatically.

|filter[name]|query|string|false|Return avatars whose names contain this value, using case-insensitive matching.|
|filter[id]|query|[AvatarId](#schemaavatarid)|false|Return the avatar with this exact ID.|
|filter[avatar_type]|query|[AvatarType](#schemaavatartype)|false|Return only stock or custom avatars.|

## Create a custom avatar

<a id="opIdcreate_avatar_public_avatars_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/avatars \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'image_file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'name=Customer portrait'
```

`POST /ai/avatars`

Uploads an image, validates its file type, size, safe decoding, and resolution, stores it in Telnyx-managed private storage, and creates an avatar owned by the authenticated organization. Creating an avatar does not update an AI Assistant; use the returned ID separately wherever the avatar is consumed. The avatar image is stored independently from the rendering model and background, which are selected where the avatar is consumed. Supported image types are JPEG, PNG, and WebP. Images may be up to 10 MiB, must be between 256 and 8192 pixels on each side, and may contain at most 40 megapixels. A per-organization custom-avatar quota applies; the create request returns an error when the quota is reached. For best results, use a 16:9 landscape image, preferably 1920 by 1080 pixels and at least 1280 by 720 pixels. Show one centered, front-facing person from the shoulders up, keep the full head and hair visible with space around it, and use a sharp, evenly lit image with unobstructed eyes and mouth. Use a transparent PNG or WebP when the avatar will be combined with a selectable background. These composition recommendations are not enforced in the first release; the first release does not validate the number of faces, pose, or image content.

> Body parameter

```yaml
image_file: "string($binary)"
name: Customer portrait
```

<h3 id="create-a-custom-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateAvatarRequest](#schemacreateavatarrequest)|true|none|
|» image_file|body|string(binary)|true|JPEG, PNG, or WebP image file. The maximum file size is 10 MiB.|
|» name|body|string|true|Customer-facing name of the custom avatar.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "avatar_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
    "name": "Customer portrait",
    "provider": "telnyx",
    "avatar_type": "custom",
    "hosted": true,
    "image_url": "https://example.com/avatar.png",
    "image_url_expires_at": "2026-10-13T15:00:00Z",
    "suggested_voice_id": "",
    "content_type": "image/png",
    "size_bytes": 248512,
    "width_px": 1920,
    "height_px": 1080,
    "created_at": "2026-10-13T14:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-10-13T14:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10015",
      "title": "Bad Request",
      "detail": "The request contains invalid avatar parameters.",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10015"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
    {
      "code": "10027",
```

|400|Bad Request|The request body, path parameter, or query parameter failed validation.|[AvatarErrorResponse](#schemaavatarerrorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The request, uploaded image, or organization quota failed validation. Uploaded images must not exceed 10 MiB.|[AvatarErrorResponse](#schemaavatarerrorresponse)|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-bot-signup">Bot Signup</h1>

Agentic (bot) signup for Telnyx accounts. An AI agent solves a reverse-CAPTCHA challenge designed to be easy for LLMs and hard for humans, registers an account, and signs in by consuming a magic link emailed to the account owner. All endpoints are public and unauthenticated; signup endpoints are additionally gated by the freemium feature flags and per-country availability.

## Issue a bot challenge

<a id="opIdcreateBotChallenge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/bot_challenge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "llm_model_name": "claude-opus-4",
    "llm_parameter_count": "175B",
    "llm_quantization": "int8"
  }'
```

`POST /bot_challenge`

Generates a reverse-CAPTCHA challenge used to gate the bot signup flow. A random active problem is selected from the pool; math problems are returned obfuscated (case randomization, symbol injection, spacing noise) with an unobfuscated rounding instruction appended, while string and binary problems are returned as-is. The response contains a single-use nonce, the problem text, and the current terms-and-conditions and privacy-policy URLs, which must be echoed back on the signup request. Challenges expire after a short window (10 minutes by default) and can only be answered once. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "llm_model_name": "claude-opus-4",
  "llm_parameter_count": "175B",
  "llm_quantization": "int8"
}
```

<h3 id="issue-a-bot-challenge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BotChallengeRequest](#schemabotchallengerequest)|false|Optional self-reported metadata about the LLM solving the challenge. Used for analytics only; it does not influence which problem is served.|
|» llm_model_name|body|string|false|Name of the LLM the client is using.|
|» llm_parameter_count|body|string|false|Parameter count of the client LLM.|
|» llm_quantization|body|string|false|Quantization of the client LLM.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "nonce": "c6feda4e-6501-4db9-a21f-665e5b4ce2ba",
    "problem": "W#hAt iS f!Ve tImEs sEvEn? Round to 0 decimal places. Omit units.",
    "challenge_type": "math",
    "precision": 0,
    "terms_and_conditions_url": "https://telnyx.com/terms-and-conditions-of-service",
    "privacy_policy_url": "https://telnyx.com/privacy-policy"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "There was a problem in the JSON you submitted. Please check your formatting and try again."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "No bot challenge problems available"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="issue-a-bot-challenge-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Challenge issued.|[BotChallengeResponse](#schemabotchallengeresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The JSON request body could not be parsed.|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|No bot challenge problems are currently available.|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Exchange a magic link token for a session

<a id="opIdcreateBotSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.telnyx.com/v2/bot_sessions?email=agent-owner%40example.com&portal_redirect_token=01890a7e-e2f7-7c3d-8dbb-9a2c5f3d1e0b' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /bot_sessions`

Consumes the one-time portal redirect (magic link) token emailed during bot signup and returns an API session. The token is a UUIDv7 that encodes its creation time; it expires after a configurable validity window (15 minutes by default) and is cleared on first use. Although the action creates a session, the route uses the GET verb because it is opened from an email link. On first use the account is also initialized. For bot signup (freemium) accounts the response is a minimal envelope containing only the `api_v2_token`; accounts that are permitted to use magic links but are not freemium accounts may instead receive an extended session payload when additional steps (such as two-factor authentication or identity verification) are required. This endpoint is public; the magic link token in the query string is the credential.

<h3 id="exchange-a-magic-link-token-for-a-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|query|string(email)|true|Email address associated with the magic link token.|
|portal_redirect_token|query|string(uuid)|true|Single-use portal redirect (magic link) token, a UUIDv7 sent to the account owner's email.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "api_v2_token": "KEY0189A1B2C3D4E5F6071829AB3C4D5E_5FhZonmFvcw8Yq0dME27Bg"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Account could not be initialized"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Your sign-in link has expired. Please request a new one-time sign-in link."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Your registration cannot be accepted as it does not comply with our security standards. You may contact support for assistance."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10005",
      "title": "Resource not found",
      "detail": "The requested resource or URL could not be found.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/"
      },
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="exchange-a-magic-link-token-for-a-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Session created. Bot signup accounts receive a minimal token envelope.|[BotSessionResponse](#schemabotsessionresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The account could not be initialized.|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing or invalid email or token, expired token, or the account is not eligible to sign in (inactive, suspended, not permitted to use magic links, or must use SSO).|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Request blocked by security policy (for example, the caller's country is not accepted).|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|404|Not Found|Bot signup is not available (freemium master switch disabled or the caller's country is not enabled).|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Register via bot signup

<a id="opIdcreateBotSignup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/bot_signup \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "agent-owner@example.com",
    "terms_of_service": true,
    "terms_and_conditions_url": "https://telnyx.com/terms-and-conditions-of-service",
    "privacy_policy_url": "https://telnyx.com/privacy-policy",
    "bot_challenge_nonce": "c6feda4e-6501-4db9-a21f-665e5b4ce2ba",
    "bot_challenge_answer": "35"
  }'
```

`POST /bot_signup`

Creates a freemium Telnyx account through the agentic signup flow. The request must carry a valid answer to a previously issued bot challenge (`bot_challenge_nonce` and `bot_challenge_answer`), accept the terms of service, and echo the exact terms-and-conditions and privacy-policy URLs returned by the challenge endpoint. When EU consent enforcement is enabled, `terms_of_service_eu` and `terms_and_conditions_eu_url` are also required. On success a one-time sign-in (magic) link is emailed to the address provided; if the email address belongs to an existing account, a sign-in link is sent instead of creating a duplicate account. `email` may only be omitted when placeholder-email registration is enabled server-side. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated, gated by the freemium feature flags and per-country availability, and subject to per-IP and per-domain registration limits.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "agent-owner@example.com",
  "terms_of_service": true,
  "terms_and_conditions_url": "https://telnyx.com/terms-and-conditions-of-service",
  "privacy_policy_url": "https://telnyx.com/privacy-policy",
  "bot_challenge_nonce": "c6feda4e-6501-4db9-a21f-665e5b4ce2ba",
  "bot_challenge_answer": "35"
}
```

<h3 id="register-via-bot-signup-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BotSignupRequest](#schemabotsignuprequest)|true|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|Email address for the new account. The magic link is sent here. May only be omitted when placeholder-email registration is enabled server-side.|
|» terms_of_service|body|boolean|true|Must be true to accept the terms of service.|
|» terms_and_conditions_url|body|string|true|Must exactly match the terms-and-conditions URL returned by the challenge endpoint.|
|» privacy_policy_url|body|string|true|Must exactly match the privacy-policy URL returned by the challenge endpoint.|
|» terms_of_service_eu|body|boolean|false|EU terms-of-service acceptance. Required when EU consent enforcement is enabled.|
|» terms_and_conditions_eu_url|body|string|false|EU terms-and-conditions URL. Required when EU consent enforcement is enabled.|
|» bot_challenge_nonce|body|string(uuid)|true|Nonce from a previously issued bot challenge.|
|» bot_challenge_answer|body|string|true|Answer to the issued bot challenge.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» terms_of_service|true|
|» terms_of_service_eu|true|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "A one-time sign-in link has been sent to your email address."
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Bot challenge parameters are required"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Your registration cannot be accepted as it does not comply with our security standards. You may contact support for assistance."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10005",
      "title": "Resource not found",
      "detail": "The requested resource or URL could not be found.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/"
      },
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10027",
      "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
      "detail": "Email is invalid",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/email"
      },
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10027"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10011",
      "title": "Too many requests",
      "detail": "You have exceeded the maximum number of allowed requests.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/"
      },
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10011"
```

<h3 id="register-via-bot-signup-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Registration accepted and a magic link emailed.|[SuccessResponse](#schemasuccessresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bot challenge parameters missing or verification failed, terms of service not accepted, or terms/privacy URLs missing or not matching the expected values.|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Registration blocked by security policy (for example, registration from the caller's country is not accepted).|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|404|Not Found|Bot signup is not available (freemium master switch disabled or the caller's country is not enabled).|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed (for example an invalid email address), or the IP address has reached its bot signup limit.|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many registrations from this email domain.|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|

This operation does not require authentication
