## Resend a bot signup magic link

<a id="opIdresendBotSignupMagicLink"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/bot_signup/resend_magic_link \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "agent-owner@example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /bot_signup/resend_magic_link`

Resends the one-time sign-in (magic) link for an eligible bot signup account. Eligibility (account exists, was registered through bot signup, is active, and has not exceeded the resend limit or rate window) is evaluated server-side; the response is intentionally uniform and does not reveal whether the account exists or whether a link was actually sent. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated, gated by the freemium feature flags and per-country availability.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "agent-owner@example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="resend-a-bot-signup-magic-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ResendMagicLinkRequest](#schemaresendmagiclinkrequest)|true|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|Email address of the bot signup account to resend the magic link to.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "A one-time sign-in link has been sent to your email address."
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "There was a problem in the JSON you submitted. Please check your formatting and try again."
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Your registration cannot be accepted as it does not comply with our security standards. You may contact support for assistance."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10005",
      "title": "Resource not found",
      "detail": "The requested resource or URL could not be found.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/"

        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005"

}
```

|403|Forbidden|Request blocked by security policy (for example, the caller's country is not accepted).|[bot-signup_ErrorResponse](#schemabot-signup_errorresponse)|

This endpoint is used to create a new brand. A brand is an entity created by The Campaign Registry (TCR) that represents an organization or a company. It is this entity that TCR created campaigns will be associated with. Each brand creation will entail an upfront, non-refundable $4 expense.

## Get Brand Feedback By Id

<a id="opIdGetBrandFeedbackById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/10dlc/brand/feedback/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /10dlc/brand/feedback/{brandId}`

Get feedback about a brand by ID. This endpoint can be used after creating or revetting
a brand.

Possible values for `.category[].id`:

* `TAX_ID` - Data mismatch related to tax id and its associated properties.
* `STOCK_SYMBOL` - Non public entity registered as a public for profit entity or
  the stock information mismatch.
* `GOVERNMENT_ENTITY` - Non government entity registered as a government entity.
  Must be a U.S. government entity.
* `NONPROFIT` - Not a recognized non-profit entity. No IRS tax-exempt status
  found.
* `OTHERS` - Details of the data misrepresentation if any.

<h3 id="get-brand-feedback-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brandId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the brand.|

```json
{
  "brandId": "d88dd2aa-1bb9-4ef0-9ec8-1752b80316a5",
  "category": [
    {
      "id": "TAX_ID",
      "displayName": "Tax Id",
      "description": "Tax Id does not match with the company name or business type.",

}
```

## Get Brand SMS OTP Status

<a id="opIdGetBrandSmsOtpStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/10dlc/brand/smsOtp/OTP4B2001 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /10dlc/brand/smsOtp/{referenceId}`

Query the status of an SMS OTP (One-Time Password) for Sole Proprietor brand verification.

This endpoint allows you to check the delivery and verification status of an OTP sent during the Sole Proprietor brand verification process. You can query by either:

* `referenceId` - The reference ID returned when the OTP was initially triggered
* `brandId` - Query parameter for portal users to look up OTP status by Brand ID

The response includes delivery status, verification dates, and detailed delivery information.

<h3 id="get-brand-sms-otp-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|referenceId|path|string|true|The reference ID returned when the OTP was initially triggered|
|brandId|query|string|false|Filter by Brand ID for easier lookup in portal applications|

|» city|body|string|false|City name|
|» state|body|string|false|State. Must be 2 letters code for United States.|
|» postalCode|body|string|false|Postal codes. Use 5 digit zipcode for United States|
|» country|body|string|true|ISO2 2 characters country code. Example: US - United States|

|» stockSymbol|body|string|false|(Required for public company) stock symbol.|
|» stockExchange|body|object|false|(Required for public company) stock exchange.|
|» ipAddress|body|string|false|IP address of the browser requesting to create brand identity.|

|» webhookURL|body|string|false|Webhook URL for brand status updates.|
|» webhookFailoverURL|body|string|false|Webhook failover URL for brand status updates.|
|» altBusinessId|body|string|false|Alternate business identifier such as DUNS, LEI, or GIIN|

`POST /10dlc/brand/{brandId}/externalVetting`

## Verify Brand SMS OTP

<a id="opIdVerifyBrandSmsOtp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/10dlc/brand/4b20019b-043a-78f8-0657-b3be3f4b4002/smsOtp \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "otpPin": "123456"
  }'
```

`PUT /10dlc/brand/{brandId}/smsOtp`

Verify the SMS OTP (One-Time Password) for Sole Proprietor brand verification.

**Verification Flow:**

1. User receives OTP via SMS after triggering
2. User submits the OTP pin through this endpoint
3. Upon successful verification:
   - A `BRAND_OTP_VERIFIED` webhook event is sent to the CSP
   - The brand's `identityStatus` changes to `VERIFIED`
   - Campaigns can now be created for this brand

**Error Handling:**

Provides proper error responses for:
* Invalid OTP pins
* Expired OTPs
* OTP verification failures

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "otpPin": "123456"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-brand-sms-otp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brandId|path|string|true|The Brand ID for which to verify the OTP|
|body|body|[VerifyBrandSmsOtpRequest](#schemaverifybrandsmsotprequest)|true|none|
|» otpPin|body|string|true|The OTP PIN received via SMS|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "Message",
      "type": "Error Type"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
```

```json
{

}
```

## Trigger Brand SMS OTP

<a id="opIdTriggerBrandSmsOtp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/10dlc/brand/4b20019b-043a-78f8-0657-b3be3f4b4002/smsOtp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "pinSms": "Your PIN is @OTP_PIN@",
    "successSms": "Verification successful!"
  }'
```

`POST /10dlc/brand/{brandId}/smsOtp`

Trigger or re-trigger an SMS OTP (One-Time Password) for Sole Proprietor brand verification.

**Important Notes:**

* Only allowed for Sole Proprietor (`SOLE_PROPRIETOR`) brands
* Triggers generation of a one-time password sent to the `mobilePhone` number in the brand's profile
* Campaigns cannot be created until OTP verification is complete
* US/CA numbers only for real OTPs; mock brands can use non-US/CA numbers for testing
* Returns a `referenceId` that can be used to check OTP status via the GET `/10dlc/brand/smsOtp/{referenceId}` endpoint

**Use Cases:**

* Initial OTP trigger after Sole Proprietor brand creation
* Re-triggering OTP if the user didn't receive or needs a new code

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pinSms": "Your PIN is @OTP_PIN@",
  "successSms": "Verification successful!"
}
```

<h3 id="trigger-brand-sms-otp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brandId|path|string|true|The Brand ID for which to trigger the OTP|
|body|body|[TriggerBrandSmsOtpRequest](#schematriggerbrandsmsotprequest)|true|none|
|» pinSms|body|string|true|SMS message template to send the OTP. Must include `@OTP_PIN@` placeholder which will be replaced with the actual PIN|
|» successSms|body|string|true|SMS message to send upon successful OTP verification|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "brandId": "4b20019b-043a-78f8-0657-b3be3f4b4002",
```

## Get Brand Feedback By Id

<a id="opIdGetBrandFeedbackById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/10dlc/brand_feedback/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /10dlc/brand_feedback/{brandId}`

Get feedback about a brand by ID. This endpoint can be used after creating or revetting
a brand.

Possible values for `.category[].id`:

* `TAX_ID` - Data mismatch related to tax id and its associated properties.
* `STOCK_SYMBOL` - Non public entity registered as a public for profit entity or
  the stock information mismatch.
* `GOVERNMENT_ENTITY` - Non government entity registered as a government entity.
  Must be a U.S. government entity.
* `NONPROFIT` - Not a recognized non-profit entity. No IRS tax-exempt status
  found.
* `OTHERS` - Details of the data misrepresentation if any.

<h3 id="get-brand-feedback-by-id-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|brandId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the brand.|

<a id="opIdCloseBrowserSession"></a>

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /browser_sessions/{id}`

Closes a ready session and releases its resources. An already closed, failed, or expired session is returned unchanged; a provisioning session returns 409 session_not_ready.

<h3 id="close-browser-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "bsess_3b108e10-906a-486e-9132-196726ba7979",
    "status": "provisioning",
    "failure_reason": "string",
    "policy": {
      "allowed_domains": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "limits": {
      "lifetime_s": 0,
      "idle_timeout_s": 0
    },
    "metadata": {},
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "ready_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "last_activity_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "expires_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "closed_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10009",
      "title": "Authentication failed",
      "detail": "Could not find any usable credentials in the request.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/"
      },
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10009"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "session not found",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "session_not_ready",
    "message": "session is still provisioning",
    "retryable": true
  }
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "execution_lost",
    "message": "Request could not be completed reliably",
    "retryable": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="close-browser-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Session after close, or its unchanged terminal state.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized — missing or invalid API key.|[GatewayError](#schemagatewayerror)|
|404|Not Found|Session or artifact not found.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|Session is still provisioning. Poll its state before retrying the close.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The request could not be completed reliably. Retrieve action and session state before retrying; a mutation may already have taken effect. Do not blindly repeat it with a new idempotency key or session.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

<h3 id="close-browser-session-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[Session](#schemasession)|false|none|none|

bearerAuth

<h1 id="telnyx-api-bulk-phone-number-campaigns">Bulk Phone Number Campaigns</h1>

Phone number campaign bulk assignment

## Assign Messaging Profile To Campaign

<a id="opIdPostAssignMessagingProfileToCampaign"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/10dlc/phoneNumberAssignmentByProfile \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "messagingProfileId": "4001767e-ce0f-4cae-9d5f-0d5e636e7809",
    "tcrCampaignId": "CWZTFH1",
    "campaignId": "4b300178-131c-d902-d54e-72d90ba1620j"
  }'
```

`POST /10dlc/phoneNumberAssignmentByProfile`

This endpoint allows you to link all phone numbers associated with a Messaging Profile to a campaign. **Please note:** if you want to assign phone numbers to a campaign that you did not create with Telnyx 10DLC services, this endpoint allows that provided that you've shared the campaign with Telnyx. In this case, only provide the parameter, `tcrCampaignId`, and not `campaignId`. In all other cases (where the campaign you're assigning was created with Telnyx 10DLC services), only provide `campaignId`, not `tcrCampaignId`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "messagingProfileId": "4001767e-ce0f-4cae-9d5f-0d5e636e7809",
  "tcrCampaignId": "CWZTFH1",
  "campaignId": "4b300178-131c-d902-d54e-72d90ba1620j"
}
```

<h3 id="assign-messaging-profile-to-campaign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AssignProfileToCampaignRequest](#schemaassignprofiletocampaignrequest)|true|none|
|» messagingProfileId|body|string|true|The ID of the messaging profile that you want to link to the specified campaign.|
|» tcrCampaignId|body|string|false|The TCR ID of the shared campaign you want to link to the specified messaging profile (for campaigns not created using Telnyx 10DLC services only). If you supply this ID in the request, do not also include a campaignId.|
|» campaignId|body|string|false|The ID of the campaign you want to link to the specified messaging profile. If you supply this ID in the request, do not also include a tcrCampaignId.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "messagingProfileId": "4001767e-ce0f-4cae-9d5f-0d5e636e7809",
  "tcrCampaignId": "CWZTFH1",
  "campaignId": "4b300178-131c-d902-d54e-72d90ba1620j",
  "taskId": "667a80f8-b0a9-49d0-b9ab-a7a1bcc45086"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "string",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string",
        "parameter": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="assign-messaging-profile-to-campaign-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Successful Response|[AssignProfileToCampaignResponse](#schemaassignprofiletocampaignresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Error searching for phone numbers|[SettingsDataErrorMessage](#schemasettingsdataerrormessage)|
|4XX|Client Error|Generic response error|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|

bearerAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="telnyx-api-bulk-phone-number-operations">Bulk Phone Number Operations</h1>

Background jobs performed over a batch of phone numbers

## Lists the phone numbers jobs

<a id="opIdListPhoneNumbersJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/phone_numbers/jobs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /phone_numbers/jobs`

Returns background jobs that operate on phone numbers. Filter by job type, target phone numbers, job status, or creation-time customer reference, and sort by creation time. Multiple phone-number or status values use OR semantics within that filter; different filter categories use AND semantics. Results include pagination metadata.

<h3 id="lists-the-phone-numbers-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|object|false|Consolidated page parameter (deepObject style). Originally: page[size], page[number]|
|sort|query|string|false|Specifies the sort order for results. If not given, results are sorted by created_at in descending order.|
|filter|query|object|false|Consolidated filter parameter (deepObject style). Originally: filter[type], filter[phone_number], filter[phone_number][], filter[status][], filter[customer_reference]|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created_at|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "42587e44-3a3e-46de-9255-0c9a7a1d1ec7",
      "record_type": "phone_numbers_job",
      "status": "pending",
      "type": "update_emergency_settings",
      "etc": "2020-10-30T18:10:00.000Z",
      "created_at": "2020-10-23T18:10:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-10-23T18:10:01.000Z",
      "phone_numbers": [
        {
          "id": "2637816387126861836"
```

## Update a batch of numbers

<a id="opIdCreateUpdatePhoneNumbersJob"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/phone_numbers/jobs/update_phone_numbers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "phone_numbers": [
      "1583466971586889004",
      "+13127367254"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "tag"
    ],
    "external_pin": "123456",
    "customer_reference": "customer-reference",
    "connection_id": "dc8e4d67-33a0-4cbb-af74-7b58f05bd494",
    "billing_group_id": "dc8e4d67-33a0-4cbb-af74-7b58f05bd494",
    "deletion_lock_enabled": true,
    "voice": {
      "call_forwarding": {
        "call_forwarding_enabled": true,
        "forwards_to": "+13035559123",
        "forwarding_type": "always"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /phone_numbers/jobs/update_phone_numbers`

Creates a new background job to update a batch of numbers. At most one thousand numbers can be updated per API call. At least one of the updateable fields must be submitted. IMPORTANT: You must either specify filters (using the filter parameters) or specific phone numbers (using the phone_numbers parameter in the request body). If you specify filters, ALL phone numbers that match the given filters (up to 1000 at a time) will be updated. If you want to update only specific numbers, you must use the phone_numbers parameter in the request body. When using the phone_numbers parameter, ensure you follow the correct format as shown in the example (either phone number IDs or phone numbers in E164 format).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "phone_numbers": [
    "1583466971586889004",
    "+13127367254"
  ],
  "tags": [
    "tag"
  ],
  "external_pin": "123456",
  "customer_reference": "customer-reference",
  "connection_id": "dc8e4d67-33a0-4cbb-af74-7b58f05bd494",
  "billing_group_id": "dc8e4d67-33a0-4cbb-af74-7b58f05bd494",
  "deletion_lock_enabled": true,
  "voice": {
    "call_forwarding": {
      "call_forwarding_enabled": true,
      "forwards_to": "+13035559123",
      "forwarding_type": "always"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-batch-of-numbers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|object|false|Consolidated filter parameter (deepObject style). Originally: filter[has_bundle], filter[tag], filter[connection_id], filter[phone_number], filter[status], filter[voice.connection_name], filter[voice.usage_payment_method], filter[billing_group_id], filter[emergency_address_id], filter[customer_reference]|
|body|body|[numbers_PhoneNumbersJobUpdatePhoneNumbersRequest](#schemanumbers_phonenumbersjobupdatephonenumbersrequest)|true|none|
|» phone_numbers|body|[string]|true|Array of phone number ids and/or phone numbers in E164 format to update. This parameter is required if no filter parameters are provided. If you want to update specific numbers rather than all numbers matching a filter, you must use this parameter. Each item must be either a valid phone number ID or a phone number in E164 format (e.g., '+13127367254').|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|A list of user-assigned tags to help organize phone numbers.|
|» external_pin|body|string|false|If someone attempts to port your phone number away from Telnyx and your phone number has an external PIN set, we will attempt to verify that you provided the correct external PIN to the winning carrier. Note that not all carriers cooperate with this security mechanism.|
|» customer_reference|body|string|false|Sets the customer reference on the selected phone numbers and retains the supplied value on the job. Recover the job without its ID using GET /phone_numbers/jobs with filter[customer_reference] within 90 days of job creation. This body field updates the numbers; the separate filter[customer_reference] query parameter selects numbers by their current reference.|
|» connection_id|body|string|false|Identifies the connection associated with the phone number.|
|» billing_group_id|body|string|false|Identifies the billing group associated with the phone number.|
|» hd_voice_enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether to enable or disable HD Voice on each phone number. HD Voice is a paid feature and may not be available for all phone numbers, more details about it can be found in the Telnyx support documentation.|
|» deletion_lock_enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether to enable or disable the deletion lock on each phone number. When enabled, this prevents the phone number from being deleted via the API or Telnyx portal.|
|» voice|body|[UpdatePhoneNumberVoiceSettingsRequest](#schemaupdatephonenumbervoicesettingsrequest)|false|none|

<h3 id="create-a-new-cdr-report-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CdrDetailedRequest](#schemacdrdetailedrequest)|true|CDR detailed report request data|
|» start_time|body|string(date-time)|true|Start time in ISO format|
|» end_time|body|string(date-time)|true|End time in ISO format|
|» timezone|body|string|false|Timezone for the report|
|» call_types|body|[integer(int32)]|false|List of call types to filter by (Inbound = 1, Outbound = 2)|
|» record_types|body|[integer(int32)]|false|List of record types to filter by (Complete = 1, Incomplete = 2, Errors = 3)|
|» connections|body|[integer(int64)]|false|List of connections to filter by|
|» report_name|body|string|false|Name of the report|
|» source|body|string|false|Source of the report. Valid values: calls (default), call-control, fax-api, webrtc|
|» include_all_metadata|body|boolean|false|Whether to include all metadata|
|» filters|body|[[Filter](#schemafilter)]|false|List of filters to apply|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|Set of fields to include in the report|
|» managed_accounts|body|[string(uuid)]|false|List of managed accounts to include|
|» select_all_managed_accounts|body|boolean|false|Whether to select all managed accounts|

`GET /reports/cdr_usage_reports/sync`

Generate and fetch voice usage report synchronously. This endpoint will both generate and fetch the voice report over a specified time period. No polling is necessary but the response may take up to a couple of minutes.

|aggregation_type|query|string|true|Type of aggregation to apply to the results.|
|product_breakdown|query|string|true|Filter results by product breakdown.|

`POST /calls`

Dial a number or SIP URI from a given connection. A successful response will include a `call_leg_id` which can be used to correlate the command with subsequent webhooks.

To place the call with an AI assistant from the start, include `assistant.id` and any per-call overrides in the `assistant` object; Telnyx attempts to warm up the assistant before placing the call and starts it automatically when the called party answers.

**Expected Webhooks:**

- `call.initiated`
- `call.answered` or `call.hangup`
- `call.conversation.created` when the requested assistant conversation is created, or `call.conversation.start_failed` when it could not be started after the called party answered
- `call.hold` and `call.unhold` if the call is held/unheld
- `call.machine.detection.ended` if `answering_machine_detection` was requested
- `call.machine.greeting.ended` if `answering_machine_detection` was requested to detect the end of machine greeting
- `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` if `answering_machine_detection=premium` was requested
- `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended` if `answering_machine_detection=premium` was requested and a beep was detected
- `call.machine.premium.call_screening.detected` if `answering_machine_detection=premium_ios_call_screening_detection` was requested and an Apple Call Screening tone was detected
- `call.deepfake_detection.result` if `deepfake_detection` was enabled
- `call.deepfake_detection.error` if `deepfake_detection` was enabled and an error occurred
- `streaming.started`, `streaming.stopped` or `streaming.failed` if `stream_url` was set

When the `record` parameter is set to `record-from-answer`, the response will include a `recording_id` field.

<h3 id="dial-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CallRequest](#schemacallrequest)|true|Call request|
|» assistant|body|[CallAssistantRequest](#schemacallassistantrequest)|false|AI Assistant configuration and per-call overrides. All fields except `id` are optional. Omitted assistant fields use the stored configuration. Supplied `voice_settings` and `transcription` objects replace their stored objects rather than merging individual settings; include every setting you want to retain. `dynamic_variables` are merged, with request values taking precedence.|
|» conversation_relay_config|body|[ConversationRelayEmbeddedConfig](#schemaconversationrelayembeddedconfig)|false|Starts a Conversation Relay session automatically when the answered/dialed call is answered. This embedded shape is supported on `answer` and `dial`. It uses public field names (`url`, `dtmf_detection`, `greeting`, `voice`, `language`, etc.) and maps them to the underlying Conversation Relay action. `client_state`, `tts_language`, and `transcription_language` inside this object are ignored; use the parent command's `client_state` and `command_id` fields instead.|
|» to|body|string \| [string]|true|The DID or SIP URI to dial out to. Multiple DID or SIP URIs can be provided using an array of strings. For SIP URI destinations, append `;secure=true` or `;secure=srtp` to enable SRTP media encryption for that endpoint, or `;secure=dtls` to enable DTLS media encryption for that endpoint. If `media_encryption` is set to `SRTP` or `DTLS`, it takes precedence over any per-endpoint `secure` URI parameter. For a single string destination, you may append a comma followed by DTMF digits (e.g. `+18004247767,200`) to play those digits as DTMF once the called party answers — equivalent to setting `send_digits_on_answer` separately. If both are present, the explicit `send_digits_on_answer` parameter takes precedence. This shorthand is not supported when `to` is an array.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» from|body|string|true|The `from` number to be used as the caller id presented to the destination (`to` number). The number should be in +E164 format.|
|» diversion|body|string|false|The `to` number of an active inbound call, in +E164 format. Telnyx checks whether there is currently an active inbound call where `to` matches this `diversion` value and `from` matches the `from` number supplied for this request. If such a call exists, the `from` number is treated as verified (since it is already on an active inbound call to you) and can be used as the caller id for this outbound call.|
|» from_display_name|body|string|false|The `from_display_name` string to be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`to` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and -_~!.+ special characters. If ommited, the display name will be the same as the number in the `from` field.|
|» privacy|body|string|false|Indicates the privacy level to be used for the call. When set to `id`, caller ID information (name and number) will be hidden from the called party. When set to `none` or omitted, caller ID will be shown normally.|
|» connection_id|body|string|true|The ID of the Call Control App (formerly ID of the connection) to be used when dialing the destination.|
|» audio_url|body|string|false|The URL of a file to be played back to the callee when the call is answered. The URL can point to either a WAV or MP3 file. media_name and audio_url cannot be used together in one request.|
|» send_digits_on_answer|body|string|false|DTMF digits to send automatically after the called party answers. Useful for reaching an extension behind an IVR (e.g. `"200"` to dial extension 200 once the called party picks up). Allowed characters: `0-9`, `A-D`, `w` (0.5s pause), `W` (1s pause), `*`, `#`. Maximum 64 characters. When omitted, no automatic DTMF is sent. May also be supplied inline by appending `,<digits>` to `to` (e.g. `to=+18004247767,200`); if both forms are present, this explicit field takes precedence.|
|» media_name|body|string|false|The media_name of a file to be played back to the callee when the call is answered. The media_name must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. The file must either be a WAV or MP3 file.|
|» preferred_codecs|body|string|false|The list of comma-separated codecs in a preferred order for the forked media to be received.|
|» timeout_secs|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the call to be answered by the destination to which it is being called. If the timeout is reached before an answer is received, the call will hangup and a `call.hangup` webhook with a `hangup_cause` of `timeout` will be sent. Minimum value is 5 seconds. Maximum value is 600 seconds.|
|» retry_on_timeout|body|boolean|false|Whether to keep trying the remaining routing paths (e.g. alternate providers/gateways) for the same destination after `timeout_secs` is reached for the current attempt. When set to `false`, reaching `timeout_secs` aborts the entire dial attempt and the `call.hangup` webhook reports a `hangup_cause` of `no_answer` instead of `timeout`.|
|» time_limit_secs|body|integer(int32)|false|Sets the maximum duration of a Call Control Leg in seconds. If the time limit is reached, the call will hangup and a `call.hangup` webhook with a `hangup_cause` of `time_limit` will be sent. For example, by setting a time limit of 120 seconds, a Call Leg will be automatically terminated two minutes after being answered. The default time limit is 14400 seconds or 4 hours and this is also the maximum allowed call length.|
|» answering_machine_detection|body|string|false|Enables Answering Machine Detection. Telnyx offers Premium and Standard detections. With Premium detection, when a call is answered, Telnyx runs real-time detection and sends a `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` webhook with one of the following results: `human_residence`, `human_business`, `machine`, `silence` or `fax_detected`. If we detect a beep, we also send a `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended` webhook with the result of `beep_detected`. If we detect a beep before `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` we only send `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended`, and if we detect a beep after `call.machine.premium.detection.ended`, we send both webhooks. With Standard detection, when a call is answered, Telnyx runs real-time detection to determine if it was picked up by a human or a machine and sends an `call.machine.detection.ended` webhook with the analysis result. If `greeting_end` or `detect_words` is used and a `machine` is detected, you will receive another `call.machine.greeting.ended` webhook when the answering machine greeting ends with a beep or silence. If `detect_beep` is used, you will only receive `call.machine.greeting.ended` if a beep is detected. If `answering_machine_detection` is set to `premium_ios_call_screening_detection`, Premium AMD runs with iOS Call Screening support: after an initial `machine` result, Telnyx listens for the iOS call-screening prompt to end or for an Apple Call Screening tone, sends `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended` with `result=prompt_ended` or `call.machine.premium.call_screening.detected` with `result=screening` respectively. When the Apple Call Screening tone is detected, Premium AMD is restarted on the screened call and a `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` webhook with the post-screening classification follows.|
|» answering_machine_detection_config|body|object|false|Optional configuration parameters to modify 'answering_machine_detection' performance. Only `total_analysis_time_millis` and `greeting_duration_millis` parameters are applicable when `premium` is selected as answering_machine_detection. `prompt_end_timeout_millis` is additionally applicable when `premium_ios_call_screening_detection` is selected.|
|» » total_analysis_time_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum timeout threshold for overall detection.|
|» » beep_detection_profile|body|string|false|Selects which detectors must validate a beep. `both` requires the amplitude and frequency detectors to agree. `freq_only` uses the frequency detector alone, for beeps whose volume is too unsteady for the default profile.|
|» » beep_min_frequency_hz|body|integer(int32)|false|Lowest frequency, in Hz, that a tone must reach to be treated as a beep. Raising it above 480 excludes North American ringback (440 + 480 Hz), which can otherwise be reported as a beep when the `freq_only` profile is in use. Only used when beep detection is active.|
|» » beep_max_frequency_hz|body|integer(int32)|false|Highest frequency, in Hz, that a tone can reach and still be treated as a beep. Only used when beep detection is active.|
|» » beep_min_tone_duration_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|Shortest tone, in milliseconds, that can be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects brief tones such as call-progress blips. Only used when beep detection is active.|
|» » beep_spectral_confirmation|body|boolean|false|When enabled, a candidate beep must pass an additional spectral check before it is reported. Only used when beep detection is active.|
|» » beep_spectral_window_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|Length of the spectral confirmation window, in milliseconds. Only used when beep detection is active.|
|» » beep_spectral_min_purity|body|number|false|Minimum spectral purity, from 0 to 1, for a tone to be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects mixed tones such as ringback, which combines two frequencies. Only used when beep detection is active.|
|» » beep_spectral_reject_fax_cng|body|boolean|false|When enabled, the fax CNG tone is rejected rather than reported as a beep. Only used when beep detection is active.|
|» » after_greeting_silence_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|Silence duration threshold after a greeting message or voice for it be considered human.|
|» » between_words_silence_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum threshold for silence between words.|
|» » greeting_duration_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum threshold of a human greeting. If greeting longer than this value, considered machine.|
|» » initial_silence_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|If initial silence duration is greater than this value, consider it a machine.|
|» » maximum_number_of_words|body|integer(int32)|false|If number of detected words is greater than this value, consder it a machine.|
|» » maximum_word_length_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|If a single word lasts longer than this threshold, consider it a machine.|
|» » silence_threshold|body|integer(int32)|false|Minimum noise threshold for any analysis.|
|» » greeting_total_analysis_time_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|If machine already detected, maximum timeout threshold to determine the end of the machine greeting.|
|» » greeting_silence_duration_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|If machine already detected, maximum threshold for silence between words. If exceeded, the greeting is considered ended.|
|» » prompt_end_timeout_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum time Telnyx waits, in milliseconds, for the iOS call-screening prompt to end after Premium AMD initially detects a `machine`. Used when `answering_machine_detection` is `premium_ios_call_screening_detection`. Defaults to 5000 milliseconds.|

The default value is 0 (infinite).|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response with details about a call status that includes recording_id.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request. The request was invalid or cannot be served. Common causes include: audio file download failures, attempting to delete non-empty queues, invalid characters in the request, or character encoding errors.|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity. The request was well-formed but could not be processed due to semantic errors. This includes validation errors, invalid parameter values, call state errors, conference errors, queue errors, recording/transcription errors, and business logic violations.|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests. The number of dial attempts per second allowed for your account has been exceeded. Reduce the rate of outbound dial attempts and retry.|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error. An unexpected error occurred on the server. This is typically returned for unhandled exceptions or system failures.|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable. The service is temporarily unavailable. This may occur during maintenance or when the service is overloaded.|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|

## Add messages to AI Assistant

<a id="opIdCallAddMessagesToAIAssistant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/ai_assistant_add_messages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
    "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "system",
        "content": "Get the user'\''s favorite color"
      }
    ],
    "trigger_response": false
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/ai_assistant_add_messages`

Add messages to the conversation started by an AI assistant on the call.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "Get the user's favorite color"
    }
  ],
  "trigger_response": false
}
```

<h3 id="add-messages-to-ai-assistant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|body|body|[AIAssistantAddMessagesRequest](#schemaaiassistantaddmessagesrequest)|true|AI Assistant add messages request|
|» client_state|body|string|false|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|» command_id|body|string|false|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|» messages|body|[[UserMessage](#schemausermessage) \| [AssistantMessage](#schemaassistantmessage) \| [ToolMessage](#schematoolmessage) \| [SystemMessage](#schemasystemmessage) \| [DeveloperMessage](#schemadevelopermessage)]|false|The messages to add to the conversation.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[UserMessage](#schemausermessage)|false|Messages sent by an end user|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[AssistantMessage](#schemaassistantmessage)|false|Messages sent by the model in response to user messages.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ToolMessage](#schematoolmessage)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[SystemMessage](#schemasystemmessage)|false|Developer-provided instructions that the model should follow, regardless of messages sent by the user.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[DeveloperMessage](#schemadevelopermessage)|false|Developer-provided instructions that the model should follow, regardless of messages sent by the user.|
|» trigger_response|body|boolean|false|When `true`, the injected messages immediately trigger an assistant response/turn instead of waiting for the next natural turn or idle timeout. This may interrupt a user who is still speaking.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "data": {
    "result": "ok"
  }
}
```

```json
  "errors": [

      "code": "10004",
      "title": "Missing required parameter",
      "detail": "The 'to' parameter is required and cannot be blank.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/to"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "Unexpected error",
      "detail": "An unexpected error occured."
    }
  ]
}
```

This includes validation errors, invalid parameter values, call state errors, conference errors, queue errors, recording/transcription errors, and business logic violations.|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|

## Join AI Assistant Conversation

<a id="opIdCallJoinAIAssistant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/ai_assistant_join \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
```

## Answer call

<a id="opIdAnswerCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/answer \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "assistant": {
      "id": "asst_123"
    },
    "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
    "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
    "webhook_url": "https://www.example.com/server-b/",
    "webhook_url_method": "POST",
    "send_silence_when_idle": true,
    "deepfake_detection": {
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 15,
      "rtp_timeout": 30
    }
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/answer`

Answer an incoming call. You must issue this command before executing subsequent commands on an incoming call.

To answer with an AI assistant, include `assistant.id` and any per-call overrides in the `assistant` object. Telnyx attempts to warm up the assistant before answering the call, then starts the assistant automatically when the call is answered. Do not also send `ai_assistant_start` for this flow. The HTTP success response can arrive before the call is answered; use the `call.answered` webhook to track the answer. If warm-up fails, Telnyx falls back to starting the assistant after answering.

When `assistant.id` is supplied, obtain the conversation ID from `data.payload.conversation_id` in the [call.conversation.created](/api-reference/callbacks/call-conversation-created) webhook and correlate it using `data.payload.call_control_id`. The `answer` HTTP response does not include `conversation_id`. The created event is emitted during assistant startup and does not indicate that the assistant is ready to speak.

Set the assistant voice with `assistant.voice_settings.voice` and speech-to-text settings with `assistant.transcription`. You can reuse one stored assistant with different per-call settings. Warm-up prepares assistant configuration and dependencies; it does not wait for the greeting audio to be ready or guarantee zero silence after answer. A plain `answer` followed by `ai_assistant_start` performs assistant startup after the call has already been answered.

**Expected Webhooks:**

- `call.answered`
- `call.conversation.created` when the requested assistant conversation is created
- `call.hold` and `call.unhold` if the call is held/unheld
- `call.deepfake_detection.result` if `deepfake_detection` was enabled
- `call.deepfake_detection.error` if `deepfake_detection` was enabled and an error occurred
- `streaming.started`, `streaming.stopped` or `streaming.failed` if `stream_url` was set

When the `record` parameter is set to `record-from-answer`, the response will include a `recording_id` field.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assistant": {
    "id": "asst_123"
  },
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
  "webhook_url": "https://www.example.com/server-b/",
  "webhook_url_method": "POST",
  "send_silence_when_idle": true,
  "deepfake_detection": {
    "enabled": true,
    "timeout": 15,
    "rtp_timeout": 30
  }
}
```

<h3 id="answer-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|body|body|[AnswerRequest](#schemaanswerrequest)|true|Answer call request|
|» assistant|body|[CallAssistantRequest](#schemacallassistantrequest)|false|AI Assistant configuration and per-call overrides. All fields except `id` are optional. Omitted assistant fields use the stored configuration. Supplied `voice_settings` and `transcription` objects replace their stored objects rather than merging individual settings; include every setting you want to retain. `dynamic_variables` are merged, with request values taking precedence.|
|» conversation_relay_config|body|[ConversationRelayEmbeddedConfig](#schemaconversationrelayembeddedconfig)|false|Starts a Conversation Relay session automatically when the answered/dialed call is answered. This embedded shape is supported on `answer` and `dial`. It uses public field names (`url`, `dtmf_detection`, `greeting`, `voice`, `language`, etc.) and maps them to the underlying Conversation Relay action. `client_state`, `tts_language`, and `transcription_language` inside this object are ignored; use the parent command's `client_state` and `command_id` fields instead.|
|» billing_group_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Use this field to set the Billing Group ID for the call. Must be a valid and existing Billing Group ID.|
|» client_state|body|string|false|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|» command_id|body|string|false|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|» custom_headers|body|[[CustomSipHeader](#schemacustomsipheader)]|false|Custom headers to be added to the SIP INVITE response.|
|» preferred_codecs|body|string|false|The list of comma-separated codecs in a preferred order for the forked media to be received.|
|» sip_headers|body|[[SipHeader](#schemasipheader)]|false|SIP headers to be added to the SIP INVITE response. Currently only User-to-User header is supported.|
|» sound_modifications|body|[SoundModifications](#schemasoundmodifications)|false|Use this field to modify sound effects, for example adjust the pitch.|
|» stream_url|body|string|false|The destination WebSocket address where the stream is going to be delivered.|
|» stream_track|body|string|false|Specifies which track should be streamed.|
|» stream_codec|body|[StreamCodec](#schemastreamcodec)|false|Specifies the codec to be used for the streamed audio. When set to 'default' or when transcoding is not possible, the codec from the call will be used.|
|» stream_bidirectional_mode|body|[StreamBidirectionalMode](#schemastreambidirectionalmode)|false|Configures method of bidirectional streaming (mp3, rtp).|
|» stream_bidirectional_codec|body|[StreamBidirectionalCodec](#schemastreambidirectionalcodec)|false|Indicates codec for bidirectional streaming RTP payloads. Used only with stream_bidirectional_mode=rtp. Case sensitive.|
|» stream_bidirectional_target_legs|body|[StreamBidirectionalTargetLegs](#schemastreambidirectionaltargetlegs)|false|Specifies which call legs should receive the bidirectional stream audio.|
|» send_silence_when_idle|body|boolean|false|Generate silence RTP packets when no transmission available.|
|» webhook_url|body|string|false|Use this field to override the URL for which Telnyx will send subsequent webhooks to for this call.|
|» webhook_url_method|body|string|false|HTTP request type used for `webhook_url`.|
|» transcription|body|boolean|false|Enable standalone call transcription upon call answer. The default value is false. Configure this feature with `transcription_config`. To configure speech recognition for an AI assistant, use `assistant.transcription` instead.|
|» transcription_config|body|[TranscriptionStartRequest](#schematranscriptionstartrequest)|false|none|
|» record|body|string|false|Start recording automatically after an event. Disabled by default.|
|» record_channels|body|string|false|Defines which channel should be recorded ('single' or 'dual') when `record` is specified.|
|» record_format|body|string|false|Defines the format of the recording ('wav' or 'mp3') when `record` is specified.|
|» record_max_length|body|integer(int32)|false|Defines the maximum length for the recording in seconds when `record` is specified. The minimum value is 0. The maximum value is 43200. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|» record_timeout_secs|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected when `record` is specified. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that call transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|» record_track|body|string|false|The audio track to be recorded. Can be either `both`, `inbound` or `outbound`. If only single track is specified (`inbound`, `outbound`), `channels` configuration is ignored and it will be recorded as mono (single channel).|
|» record_trim|body|string|false|When set to `trim-silence`, silence will be removed from the beginning and end of the recording.|
|» record_custom_file_name|body|string|false|The custom recording file name to be used instead of the default `call_leg_id`. Telnyx will still add a Unix timestamp suffix.|
|» webhook_urls|body|object|false|A map of event types to arrays of webhook URLs. When an event of the specified type occurs, the webhook URLs associated with that event type will be called instead of `webhook_url`. Events not mapped here will use the default `webhook_url`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[string(uri)]|false|none|
|» webhook_urls_method|body|string|false|HTTP request method to invoke `webhook_urls`.|
|» webhook_retries_policies|body|object|false|A map of event types to retry policies. Each retry policy contains an array of `retries_ms` specifying the delays between retry attempts in milliseconds. Maximum 5 retries, total delay cannot exceed 60 seconds.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » retries_ms|body|[integer]|false|Array of delays in milliseconds between retry attempts. Total sum cannot exceed 60000ms.|
|» deepfake_detection|body|object|false|Enables deepfake detection on the call. When enabled, audio from the remote party is streamed to a detection service that analyzes whether the voice is AI-generated. Results are delivered via the `call.deepfake_detection.result` webhook.|

|» » timeout|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum time in seconds to wait for a detection result before timing out.|

## Bridge calls

<a id="opIdBridgeCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/bridge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "call_control_id": "v3:MdI91X4lWFEs7IgbBEOT9M4AigoY08M0WWZFISt1Yw2axZ_IiE4pqg",
    "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
    "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
    "park_after_unbridge": "self"
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/bridge`

Bridge two call control calls.

**Expected Webhooks:**

- `call.bridged` for Leg A
- `call.bridged` for Leg B


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "call_control_id": "v3:MdI91X4lWFEs7IgbBEOT9M4AigoY08M0WWZFISt1Yw2axZ_IiE4pqg",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
  "park_after_unbridge": "self"
}
```

<h3 id="bridge-calls-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|body|body|[BridgeRequest](#schemabridgerequest)|true|Bridge call request|
|» call_control_id|body|string|true|The Call Control ID of the call you want to bridge with, can't be used together with queue parameter or video_room_id parameter.|
|» client_state|body|string|false|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|» command_id|body|string|false|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|» queue|body|string|false|The name of the queue you want to bridge with, can't be used together with call_control_id parameter or video_room_id parameter. Bridging with a queue means bridging with the first call in the queue. The call will always be removed from the queue regardless of whether bridging succeeds. Returns an error when the queue is empty.|
|» video_room_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the video room you want to bridge with, can't be used together with call_control_id parameter or queue parameter.|
|» video_room_context|body|string|false|The additional parameter that will be passed to the video conference. It is a text field and the user can decide how to use it. For example, you can set the participant name or pass JSON text. It can be used only with video_room_id parameter.|
|» prevent_double_bridge|body|boolean|false|When set to `true`, it prevents bridging if the target call is already bridged to another call. Disabled by default.|
|» park_after_unbridge|body|string|false|Specifies behavior after the bridge ends (i.e. the opposite leg either hangs up or is transferred). If supplied with the value `self`, the current leg will be parked after unbridge. If not set, the default behavior is to hang up the leg.|
|» play_ringtone|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether to play a ringtone if the call you want to bridge with has not yet been answered.|
|» ringtone|body|string|false|Specifies which country ringtone to play when `play_ringtone` is set to `true`. If not set, the US ringtone will be played.|
|» record|body|string|false|Start recording automatically after an event. Disabled by default.|
|» record_channels|body|string|false|Defines which channel should be recorded ('single' or 'dual') when `record` is specified.|
|» record_format|body|string|false|Defines the format of the recording ('wav' or 'mp3') when `record` is specified.|
|» record_max_length|body|integer(int32)|false|Defines the maximum length for the recording in seconds when `record` is specified. The minimum value is 0. The maximum value is 43200. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|» record_timeout_secs|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected when `record` is specified. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that call transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|» record_track|body|string|false|The audio track to be recorded. Can be either `both`, `inbound` or `outbound`. If only single track is specified (`inbound`, `outbound`), `channels` configuration is ignored and it will be recorded as mono (single channel).|
|» record_trim|body|string|false|When set to `trim-silence`, silence will be removed from the beginning and end of the recording.|
|» record_custom_file_name|body|string|false|The custom recording file name to be used instead of the default `call_leg_id`. Telnyx will still add a Unix timestamp suffix.|
|» mute_dtmf|body|string|false|When enabled, DTMF tones are not passed to the call participant. The webhooks containing the DTMF information will be sent.|
|» hold_after_unbridge|body|boolean|false|Specifies behavior after the bridge ends. If set to `true`, the current leg will be put on hold after unbridge instead of being hung up.|

## Start Conversation Relay

<a id="opIdCallStartConversationRelay"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/conversation_relay_start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "wss://example.com/conversation-relay",
    "dtmf_detection": true,
    "interruptible": "speech",
    "interruptible_greeting": "dtmf",
    "greeting": "Hi! Ask me anything!",
    "voice": "Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af",
    "tts_provider": "telnyx",
    "voice_settings": {
      "type": "telnyx"
    },
    "language": "en-US",
    "languages": [
      {
        "language": "en-US",
        "tts_provider": "telnyx",
        "voice": "Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af",
        "transcription_engine": "Deepgram",
        "transcription_engine_config": {
          "transcription_model": "deepgram/nova-3"
        }
      }
    ],
    "custom_parameters": {
      "customer_id": "12345"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/conversation_relay_start`

Start a Conversation Relay session on an active call. Conversation Relay connects the call audio to your WebSocket so your application can exchange realtime messages with the caller while Telnyx handles speech recognition and text-to-speech. Only one AI Assistant or Conversation Relay session can be active on a call at a time.

**Expected Webhooks:**

- `call.conversation.ended` - Sent when the Conversation Relay session ends. If the customer WebSocket disconnects, the webhook payload `reason` is `customer_disconnect`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "wss://example.com/conversation-relay",
  "dtmf_detection": true,
  "interruptible": "speech",
  "interruptible_greeting": "dtmf",
  "greeting": "Hi! Ask me anything!",
  "voice": "Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af",
  "tts_provider": "telnyx",
  "voice_settings": {
    "type": "telnyx"
  },
  "language": "en-US",
  "languages": [
    {
      "language": "en-US",
      "tts_provider": "telnyx",
      "voice": "Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af",
      "transcription_engine": "Deepgram",
      "transcription_engine_config": {
        "transcription_model": "deepgram/nova-3"
      }
    }
  ],
  "custom_parameters": {
    "customer_id": "12345"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="start-conversation-relay-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|body|body|[ConversationRelayStartRequest](#schemaconversationrelaystartrequest)|true|Conversation Relay start request|
|» conversation_relay_settings|body|[ConversationRelaySettings](#schemaconversationrelaysettings)|false|Conversation Relay connection settings. This object can provide `url`, `dtmf_detection`, `interruptible`, `interruptible_greeting`, and `languages`. Top-level aliases override nested values when both are present.|
|» url|body|string|false|Public alias for `conversation_relay_url`. Must start with `ws://` or `wss://`. If both are present, this value wins.|
|» dtmf_detection|body|boolean|false|Public alias for `conversation_relay_dtmf_detection`. If both are present, this value wins.|
|» conversation_relay_url|body|string|false|WebSocket URL for your Conversation Relay server. Must start with `ws://` or `wss://`.|
|» conversation_relay_dtmf_detection|body|boolean|false|Enable DTMF detection for the relay session.|
|» voice|body|[VoiceConfig](#schemavoiceconfig)|false|The voice to be used by the voice assistant. Currently we support ElevenLabs, Telnyx and AWS voices.<br><br> **Supported Providers:**<br>- **AWS:** Use `AWS.Polly.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna`). For neural voices, which provide more realistic, human-like speech, append `-Neural` to the `VoiceId` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna-Neural`). Check the [available voices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/available-voices.html) for compatibility.<br>- **Azure:** Use `Azure.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Azure.en-CA-ClaraNeural`, `Azure.en-CA-LiamNeural`, `Azure.en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural`, `Azure.en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural`). For a complete list of voices, go to [Azure Voice Gallery](https://speech.microsoft.com/portal/voicegallery).<br>- **ElevenLabs:** Use `ElevenLabs.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `ElevenLabs.BaseModel.John`). The `ModelId` part is optional. To use ElevenLabs, you must provide your ElevenLabs API key as an integration secret under `"voice_settings": {"api_key_ref": "<secret_id>"}`. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) for details. Check [available voices](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/get-voices).<br> - **Telnyx:** Use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>`<br>- **Inworld:** Use `Inworld.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Inworld.Mini.Loretta`, `Inworld.Max.Oliver`, `Inworld.TTS2.Loretta`). Supported models: `Mini`, `Max`, `TTS2`.<br>- **Fish Audio:** Use `FishAudio.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `FishAudio.s2.1-pro.<reference_id>`). Supported models: `s2.1-pro`, `s2-pro`, `s1`. `VoiceId` is a Fish Voice-Library reference ID.<br>- **Soniox:** Use `Soniox.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma`). Supported model: `tts-rt-v2`. Browse the catalog via the [Voices API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/text-to-speech-commands/list-available-voices). Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the text, for example `it`. SSML is not supported. Use `voice_settings` to configure `speed` (0.7 to 1.3) and `reduce_silence`.<br>- **xAI:** Use `xAI.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `xAI.eve`). Available voices: `eve`, `ara`, `rex`, `sal`, `leo`.<br>- **Humain:** Use `Humain.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Humain.sara-ar`). Available voices: `sara-en`, `abdulaziz-en`, `sara-ar`, `abdulaziz-ar`, `nourah-ar`, `abdullah-ar`. Native Arabic (Saudi dialect) and English voices only — no `ModelId` segment.|
|» voice_settings|body|[ElevenLabsVoiceSettings](#schemaelevenlabsvoicesettings) \| [TelnyxVoiceSettings](#schematelnyxvoicesettings) \| [AWSVoiceSettings](#schemaawsvoicesettings) \| [MinimaxVoiceSettings](#schemaminimaxvoicesettings) \| [AzureVoiceSettings](#schemaazurevoicesettings) \| [ResembleVoiceSettings](#schemaresemblevoicesettings) \| [InworldVoiceSettings](#schemainworldvoicesettings) \| [XAIVoiceSettings](#schemaxaivoicesettings) \| [SonioxVoiceSettings](#schemasonioxvoicesettings) \| [AssemblyAIVoiceSettings](#schemaassemblyaivoicesettings)|false|The settings associated with the voice selected|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ElevenLabsVoiceSettings](#schemaelevenlabsvoicesettings)|false|none|

|» greeting|body|string|false|Text played when the relay session starts.|
|» language|body|string|false|Default language for the relay session. This value is used for both text-to-speech and speech recognition.|
|» languages|body|[[ConversationRelayLanguage](#schemaconversationrelaylanguage)]|false|Per-language TTS and transcription settings.|
|» interruption_settings|body|[ConversationRelayInterruptionSettings](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptionsettings)|false|Settings for handling caller interruptions during Conversation Relay speech.|

|» command_id|body|string|false|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|» tts_provider|body|string|false|Text-to-speech provider. If omitted, Telnyx derives it from `voice` or `provider`.|

|» transcription_engine_config|body|[ConversationRelayTranscriptionEngineConfig](#schemaconversationrelaytranscriptionengineconfig)|false|Engine-specific transcription settings for Conversation Relay. This accepts the same provider-specific options used by the Call Transcription Start command, such as `transcription_model`, without requiring the engine discriminator to be repeated inside this object. With Deepgram Flux (`deepgram/flux`), `interim_results`, `eot_threshold` and `eager_eot_threshold` control the interim prompts and the `eagerEndOfTurn` and `turnResumed` frames sent to your WebSocket server.|
|» interruptible|body|[ConversationRelayInterruptible](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptible)|false|Controls when caller input can interrupt assistant speech. `any` allows speech or DTMF interruptions; `none` disables interruptions; `speech` allows speech only; `dtmf` allows DTMF only.|
|» interruptible_greeting|body|[ConversationRelayInterruptible](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptible)|false|Controls when caller input can interrupt assistant speech. `any` allows speech or DTMF interruptions; `none` disables interruptions; `speech` allows speech only; `dtmf` allows DTMF only.|
|» custom_parameters|body|object|false|Custom key-value parameters forwarded to the relay session as `assistant.dynamic_variables`. If `assistant.dynamic_variables` is also present, these values are merged in.|

## Enqueue call

<a id="opIdEnqueueCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/enqueue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "queue_name": "support",
    "max_wait_time_secs": 600,
    "max_size": 20,
    "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
    "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/enqueue`

Places the call into a queue, where it waits until it is removed or bridged to another leg. Queue behavior is configured through the request body.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "queue_name": "support",
  "max_wait_time_secs": 600,
  "max_size": 20,
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

<h3 id="enqueue-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|body|body|[EnqueueRequest](#schemaenqueuerequest)|true|Enqueue call request|
|» queue_name|body|string|true|The name of the queue the call should be put in. If a queue with a given name doesn't exist yet it will be created.|
|» client_state|body|string|false|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|» command_id|body|string|false|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|» max_wait_time_secs|body|integer|false|The number of seconds after which the call will be removed from the queue.|
|» max_size|body|integer|false|The maximum number of calls allowed in the queue at a given time. Can't be modified for an existing queue.|
|» keep_after_hangup|body|boolean|false|If set to true, the call will remain in the queue after hangup. In this case bridging to such call will fail with necessary information needed to re-establish the call.|

```json
    "result": "ok"
  }
}
```

```json
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
    }
```

## Forking start

<a id="opIdStartCallFork"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/fork_start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "rx": "udp:192.0.2.1:9000",
    "tx": "udp:192.0.2.1:9001",
    "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
    "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/fork_start`

Call forking allows you to stream the media from a call to a specific target in realtime. 
This stream can be used to enable realtime audio analysis to support a 
variety of use cases, including fraud detection, or the creation of AI-generated audio responses. 
Requests must specify either the `target` attribute or the `rx` and `tx` attributes.

**Expected Webhooks:**

- `call.fork.started`
- `call.fork.stopped`



> Body parameter

```json
{
  "rx": "udp:192.0.2.1:9000",
  "tx": "udp:192.0.2.1:9001",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

<h3 id="forking-start-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|body|body|[StartForkingRequest](#schemastartforkingrequest)|true|Fork media request|
|» rx|body|string|false|The network target, <udp:ip_address:port>, where the call's incoming RTP media packets should be forwarded.|
|» stream_type|body|string|false|Optionally specify a media type to stream. If `decrypted` selected, Telnyx will decrypt incoming SIP media before forking to the target. `rx` and `tx` are required fields if `decrypted` selected.|
|» tx|body|string|false|The network target, <udp:ip_address:port>, where the call's outgoing RTP media packets should be forwarded.|
|» client_state|body|string|false|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|» command_id|body|string|false|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» stream_type|decrypted|

```json
{
  "data": {
    "result": "ok"
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10004",
      "title": "Missing required parameter",
      "detail": "The 'to' parameter is required and cannot be blank.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/to"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "Unexpected error",
      "detail": "An unexpected error occured."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Gather

<a id="opIdGatherCall"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/gather \
  -X POST \

  -d '{
    "minimum_digits": 1,
    "maximum_digits": 10,
    "timeout_millis": 60000,
    "inter_digit_timeout_millis": 10000,
    "initial_timeout_millis": 10000,
    "terminating_digit": "#",
    "valid_digits": "123",
    "gather_id": "my_gather_id",
    "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
    "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/gather`

Gather DTMF signals to build interactive menus.

You can pass a list of valid digits. The `Answer` command must be issued before the `gather` command.

**Expected Webhooks:**

- `call.dtmf.received` (you may receive many of these webhooks)
- `call.gather.ended`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "minimum_digits": 1,
  "maximum_digits": 10,
  "timeout_millis": 60000,
  "inter_digit_timeout_millis": 10000,
  "initial_timeout_millis": 10000,
  "terminating_digit": "#",
  "valid_digits": "123",
  "gather_id": "my_gather_id",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

<h3 id="gather-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|body|body|[GatherRequest](#schemagatherrequest)|true|Gather|
|» minimum_digits|body|integer(int32)|false|The minimum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a minimum value of 1.|
|» maximum_digits|body|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a maximum value of 128.|
|» timeout_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of milliseconds to wait to complete the request.|
|» inter_digit_timeout_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of milliseconds to wait for input between digits.|
|» initial_timeout_millis|body|integer(int32)|false|The number of milliseconds to wait for the first DTMF.|
|» terminating_digit|body|string|false|The digit used to terminate input if fewer than `maximum_digits` digits have been gathered. Set to an empty string to disable the terminating digit entirely, so that a digit such as `#` can be collected as input per `valid_digits`.|
|» valid_digits|body|string|false|A list of all digits accepted as valid.|
|» gather_id|body|string|false|An id that will be sent back in the corresponding `call.gather.ended` webhook. Will be randomly generated if not specified.|
|» client_state|body|string|false|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|» command_id|body|string|false|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "data": {
    "result": "ok"
  }
}
```

## Gather using AI

<a id="opIdcallGatherUsingAI"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/calls/string/actions/gather_using_ai \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "parameters": {
      "properties": {
        "age": {
          "description": "The age of the customer.",
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "location": {
          "description": "The location of the customer.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "age",
        "location"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "voice": "Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af",
    "greeting": "Hello, can you tell me your age and where you live?",
    "send_partial_results": true,
    "send_message_history_updates": true,
    "message_history": [
      {
        "content": "Hello, what'\''s your name?",
        "role": "assistant"
      },
      {
        "content": "Hello, I'\''m John.",
        "role": "user"
      }
    ],
    "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
    "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
    "user_response_timeout_ms": 5000
  }'
```

`POST /calls/{call_control_id}/actions/gather_using_ai`

Gather parameters defined in the request payload using a voice assistant.

 You can pass parameters described as a JSON Schema object and the voice assistant will attempt to gather these informations. 

**Expected Webhooks:**

- [`call.conversation.created`](/api-reference/callbacks/call-conversation-created) includes `conversation_id` during startup
- `call.ai_gather.ended`
- `call.conversation.ended`
- `call.ai_gather.partial_results` (if `send_partial_results` is set to `true`)
- `call.ai_gather.message_history_updated` (if `send_message_history_updates` is set to `true`)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "parameters": {
    "properties": {
      "age": {
        "description": "The age of the customer.",
        "type": "integer"
      },
      "location": {
        "description": "The location of the customer.",
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": [
      "age",
      "location"
    ],
    "type": "object"
  },
  "voice": "Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af",
  "greeting": "Hello, can you tell me your age and where you live?",
  "send_partial_results": true,
  "send_message_history_updates": true,
  "message_history": [
    {
      "content": "Hello, what's your name?",
      "role": "assistant"
    },
    {
      "content": "Hello, I'm John.",
      "role": "user"
    }
  ],
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
  "user_response_timeout_ms": 5000
}
```
