## Submit a DIR's references

<a id="opIdsubmitDirReferences"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011/references \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "business_references": [
      {
        "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
        "job_title": "VP of Operations",
        "organization": "Acme Logistics",
        "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
        "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
        "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
        "timezone": "America/New_York"
      },
      {
        "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
        "job_title": "VP of Operations",
        "organization": "Acme Logistics",
        "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
        "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
        "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
        "timezone": "America/New_York"
      }
    ],
    "financial_reference": {
      "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
      "job_title": "VP of Operations",
      "organization": "Acme Logistics",
      "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
      "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
      "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /dir/{dir_id}/references`

Submit the two business references and one financial reference for a DIR.

References (two business references and one financial reference) are needed only if the documents uploaded with the DIR don't already prove the business is legitimate and financially stable. Any one of these is enough proof: audited or certified financial statements (uploaded as `other`, with a description), a commercial credit report (uploaded as `business_credit_report`), or references. Telnyx reviewers decide during vetting whether your documents are enough.

References can't be changed while the DIR is `verified`. Update the DIR first, which returns it to draft.

The request body carries exactly two business references plus one financial reference. The first submission stores them and returns `201`. Resubmitting returns `200`: identical values are simply confirmed and nothing is written, while changed values replace those references.

A replaced reference's pending verification call is cancelled and its dial-in code stops working, and the replacement contact is emailed fresh scheduling details. References whose details did not change keep their existing call, code, and the notice already sent to them.

The response always echoes the stored references in the same shape as the GET.

Who qualifies: the two business references confirm the company's reputation and operations. Each should be a senior contact at an organization the business works with, such as a vendor, partner, or client: a C-suite executive (CEO, CFO, CTO, COO), an owner or founder as reflected in the company's corporate records, or a senior manager, director, or executive. The financial reference confirms the company pays its bills and should be a licensed certified public accountant (CPA) the company uses, a contact at a bank or financial institution that has a relationship with the company, or a reasonable alternative banking or financial reference.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "business_references": [
    {
      "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
      "job_title": "VP of Operations",
      "organization": "Acme Logistics",
      "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
      "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
      "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    },
    {
      "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
      "job_title": "VP of Operations",
      "organization": "Acme Logistics",
      "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
      "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
      "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    }
  ],
  "financial_reference": {
    "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
    "job_title": "VP of Operations",
    "organization": "Acme Logistics",
    "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
    "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
    "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
    "timezone": "America/New_York"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-dirs-references-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|
|body|body|[ReferenceSubmissionRequest](#schemareferencesubmissionrequest)|true|none|
|» business_references|body|[[ReferenceInput](#schemareferenceinput)]|true|Exactly two business references. Array order determines each one's slot: the first entry becomes slot 1 and the second becomes slot 2. Those slots are what you pass when updating a single reference later. Each should be a senior contact who can speak to your company's reputation and operations: a C-suite executive (CEO, CFO, CTO, COO), an owner or founder as reflected in your corporate records, or a senior manager, director, or executive at an organization you work with, such as a vendor, partner, or client.|
|» financial_reference|body|object|true|One financial reference who can confirm the company pays its bills: a licensed certified public accountant (CPA) the company uses, a contact at a bank or financial institution that has a relationship with the company, or a reasonable alternative banking or financial reference.|
|» » full_name|body|string|true|Full name of the reference contact.|
|» » job_title|body|string \| null|false|Job title of the reference contact.|
|» » organization|body|string \| null|false|Organization the reference contact belongs to.|
|» » relationship_to_registrant|body|string \| null|false|How the reference contact is related to the registering business.|
|» » phone_e164|body|string|true|Reference phone number in E.164 format, e.g. +14155550123.|
|» » email|body|string(email)|true|Reference contact email address. Required: the reference is emailed scheduling and dial-in notices.|
|» » timezone|body|string|true|IANA timezone id for the reference (e.g. America/New_York). Required: calls are only placed within the reference's local 8am-9pm window.|

> Example responses

```json
    {

      "organization": "Acme Logistics",
      "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
      "phone_e164": "+14155550123",

    }
  ]
}
```

## Update a DIR reference

<a id="opIdupdateDirReference"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011/references/business/1 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
    "job_title": "VP of Operations",
    "organization": "Acme Logistics",
    "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
    "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
    "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
    "timezone": "America/New_York"
  }'
```

`PATCH /dir/{dir_id}/references/{ref_type}/{slot}`

Partially update one reference, addressed by the DIR id plus the reference's type (business or financial) and slot.

Cosmetic fields (full name, job title, organization, relationship, email) are always editable. The phone number and timezone may only be changed while a scheduled call has not yet been dialed; if a call is in progress or all attempts are complete, those fields are locked. Changing the timezone reschedules any pending call into the new local calling window.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
  "job_title": "VP of Operations",
  "organization": "Acme Logistics",
  "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
  "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
  "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
  "timezone": "America/New_York"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-dir-reference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|
|ref_type|path|string|true|Reference type to address.|
|slot|path|integer|true|Reference slot, counting from 1. Business references are slots 1 and 2, matching the order they were sent in the `business_references` array; the financial reference is slot 1. Every reference returned by the submit and list endpoints carries its own `ref_type` and `slot`, so you do not need to derive them.|
|body|body|[ReferenceUpdateRequest](#schemareferenceupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» full_name|body|string|false|The full name of the person we should contact as your reference.|
|» job_title|body|string \| null|false|The reference contact's job title, for example CFO or Owner.|
|» organization|body|string \| null|false|The name of the organization the reference contact works for.|
|» relationship_to_registrant|body|string \| null|false|How the reference contact is related to the registering business.|
|» phone_e164|body|string|false|The reference's phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550123. We call this number during their local business hours.|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|The reference's email address. We email them scheduling and dial-in instructions before we call, so use an address they check.|
|» timezone|body|string|false|The reference's IANA time zone, for example America/New_York. We only call during their local 8am to 9pm hours, which is why we need it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ref_type|business|
|ref_type|financial|

> 200 Response

```json
  "data": {
    "record_type": "dir_reference",
    "ref_type": "business",
    "slot": 1,
    "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
    "job_title": "VP of Operations",
    "organization": "Acme Logistics",
    "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
    "phone_e164": "+14155550123",

  }
}
```

<a id="opIdListMigrationSourceCoverage"></a>

## List call events

<a id="opIdListCallEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/call_events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /call_events`

Filters call events by given filter parameters. Events are ordered by `occurred_at`. If filter for `leg_id` or `application_session_id` is not present, it only filters events from the last 24 hours.

**Note**: Only one `filter[occurred_at]` can be passed.


<h3 id="list-call-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|object|false|Consolidated filter parameter (deepObject style). Originally: filter[application_name][contains], filter[outbound.outbound_voice_profile_id], filter[leg_id], filter[application_session_id], filter[connection_id], filter[product], filter[failed], filter[from], filter[to], filter[name], filter[type], filter[occurred_at][eq/gt/gte/lt/lte], filter[status]|
|page|query|object|false|Consolidated page parameter (deepObject style). Originally: page[after], page[before], page[limit], page[size], page[number]|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "record_type": "call_event",
      "call_leg_id": "308fe500-5213-11e9-ace7-02420a0f0668",
      "call_session_id": "308fec30-5213-11e9-9d3f-02420a0f0668",
      "event_timestamp": "2019-03-29T11:10:19.127783Z",
      "name": "call.hangup",
      "type": "webhook",
      "metadata": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total_pages": 3,
    "total_results": 55,
    "page_number": 2,
    "page_size": 25
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10004",
      "title": "Missing required parameter",
      "detail": "The 'to' parameter is required and cannot be blank.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/to"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "Unexpected error",
      "detail": "An unexpected error occured."
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-call-events-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response with a list of call events.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity. The request was well-formed but could not be processed due to semantic errors. This includes validation errors, invalid parameter values, call state errors, conference errors, queue errors, recording/transcription errors, and business logic violations.|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|[call-control_Errors](#schemacall-control_errors)|

<h3 id="list-call-events-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[CallEvent](#schemacallevent)]|false|none|none|
|meta|[PaginationMeta](#schemapaginationmeta)|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="telnyx-api-decision-models">Decision Models</h1>

Beta API for evaluating shared context with typed questions and structured answers using Flash or Pro.

## Evaluate decision models (TypeSafe-compatible)

<a id="opIdcreate_typesafe_systemone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/typesafe/v1/systemone \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "telnyx/decision-flash",
    "state": "Our production calls are failing. Every customer is affected.",
    "questions": {
      "team": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "Choose the team that should handle this incident.",
        "criteria": {
          "billing": "Payments and refunds",
          "technical_support": "Service faults and technical problems",
          "sales": "New purchases"
        }
      },
      "production_incident": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the message describe an active production incident?"
      },
      "urgency": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "Rate operational urgency.",
        "criteria": [
          "Low",
          "Normal",
          "High",
          "Critical"
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /ai/typesafe/v1/systemone`

**Beta API.** Choose telnyx/decision-flash for the lowest cost and latency, or telnyx/decision-pro for decisions that require long context, including inputs beyond Jev’s 32k per-decision limit. Omitted model defaults to telnyx/decision-flash.

Evaluate shared context using named choice, noul (yes/no), and score questions. Returns TypeSafe System One-compatible answer shapes, the selected public model alias, and token usage. See the [decision model guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/decision-models) for examples and compatibility limits.

The supported request subset requires instructions for every question, string descriptions for criteria (or null for choice descriptions), 1–64 questions, and 2–64 options for choice and score questions. The model field accepts only telnyx/decision-flash or telnyx/decision-pro. Unsupported model values and unknown fields are rejected. The endpoint is synchronous and does not stream.

Use the TypeSafe Python SDK with base_url set to https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/typesafe and a Telnyx API key. The SDK appends /v1/systemone; explicitly set model to a supported Telnyx alias because its own default model is not supported. Compatibility covers this operation and the documented request subset; it does not include TypeSafe model listing. Scores describe relative preference, not calibrated correctness.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "telnyx/decision-flash",
  "state": "Our production calls are failing. Every customer is affected.",
  "questions": {
    "team": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Choose the team that should handle this incident.",
      "criteria": {
        "billing": "Payments and refunds",
        "technical_support": "Service faults and technical problems",
        "sales": "New purchases"
      }
    },
    "production_incident": {
      "type": "noul",
      "instructions": "Does the message describe an active production incident?"
    },
    "urgency": {
      "type": "score",
      "instructions": "Rate operational urgency.",
      "criteria": [
        "Low",
        "Normal",
        "High",
        "Critical"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="evaluate-decision-models-typesafe-compatible-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DecisionModelRequest](#schemadecisionmodelrequest)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|false|Public model alias. telnyx/decision-flash offers the lowest cost and latency; telnyx/decision-pro supports decisions that require long context, including inputs beyond Jev’s 32k per-decision limit. Applies to every question in the request. Other values are rejected.|
|» state|body|[DecisionModelContent](#schemadecisionmodelcontent)|true|Shared context evaluated by every question.|
|» questions|body|object|true|Between 1 and 64 named questions. Each key identifies the corresponding answer.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[DecisionModelQuestion](#schemadecisionmodelquestion)|false|A choice, yes/no, or ordered-score question.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» model|telnyx/decision-flash|
|» model|telnyx/decision-pro|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "model": "telnyx/decision-flash",
  "answers": {
    "team": {
      "type": "choice",
      "choice": "technical_support",
      "probabilities": {
        "billing": 0.0024719786572585446,
        "technical_support": 0.9972674768333701,
        "sales": 0.00026054450937119613
      },
      "confidence": 0.9820522416354122
    },
    "production_incident": {
      "type": "noul",
      "noul": 0.9991959141264766
    },
    "urgency": {
```

<h1 id="telnyx-api-dedicated-ips">Dedicated IPs</h1>

Purchase and manage dedicated sending IP addresses for your Telnyx email traffic.

## List dedicated IPs

<a id="opIdlistDedicatedIps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/dedicated_ips \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email/dedicated_ips`

List the dedicated sending IPs owned by the account, newest first. Narrow the list with `filter[status]`, `filter[pool_id]`, and `filter[region]`; supplied filters combine, so an IP must match every one. An empty value, or a nested or array value such as `filter[status][]=active`, applies no filter, and other `filter[...]` keys are ignored. A value that no IP can match (an unknown status, a `pool_id` that is not a UUID, or a value containing a NUL byte) returns an empty list, not an error.

<h3 id="list-dedicated-ips-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[status]|query|string|false|Return only IPs in this lifecycle status (exact match). Any other value returns an empty list. An empty value applies no filter.|
|filter[pool_id]|query|string(uuid)|false|Return only IPs in this pool (exact match on `pool_id`). A value that is not a UUID returns an empty list. An empty value applies no filter.|
|filter[region]|query|string|false|Return only IPs in this region (exact, case-sensitive match on `region`). An empty value applies no filter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[status]|provisioning|
|filter[status]|warming_up|
|filter[status]|active|
|filter[status]|suspended|
|filter[status]|released|

## Purchase a dedicated IP

<a id="opIdcreateDedicatedIp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/dedicated_ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9326' \
  -d '{
    "region": "ewr-nj1",
    "ip_version": "ipv4"
  }'
```

`POST /email/dedicated_ips`

Purchase a dedicated sending IP. Requires a verified, enterprise, or legacy account, and an `Idempotency-Key` header: a request without the header returns `400` (code `10015`) and allocates nothing. Telnyx allocates the next available IP from stock. The optional `region` and `ip_version` fields each restrict which stock IP is allocated; they never change the allocated IP's metadata. An omitted field applies no restriction for that field, and omitting the body applies neither restriction. An unsupported selector value returns `422`; a supported value that matches no available IP returns `429` and records the request on the waitlist. Billing: $14/month/IP, charged as a monthly recurring charge (MRC) from purchase. The IP is returned in `provisioning` status with a Telnyx-managed PTR hostname and carries no mail until you call `start_warmup` and add it to a pool that routes mail.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "region": "ewr-nj1",
  "ip_version": "ipv4"
}
```

<h3 id="purchase-a-dedicated-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|true|Required. Opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same purchase. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each purchase and reuse it only when retrying that purchase with the same request. A missing header, or an invalid one —including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—returns 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[DedicatedIpCreateRequest](#schemadedicatedipcreaterequest)|false|none|
|» region|body|string|false|Allocate an IP in this region. Supported value: `ewr-nj1`. Any other value, including an empty string or `null`, returns `422`.|
|» ip_version|body|string|false|Allocate an IP of this address family. Supported value: `ipv4`. Any other value, including `ipv6` or `null`, returns `422`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» region|ewr-nj1|
|» ip_version|ipv4|

## Release a dedicated IP

<a id="opIddeleteDedicatedIp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/dedicated_ips/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "No longer needed"
  }'
```

`DELETE /email/dedicated_ips/{id}`

Release the dedicated IP to Telnyx. The IP stops carrying mail immediately, leaves its pool, and moves to `released`. Telnyx sets `quarantine_until` to 30 days after release. Release requests that the MRC stop asynchronously. Check `billing`: `stopping` means the stop is pending, `stopped` means it completed, and `stop_failed` means the charge remains. If the charge was never created or its creation has not completed, `billing` keeps showing the creation status (`not_started`, `pending`, `in_progress`, or `failed`). Any status except `released` can be released. Releasing the last IP in a pool requires `force=true` and `drain=true`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "No longer needed"
}
```

<h3 id="release-a-dedicated-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The dedicated IP identifier (UUID).|
|force|query|boolean|false|Set together with `drain=true` to release the last IP in a pool. Either flag alone has no effect. Also accepted in the JSON body.|
|drain|query|boolean|false|Set together with `force=true` to release the last IP in a pool. Acknowledges that mail routed to the emptied pool is held until the pool has a sendable IP again. Also accepted in the JSON body.|
|reason|query|string|false|Free-text reason recorded with the release. Also accepted in the JSON body.|
|body|body|[DedicatedIpDeleteRequest](#schemadedicatedipdeleterequest)|false|none|
|» force|body|boolean|false|Set together with `drain: true` to release the last IP in a pool. Either flag alone has no effect.|
|» drain|body|boolean|false|Set together with `force: true` to release the last IP in a pool. Acknowledges that mail routed to the emptied pool is held until the pool has a sendable IP again.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Free-text reason recorded with the release.|

## Update a dedicated IP

<a id="opIdupdateDedicatedIp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/dedicated_ips/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "pool_id": "9b1c4d70-abcd-4e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b",
    "weight": 100
  }'
```

`PATCH /email/dedicated_ips/{id}`

Move the IP to another pool, or pause/resume its warm-up ramp. One change applies per request. `pool_id` takes precedence over warm-up changes. Otherwise, use `warmup_paused` or `warmup.paused`; a Boolean `warmup_paused` takes precedence. Moving the last IP out of a pool requires `force: true` and `drain: true`. The PTR hostname is managed by Telnyx: a request that includes `ptr_hostname` returns `422` unless `pool_id` or a warm-up field is present, in which case `ptr_hostname` is ignored.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pool_id": "9b1c4d70-abcd-4e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b",
  "weight": 100
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-dedicated-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The dedicated IP identifier (UUID).|
|body|body|[DedicatedIpUpdateRequest](#schemadedicatedipupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» pool_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Move the IP to this pool, replacing its current membership. Use the IP's current pool to change only its weight. To take an IP out of a pool, use `DELETE /email/ip_pools/{id}/ips/{ip_id}`.|
|» weight|body|integer|false|Routing weight in the target pool. Used only with `pool_id`.|
|» force|body|boolean|false|Set together with `drain: true` to move the last IP out of its current pool. Used only with `pool_id`.|
|» drain|body|boolean|false|Set together with `force: true` to move the last IP out of its current pool. Acknowledges that mail routed to the emptied pool is held. Used only with `pool_id`.|
|» warmup_paused|body|boolean|false|Pause (`true`) or resume (`false`) the warm-up ramp; equivalent to the `pause_warmup` and `resume_warmup` actions. A Boolean value takes precedence over `warmup.paused`. When a pause field is present and `pool_id` is absent, supplying neither pause field as a Boolean invokes resume.|
|» warmup|body|object|false|Alias for `warmup_paused`.|
|» » paused|body|boolean|false|Pause (`true`) or resume (`false`) the warm-up ramp. Used only when `warmup_paused` is not a Boolean.|

## Manually complete warmup

<a id="opIdcompleteDedicatedIpWarmup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/dedicated_ips/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/actions/complete_warmup \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /email/dedicated_ips/{id}/actions/complete_warmup`

Manually complete the warm-up ramp (`warming_up` to `active`), bypassing the schedule. Use only for an IP already warmed elsewhere. Completion sets `warmup.progress` to `100`, clears `warmup.daily_cap`, and applies the ramp-complete allowance to the current UTC day: `warmup.today.cap` becomes `100000000`, `warmup.today.granted` keeps the sends already released today, and `warmup.today.remaining` becomes `cap` minus `granted`. Once completion applies this allowance, an exhausted stage allowance does not block the next eligible first-attempt send. The response reports these values. On an `active` IP, `warmup.progress` and `warmup.daily_cap` are informational: they can keep earlier values after a suspension is lifted and do not limit sending.

<h3 id="manually-complete-warmup-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The dedicated IP identifier (UUID).|

|422|Unprocessable Entity|The IP is `warming_up`, `active`, or `released`.|[ErrorEnvelope](#schemaerrorenvelope)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

`GET /detail_records`

Search for any detail record across the Telnyx Platform

<h3 id="search-detail-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|object|false|Filter records on a given record attribute and value. <br/>Example: filter[status]=delivered. <br/>Required: filter[record_type] must be specified. <br/>The valid filter fields depend on the record_type: filtering by a field that does not exist for the selected record_type is rejected with a 400 error. Call-control and sip-trunking records use started_at, finished_at and answered_at (they have no created_at); messaging records use created_at. To list the fields available for a record_type, use the /v2/detail_records/options endpoint.|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Specifies the sort order for results. <br/>Example: sort=-created_at <br/>The valid sort fields depend on the record_type: sort by a field that does not exist for the selected record_type is rejected with a 400 error. Call-control and sip-trunking records use started_at, finished_at and answered_at (they have no created_at); messaging records use created_at. To list the fields available for a record_type, use the /v2/detail_records/options endpoint.|
|page|query|object|false|Consolidated page parameter (deepObject style). Originally: page[number], page[size]|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-display-identity-records">Display Identity Records</h1>

A Display Identity Record (DIR) is the verified calling identity (display name, logo, call reasons) shown to recipients on outbound calls.

## List all DIRs across your enterprises

<a id="opIdlistAllDirs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /dir`

Returns every DIR (Display Identity Record) you own, across all of your enterprises, as a single list. Pagination is JSON:API style (`page[number]`, `page[size]`, max 250). Supports `filter[]` query params: `filter[enterprise_id]`, `filter[status]`, `filter[display_name][contains]`, `filter[call_reason][contains]`, plus the renewal-window filters `filter[expiring_at][gte]` / `filter[expiring_at][lte]`. Sortable by `created_at`, `updated_at`, `display_name`, `status` (prefix `-` for descending; default `-created_at`).

<h3 id="list-all-dirs-across-your-enterprises-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Out-of-range values return an empty page with correct meta.|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Items per page. Maximum 250; values above are clamped to 250.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort field. Allowed values: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `display_name`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending. Default `-created_at`.|
|filter[expiring_at][gte]|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only DIRs whose `expiring_at` is at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Pairs with the `[lte]` variant to build renewal-window dashboards.|
|filter[expiring_at][lte]|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only DIRs whose `expiring_at` is at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp.|
|filter[enterprise_id]|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter by enterprise ID.|
|filter[status]|query|[DirStatus](#schemadirstatus)|false|Filter by DIR status.|
|filter[display_name][contains]|query|string|false|Case-insensitive partial match on display name.|
|filter[call_reason][contains]|query|string|false|Case-insensitive partial match on call reason.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created_at|
|sort|-created_at|
|sort|updated_at|
|sort|-updated_at|
|sort|display_name|
|sort|-display_name|
|sort|status|
|sort|-status|
|filter[status]|draft|
|filter[status]|submitted|
|filter[status]|in_review|
|filter[status]|verified|
|filter[status]|rejected|
|filter[status]|unsuccessful|
|filter[status]|suspended|
|filter[status]|expired|
|filter[status]|infringement_claimed|
|filter[status]|permanently_rejected|
|filter[status]|delete_requested|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
```

## Request deletion of a DIR

<a id="opIddeleteDirSimple"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /dir/{dir_id}`

Request deletion of a DIR. This does not remove the DIR on this call: it records the request, moves the DIR to `delete_requested`, and Telnyx completes the removal (de-registration and cleanup) shortly after. A verified DIR keeps serving its branded identity, and keeps billing, until the removal is executed. Failure modes: `400` if a child phone number is still attached or the DIR is `in_review` (wait for the review to finish), `409` if the DIR has an unresolved infringement claim, `404` if the DIR is not yours.

<h3 id="request-deletion-of-a-dir-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|

```json
}
```

## Update a DIR

<a id="opIdupdateDirSimple"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "display_name": "Acme Plumbing & Wellness",
    "call_reasons": [
      "Appointment reminders",
      "Billing inquiries",
      "Lab results"
    ],
    "logo_url": "https://acmeplumbing.example.com/logo-v2-256.bmp"
  }'
```

`PATCH /dir/{dir_id}`

Edit a DIR. DIRs in `draft`, `rejected`, `unsuccessful`, or `suspended` can be edited freely: PATCH is a pure edit, `status` is never changed, and you re-vet by calling `POST /v2/dir/{dir_id}/submit` explicitly. A `verified` DIR can also be edited in place: a PATCH that changes any value returns the DIR to `draft`; the currently approved identity keeps displaying, and the edited content goes live only after you re-submit and the DIR is approved again. A PATCH that changes nothing (an empty body or values identical to the current ones) leaves the DIR `verified`, so idempotent retries are safe. Changing only `bpo_authorizations` or `webhook_url` is the exception: the DIR stays `verified`. Each BPO authorization is reviewed on its own instead. DIRs in any other status (`submitted`, `in_review`, `expired`, `infringement_claimed`, `permanently_rejected`) cannot be edited.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "display_name": "Acme Plumbing & Wellness",
  "call_reasons": [
    "Appointment reminders",
    "Billing inquiries",
    "Lab results"
  ],
  "logo_url": "https://acmeplumbing.example.com/logo-v2-256.bmp"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-dir-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|
|body|body|[DirUpdateRequest](#schemadirupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» display_name|body|string|false|Name shown to call recipients. 1–35 characters, no emoji, not whitespace-only.|
|» reselling|body|boolean|false|Set to true if your organization places calls on behalf of other enterprises (BPO/reseller). Updating this triggers re-vetting on next submit.|
|» authorizer_name|body|string|false|Name of the person at your enterprise authorizing this DIR. Must be a real individual.|
|» authorizer_email|body|string(email)|false|Contact email of the authorizer. Telnyx may send verification or infringement notices here.|
|» logo_url|body|string(uri)|false|Publicly accessible HTTPS URL (max 128 chars) to a 256x256 BMP logo (max 1 MB).|
|» call_reasons|body|[string]|false|1–10 reasons your business calls customers. Validate phrasing against `POST /call_reasons/validate`.|
|» certify_brand_is_accurate|body|boolean|false|Certification that the DIR information is accurate. Must be `true` for the DIR to be submitted for vetting.|
|» certify_no_shaft_content|body|boolean|false|Certification that this DIR is not used for SHAFT content (Sex, Hate, Alcohol, Firearms, Tobacco) where prohibited. Must be `true` for the DIR to be submitted for vetting.|
|» certify_ip_ownership|body|boolean|false|Certification of ownership of any logos/trademarks shown. Must be `true` for the DIR to be submitted for vetting.|
|» documents|body|[[Document](#schemadocument)]|false|Additional supporting documents to attach. Append-only: existing documents are never removed or replaced, and an empty or omitted list is a no-op. Each `document_id` may appear at most once on a DIR.|
|» webhook_url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|Optional `https://` URL that receives webhook notifications when this DIR's compliance review completes. Send `null` to clear. Changing only this field on a `verified` DIR does not re-vet it. Maximum 2048 characters.|
|» bpo_authorizations|body|[[BpoAuthorizationInput](#schemabpoauthorizationinput)]|false|Optional. Replace this DIR's authorized BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) accounts with these, each with its signed Letter of Authorization. The supplied list replaces the current one: a BPO left out has its authorization removed, and a new BPO (or a changed Letter of Authorization) is created `pending` admin review. Send an empty list to clear all authorizations; omit the field to leave them unchanged. Editing this list does not re-vet the DIR. Maximum 10.|

## List a DIR's authorized BPOs

<a id="opIdlistDirBpoAuthorizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011/bpo_authorizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /dir/{dir_id}/bpo_authorizations`

List the BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) accounts a Brand Owner has authorized on this DIR, together with the review state of each authorization.

Authorizations are supplied as the `bpo_authorizations` array when creating or updating a DIR, and each one is reviewed on its own. Only an `approved` authorization adds that BPO to this DIR's authorized callers in the branded calling registry; `pending` and `rejected` authorizations do not. Each entry includes the `loa_document_id` you submitted: because `bpo_authorizations` replaces the whole list on every DIR update, send each entry you want to keep back with its `loa_document_id` unchanged, and it keeps its review state. A rejected entry carries a `rejection_reason`. Returns an empty list when the DIR has authorized no BPOs.

<h3 id="list-a-dirs-authorized-bpos-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Out-of-range values return an empty page with correct meta.|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Items per page. Maximum 250; values above are clamped to 250.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "data": [
    {
      "record_type": "bpo_authorization",
      "bpo_enterprise_id": "4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6",
      "status": "pending",
      "loa_document_id": "2a7e8337-e803-4057-a4ae-26c40eb0bc6c",
      "rejection_reason": "Letter of Authorization is unsigned"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total_pages": 3,
    "total_results": 42,
    "page_number": 1,
    "page_size": 20
  }
}
```

```json
      },
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/body/legal_name"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Render the BPO Authorization LOA for a DIR

<a id="opIdrenderDirBpoLoa"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/bpo_loa \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bpo_enterprise_id": "4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6",
    "signature": {
      "image_base64": "string",
      "signer_name": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /dir/{dir_id}/bpo_loa`

The Letter of Authorization in which a Brand Owner authorizes an approved BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) to place branded calls that display this DIR on the owner's behalf. Both parties are read from the caller's account: the Brand Owner is the enterprise that owns the DIR, and the BPO is `bpo_enterprise_id`. No business identity is accepted in the body.

When `signature` is omitted the PDF is returned unsigned so the Brand Owner can sign it externally and the BPO can upload it via the Documents API. When `signature` is present the PDF embeds the supplied image, printed name, and signed-at date.

Returns `application/pdf`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bpo_enterprise_id": "4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6",
  "signature": {
    "image_base64": "string",
    "signer_name": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="render-the-bpo-authorization-loa-for-a-dir-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id.|
|body|body|[BpoAuthorizationLoaRenderRequest](#schemabpoauthorizationloarenderrequest)|true|none|
|» bpo_enterprise_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The approved BPO enterprise the Brand Owner is authorizing. Must be a BPO account on the caller's organization that has already been approved.|
|» signature|body|object|false|Optional. When provided the rendered PDF embeds the signature image, printed name, and signed-at date. When absent the PDF is returned unsigned so the Brand Owner can sign externally and the BPO can upload it via the Documents API.|
|» » image_base64|body|string|true|PNG image, base64-encoded.|
|» » signer_name|body|string \| null|false|Optional. When absent the rendered PDF falls back to the enterprise contact's legal name.|

```json
      },
      "source": {

      }
    }
```

## Render the Branded Calling LOA for a DIR

<a id="opIdrenderDirLoa"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/loa \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "phone_numbers": [
      "+13125550000"
    ],
    "agent": {
      "legal_name": "string",
      "dba": "string",
      "street_address": "string",
      "extended_address": "string",
      "city": "string",
      "administrative_area": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "country": "US",
      "contact_name": "string",
      "contact_title": "string",
      "contact_email": "user@example.com",
      "contact_phone": "+13125550000"
    },
    "signature": {
      "image_base64": "string",
      "signer_name": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /dir/{dir_id}/loa`

Generate a pre-filled Letter of Authorization (LOA) PDF for a DIR. Enterprise identity (legal name, DBA, address, contact, website, tax id) and the DIR display name are read server-side; the caller supplies the telephone numbers to authorize, an optional Authorized Agent block, and an optional drawn signature.

When `signature` is omitted the PDF is returned unsigned so the customer can sign it externally and upload it via the Documents API. When `signature` is present the PDF embeds the supplied image, printed name, and signed-at date.

Returns `application/pdf`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "phone_numbers": [
    "+13125550000"
  ],
  "agent": {
    "legal_name": "string",
    "dba": "string",
    "street_address": "string",
    "extended_address": "string",
    "city": "string",
    "administrative_area": "string",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "country": "US",
    "contact_name": "string",
    "contact_title": "string",
    "contact_email": "user@example.com",
    "contact_phone": "+13125550000"
  },
  "signature": {
    "image_base64": "string",
    "signer_name": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="render-the-branded-calling-loa-for-a-dir-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id.|
|body|body|[BrandLoaRenderRequest](#schemabrandloarenderrequest)|true|none|
|» phone_numbers|body|[string]|true|Telephone numbers to authorize on the DIR, in `+E164` format (`+` followed by 10-15 digits). Max 15 per request.|
|» agent|body|object|false|Optional. The third-party reseller / partner managing the enterprise's phone numbers on its behalf; omitted, the LOA marks the Authorized Agent block as N/A. A call center (BPO) adding numbers to a client's DIR puts its own details here. The letter is signed by the DIR enterprise's organization contact (the client, in the BPO case), not by the agent.|
|» » legal_name|body|string|true|The legal name of the third-party partner or reseller managing these numbers on your behalf.|
|» » dba|body|string \| null|false|The trade name (Doing Business As) the partner operates under, if different from its legal name. Leave blank if it does not apply.|
|» » street_address|body|string|true|The street address of the partner, including the building number and street name.|
|» » extended_address|body|string \| null|false|An optional second address line for the partner, such as a suite, unit, or floor. Leave blank if it does not apply.|
|» » city|body|string|true|The city of the partner's address.|
|» » administrative_area|body|string|true|The state or province of the partner's address, as its code, for example IL or ON.|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal or ZIP code of the partner's address.|
|» » country|body|string|true|The two-letter country code of the partner's address, for example US.|
|» » contact_name|body|string|true|The name of a contact person at the partner.|
|» » contact_title|body|string|true|The job title of the contact person at the partner.|
|» » contact_email|body|string(email)|true|The email address of the contact person at the partner.|
|» » contact_phone|body|string|true|The phone number of the contact person at the partner, in E.164 format, for example +13125550000.|
|» signature|body|object|false|Optional. When provided the rendered PDF embeds the signature image, printed name, and signed-at date. When absent the PDF is returned unsigned so the customer can sign externally and upload it via the Documents API.|
|» » image_base64|body|string|true|PNG image, base64-encoded.|
|» » signer_name|body|string \| null|false|Optional. When absent the rendered PDF falls back to the enterprise contact's legal name.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10005",
      "title": "Invalid parameters",
      "detail": "field required",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005"
      },

        "pointer": "/body/legal_name"
```

## Submit a DIR for vetting

<a id="opIdsubmitDirSimple"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011/submit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /dir/{dir_id}/submit`

Submit a DIR for vetting. Sends the DIR back through the vetting cycle from any non-terminal status. When re-submitting from `suspended` or `expired`, the DIR's previous Branded Calling registration is torn down transactionally and its phone numbers flip back to `submitted`. When re-submitting from `verified`, the existing registration stays live throughout the new vetting cycle.

Returns `400` from `submitted`/`in_review`/`permanently_rejected`. Returns `400` if the DIR has an unresolved infringement claim.

<h3 id="submit-a-dir-for-vetting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|

## List DIRs in an enterprise

<a id="opIdlistDirsForEnterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/enterprises/4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6/dir \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise_id}/dir`

Return the DIRs (Display Identity Records) belonging to a single enterprise. Pagination is JSON:API style (`page[number]`, `page[size]`, max 250). Supports `filter[]` query params: `filter[status]`, `filter[display_name][contains]`, `filter[call_reason][contains]`, plus the renewal-window filters `filter[expiring_at][gte]` / `filter[expiring_at][lte]` and the convenience `filter[expiring_within_days]` (mutually exclusive with the explicit gte/lte form). Sortable by `created_at`, `updated_at`, `display_name`, `status`, `submitted_at`, `verified_at`, `expiring_at` (prefix `-` for descending; default `-created_at`).

<h3 id="list-dirs-in-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The enterprise id. Lowercase UUID.|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Out-of-range values return an empty page with correct meta.|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Items per page. Maximum 250; values above are clamped to 250.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort field. Allowed: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `display_name`, `status`, `submitted_at`, `verified_at`, `expiring_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending. Default `-created_at`.|
|filter[expiring_at][gte]|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only DIRs whose `expiring_at` is at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp.|
|filter[expiring_at][lte]|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only DIRs whose `expiring_at` is at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp.|
|filter[expiring_within_days]|query|integer|false|Convenience: returns DIRs whose `expiring_at` falls within the next N days (1–365). Equivalent to setting `filter[expiring_at][gte]=<now>` + `filter[expiring_at][lte]=<now+N>`. Mutually exclusive with the explicit `[gte]`/`[lte]` filters - combining returns 400.|
|filter[status]|query|[DirStatus](#schemadirstatus)|false|Filter by DIR status.|
|filter[display_name][contains]|query|string|false|Case-insensitive partial match on display name.|
|filter[call_reason][contains]|query|string|false|Case-insensitive partial match on call reason.|

## Create a Display Identity Record (DIR)

<a id="opIdcreateDir"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/enterprises/4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6/dir \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "display_name": "Acme Plumbing",
    "reselling": false,
    "certify_brand_is_accurate": true,
    "certify_no_shaft_content": true,
    "certify_ip_ownership": true,
    "authorizer_name": "Sam Owner",
    "authorizer_email": "sam@acmeplumbing.example.com",
    "call_reasons": [
      "Appointment reminders",
      "Billing inquiries"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /enterprises/{enterprise_id}/dir`

Create a new DIR under the given enterprise. The DIR starts in `draft` status; it must be submitted (`POST .../submit`) and approved by Telnyx before any phone number can be attached.

**Field rules**
- `display_name`: 1–35 characters, no emoji or whitespace-only strings; this is the name shown to recipients.
- `call_reasons`: 1–10 strings, each ≤64 characters; describe why your business calls customers (e.g. 'Appointment reminders', 'Billing inquiries'). Validate the wording against `POST /call_reasons/validate`.
- `logo_url`: HTTPS URL (max 128 chars) to a 256×256 BMP (max 1 MB). The image is downloaded and hashed at submission time.
- `documents`: up to 20 entries; each `document_id` must be obtained by uploading the file via the Telnyx Documents API first. Within one DIR a `document_id` may only appear once.
- `certify_brand_is_accurate`, `certify_no_shaft_content`, `certify_ip_ownership` MUST all be `true`.

**Failure modes**
- `400` - validation error; `errors[].source.pointer` names the offending field.
- `400` - a certification field is not `true`.
- `400` - Branded Calling not activated on this enterprise (see `POST /enterprises/{id}/branded_calling`).
- `400` - the enterprise is a BPO enterprise (`role_type` `bpo`), which cannot own a DIR.
- `400` - a `bpo_authorizations` entry is not an approved BPO enterprise in your account, or its `loa_document_id` could not be validated.
- `404` - enterprise does not exist or does not belong to your account.
- `503` - the document check is temporarily unavailable; retry.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "display_name": "Acme Plumbing",
  "reselling": false,
  "certify_brand_is_accurate": true,
  "certify_no_shaft_content": true,
  "certify_ip_ownership": true,
  "authorizer_name": "Sam Owner",
  "authorizer_email": "sam@acmeplumbing.example.com",
  "call_reasons": [
    "Appointment reminders",
    "Billing inquiries"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-display-identity-record-dir-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The enterprise id. Lowercase UUID.|
|body|body|[DirCreateRequest](#schemadircreaterequest)|true|none|
|» display_name|body|string|true|Name shown to call recipients. No emoji; not whitespace-only.|
|» reselling|body|boolean|false|Set to true if your organization places calls on behalf of other enterprises (BPO/reseller).|
|» certify_brand_is_accurate|body|boolean|true|Certification that the DIR information is accurate. Must be `true` for the DIR to be submitted for vetting.|
|» certify_no_shaft_content|body|boolean|true|Must be `true`. Confirms this DIR is not used for SHAFT content (Sex, Hate, Alcohol, Firearms, Tobacco) where prohibited.|
|» certify_ip_ownership|body|boolean|true|Must be `true`. Confirms ownership of any logos/trademarks shown.|
|» authorizer_name|body|string|true|Name of the person at your enterprise who is authorizing this DIR registration. Must be a real individual (used for audit and trademark-claim contests).|
|» authorizer_email|body|string(email)|true|Contact email of the authorizer. Telnyx may send verification or infringement-notice email here; use a monitored mailbox.|
|» logo_url|body|string(uri)|false|Publicly accessible HTTPS URL (max 128 chars) to a 256x256 BMP logo (max 1 MB).|
|» call_reasons|body|[string]|true|1–10 reasons your business calls customers. Validate phrasing against `POST /call_reasons/validate`.|
|» documents|body|[[Document](#schemadocument)]|false|Supporting documents. Each `document_id` may appear at most once on a DIR.|
|» webhook_url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|Optional `https://` URL that receives webhook notifications when this DIR's compliance review completes (rejection outcomes include structured rejection reasons). Maximum 2048 characters.|
|» bpo_authorizations|body|[[BpoAuthorizationInput](#schemabpoauthorizationinput)]|false|Optional. Approved BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) accounts on your organization authorized to place branded calls for this DIR, each with the signed Letter of Authorization the Brand Owner granted it. Each authorization starts `pending` and takes effect only after an admin reviews its Letter of Authorization. Omit or send an empty list to authorize no BPO on this DIR. Maximum 10.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» certify_brand_is_accurate|true|
|» certify_no_shaft_content|true|
|» certify_ip_ownership|true|

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_domains/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/dns_records \
```

`GET /email_domains/{domain_id}/dns_records`

Returns the DNS records Telnyx generated for domain ownership and DKIM verification, plus MX records when inbound delivery is enabled.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Rotate the DKIM key for an email domain

<a id="opIdrotateEmailDomainDKIMKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_domains/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/rotate_dkim \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /email_domains/{domain_id}/rotate_dkim`

Generates a new DKIM key for the domain, activates it, and retires the previous key. The response includes the updated DKIM DNS records the customer must publish. Selectors are fixed, so rotation replaces the TXT value at the existing `<selector>._domainkey.<domain>` host rather than adding a second record — `old_selector_retained` is false and the new TXT value must be published promptly, since signing switches to the new key immediately and the old TXT value will no longer match. The previous key is retired to a `retiring` state (retained, not revoked) so it can be revoked after the DNS propagation grace period.


<h3 id="rotate-the-dkim-key-for-an-email-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email domain UUID|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "email_domain_dkim_rotation",
    "domain_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174002",
    "domain": "example.com",
    "dkim": {
      "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-42661417400a",
      "selector": "telnyx1",
      "algorithm": "rsa-sha256",
      "key_length": 2048,
      "version": 2,
      "status": "active",
      "activated_at": "2026-09-11T12:00:00Z"
    },
    "previous_dkim_key": {
      "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174009",
      "selector": "telnyx1",
      "version": 1,
      "status": "retiring"
    },
    "old_selector_retained": false,
    "dns_records": [
      {
        "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-42661417400b",
        "purpose": "dkim",
        "record_type": "TXT",
        "host": "telnyx1._domainkey.example.com",
        "value": "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkqh...",
        "actual_value": null,
        "priority": null,
        "required": true,
        "status": "pending"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10008",
      "title": "Forbidden",
      "detail": "Shared email domains are managed by Telnyx and cannot have their DKIM keys rotated by this account"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10001",
      "title": "Not Found",
      "detail": "The requested email domain was not found"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "40901",
      "title": "Conflict",
      "detail": "DKIM rotation conflicted with a concurrent operation on this domain. Safe to retry."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10015",
      "title": "Validation Failed",
      "detail": "domain is invalid",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/data/attributes/domain"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "500",
      "title": "Internal Server Error",
      "detail": "An unexpected error occurred"
    }
  ]
}
```

|201|Created|DKIM key rotated|[EmailDomainDKIMRotationResponse](#schemaemaildomaindkimrotationresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden — shared email domains are managed by Telnyx and cannot have their DKIM keys rotated by this account.<br>|[DomainsErrorResponse](#schemadomainserrorresponse)|

## Update an email domain

<a id="opIdupdateEmailDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_domains/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \

    "inbound_enabled": true,
    "tracking": {
      "open_tracking": false
    }
```

`PATCH /email_domains/{id}`

Updates mutable settings for an existing email domain, including inbound delivery and tracking configuration. Shared domains are read-only for non-owner accounts.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inbound_enabled": true,
  "tracking": {
    "open_tracking": false
  }
}
```

|» inbound_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable or disable inbound routing for this domain|
|» dmarc_policy|body|object \| null|false|Update the DMARC policy. The recommended _dmarc TXT record is rebuilt and its verification reset to pending.<br>|
|» » p|body|string|false|Policy applied to messages that fail alignment.|
|» » pct|body|integer|false|Percentage of messages the policy applies to. Omitted from the record when 100.|
|» » rua|body|string \| null|false|URI for aggregate reports. Defaults to the Telnyx address when absent; null omits it.|
|» » sp|body|string \| null|false|Policy for subdomains. Omitted from the record when null.|
|» tracking|body|[DomainsTrackingSettings](#schemadomainstrackingsettings)|false|none|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-drafts">Email Drafts</h1>

## Create a draft

<a id="opIdCreateEmailDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/drafts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "to": [
      {
        "email": "recipient@example.com",
        "name": "Recipient"
      }
    ],
    "subject": "Quarterly update",
    "text_body": "Here is the update.",
    "labels": [
      "important"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/drafts`

Creates an unsent draft in the inbox. Every field is optional — a draft is a
work-in-progress and may be saved incomplete. Send-time requirements (sender,
subject, at least one recipient) are enforced when the draft is sent, not when
it is created.

Drafts are unbillable and emit no Email Detail Records until they are sent.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "to": [
    {
      "email": "recipient@example.com",
      "name": "Recipient"
    }
  ],
  "subject": "Quarterly update",
  "text_body": "Here is the update.",
  "labels": [
    "important"
  ]
}
```

|» from_email|body|string|false|none|
|» from_name|body|string|false|none|
|» to|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|
|» cc|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|
|» bcc|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|

## Update a draft

<a id="opIdUpdateEmailDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/drafts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "subject": "Quarterly update (revised)",
    "text_body": "Updated body."
  }'
```

`PUT /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/drafts/{draft_id}`

Updates the supplied fields on a draft. `account_id` and `inbox_id` are
server-owned and ignored if present in the body, so a draft can never be moved
between accounts or inboxes.

A draft that is being sent or has already been sent is immutable and returns
422 — modifying it would race with delivery or rewrite the record of what was
actually sent.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subject": "Quarterly update (revised)",
  "text_body": "Updated body."
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inbox_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email inbox UUID.|
|draft_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email draft UUID.|
|body|body|[EmailDraftRequest](#schemaemaildraftrequest)|true|none|
|» from_email|body|string|false|none|
|» from_name|body|string|false|none|
|» to|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|
|» cc|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|
|» bcc|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|
|» reply_to|body|string|false|none|
|» subject|body|string|false|none|
|» text_body|body|string|false|none|
|» html_body|body|string|false|none|
|» text|body|string|false|Alias for `text_body`, matching the send endpoint.|
|» html|body|string|false|Alias for `html_body`, matching the send endpoint.|
|» headers|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» attachments|body|[object]|false|none|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

## Send a draft

<a id="opIdSendEmailDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/drafts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/send \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/drafts/{draft_id}/send`

Sends the draft through the standard send pipeline — the same domain resolution,
suppression, reputation, daily-quota, persistence and Detail Record behaviour as
`POST /v2/email_messages`. The response body is the created email message.

If the draft has no explicit `from_email`, the inbox address is used.

The draft is marked `sent` only after the send is accepted; a send rejected for
suppression, quota or reputation leaves the draft editable so it can be fixed and
retried. A draft that is already `sent` returns 422 rather than sending twice.


<h3 id="send-a-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inbox_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email inbox UUID.|
|draft_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email draft UUID.|

<h3 id="send-a-draft-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **429**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[DailySendLimitError](#schemadailysendlimiterror)|false|none|Error envelope returned when the account's daily recipient quota is exhausted before message creation.|
|*oneOf*|[DomainGraduationLimitExceededError](#schemadomaingraduationlimitexceedederror)|false|none|Error envelope returned when a newly sending custom domain on shared egress would exceed its current daily graduation ceiling. The send is rejected before message creation.|
|*oneOf*|[ReputationSuspendedError](#schemareputationsuspendederror)|false|none|Non-standard error envelope returned when the sending domain's reputation band is 'poor'. Uses string code `reputation_suspended` instead of a numeric code.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Seconds until the next UTC-midnight reset. Present only for domain_graduation_limit_exceeded; omitted for 10011 and reputation_suspended.|

## Create a reply draft

<a id="opIdCreateEmailReplyDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/drafts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "text_body": "Thanks for the update — I will review today."
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/{message_id}/drafts`

Creates an unsent reply draft for an inbound message. Unlike the
`/actions/reply` endpoint, which sends immediately, this stores a draft that can
be reviewed and edited before sending.

`reply_to_message_id` and `thread_id` are inherited from the parent message and
cannot be set by the caller. The recipient, `Re:` subject and
`In-Reply-To`/`References` headers are pre-filled from the parent using the same
rules as a live reply, so sending the draft threads identically. Supplying `to`
or `subject` explicitly overrides the pre-filled value.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text_body": "Thanks for the update — I will review today."
}
```

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-events">Email Events</h1>

Retrieve account-level email events and event statistics.

## List account email events

<a id="opIdListEmailEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_events`

Lists account-level email events sorted oldest first by `occurred_at asc, id asc`. Each row contains a legacy email.-prefixed event_type and an additive canonical_event_type. Gateway rejection renders email.failed with canonical email.gw_reject; ambiguous injection timeout renders email.injection_timeout in both; MTA expiration renders email.bounced with canonical email.expired. Message-scoped queued, sending, sandbox, cancelled, and daily_limit_exceeded rows fan out per durable recipient with stable derived IDs matching webhook delivery. Scheduled is the cardinality exception: account polling retains one message-scoped scheduled row with its stored event ID, while scheduled webhook publication fans out per recipient with derived IDs; reconcile scheduled events by message ID, event type, and occurrence time rather than event UUID. Recipient-scoped stored rows retain their stored UUIDs across polling and webhook delivery. Legacy names are derived from stored rows; an AdminBounce row stored as failed renders email.failed in polling while its webhook retains email.bounced, both with canonical email.failed.

<h3 id="list-account-email-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of results to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100. Invalid values are clamped to the valid range.|
|page[cursor]|query|string|false|Opaque URL-safe Base64 cursor returned by a previous event list response. The legacy `page[after]` and flat `page_cursor` forms are also accepted.|
|event_type|query|string \| [string]|false|Comma-separated list of event types to include. Also accepts repeated<br>query parameters (e.g. event_type=delivered&event_type=bounced).<br>Unknown values return no matches.<br><br>Dual-name compatibility: values are accepted<br>bare or `email.`-prefixed. A legacy value keeps matching the<br>rows it matched pre-rename — no widening: `failed` also<br>matches the rows that now store the canonical names of the<br>outcomes it covered (`gw_reject`, `injection_timeout`,<br>`expired`); `bounced` matches stored `bounced` rows only<br>(recipient-scoped Expirations stored `failed` pre-rename and<br>never matched `bounced`, so `expired` is deliberately not a<br>`bounced` expansion). A canonical value matches its own rows<br>plus legacy rows whose recorded payload evidence proves that<br>outcome (`expired` also surfaces legacy `bounced` rows with<br>`bounce_category: transient`). The additive<br>`canonical_event_type` field in each response row names the<br>canonical outcome.<br>|
|email_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter events for a specific email message UUID. Invalid UUID values are silently ignored (no filter applied).|
|from|query|string(date-time)|false|Inclusive ISO 8601 start timestamp. Defaults to 30 days ago when omitted.|
|to|query|string(date-time)|false|Inclusive ISO 8601 end timestamp. When `from` is provided without `to`, defaults to `from + 30 days`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "f3a2c1d0-1234-4abc-9def-67890abcdef0",
      "event_type": "email.delivered",
      "canonical_event_type": "email.delivered",
      "occurred_at": "2026-07-06T18:24:00.000Z",
      "recipient_id": "7c1e9a44-2f60-4d1b-9a0e-3c7b5e8d1f22",
      "payload": {
        "id": "b0c7e8cb-6227-4c74-9f32-c7f80c30934b",
        "recipient_id": "7c1e9a44-2f60-4d1b-9a0e-3c7b5e8d1f22",
        "status": "delivered",
        "occurred_at": "2026-07-06T18:24:00.000Z",
        "from": {
          "email": "sender@example.com",
          "name": "Telnyx"
        },
        "to": {
          "email": "recipient@example.com",
          "name": null,
          "kind": "to"
        },
        "subject": "Welcome"
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page_size": 50,
    "time_range": {
      "from": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z",
      "to": "2026-07-31T00:00:00Z"
    }
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10006",
      "title": "Not authorized",
      "detail": "Invalid API key",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10006"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create an email inbox

<a id="opIdCreateEmailInbox"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /email_inboxes`

Creates an inbox on an inbound-enabled domain. When `domain_id` is omitted, Telnyx
allocates the account's shared inbound subdomain so the inbox is immediately usable
without customer DNS setup. When `username` is omitted, a unique username is generated.


> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="create-an-email-inbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateEmailInboxRequest](#schemacreateemailinboxrequest)|false|none|
|» username|body|string|false|Inbox local part. Trimmed and lowercased before validation; the normalized value must be 1-64 characters, start and end with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores. Generated when omitted.|
|» domain_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Account-owned, inbound-enabled domain UUID. The account's shared inbound subdomain is allocated when omitted.|

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",

    "domain": "abc123def456.mail.test.telnyx.com",
    "settings": {},

}

}
```

```json
    {
```
```json
      "code": "10015",
```

## Add sender filter entries to an inbox

<a id="opIdAddEmailInboxFilterEntries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/filters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "blocklist",
    "entries": [
      "@spam.example"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/filters`

Adds entries to either the allowlist or blocklist. The operation is an
idempotent set union: entries already present remain unchanged.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "blocklist",
  "entries": [
    "@spam.example"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-sender-filter-entries-to-an-inbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inbox_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email inbox UUID.|
|body|body|[MutateInboxFiltersRequest](#schemamutateinboxfiltersrequest)|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The list to change.|
|» entries|body|[InboxFilterEntryList](#schemainboxfilterentrylist)|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|allowlist|
|» type|blocklist|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## List and search messages in an inbox

<a id="opIdListEmailInboxMessages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/messages \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages`

Lists inbound messages newest first. All access is scoped to the authenticated
account. `filter[search]` performs PostgreSQL full-text search over the subject,
plain-text body, and HTML body. Filters compose with stable cursor pagination.


<h3 id="list-and-search-messages-in-an-inbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inbox_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email inbox UUID.|
|filter[from]|query|string|false|Case-insensitive literal substring of the sender address.|
|filter[subject]|query|string|false|Case-insensitive literal substring of the subject.|
|filter[received_after]|query|string(date-time)|false|Inclusive ISO 8601 lower bound for the received timestamp.|
|filter[received_before]|query|string(date-time)|false|Inclusive ISO 8601 upper bound for the received timestamp.|
|filter[read]|query|boolean|false|Whether the message has a read timestamp.|
|filter[unread]|query|boolean|false|Whether the message has no read timestamp. Set to `true` to return only unread messages.|
|filter[label]|query|string|false|Returns only messages carrying this label. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Reserved `telnyx:` labels can be filtered on even though they cannot be written by customers.|
|filter[search]|query|string|false|Full-text query over subject and body, up to 500 characters.|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Number of results to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100.|
|page[after]|query|string|false|Opaque cursor returned by the previous page.|

## Update an inbox message

<a id="opIdUpdateEmailInboxMessage"></a>

> Code samples


`PATCH /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/{message_id}`

Updates the explicit read state of an account-scoped inbound message. Set `read_at`
to `true` to mark the message read at the server's current time, to an ISO 8601
timestamp to use that timestamp, or to `null` to mark the message unread. Repeating
the same update is idempotent.

```json
}
```

## Forward an inbox message

<a id="opIdForwardEmailInboxMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/actions/forward \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "to": "new@example.com",
    "cc": [
      {
        "email": "copy@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "bcc": [
      "blind@example.com"
    ],
    "text": "FYI"
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/{message_id}/actions/forward`

Sends from the inbox address through the standard email send pipeline to caller-supplied
To, Cc, and Bcc recipients. `to` must contain at least one recipient. Optional `text` and
`html` are prepended to a forwarded-message block containing the original metadata and
available body content. The subject is prefixed with `Fwd:` unless it already has that prefix.

Threading headers are derived from the original message: `In-Reply-To` is set to its
RFC Message-ID, and `References` contains the original References values plus that
Message-ID, de-duplicated and limited to the most recent 20 values.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "to": "new@example.com",
  "cc": [
    {
      "email": "copy@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "bcc": [
    "blind@example.com"
  ],
  "text": "FYI"
}
```

<h3 id="forward-an-inbox-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inbox_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email inbox UUID.|
|message_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Inbound email message UUID.|
|body|body|[ForwardEmailInboxMessageRequest](#schemaforwardemailinboxmessagerequest)|true|none|
|» to|body|[RequiredInboxActionRecipientInput](#schemarequiredinboxactionrecipientinput)|true|One recipient or a non-empty recipient array. Each recipient may be an email string or an object with `email` and optional `name`.|
|» cc|body|[InboxActionRecipientInput](#schemainboxactionrecipientinput)|false|One recipient or a recipient array. Each recipient may be an email string or an object with `email` and optional `name`.|
|» bcc|body|[InboxActionRecipientInput](#schemainboxactionrecipientinput)|false|One recipient or a recipient array. Each recipient may be an email string or an object with `email` and optional `name`.|
|» text|body|string|false|Optional plain-text note prepended to the generated forwarded-message block. Blank values are treated as omitted.|
|» html|body|string|false|Optional HTML note prepended to the generated forwarded-message block. Blank values are treated as omitted.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "email_message",
    "id": "44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444",
    "status": "queued",
    "from": {
      "email": "agent@inbox.example.test"
    },
```
