      {
        "email": "new@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "cc": [
      {
        "email": "copy@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "bcc": [
      {
        "email": "blind@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "reply_to": null,
    "subject": "Fwd: Project update",
    "tags": [],
    "metadata": {},
    "template_id": null,
    "template_variables": {},
    "attachments": [],
    "events": [],
    "created_at": "2026-07-15T12:35:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10015",
      "title": "Bad Request",
      "detail": "email is required"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10006",
      "title": "Not authorized",
      "detail": "Invalid API key",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10006"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "Forbidden",
      "detail": "Domain is not verified. Complete DNS setup before sending email."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

      "code": "10001",

    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

      "code": "10015",

<h3 id="forward-an-inbox-message-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Forward accepted by the standard email send pipeline.|[EmailMessageResponse](#schemaemailmessageresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request / Validation Failed (10015).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Not authorized (10006).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden (10007), such as domain not verified, suspended, degraded, or missing DKIM.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|404|Not Found|The inbox, source message, or sending domain was not found (10001).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Forward validation failed (10015), or all recipients are suppressed.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Send rejected before message creation because the account daily recipient quota was exhausted (10011), the sender-domain graduation ceiling was exceeded (domain_graduation_limit_exceeded), or domain reputation is poor (reputation_suspended).|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Inbox message actions or the email domain service are temporarily unavailable (10016).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|

<h3 id="forward-an-inbox-message-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **429**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[DailySendLimitError](#schemadailysendlimiterror)|false|none|Error envelope returned when the account's daily recipient quota is exhausted before message creation.|
|*oneOf*|[DomainGraduationLimitExceededError](#schemadomaingraduationlimitexceedederror)|false|none|Error envelope returned when a newly sending custom domain on shared egress would exceed its current daily graduation ceiling. The send is rejected before message creation.|
|*oneOf*|[ReputationSuspendedError](#schemareputationsuspendederror)|false|none|Non-standard error envelope returned when the sending domain's reputation band is 'poor'. Uses string code `reputation_suspended` instead of a numeric code.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|X-Telnyx-Reputation-Warning|string||Present with `warn` when the accepted send uses a sender domain in the reputation warn band; delivery proceeds with reduced sending limits.|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Seconds until the next UTC-midnight reset. Present only for domain_graduation_limit_exceeded; omitted for 10011 and reputation_suspended.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Reply to an inbox message

<a id="opIdReplyToEmailInboxMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/actions/reply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Thanks for the update."
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/{message_id}/actions/reply`

Sends from the inbox address through the standard email send pipeline. The recipient is
the original `Reply-To`, falling back to `From`; original Cc recipients are not included.
The subject is prefixed with `Re:` unless it already has that prefix.

Threading headers are derived from the original message: `In-Reply-To` is set to its
RFC Message-ID, and `References` contains the original References values plus that
Message-ID, de-duplicated and limited to the most recent 20 values.

```json

  "text": "Thanks for the update."
}
```

<h3 id="reply-to-an-inbox-message-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **429**

|*oneOf*|[ReputationSuspendedError](#schemareputationsuspendederror)|false|none|Non-standard error envelope returned when the sending domain's reputation band is 'poor'. Uses string code `reputation_suspended` instead of a numeric code.|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Reply all to an inbox message

<a id="opIdReplyAllToEmailInboxMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/actions/reply_all \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Everyone, please review."
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/{message_id}/actions/reply_all`

Sends from the inbox address through the standard email send pipeline. The To list starts
with the original `Reply-To` (or `From`) and includes original To recipients; the Cc list
includes original Cc recipients. The inbox address is excluded, and recipients are
de-duplicated case-insensitively across To and Cc. Bcc is always empty. The subject is
prefixed with `Re:` unless it already has that prefix.

Threading headers are derived from the original message: `In-Reply-To` is set to its
RFC Message-ID, and `References` contains the original References values plus that
Message-ID, de-duplicated and limited to the most recent 20 values.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "Everyone, please review."
}
```

## Add labels to an inbox message

<a id="opIdAddEmailInboxMessageLabels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/labels \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "labels": [
      "spam",
      "urgent"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/{message_id}/labels`

Adds one or more mutable labels to a message. Labels carry agent
workflow state such as `spam`, `needs_review`, or `processed`.

Labels are **not** the same as the send-time `tags` on outbound
messages: `tags` are immutable and propagate to Email Detail Records
and Mission Control for billing attribution, while labels are mailbox
state that never reaches the reporting contract.

The operation is an idempotent set union — adding a label the message
already carries is a no-op and still returns 200. Labels are
case-sensitive, and message labels are independent of thread labels.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "labels": [
    "spam",
    "urgent"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-labels-to-an-inbox-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inbox_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email inbox UUID.|
|message_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Inbound message UUID.|
|body|body|[LabelMutationRequest](#schemalabelmutationrequest)|true|none|
|» labels|body|[string]|true|One or more labels. Each label is a freeform, case-sensitive string of at most 255 characters; a message or thread may carry at most 50 labels. The `telnyx:` prefix is a reserved system namespace and is rejected on customer writes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555",
    "record_type": "email_message",
    "direction": "inbound",
    "status": "received",
    "inbox_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
    "thread_id": "33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333",
    "message_id": "<message@example.com>",
    "in_reply_to": "<earlier@example.com>",
    "references": [
      "<earlier@example.com>"
    ],
    "from": {
      "email": "alice@example.com",
      "name": "Alice"
    },
    "to": [
      {
        "email": "agent@inbox.example.test"
      }
    ],
    "cc": [],
    "bcc": [],
    "reply_to": [],
    "subject": "Project update",
    "text_body_url": null,
    "html_body_url": null,
    "reply_text": "Thanks, I will send it today.",
    "has_quoted_text": true,
    "headers": {},
    "inline_files": [],
    "attachments": [],
    "labels": [
      "spam",
      "urgent"
    ],
    "read_at": null,
    "received_at": "2026-07-15T12:30:00Z",
    "sent_at": null,
    "created_at": "2026-07-15T12:30:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-07-15T12:30:00Z"
  }

```

> 401 Response

    {
      "code": "10006",
      "title": "Not authorized",
      "detail": "Invalid API key",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10006"
      }
    }

}

## Add labels to an inbox thread

<a id="opIdAddEmailInboxThreadLabels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_inboxes/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/threads/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/labels \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    "labels": [
      "needs_review"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /email_inboxes/{inbox_id}/threads/{thread_id}/labels`

Adds one or more mutable labels to a thread, letting an agent mark a
whole conversation (for example `needs_review`) without labelling each
message individually.

Thread labels are independent of message labels: labelling a thread
does not label its messages, and labelling a message does not label its
thread. Idempotent and case-sensitive.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "labels": [
    "needs_review"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-labels-to-an-inbox-thread-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|inbox_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email inbox UUID.|
|thread_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Thread UUID.|
|body|body|[LabelMutationRequest](#schemalabelmutationrequest)|true|none|
|» labels|body|[string]|true|One or more labels. Each label is a freeform, case-sensitive string of at most 255 characters; a message or thread may carry at most 50 labels. The `telnyx:` prefix is a reserved system namespace and is rejected on customer writes.|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-messages">Email Messages</h1>

Send and manage email messages. Legacy `/v2/emails` routes are aliases for these endpoints.

## List email messages

<a id="opIdListEmailMessages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_messages \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_messages`

Lists messages sorted newest first by `created_at desc, id desc`. Tags and metadata filters compose with cursor pagination. The legacy `/v2/emails` GET route is a backward-compatible alias for this operation.


<h3 id="list-email-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of results to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100. Invalid values are clamped to the valid range.|
|page_cursor|query|string|false|Opaque URL-safe Base64 cursor returned by a previous list response.|
|filter[tags]|query|string|false|Comma-separated tags. Each segment is trimmed, and messages having at least one supplied tag are returned; matching is exact and case-sensitive after trimming. Because commas delimit values and surrounding whitespace is removed, this filter cannot represent stored tags containing literal commas or leading/trailing whitespace. An empty value omits the filter. Empty segments and non-string/nested query shapes return HTTP 400.|
|filter[metadata]|query|string|false|Metadata containment filter, supplied as a JSON object or comma-separated `key=value` pairs. All supplied key/value pairs must be contained in the message metadata. An empty value or empty JSON object omits the filter. Malformed values, valid non-object JSON, pairs without `=`, empty keys, and non-string/nested query shapes return HTTP 400.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "data": [
    {
      "record_type": "email_message",

        }

## Create or send an email message

<a id="opIdCreateEmailMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_messages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from": "sender@example.com",
    "to": [
      "recipient@example.com"
    ],
    "subject": "Hello from Telnyx",
    "text_body": "This is a test email."
  }'
```

`POST /email_messages`

Queues, schedules, or sandbox-sends an email message. The legacy `/v2/emails` POST route
is a backward-compatible alias for this operation.

`subject` is required unless `template_id` is supplied. When using `template_id`, do not
also provide `subject`, `html_body`, or `text_body`; the template is rendered with
`template_variables`.

Note: template lookup failures (not found, wrong account) return 400, not 404.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from": "sender@example.com",
  "to": [
    "recipient@example.com"
  ],
  "subject": "Hello from Telnyx",
  "text_body": "This is a test email."
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-send-an-email-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateEmailRequest](#schemacreateemailrequest)|true|none|
|» from|body|[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)|true|none|
|» from_name|body|string|false|Optional display name for string `from`; overrides `from.name` when provided.|
|» to|body|[EmailAddressArrayInput](#schemaemailaddressarrayinput)|true|none|
|» cc|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|
|» bcc|body|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|
|» reply_to|body|[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)|false|Reply-to address. If provided as an object with a name, only the email is stored; the name is ignored.|
|» subject|body|string|false|Required unless `template_id` is supplied. When using a template, the template's subject is rendered; if the template has no subject or renders empty, the request returns 400.|
|» html_body|body|string|false|HTML email body. Returned only by `GET /email_messages/{id}`; omitted from create and list responses.|
|» text_body|body|string|false|Plain text email body. Returned only by `GET /email_messages/{id}`; omitted from create and list responses.|
|» headers|body|object|false|Custom email headers. Write-only; not returned in responses.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» attachments|body|[[AttachmentRequest](#schemaattachmentrequest)]|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for categorization and filtering. Stored on the message, returned on message responses, and propagated to Email Detail Records. Usable in `filter[tags]` when listing messages.|
|» group_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Optional unsubscribe-group UUID used for group-scoped suppression checks and unsubscribe handling.|
|» ignore_suppression|body|boolean|false|When true, allows delivery to recipients whose suppressions explicitly<br>permit an override. Hard bounces, spam complaints, and invalid-address<br>suppressions cannot be overridden. Requires the `email:override` API scope.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Custom metadata key/value pairs. Stored on the message, returned on message responses, and propagated to Email Detail Records. Usable in `filter[metadata]` when listing messages.|
|» tracking_settings|body|[TrackingSettings](#schematrackingsettings)|false|Per-send open and click tracking overrides. Omitted properties inherit the sender domain's tracking settings.|
|» template_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» template_variables|body|object|false|Variables for Liquid template rendering. Non-object values may cause a 422 validation error on message creation, but are silently treated as an empty object for template rendering. When the template enables `strict_variables`, a missing required variable fails the request with 422 (single send) or a per-item `unprocessable_entity` error (batch) naming the variable; no message is persisted for the failed item.|
|» scheduled_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|Future ISO 8601 delivery time. Invalid or non-future timestamps are rejected. Single sends return HTTP 422; in batch sends the invalid item is reported in the 207 per-item errors while other items continue. `send_at` remains a deprecated request alias. A non-null `scheduled_at` takes precedence over `send_at`; when `scheduled_at` is omitted or null, `send_at` is used.|
|» send_at|body|string(date-time)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated alias for `scheduled_at`.|
|» inline_css|body|boolean|false|none|
|» sandbox_mode|body|boolean|false|Validates and accepts the message without injecting it into the MTA or outbound Kafka path. Nothing is delivered: sandbox records are non-billable, consume no daily-send-limit quota, and feed no delivery-reputation signals.<br><br>The reserved sandbox test-recipient domain is `test.telnyx.com`. In sandbox mode, these addresses produce deterministic recipient-scoped lifecycle events:<br><br>- `delivered@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> delivered<br>- `hard-bounce@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> bounced (permanent)<br>- `soft-bounce@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> bounced (transient)<br>- `complaint@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> complained<br>- `suppressed@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> suppressed<br>- `invalid@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> failed (invalid recipient)<br>- `dkim-fail@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> failed (DKIM unavailable)<br>- `rate-limit@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> failed (rate limit exceeded)<br><br>Matching is case-insensitive for both the local part and the domain and requires the exact domain `test.telnyx.com` — subdomains and other domains do not match. Mixed sandbox sends simulate only reserved test recipients; other recipients retain ordinary sandbox behavior (accepted, no delivery attempted). Hard-bounce and complaint outcomes also use the normal automatic-suppression pipeline. Non-sandbox sends to these addresses use the normal delivery path.|
|» in_reply_to_message_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Telnyx message UUID of the message this send replies to. When provided,<br>the API sets RFC 5322 `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers on the<br>outbound MIME so the recipient's mailbox (Gmail/Outlook) threads it<br>correctly. The parent is looked up under the caller's account scope;<br>a UUID belonging to another account yields a non-enumerating 404.<br><br>Wire-only (Phase 1): the API sets the headers and does NOT resolve or<br>mutate `thread_id` on the server side. Messages sent without this<br>parameter are standalone (no threading headers injected).<br><br>Cannot be combined with `forward_of_message_id` (422).|
|» reply_to_all|body|boolean \| null|false|Indicates a reply-all intent. In Phase 1 (wire-only) this does not<br>change the threading headers — recipient selection is customer-<br>controlled (`to`/`cc`), and a thread is not defined by its audience.<br>When the referenced message has no thread context, reply-all<br>degrades to a plain reply (parent ID only in `References`). The<br>resolution engine (separate work) will expand the ancestor chain<br>at a later phase with no API change.<br><br>Only meaningful alongside `in_reply_to_message_id`.|
|» forward_of_message_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Telnyx message UUID of the message this send forwards. Forwarded<br>messages start a NEW thread per RFC 5322 — NO `In-Reply-To` or<br>`References` headers are set on the outbound MIME. The id is<br>recorded in the message's metadata for EDR provenance only.<br><br>The id is validated as a UUID but is NOT looked up against the<br>message store — existence is the caller's responsibility (the<br>forward is pure metadata; it does not affect delivery). Cannot be<br>combined with `in_reply_to_message_id` (422).|

|401|Unauthorized|Not authorized (10006).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden (10007), such as domain not verified, suspended, degraded, or missing DKIM.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found (10001).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (10036). Retry later with the same key and request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Request body exceeds the 8,000,000-byte limit for this endpoint.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed (including an invalid or non-future `scheduled_at`/`send_at`), send-time template rendering failed (including a strict-variable failure naming the missing required variable), or all recipients suppressed (code `recipient_suppressed`, includes top-level `suppressed` array). Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different request also returns 422 (10027).|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Send rejected before message creation because the account daily recipient quota was exhausted (10011), the sender-domain graduation ceiling was exceeded (domain_graduation_limit_exceeded), or domain reputation is poor (reputation_suspended).|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable (10016), including an unavailable upstream dependency or unavailable Edge idempotency protection for a keyed request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|

<h3 id="create-or-send-an-email-message-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[RenderErrorResponse](#schemarendererrorresponse)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[RecipientSuppressedError](#schemarecipientsuppressederror)|false|none|Non-standard error envelope returned when all recipients are suppressed and ignore_suppression was not set/allowed. Includes a top-level `suppressed` array alongside `errors`.|

Status Code **429**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[DailySendLimitError](#schemadailysendlimiterror)|false|none|Error envelope returned when the account's daily recipient quota is exhausted before message creation.|
|*oneOf*|[DomainGraduationLimitExceededError](#schemadomaingraduationlimitexceedederror)|false|none|Error envelope returned when a newly sending custom domain on shared egress would exceed its current daily graduation ceiling. The send is rejected before message creation.|
|*oneOf*|[ReputationSuspendedError](#schemareputationsuspendederror)|false|none|Non-standard error envelope returned when the sending domain's reputation band is 'poor'. Uses string code `reputation_suspended` instead of a numeric code.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Idempotent-Replayed|boolean||Present with value `true` when Edge replayed a stored successful response for the supplied Idempotency-Key. Omitted for first-time requests and error responses.|
|202|X-Telnyx-Reputation-Warning|string||Present with `warn` when the accepted send uses a sender domain in the reputation warn band; delivery proceeds with reduced sending limits.|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Seconds until the next UTC-midnight reset. Present only for domain_graduation_limit_exceeded; omitted for 10011 and reputation_suspended.|

## Delete email messages by address

<a id="opIdDeleteEmailMessagesByAddress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_messages?address=user%40example.com' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /email_messages`

Permanently deletes every email in the authenticated account sent from or to the
supplied address, including retained events whose parent message has expired.
Events and durable recipients are deleted immediately with each message. The
operation never searches or reports matches in another account. The legacy
`/v2/emails` DELETE route is a backward-compatible alias.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|query|string(email)|true|Sender or recipient address to delete. Matching is trimmed and case-insensitive.|

## Create a batch of email messages

<a id="opIdCreateEmailMessageBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_messages/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sandbox_mode": false,
    "messages": [
      {
        "from": "sender@example.com",
        "to": [
          "recipient1@example.com"
        ],
        "subject": "Hello 1",
        "text_body": "Message 1"
      },
      {
        "from": "sender@example.com",
        "to": [
          "recipient2@example.com"
        ],
        "subject": "Hello 2",
        "text_body": "Message 2"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /email_messages/batch`

Creates up to 1,000 email messages in a single request. Request-wide admission checks run first and can reject the whole batch before message creation. After those checks pass, each message is validated and sent independently; item-level failures do not affect other messages, and the processed batch returns 207 Multi-Status. Per-message failures include validation errors; when a template has `strict_variables` enabled, a missing required variable produces a per-item `unprocessable_entity` error naming that variable while the other messages continue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sandbox_mode": false,
  "messages": [
    {
      "from": "sender@example.com",
      "to": [
        "recipient1@example.com"
      ],
      "subject": "Hello 1",
      "text_body": "Message 1"
    },
    {
      "from": "sender@example.com",
      "to": [
        "recipient2@example.com"
      ],
      "subject": "Hello 2",
      "text_body": "Message 2"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-batch-of-email-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateEmailBatchRequest](#schemacreateemailbatchrequest)|true|none|
|» messages|body|[[CreateEmailBatchItemRequest](#schemacreateemailbatchitemrequest)]|true|Array of email messages to send. Up to 1,000 messages per batch request. Each message is validated and sent independently; per-message failures do not affect other messages in the batch.|
|» sandbox_mode|body|boolean|false|Applies sandbox mode to all messages in the batch and overrides any per-message `sandbox_mode` value — each message's effective `sandbox_mode` is exactly this envelope value. Reserved recipients at `test.telnyx.com` produce the deterministic event chains documented on CreateEmailRequest.sandbox_mode; no batch item is injected into the MTA or outbound Kafka path. Sandbox batch items are non-billable, consume no daily-send-limit quota, and feed no delivery-reputation signals.|

## List events for an email message

<a id="opIdListEmailMessageEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_messages/{email_id}/events`

Lists events for a single message sorted oldest first by `occurred_at asc, id asc`.
The legacy `/v2/emails/{id}/events` GET route is a backward-compatible alias.

For compatibility, each event carries the legacy
customer-visible `event_type` (`email.`-prefixed), the additive
`canonical_event_type` (`email.`-prefixed), and the deprecated
`type` duplicate — whose value keeps the exact legacy format:
the bare stored event name, never `email.`-prefixed. Gateway
rejections render `email.failed` + canonical `email.gw_reject`; MTA
expirations render `email.bounced` + canonical `email.expired`;
every unchanged outcome carries identical `event_type` and
`canonical_event_type` values (and `type` keeps the stored name).


<h3 id="list-events-for-an-email-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email message UUID.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of results to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100. Invalid values are clamped to the valid range.|
|page_cursor|query|string|false|Opaque URL-safe Base64 cursor returned by a previous list response.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "type": "queued",
      "event_type": "email.queued",
      "canonical_event_type": "email.queued",
      "occurred_at": "2026-07-06T18:24:00.000Z"
    },
    {
      "type": "gw_reject",
      "event_type": "email.failed",
      "canonical_event_type": "email.gw_reject",
      "occurred_at": "2026-07-06T18:24:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page_size": 50
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10006",
      "title": "Not authorized",
      "detail": "Invalid API key",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10006"

## List recipients for an email message

<a id="opIdListEmailMessageRecipients"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/recipients \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_messages/{email_id}/recipients`

Lists per-recipient delivery states for a single message with cursor pagination.
Each recipient has an independent status, billable flag, and lifecycle timestamps.
BCC recipient addresses are redacted (returned as null) to protect BCC privacy.
Default page size is 25, maximum is 100.


<h3 id="list-recipients-for-an-email-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email message UUID.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of results to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100. Invalid values are clamped to the valid range.|
|page_cursor|query|string|false|Opaque URL-safe Base64 cursor returned by a previous list response.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter recipients by status.|
|kind|query|string|false|Filter recipients by address kind.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|queued|
|status|sending|
|status|sent|
|status|deferred|
|status|delivered|
|status|bounced|
|status|failed|
|status|gw_reject|
|status|cancelled|
|status|injection_timeout|
|status|expired|
|kind|to|
|kind|cc|
|kind|bcc|

> 200 Response

      "address": "example@telnyx.com",
      "kind": "to",

      "billable": false,

      "delivered_at": "2024-01-23T18:10:02.574Z",
      "failed_at": "2024-01-23T18:10:02.574Z",
      "smtp_code": 0,
      "smtp_response": "string"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page_size": 1,
    "page_cursor": "string"
  }
}
```

## Reschedule a scheduled email message

<a id="opIdRescheduleEmailMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_messages/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/schedule \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

`PATCH /email_messages/{email_id}/schedule`

Moves an existing scheduled email to a new future send time. Only the delivery time (`scheduled_at`) changes; the message ID, content, recipients, tags, and metadata remain unchanged. Returns `409 Conflict` if the message is no longer scheduled or its scheduled-send worker has already started processing it. This route emits no dedicated `rescheduled` event.

}

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-suppression-imports">Email Suppression Imports</h1>

Async CSV import of competitor suppression lists.

## Create an async CSV import job

<a id="opIdcreateEmailBlockImport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_blocks/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'block_ttl_days=30'
```

`POST /email_blocks/import`

Accepts `multipart/form-data` with a `file` field (the CSV) and an
optional `block_ttl_days` (integer >0, default 30). Validates:
  - content ≤ 25 MiB, else `413`
  - row count ≤ 250 000, else `413`
  - header-only / all-blank / undetectable provider → `400`
Returns `202` with the import record (status `pending`); an Oban
worker (`EmailBlockImportWorker`, max_attempts 3) transitions
`pending → processing → completed | failed`.

Native Telnyx exports are detected by the stable first-12-column
header signature (`id` … `group_id`) and are restored with their
original `from`, `domain_id`, `group_id`, `source`, `status`,
`expires_at`, plus `bounce_category`, `dsn_code`, and `meta` when
present (`scope` is re-derived from `domain_id`/`from`; the
exported `scope` cell must be a valid enum value). Lifecycle
changes reconcile through the same create path as the API: a row
already in the requested state restores its mutable backup fields
without a new audit event, and a real transition (e.g. tombstone
→ active) appends the matching lifecycle event. `block_ttl_days`
is not applied to native rows — their exported `expires_at` is
preserved verbatim.

Competitor and generic imports (SendGrid / Mailgun / SES /
generic) remain account-scoped (`from`, `domain_id`, `group_id`,
`scope` are not read) and `block_ttl_days` applies only to
imported `manual_block` rows; other reasons get `expires_at: nil`.
Provider is auto-detected from the CSV header
(`sendgrid` / `mailgun` / `ses` / `generic`).


> Body parameter

```yaml
file: blocks.csv
block_ttl_days: 30
```

<h3 id="create-an-async-csv-import-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateImportRequest](#schemacreateimportrequest)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The CSV file (Plug.Upload). Missing/non-upload → 400.|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-suppressions">Email Suppressions</h1>

Recipient suppression records (`/v2/email_blocks`).

## List suppressions

<a id="opIdlistEmailBlocks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_blocks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_blocks`

Account-scoped list. Two mutually exclusive pagination modes:

  - **Offset**: `page[number]` (default 1) + `page[size]`
    (default 25, max 100). `meta` contains `total_pages`.
  - **Cursor**: `page[after]` and/or `page[before]` (opaque
    `Base.url_encode64` of `{"created_at","id"}`). Cannot combine
    with `page[number]`; `after`+`before` together is an error.
    `meta` contains `next_cursor` / `previous_cursor` (omitted when
    their flag is false).

Sort defaults to `-created_at` (desc); only `created_at` is sortable.
A `--` prefix is an error. `nil`/empty filter values are silently dropped.


<h3 id="list-suppressions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|Offset page number (≥1, default 1).|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Page size (1–100, default 25).|
|page[after]|query|string|false|Opaque cursor (`Base.url_encode64` of `{"created_at","id"}`). Cursor mode; mutually exclusive with `page[number]` and `page[before]`.|
|page[before]|query|string|false|Opaque cursor (see `page[after]`). Mutually exclusive with `page[after]` and `page[number]`.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort field. Leading `-` = desc; only `created_at` is sortable. Default `-created_at`. `--` is an error.|
|filter[reason]|query|[Reason](#schemareason)|false|Exact-match filter on reason.|
|filter[domain_id]|query|string(uuid)|false|Exact-match filter on domain_id (UUID).|
|filter[created_after]|query|string(date-time)|false|`created_at > value` (ISO 8601).|
|filter[created_before]|query|string(date-time)|false|`created_at < value` (ISO 8601).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created_at|
|sort|-created_at|
|filter[reason]|hard_bounce|
|filter[reason]|spam_complaint|
|filter[reason]|unsubscribe|
|filter[reason]|invalid|
|filter[reason]|manual_block|

## Create a manual suppression

<a id="opIdcreateEmailBlock"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_blocks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "to": "spammer@bad.tld",
    "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"
  }'
```

`POST /email_blocks`

Creates a suppression with `reason: manual_block` and `source: manual`.
Caller-supplied `reason` / `source` are **ignored**; `scope` is
**derived** server-side from `domain_id` / `from` and is never
trusted. Idempotent: if a matching row already exists (NULL-safe
dedupe key: account_id, scope, to, reason, domain_id, from),
returns the existing record with `200` (no new audit event).

`bounce_category`, `dsn_code`, `meta`, and `group_id` are **not
accepted** on the public surface. Use the unsubscribe-group
suppression endpoint or the internal create surface for those.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "to": "spammer@bad.tld",
  "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-manual-suppression-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateEmailBlockRequest](#schemacreateemailblockrequest)|true|none|
|» to|body|string|true|Recipient address (normalized: trim + lower-case).|
|» from|body|string \| null|false|Sender address (normalized). `null` ⇒ account/domain scope.|
|» domain_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|`null` ⇒ account scope.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|

## Export suppressions as CSV

<a id="opIdexportEmailBlocks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_blocks/export \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_blocks/export`

Streams the account's suppressions as a chunked CSV (server-side
cursor; never materialized). Content-type `text/csv`, header
`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="email_blocks_export.csv"`.

Filters (`filter[reason]`, `filter[domain_id]`,
`filter[created_after]`, `filter[created_before]`) are the only
params that affect output. `sort` and `page[*]` are **parsed**
(bad values still produce `400`) but **ignored** — rows stream
`ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC` with no pagination.

CSV columns: `id,to,from,reason,source,scope,status,domain_id,
created_at,updated_at,expires_at,group_id,bounce_category,dsn_code,
meta` (15 columns). The first 12 columns are the stable native
signature; `bounce_category`, `dsn_code`, and `meta` are optional
backup fields (empty when unset). The CSV carries the `group_id`
column so group-scoped suppressions' group link survives the
export (empty for account-scope rows).


<h3 id="export-suppressions-as-csv-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort field. Leading `-` = desc; only `created_at` is sortable. Default `-created_at`. `--` is an error.|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|Offset page number (≥1, default 1).|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Page size (1–100, default 25).|
|filter[reason]|query|[Reason](#schemareason)|false|Exact-match filter on reason.|
|filter[domain_id]|query|string(uuid)|false|Exact-match filter on domain_id (UUID).|
|filter[created_after]|query|string(date-time)|false|`created_at > value` (ISO 8601).|
|filter[created_before]|query|string(date-time)|false|`created_at < value` (ISO 8601).|

## Soft-delete a suppression

<a id="opIddeleteEmailBlock"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_blocks/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /email_blocks/{id}`

Soft-deletes (status → `removed`; tombstone retained). A `removed`
audit event is appended unless the block was already `removed`
(idempotent — returns the existing row with `200` and no new event).
Mutates `updated_at`.

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-templates">Email Templates</h1>

Create, list, retrieve, update, delete, and render Liquid email templates.

## List email templates

<a id="opIdListEmailTemplates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_templates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_templates`

Lists templates sorted newest first by `created_at desc, id desc`. Optional filters match a case-insensitive literal name/subject query, stored body presence, and the `strict_variables` and `autoescape` settings. Filters intersect, remain scoped to the authenticated account, and apply before cursor pagination. Invalid filter names or values return 400.

<h3 id="list-email-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of results to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100. Invalid values are clamped to the valid range.|
|page_cursor|query|string|false|Opaque URL-safe Base64 cursor returned by a previous list response.|
|filter[query]|query|string|false|Case-insensitive literal substring match over the template `name` or stored `subject` only; bodies are never searched. `%`, `_`, and `\` are literal characters with no wildcard meaning. A blank value is treated as omitted.|
|filter[content_type]|query|string|false|Matches templates by stored body presence. `html_and_text` requires both an HTML and text body; `html_only` requires HTML and no text body; `text_only` requires text and no HTML body; `no_body` requires neither. `null` and exactly `""` count as absent; whitespace-only strings count as content. An empty or unsupported value returns a 400 response.|
|filter[strict_variables]|query|string|false|Exact match on the template's `strict_variables` option. Only the exact query strings `true` and `false` are accepted; other values, including blank, return 400.|
|filter[autoescape]|query|string|false|Exact match on the template's `autoescape` option. Only the exact query strings `true` and `false` are accepted; other values, including blank, return 400.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter[content_type]|html_and_text|
|filter[content_type]|html_only|
|filter[content_type]|text_only|
|filter[content_type]|no_body|
|filter[strict_variables]|true|
|filter[strict_variables]|false|
|filter[autoescape]|true|
|filter[autoescape]|false|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "record_type": "email_template",
      "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
      "name": "string",
      "subject": "string",
      "html_body": "string",
      "text_body": "string",

        "string"
      ],
      "variables_mode": "automatic",
      "strict_variables": false,

      "created_at": "2024-01-23T18:10:02.574Z",
      "updated_at": "2024-01-23T18:10:02.574Z"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page_size": 1,
    "page_cursor": "string"
  }
}
```

## Create an email template

<a id="opIdCreateEmailTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_templates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Welcome Email",
    "subject": "Welcome, {{ first_name }}!",
    "html_body": "<h1>Hello {{ first_name }}</h1>",
    "text_body": "Hello {{ first_name }}"
  }'
```

`POST /email_templates`

Creates a Liquid email template. Variables are auto-extracted when omitted.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Welcome Email",
  "subject": "Welcome, {{ first_name }}!",
  "html_body": "<h1>Hello {{ first_name }}</h1>",
  "text_body": "Hello {{ first_name }}"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-email-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateEmailTemplateRequest](#schemacreateemailtemplaterequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and underscores only.|
|» subject|body|string \| null|false|Liquid template subject.|
|» html_body|body|string \| null|false|Liquid template HTML body.|
|» text_body|body|string \| null|false|Liquid template text body.|
|» variables|body|[string]|false|Persisted variable names. In `automatic` mode a non-null array is rejected; in `explicit` mode this is the exact manual array and each item is limited to 255 Unicode code points.|
|» variables_mode|body|string|false|Controls how `variables` is maintained. If both fields are omitted (or `variables` is null), the template uses `automatic` mode and extracts variable names from the effective subject, HTML body, and text body. A non-null `variables` array with no mode selects `explicit`. `automatic` rejects a simultaneous non-null array; `explicit` requires a non-null array, including valid `[]`, and preserves its exact order, duplicates, and string contents.|
|» strict_variables|body|boolean|false|Per-template strict variable-validation setting. Defaults to `false` for backward compatibility. When `true`, a send or render that is missing a variable marked `required: true` in `variable_schema` fails with 422 naming the variable. Missing optional variables never fail; their schema `default` (when set) is applied to the render.|
|» autoescape|body|boolean|false|Per-template HTML autoescaping setting. Defaults to `false` for backward compatibility. When `true`, the rendered `html_body` HTML-escapes each Liquid expression's output at the output boundary (after its filters run, before concatenation with literal template markup). Input values are never mutated and `subject`/`text_body` are never autoescaped. The boundary escape is idempotent: HTML entities already present in the output (e.g. from an explicit `escape` filter) are preserved, so an explicit `escape`/`escape_once` is never double-escaped, and markup introduced by any later filter in the chain is still escaped.|
|» variable_schema|body|object \| null|false|Structured variable requirements. Required variables cannot define defaults; invalid combinations return 422. This is independent of the legacy `variables` array. On render with `strict_variables` enabled: `required` variables must be supplied as non-empty values — absent, `null`, empty string, empty object `{}`, and empty array `[]` all fail with 422 naming the variable, while present values such as `false` and `0` pass (they are present, not empty). Optional variables fall back to their `default` when absent.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[VariableSchemaEntry](#schemavariableschemaentry)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» variables_mode|automatic|
|» variables_mode|explicit|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "email_template",
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "name": "string",
    "html_body": "string",
    "text_body": "string",
    "variables": [
      "string"
    ],
    "variables_mode": "automatic",
    "strict_variables": true,
    "autoescape": true,
    "variable_schema": {
      "property1": {
        "required": true,
        "default": "string"
      },
      "property2": {
        "required": true,
        "default": "string"
      }
    },
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "subject": "string"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

    {
      "code": "10015",
      "title": "Bad Request",
      "detail": "email is required"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

    {
      "code": "10006",
      "title": "Not authorized",
      "detail": "Invalid API key",

        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10006"
      }

> 409 Response

<h3 id="create-an-email-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Template created.|[EmailTemplateResponse](#schemaemailtemplateresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request / Validation Failed (10015). Invalid, duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong Idempotency-Key headers are rejected by Edge with HTTP 400 and error code 10015.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Not authorized (10006).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|

|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Failed (10015) or changeset validation error. Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different request also returns 422 (10027).|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable (10016), including an unavailable upstream dependency or unavailable Edge idempotency protection for a keyed request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|

`PATCH /email_templates/{id}`

Updates one or more fields of the specified email template and returns the updated template.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subject": "Welcome aboard, {{first_name}}!"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-email-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» subject|body|string \| null|false|Liquid template subject.|
|» html_body|body|string \| null|false|Liquid template HTML body.|
|» text_body|body|string \| null|false|Liquid template text body.|
|» variables|body|[string]|false|Persisted variable names. In `automatic` mode a non-null array is rejected; in `explicit` mode this is the exact manual array and each item is limited to 255 Unicode code points.|
|» variables_mode|body|string|false|Controls how `variables` is maintained. Setting `automatic` re-extracts immediately from the effective subject, HTML body, and text body and rejects a simultaneous non-null array. Setting `explicit` requires the exact non-null array, including valid `[]`. With the mode omitted, a non-null array selects explicit mode, null selects automatic mode, and omitting both fields preserves the current mode. Source-content changes re-extract only in automatic mode.|
|» strict_variables|body|boolean|false|Per-template strict variable-validation setting.|
|» autoescape|body|boolean|false|Per-template HTML autoescaping setting.|
|» variable_schema|body|object \| null|false|Structured variable requirements. Required variables cannot define defaults; invalid combinations return 422. Set to `null` to clear the schema.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[VariableSchemaEntry](#schemavariableschemaentry)|false|none|

|» variables_mode|explicit|

<a id="opIdRenderEmailTemplate"></a>

`POST /email_templates/{id}/render`

Renders a template using the provided Liquid variables. Missing `template_variables` defaults to `{}`.

When the template has `strict_variables` enabled and a required variable (per `variable_schema`) is missing, returns 422 naming the variable. When the template has `autoescape` enabled, the rendered `html_body` expression output is HTML-escaped at the output boundary; `subject` and `text_body` are not autoescaped.

{
  "template_variables": {
    "first_name": "Ada"
  }
}

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-threads">Email Threads</h1>

Account-wide conversation threads across every inbox, for agents operating many inboxes at once.

## List threads across every inbox in the account

<a id="opIdListEmailThreads"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_threads \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_threads`

Lists thread summaries for the whole account, newest first, using stable
cursor pagination. An agent operating many inboxes gets every
conversation in one call instead of one call per inbox. Each thread
carries its own `inbox_id` so a reply can be routed back to the right
inbox. Use `filter[inbox_id]` (repeatable) to narrow the result to
specific inboxes. Because a thread ID can be delivered to multiple
inboxes, each result is identified by its `(inbox_id, id)` pair.


<h3 id="list-threads-across-every-inbox-in-the-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter[inbox_id]|query|[string(uuid)]|false|Restrict results to one or more inboxes. Repeat the parameter<br>(`filter[inbox_id][]=...&filter[inbox_id][]=...`) or pass a<br>comma-separated list. Omit to list every inbox in the account.<br>Inboxes outside the account are silently excluded. If the filter<br>is present, it must contain at least one non-empty UUID.<br>|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Number of results to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100.|
|page[after]|query|string|false|Opaque cursor returned by the previous page.|
|filter[label]|query|string|false|Returns only threads carrying this label. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Thread labels are independent of the labels on the thread's messages.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "data": [
    {

      "inbox_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",

## Get an account-wide thread and a page of its messages

<a id="opIdGetEmailThread"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_threads/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08?inbox_id=497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_threads/{thread_id}`

Returns a thread and a bounded page of its inbound and outbound messages,
interleaved in chronological order. The `inbox_id` returned by the list
endpoint is required because a thread ID can occur in multiple inboxes.
Only messages matching that `(inbox_id, thread_id)` pair are returned. Threads outside the account
return an opaque 404.


<h3 id="get-an-account-wide-thread-and-a-page-of-its-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|thread_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Email thread UUID.|
|inbox_id|query|string(uuid)|true|Inbox UUID that, together with `thread_id`, identifies the thread.|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Number of thread messages to return. Defaults to 25; maximum is 100.|
|page[after]|query|string|false|Opaque message cursor returned by the previous thread-detail page.|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-email-unsubscribe-groups">Email Unsubscribe Groups</h1>

Named groups and group-scoped suppressions.

## List unsubscribe groups

<a id="opIdlistUnsubscribeGroups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_unsubscribe_groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email_unsubscribe_groups`

Offset pagination only (`page[number]` default 1, `page[size]`
default 25, max 100). No `sort`/`filter`/cursor — ordering fixed
`desc created_at, desc id`. Uses the shared `QueryParser.parse_offset/1`
— a malformed `page` (e.g. flat `?page=1` instead of
`?page[number]=1`) returns `400` (code `10015`), consistent with
`GET /v2/email_blocks`. `meta` includes `total_pages`.


<h3 id="list-unsubscribe-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|Offset page number (≥1, default 1).|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Page size (1–100, default 25).|

{

    {
      "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",

      "description": "string",

      "detail": "Not Acceptable"
    }

}

The explicit `500.json` clause still emits<br>`code: "500"` for genuine 500s.<br>|[ErrorList](#schemaerrorlist)|

## Delete an unsubscribe group

<a id="opIddeleteUnsubscribeGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_unsubscribe_groups/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /email_unsubscribe_groups/{id}`

If the group has 0 active suppressions, hard-deletes the row. With
`force=true`, soft-deletes all active suppressions first (status →
`removed`, `group_id` cleared, `removed` audit event per block) in a
single transaction, then hard-deletes the group. Without `force`
and active suppressions present → `409`. Audit trail is preserved.
`force` only accepts the string `"true"` or boolean `true`; all other
values are false.


<h3 id="delete-an-unsubscribe-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|force|query|string \| boolean|false|Force-delete a group with active suppressions. Only `"true"` (string) or `true` (bool) are truthy; all other values are false.|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Resource UUID. Malformed UUIDs are treated as not-found (not 400).|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "Unauthorized",
      "detail": "Missing authentication"
    }
  ]
}
```

    {

      "detail": "The requested email block was not found"

  ]
}
```

> 406 Response

`GET /email_unsubscribe_groups/{id}/suppressions`

Account + group scoped. Offset pagination only (`page[number]`

## Remove a group suppression

<a id="opIdremoveGroupSuppression"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_unsubscribe_groups/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/suppressions/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /email_unsubscribe_groups/{id}/suppressions/{email}`

Soft-deletes all active blocks for (account, group, normalized
email) — one `removed` audit event per block (`actor: manual`).
The `email` path segment is normalized (trim + lower-case) before
matching. Idempotent on already-removed rows (returns `404` since
they're no longer `active`).

Two distinct `404` cases: a missing/cross-account **group** returns
`10001 "The requested unsubscribe group was not found"`; a group that
exists but has **no active suppression** for that email returns
`10001 "The requested group suppression was not found"`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Resource UUID. Malformed UUIDs are treated as not-found (not 400).|

## Validate a single email address

<a id="opIdCreateEmailValidation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email_validations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /email_validations`

Validates a single email address and returns deliverability checks.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-single-email-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateEmailValidationRequest](#schemacreateemailvalidationrequest)|true|none|
|» email|body|string|true|Email address to validate. Any non-empty string is accepted; invalid syntax returns valid=false rather than a request error.|

{

## Send an email-ownership verification code

<a id="opIdrequestDirEmailVerification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011/verify_email \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /dir/{dir_id}/verify_email`

Email a 6-digit code to the DIR's authorizer email to confirm ownership of that address. The code goes to the authorizer, not to the caller. If the authorizer is someone else (for example a client's executive), that person has to share the code with whoever is completing setup.

How long the code lasts: 15 minutes by default. 8 hours when the DIR has a call center (BPO) linked through `bpo_authorizations` whose authorization is pending review or approved (a rejected authorization does not count). Link the call center before you send the code: a code sent before the link keeps the 15-minute window, and a code sent after the link lasts 8 hours. The email states the window, and `expires_at` in the response always shows the exact expiry.

To resend, call this endpoint again. Each send issues a fresh code and invalidates the previous one. Sends are limited to one every 60 seconds and 10 per DIR per UTC day. A throttled send returns `429` with `retry_after_secs` and `sends_remaining_today` in the error `meta`.

Submit the code to `POST /dir/{dir_id}/verify_email/confirm`.

<h3 id="send-an-email-ownership-verification-code-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "email_verification",
    "email_verified": false,
    "status": "sent",
    "expires_at": "2026-07-30T17:15:00Z",
    "sends_remaining_today": 9
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

## Send an email-ownership verification code to an enterprise

<a id="opIdrequestEnterpriseEmailVerification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/enterprises/4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6/verify_email \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /enterprises/{enterprise_id}/verify_email`

Email a 6-digit code to the enterprise account's contact email to confirm ownership of that address.

A BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) account has no DIR, so it proves ownership of its own contact email here rather than through a DIR. A BPO account cannot be approved for use until this contact email is verified.

The code expires in 15 minutes. Requesting a new code invalidates any previous one. Resends are rate limited (a short cooldown plus a daily cap). Submit the code to `POST /enterprises/{enterprise_id}/verify_email/confirm`.

## Embed documents

<a id="opIdPostEmbedding"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/embeddings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bucket_name": "Bucket Name",
    "document_chunk_size": 1024,
    "document_chunk_overlap_size": 512,
    "embedding_model": "intfloat/multilingual-e5-large",
    "loader": "default"
  }'
```

`POST /ai/embeddings`

Perform embedding on a Telnyx Storage Bucket using the a embedding model.
The current supported file types are:
- PDF
- HTML
- txt/unstructured text files
- json
- csv
- audio / video (mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, wav, or webm ) - Max of 100mb file size.

Any files not matching the above types will be attempted to be embedded as unstructured text.

This process can be slow, so it runs in the background and the user can check
the status of the task using the endpoint `/ai/embeddings/{task_id}`.

 **Important Note**: When you update documents in a Telnyx Storage bucket, their associated embeddings are automatically kept up to date. If you add or update a file, it is automatically embedded. If you delete a file, the embeddings are deleted for that particular file.

You can also specify a custom `loader` param. Currently the only supported loader value is
`intercom` which loads Intercom article jsons as specified by [the Intercom article API](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/Articles/article/)
This loader will split each article into paragraphs and save additional parameters relevant to Intercom docs, such as
`article_url` and `heading`. These values will be returned by the `/v2/ai/embeddings/similarity-search` endpoint in the `loader_metadata` field.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bucket_name": "Bucket Name",
  "document_chunk_size": 1024,
  "document_chunk_overlap_size": 512,
  "embedding_model": "intfloat/multilingual-e5-large",
  "loader": "default"
}
```

<h3 id="embed-documents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[EmbeddingBucketRequest](#schemaembeddingbucketrequest)|true|none|
|» bucket_name|body|string|true|none|
|» document_chunk_size|body|integer|false|none|
|» document_chunk_overlap_size|body|integer|false|none|
|» embedding_model|body|object|false|none|
|» loader|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "task_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
    "task_name": "Task Name",
    "status": "Status",
    "created_at": "Created At",
    "user_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10036",
      "detail": "A request with this Idempotency-Key is already being processed.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/header/Idempotency-Key"
      },
      "title": "Resource is being processed"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }

}
```

<h3 id="embed-documents-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[EmbeddingResponse](#schemaembeddingresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request / Validation Failed (10015). Invalid, duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong Idempotency-Key headers are rejected by Edge with HTTP 400 and error code 10015.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (10036). Retry later with the same key and request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|

Requests sent without the header are not subject to this limit.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|

## Search for documents

<a id="opIdPostEmbeddingSimilaritySearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/embeddings/similarity-search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bucket_name": "Bucket Name",
    "query": "Query",
    "num_of_docs": 3
  }'
```

`POST /ai/embeddings/similarity-search`

Perform a similarity search on a Telnyx Storage Bucket, returning the most similar `num_docs` document chunks to the query.

Currently the only available distance metric is cosine similarity which will return a `distance` between 0 and 1.
The lower the distance, the more similar the returned document chunks are to the query.
A `certainty` will also be returned, which is a value between 0 and 1 where the higher the certainty, the more similar the document.
You can read more about Weaviate distance metrics here: [Weaviate Docs](https://weaviate.io/developers/weaviate/config-refs/distances)

If a bucket was embedded using a custom loader, such as `intercom`, the additional metadata will be returned in the 
`loader_metadata` field.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bucket_name": "Bucket Name",
  "query": "Query",
  "num_of_docs": 3
}
```

<h3 id="search-for-documents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[EmbeddingSimilaritySearchRequest](#schemaembeddingsimilaritysearchrequest)|true|none|
|» bucket_name|body|string|true|none|
|» query|body|string|true|none|
|» num_of_docs|body|integer|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "document_chunk": "Document Chunk",
      "distance": 0,
      "metadata": {
        "source": "Source",
        "checksum": "Checksum",
        "embedding": "Embedding",
        "filename": "Filename",
        "certainty": 0
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Embed URL content

<a id="opIdPostEmbeddingUrl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/embeddings/url \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "URL",
    "bucket_name": "Bucket Name"
  }'
```

`POST /ai/embeddings/url`

Embed website content from a specified URL, including child pages up to 5 levels deep within the same domain. The process crawls and loads content from the main URL and its linked pages into a Telnyx Cloud Storage bucket. As soon as each webpage is added to the bucket, its content is immediately processed for embeddings, that can be used for [similarity search](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/embeddings/search-for-documents) and [clustering](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/clusters).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "URL",
  "bucket_name": "Bucket Name"
}
```

<h3 id="embed-url-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[EmbeddingUrlRequest](#schemaembeddingurlrequest)|true|none|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL of the webpage to embed|
|» bucket_name|body|string|true|Name of the bucket to store the embeddings. This bucket must already exist.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Get an embedding task's status

<a id="opIdGetEmbeddingTask"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/embeddings/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ai/embeddings/{task_id}`

Check the status of a current embedding task. Will be one of the following:
- `queued` - Task is waiting to be picked up by a worker
- `processing` - The embedding task is running
- `success` - Task completed successfully and the bucket is embedded
- `failure` - Task failed and no files were embedded successfully
- `partial_success` - Some files were embedded successfully, but at least one failed

`POST /enterprises`

Create the legal entity (enterprise) that represents your business on the Telnyx platform.

The response carries a server-assigned `id` you use for every subsequent call. An enterprise is created once and reused; the API collects all required fields up front.

Common failure modes:
- `422` - a required field is missing or malformed (the response `errors[].source.pointer` names the field).
- `409` - an enterprise with the same identifying details already exists under your account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "legal_name": "Run 065 Debug Co",
  "organization_type": "commercial",
  "country_code": "US",
  "role_type": "enterprise",
  "website": "https://run065.example.com",
  "fein": "12-3456789",
  "industry": "technology",
  "number_of_employees": "51-200",
  "organization_legal_type": "llc",
  "doing_business_as": "Run 065 Debug",
  "jurisdiction_of_incorporation": "Delaware",
  "organization_contact": {
    "first_name": "Sam",
    "last_name": "Org",
    "email": "org@run065.example.com",
    "job_title": "Compliance Lead",
    "phone_number": "+13125550000"
  },
  "billing_contact": {
    "first_name": "Alex",
    "last_name": "Bill",
    "email": "billing@run065.example.com",
    "phone_number": "+13125550001"
  },
  "organization_physical_address": {
    "country": "US",
    "administrative_area": "IL",
    "city": "Chicago",
    "postal_code": "60601",
    "street_address": "100 Main St"
  },
  "billing_address": {
    "country": "US",
    "administrative_area": "IL",
    "city": "Chicago",
    "postal_code": "60601",
    "street_address": "100 Main St"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[EnterpriseCreate](#schemaenterprisecreate)|true|none|
|» legal_name|body|string|true|Your business's full registered legal name, exactly as it appears on your incorporation or tax documents, 3 to 64 characters.|
|» organization_type|body|string|true|Organization category for vetting purposes:<br>- `commercial` - for-profit business entities (LLC, corp, partnership, sole proprietorship). Most callers fall here.<br>- `government` - federal/state/local government bodies.<br>- `non_profit` - registered 501(c)(3)/equivalent (incl. educational institutions, charities, religious organisations).|
|» country_code|body|string|true|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Currently `US` and `CA` are supported.|
|» role_type|body|string|false|`enterprise` for an organization registering its own DIRs (the default, and the right choice when the calls display your own brand). `bpo` for a Business Process Outsourcer: a call center that places calls on behalf of other enterprises and displays their brand. A `bpo` enterprise describes the call center itself and cannot own a DIR. Each client the call center calls for gets its own `enterprise` in the same account, with the client's DIR under it; that DIR is then linked to the `bpo` enterprise through `bpo_authorizations`. Fixed at creation.|
|» website|body|string(uri)|true|Your business's public website address, including https://. Leave blank if your business has no website.|
|» fein|body|string|true|US Federal Employer Identification Number (`NN-NNNNNNN`) or Canadian equivalent.|

## Replace an enterprise

<a id="opIdupdateEnterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/enterprises/4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "legal_name": "Acme Plumbing LLC",

    "organization_legal_type": "llc",

`PUT /enterprises/{enterprise_id}`

Replace the enterprise's mutable fields. Only mutable fields may be sent. Server-assigned and immutable fields (`id`, `record_type`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, status fields, `organization_type`, `country_code`, `role_type`) cannot be changed: including any of them in the body is rejected with `400 Bad Request` (`Field 'X' is not allowed in this request`).

For an approved BPO enterprise (`role_type` `bpo`), changing any identity field (legal name, DBA, website, FEIN, industry, number of employees, physical address, organization contact, D-U-N-S number, legal type, SIC code, corporate registration number, professional license number, or jurisdiction of incorporation) resets `bpo_verification_status` to `pending` for re-approval and sets every DIR authorization for that BPO to `rejected`. After re-approval, link it again with a newly signed LOA (a new `loa_document_id`); resending the old one keeps the authorization `rejected`. Re-sending an unchanged value does not reset anything.

If Number Reputation is enabled on the enterprise, `legal_name`, `doing_business_as`, `website`, `fein`, `industry`, `number_of_employees`, `organization_physical_address`, `organization_contact`, and `dun_bradstreet_number` cannot be changed: the request is rejected with `400`.
