## Delete an enterprise

<a id="opIddeleteEnterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/enterprises/4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /enterprises/{enterprise_id}`

Soft-delete an enterprise.

Failure modes:
- `400` - the enterprise still has dependent resources in a non-deletable state. Remove those first; the response `detail` identifies what is blocking the delete.
- `409` - the enterprise has a dependent resource with an unresolved claim. Resolve it before deleting.
- `404` - the enterprise does not exist or does not belong to your account.

## Activate Branded Calling on an enterprise

<a id="opIdactivateBrandedCalling"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/enterprises/4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6/branded_calling \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /enterprises/{enterprise_id}/branded_calling`

Branded Calling must be activated on each enterprise. Activation is idempotent:
- First call: marks the enterprise as activated, effective immediately; you can create a DIR right away. The enterprise is registered with the Branded Calling platform later, after its first DIR is approved. Returns `200` with `branded_calling_enabled: true`.
- Re-call after success: no-op, returns the same enterprise body.
- Re-call after a failed registration: re-queues the registration, returns `200`.

Prerequisite: the calling user must have agreed to the Branded Calling Terms of Service (`POST /terms_of_service/branded_calling/agree`). Without that, this endpoint returns `403 terms_of_service_not_accepted`.

Failure modes:
- `400` - the account has no available credit. Add funds and retry.
- `400` - the enterprise is not in the United States. Branded Calling is currently available only to US enterprises.
- `403` - Branded Calling Terms of Service not accepted.
- `404` - enterprise does not exist or does not belong to your account.

**Pricing:** Activation itself is free, but the account must have available credit. Branded Calling fees are charged per DIR and per branded call. See https://telnyx.com/pricing/branded-calling for current pricing.

<h3 id="activate-branded-calling-on-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The enterprise id. Lowercase UUID.|

## Creates an External Connection

<a id="opIdCreateExternalConnection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/external_connections \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "external_sip_connection": "zoom",
    "active": false,
    "outbound": {
      "outbound_voice_profile_id": "1911630617284445511"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /external_connections`

Creates a new External Connection based on the parameters sent in the request. The external_sip_connection and outbound voice profile id are required. Once created, you can assign phone numbers to your application using the `/phone_numbers` endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "external_sip_connection": "zoom",
  "active": false,
  "outbound": {
    "outbound_voice_profile_id": "1911630617284445511"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="creates-an-external-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateExternalConnectionRequest](#schemacreateexternalconnectionrequest)|true|Parameters that can be set when creating a External Connection|
|» active|body|[ConnectionActive](#schemaconnectionactive)|false|Specifies whether the connection can be used.|
|» external_sip_connection|body|[ExternalSipConnectionZoomOnly](#schemaexternalsipconnectionzoomonly)|true|The service that will be consuming this connection.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the connection.|
|» webhook_event_url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_event_failover_url|body|string \| null(uri)|false|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_timeout_secs|body|integer \| null|false|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|» inbound|body|object|false|none|
|» » outbound_voice_profile_id|body|string|true|The ID of the outbound voice profile to use for inbound calls.|
|» » channel_limit|body|integer|false|When set, this will limit the number of concurrent inbound calls to phone numbers associated with this connection.|
|» outbound|body|object|true|none|
|» » channel_limit|body|integer|false|When set, this will limit the number of concurrent outbound calls to phone numbers associated with this connection.|
|» » outbound_voice_profile_id|body|[external-voice-integrations_OutboundVoiceProfileId](#schemaexternal-voice-integrations_outboundvoiceprofileid)|false|Identifies the associated outbound voice profile.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» external_sip_connection|zoom|

## Creates an Upload request

<a id="opIdCreateExternalConnectionUpload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/external_connections/1293384261075731499/uploads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "number_ids": [
      "3920457616934164700",
      "3920457616934164701",
      "3920457616934164702",
      "3920457616934164703"
    ],
    "usage": "first_party_app_assignment",
    "location_id": "67ea7693-9cd5-4a68-8c76-abb3aa5bf5d2"
  }'
```

`POST /external_connections/{id}/uploads`

Creates a new Upload request to Microsoft teams with the included phone numbers. Only one of civic_address_id or location_id must be provided, not both. The maximum allowed phone numbers for the numbers_ids array is 1000.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "number_ids": [
    "3920457616934164700",
```

## Retry an Upload request

<a id="opIdRetryUpload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/external_connections/1293384261075731499/uploads/7b6a6449-b055-45a6-81f6-f6f0dffa4cc6/retry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /external_connections/{id}/uploads/{ticket_id}/retry`

If there were any errors during the upload process, this endpoint will retry the upload request. In some cases this will reattempt the existing upload request, in other cases it may create a new upload request. Please check the ticket_id in the response to determine if a new upload request was created.

## Refresh Operator Connect integration

<a id="opIdOperatorConnectRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /operator_connect/actions/refresh`

This endpoint will make an asynchronous request to refresh the Operator Connect integration with Microsoft Teams for the current user. This will create new external connections on the user's account if needed, and/or report the integration results as [log messages](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/external-connections/list-all-log-messages#list-all-log-messages).

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
  },
```

<h3 id="create-an-fqdn-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateFqdnConnectionRequest](#schemacreatefqdnconnectionrequest)|true|Parameters that can be defined during FQDN connection creation|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Defaults to true|
|» anchorsite_override|body|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|» connection_name|body|[ConnectionName](#schemaconnectionname)|true|A user-assigned name to help manage the connection.|
|» transport_protocol|body|[FqdnConnectionTransportProtocol](#schemafqdnconnectiontransportprotocol)|false|One of UDP, TLS, or TCP. Applies only to connections with IP authentication or FQDN authentication.|
|» default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|body|boolean|false|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|» bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|body|boolean|false|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; defaults to false when omitted on creation. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|» dtmf_type|body|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|» encode_contact_header_enabled|body|boolean|false|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|» encrypted_media|body|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|» microsoft_teams_sbc|body|boolean|false|When enabled, the connection will be created for Microsoft Teams Direct Routing. A *.mstsbc.telnyx.tech FQDN will be created for the connection automatically.|
|» onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the connection.|
|» ios_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|» android_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|» webhook_event_url|body|[WebhookEventUrl](#schemawebhookeventurl)|false|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_event_failover_url|body|[WebhookEventFailoverUrl](#schemawebhookeventfailoverurl)|false|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_api_version|body|[WebhookApiVersion](#schemawebhookapiversion)|false|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|» call_cost_in_webhooks|body|boolean|false|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|» webhook_timeout_secs|body|[WebhookTimeoutSecs](#schemawebhooktimeoutsecs)|false|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|» rtcp_settings|body|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|
|» inbound|body|[InboundFqdn](#schemainboundfqdn)|false|none|
|» outbound|body|[OutboundFqdn](#schemaoutboundfqdn)|false|none|
|» noise_suppression|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|» noise_suppression_details|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|» jitter_buffer|body|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

<h3 id="update-an-fqdn-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Identifies the resource.|
|body|body|[UpdateFqdnConnectionRequest](#schemaupdatefqdnconnectionrequest)|true|Parameters that can be updated in a FQDN connection|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Defaults to true|
|» conversation_persistence|body|boolean|false|Whether conversation persistence is enabled for this connection. When enabled, calls handled by the connection are transcribed, stored, and indexed. Defaults to false.|
|» anchorsite_override|body|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|» connection_name|body|[ConnectionName](#schemaconnectionname)|false|A user-assigned name to help manage the connection.|
|» transport_protocol|body|[FqdnConnectionTransportProtocol](#schemafqdnconnectiontransportprotocol)|false|One of UDP, TLS, or TCP. Applies only to connections with IP authentication or FQDN authentication.|
|» default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|body|boolean|false|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|» bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|body|boolean|false|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; omitting this field preserves the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|» dtmf_type|body|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|» encode_contact_header_enabled|body|boolean|false|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|» encrypted_media|body|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|» onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer that the sender and receiver negotiate T38 directly when both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call according to each leg's settings.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the connection.|
|» ios_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|» android_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|» webhook_event_url|body|[WebhookEventUrl](#schemawebhookeventurl)|false|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_event_failover_url|body|[WebhookEventFailoverUrl](#schemawebhookeventfailoverurl)|false|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_api_version|body|[WebhookApiVersion](#schemawebhookapiversion)|false|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|» call_cost_in_webhooks|body|boolean|false|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|» webhook_timeout_secs|body|[WebhookTimeoutSecs](#schemawebhooktimeoutsecs)|false|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|» rtcp_settings|body|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|
|» inbound|body|[InboundFqdn](#schemainboundfqdn)|false|none|
|» outbound|body|[OutboundFqdn](#schemaoutboundfqdn)|false|none|
|» noise_suppression|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|» noise_suppression_details|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|» jitter_buffer|body|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

`POST /ai/fine_tuning/jobs`

```json

  "model": "string",
  "training_file": "string",

  }
}
```

|» model|body|string|true|The base model that is being fine-tuned.|

|» suffix|body|string|false|Optional suffix to append to the fine tuned model's name.|
|» hyperparameters|body|object|false|The hyperparameters used for the fine-tuning job.|
|» » n_epochs|body|integer|false|The number of epochs to train the model for. An epoch refers to one full cycle through the training dataset. ## Create a Global IP assignment

<a id="opIdCreateGlobalIpAssignment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/global_ip_assignments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "global_ip_id": "a836125b-20b6-452e-9c03-2653f09c7ed7",
    "wireguard_peer_id": "e66c496d-4a85-423b-8b2a-8e63fac20320",
    "is_in_maintenance": true
  }'
```

`POST /global_ip_assignments`

Assigns a Global IP to a WireGuard peer so traffic destined for the IP is delivered over that peer's tunnel. Assignment is asynchronous, so the request is accepted and completes in the background.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "global_ip_id": "a836125b-20b6-452e-9c03-2653f09c7ed7",
  "wireguard_peer_id": "e66c496d-4a85-423b-8b2a-8e63fac20320",
  "is_in_maintenance": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-global-ip-assignment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GlobalIpAssignment](#schemaglobalipassignment)|true|none|
|» global_ip_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Global IP ID.|
|» wireguard_peer_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Wireguard peer ID.|
|» is_in_maintenance|body|boolean|false|Enable/disable BGP announcement.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
    "record_type": "global_ip_assignment",
    "created_at": "2018-02-02T22:25:27.521Z",
    "updated_at": "2018-02-02T22:25:27.521Z",
    "global_ip_id": "a836125b-20b6-452e-9c03-2653f09c7ed7",
    "wireguard_peer_id": "e66c496d-4a85-423b-8b2a-8e63fac20320",
    "status": "provisioned",
    "is_connected": true,
    "is_in_maintenance": true,
    "is_announced": true
  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10027",
      "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
      "detail": "The server understood the syntax of the request but was unable to process the instructions."
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "title": "Invalid street address",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/street_address"
      },
      "code": "20207",
      "description": "The street address provided is invalid."
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-global-ip-assignment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Assignment request accepted. Provisioning is asynchronous; poll GET /global_ip_assignments/{id} with the returned id to check status.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity. Check the 'detail' field in response for details.|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|

<h3 id="create-a-global-ip-assignment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[GlobalIpAssignment](#schemaglobalipassignment)|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Create a Global IP health check

<a id="opIdCreateGlobalIpHealthCheck"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/global_ip_health_checks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "health_check_type": "http_status_2xx",
    "health_check_params": {
      "path": "/",
      "port": 8080
    },
    "global_ip_id": "a836125b-20b6-452e-9c03-2653f09c7ed7"
  }'
```

`POST /global_ip_health_checks`

Creates a health check for a Global IP to monitor the health of its assignments. Creation is asynchronous, so the request is accepted and the health check becomes active once provisioning completes.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "health_check_type": "http_status_2xx",
  "health_check_params": {
    "path": "/",
    "port": 8080
  },
  "global_ip_id": "a836125b-20b6-452e-9c03-2653f09c7ed7"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-global-ip-health-check-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GlobalIPHealthCheck](#schemaglobaliphealthcheck)|true|none|
|» health_check_type|body|string|false|The Global IP health check type.|
|» health_check_params|body|object|false|A Global IP health check params.|
|» global_ip_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Global IP ID.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
    "record_type": "global_ip_health_check",
    "created_at": "2018-02-02T22:25:27.521Z",
    "updated_at": "2018-02-02T22:25:27.521Z",
    "health_check_type": "http_status_2xx",
    "health_check_params": {
      "path": "/",
      "port": 8080
    },
    "global_ip_id": "a836125b-20b6-452e-9c03-2653f09c7ed7"
  }
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10027",

      "detail": "The server understood the syntax of the request but was unable to process the instructions."
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {
      "title": "Invalid street address",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/street_address"
      },
      "code": "20207",
      "description": "The street address provided is invalid."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create a Global IP

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /global_ips`

Requests creation of a new Global IP, a static IP address announced from the Telnyx network. Provisioning is asynchronous, so the request is accepted and the Global IP becomes available once provisioning completes.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ports": {
    "tcp": [
      80,
      8080
    ],
    "udp": [
      5000,
      5050
    ]
  },
  "name": "test interface",
  "description": "test interface"
}
```

|» name|body|string|false|A user specified name for the address.|
|» description|body|string|false|A user specified description for the address.|

<h3 id="create-an-ip-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateIpConnectionRequest](#schemacreateipconnectionrequest)|true|Parameters that can be defined during IP connection creation|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Defaults to true|
|» anchorsite_override|body|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|» connection_name|body|string|false|none|
|» transport_protocol|body|string|false|One of UDP, TLS, or TCP. Applies only to connections with IP authentication or FQDN authentication.|
|» default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|body|boolean|false|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|» bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|body|boolean|false|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; defaults to false when omitted on creation. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|» dtmf_type|body|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|» encode_contact_header_enabled|body|boolean|false|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|» encrypted_media|body|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|» onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|» ios_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|» android_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|» webhook_event_url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_event_failover_url|body|string \| null(uri)|false|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_api_version|body|string|false|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|» webhook_timeout_secs|body|integer \| null|false|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|» call_cost_in_webhooks|body|boolean|false|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the connection.|
|» rtcp_settings|body|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|
|» inbound|body|[CreateInboundIpRequest](#schemacreateinboundiprequest)|false|none|
|» outbound|body|[OutboundIp](#schemaoutboundip)|false|none|
|» noise_suppression|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|» noise_suppression_details|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|» jitter_buffer|body|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

<h3 id="update-an-ip-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Identifies the type of resource.|
|body|body|[UpdateIpConnectionRequest](#schemaupdateipconnectionrequest)|true|Parameters that can be updated in a IP connection|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Defaults to true|
|» conversation_persistence|body|boolean|false|Whether conversation persistence is enabled for this connection. When enabled, calls handled by the connection are transcribed, stored, and indexed. Defaults to false.|
|» anchorsite_override|body|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|» connection_name|body|string|false|none|
|» transport_protocol|body|string|false|One of UDP, TLS, or TCP. Applies only to connections with IP authentication or FQDN authentication.|
|» default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|body|boolean|false|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|» bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|body|boolean|false|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; omitting this field preserves the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|» dtmf_type|body|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|» encode_contact_header_enabled|body|boolean|false|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|» encrypted_media|body|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|» onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|» ios_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|» android_push_credential_id|body|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|» webhook_event_url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_event_failover_url|body|string \| null(uri)|false|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|» webhook_api_version|body|string|false|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|» webhook_timeout_secs|body|integer \| null|false|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|» call_cost_in_webhooks|body|boolean|false|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the connection.|
|» rtcp_settings|body|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|
|» inbound|body|[InboundIp](#schemainboundip)|false|none|
|» outbound|body|[OutboundIp](#schemaoutboundip)|false|none|
|» noise_suppression|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|» noise_suppression_details|body|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|» jitter_buffer|body|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-ip-pools">IP Pools</h1>

Group dedicated IPs into pools for sending.

## List IP pools

<a id="opIdlistIpPools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/ip_pools \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /email/ip_pools`

List the account's dedicated-IP pools. Member IPs are not included (`ips` is empty); retrieve a pool to see its members.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "9b1c4d70-abcd-4e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b",
      "record_type": "ip_pool",
      "name": "primary-pool",
      "is_default": true,
      "domain_id": null,
      "ips": [],
      "created_at": "2026-09-30T02:03:09.474123Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-30T02:03:09.474123Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "Unauthorized",
      "detail": "The API key provided is invalid or unauthorized"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-ip-pools-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|IP pool list|[IpPoolListResponse](#schemaippoollistresponse)|

bearerAuth
</aside>

## Create an IP pool

<a id="opIdcreateIpPool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/ip_pools \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "primary-pool",
    "is_default": true
  }'
```

`POST /email/ip_pools`

Create an account-scoped pool of dedicated IPs. Set `is_default` or `domain_id` for the pool to carry mail; a pool with neither carries none.

> Body parameter

```json
{
```

## Delete an IP pool

<a id="opIddeleteIpPool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/ip_pools/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /email/ip_pools/{id}`

Delete the pool. Member IPs are kept but leave the pool, so they carry no mail until added to another pool. Deleting a pool changes routing for subsequently resolved messages. It does not reroute messages already assigned to the deleted pool. Deleting a pool that still has IPs requires `force=true` and `drain=true`.

<h3 id="delete-an-ip-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The IP pool identifier (UUID).|
|force|query|boolean|false|Set together with `drain=true` to delete a pool that still has IPs. Either flag alone has no effect.|
|drain|query|boolean|false|Set together with `force=true` to delete a pool that still has IPs. Acknowledges deletion while the pool still has members; this flag does not reroute already queued messages.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "string",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string",
        "parameter": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10001",
      "title": "Not Found",
      "detail": "The requested ip pool was not found"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "40901",
      "title": "Conflict",
      "detail": "pool still has 2 member IP(s) — remove them first or pass force: true with drain: true"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "string",

      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string",
        "parameter": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[ErrorEnvelope](#schemaerrorenvelope)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[ErrorEnvelope](#schemaerrorenvelope)|
|409|Conflict|The pool still has IPs and `force`/`drain` were not both set.|[ErrorEnvelope](#schemaerrorenvelope)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed.|[ErrorEnvelope](#schemaerrorenvelope)|

`POST /email/ip_pools/{id}/ips`

|» dedicated_ip_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The dedicated IP to add. It must belong to the account, must not be released, and must not already be in a pool.|

## Remove a dedicated IP from a pool

<a id="opIdremoveIpFromPool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/email/ip_pools/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/ips/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /email/ip_pools/{id}/ips/{ip_id}`

Remove the dedicated IP from the pool. The IP is kept but carries no mail until added to a pool again. Removing the last IP requires `force=true` and `drain=true`.

<h3 id="remove-a-dedicated-ip-from-a-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The IP pool identifier (UUID).|
|ip_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The dedicated IP identifier (UUID).|
|force|query|boolean|false|Set together with `drain=true` to remove the last IP in the pool. Either flag alone has no effect.|
|drain|query|boolean|false|Set together with `force=true` to remove the last IP in the pool. Acknowledges that mail routed to the emptied pool is held until the pool has a sendable IP again.|

## Create an inexplicit number order

<a id="opIdCreateInexplicitNumberOrder"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/inexplicit_number_orders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ordering_groups": [
      {
        "country_iso": "US",
        "count_requested": "5",
        "phone_number_type": "local",
        "administrative_area": "CA",
        "features": [
          "voice"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /inexplicit_number_orders`

Create an inexplicit number order to programmatically purchase phone numbers without specifying exact numbers.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ordering_groups": [
    {
      "country_iso": "US",
      "count_requested": "5",
      "phone_number_type": "local",
      "administrative_area": "CA",
      "features": [
        "voice"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-inexplicit-number-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InexplicitNumberOrderRequest](#schemainexplicitnumberorderrequest)|true|none|
|» ordering_groups|body|[object]|true|Group(s) of numbers to order. You can have multiple ordering_groups objects added to a single request.|
|» » country_iso|body|string|true|Country where you would like to purchase phone numbers. Allowable values: US, CA|
|» » count_requested|body|string|true|Quantity of phone numbers to order|
|» » phone_number_type|body|string|true|Number type (local, toll-free, etc.)|
|» » national_destination_code|body|string|false|Filter by area code|
|» » phone_number|body|object|false|Phone number search criteria|
|» » » starts_with|body|string|false|Filter by the starting digits of the phone number|
|» » » ends_with|body|string|false|Filter by the ending digits of the phone number|
|» » » contains|body|string|false|Filter for phone numbers that contain the digits specified|
|» » administrative_area|body|string|false|Filter for phone numbers in a given state / province|
|» » locality|body|string|false|Filter for phone numbers in a given city / region / rate center|
|» » features|body|[string]|false|Filter for phone numbers that have the features to satisfy your use case (e.g., ["voice"])|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|Ordering strategy. Define what action should be taken if we don't have enough phone numbers to fulfill your request. Allowable values are: always = proceed with ordering phone numbers, regardless of current inventory levels; never = do not place any orders unless there are enough phone numbers to satisfy the request. If not specified, the always strategy will be enforced.|
|» » quickship|body|boolean|false|Filter to exclude phone numbers that need additional time after to purchase to activate. Only applicable for +1 toll_free numbers.|
|» » exclude_held_numbers|body|boolean|false|Filter to exclude phone numbers that are currently on hold/reserved for your account.|
|» connection_id|body|string|false|Connection id to apply to phone numbers that are purchased|
|» messaging_profile_id|body|string|false|Messaging profile id to apply to phone numbers that are purchased|
|» customer_reference|body|string|false|Reference label for the customer|
|» billing_group_id|body|string|false|Billing group id to apply to phone numbers that are purchased|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » country_iso|US|
|» » country_iso|CA|
|» » strategy|always|
|» » strategy|never|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-infringement-claims">Infringement Claims</h1>

Trademark or impersonation claims filed against your DIR. Customers may contest a claim with supporting evidence.

## List infringement claims for a DIR

<a id="opIdlistInfringementClaimsForDir"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011/infringement_claims \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /dir/{dir_id}/infringement_claims`

Return the trademark or copyright claims filed against this DIR. Each claim's `status` is `pending` (newly filed; DIR auto-suspended), `contested` (you have submitted contest evidence; awaiting resolution), or `resolved` (final). Resolution outcomes: `upheld` (claim accepted; DIR stays suspended/permanently_rejected), `rejected` (claim dismissed; DIR restored to `verified`), `modified` (partial outcome).

<h3 id="list-infringement-claims-for-a-dir-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Out-of-range values return an empty page with correct meta.|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|Items per page. Maximum 250; values above are clamped to 250.|

## Update a DIR to resolve an infringement concern

<a id="opIdupdateDirInfringement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/dir/16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011/infringement_update \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "certify_no_infringement": true,
    "certify_brand_is_accurate": true,
    "certify_no_shaft_content": true,
    "certify_ip_ownership": true,
    "infringement_resolution_notes": "Updated the display name to remove the disputed mark and re-uploaded the authorization."
  }'
```

`PUT /dir/{dir_id}/infringement_update`

Push a fix for a DIR that is `suspended` with an open infringement claim back into vetting. `POST /dir/{dir_id}/submit` is blocked while a claim is open, so this is the customer-callable path to update the DIR's content and re-certify before Telnyx adjudicates the claim. All four certification booleans must be `true`. Optional content fields (`display_name`, `logo_url`, `call_reasons`, `documents`) update the DIR; documents are append-only.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "certify_no_infringement": true,
  "certify_brand_is_accurate": true,
  "certify_no_shaft_content": true,
  "certify_ip_ownership": true,
  "infringement_resolution_notes": "Updated the display name to remove the disputed mark and re-uploaded the authorization."
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-dir-to-resolve-an-infringement-concern-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dir_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The DIR id. Lowercase UUID.|
|body|body|[DirInfringementUpdateRequest](#schemadirinfringementupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» certify_no_infringement|body|boolean|true|Check to certify that the brand no longer infringes anyone else's trademark or intellectual property.|
|» certify_brand_is_accurate|body|boolean|true|Must be `true`.|
|» certify_no_shaft_content|body|boolean|true|Must be `true`.|
|» certify_ip_ownership|body|boolean|true|Must be `true`.|
|» infringement_resolution_notes|body|string|true|Explanation of how the infringement concern was addressed.|
|» display_name|body|string \| null|false|The business name shown to call recipients, 1 to 35 characters, no emoji, not blank.|
|» logo_url|body|string \| null|false|Publicly accessible HTTPS URL (max 128 chars) to a 256x256 BMP logo (max 1 MB).|
|» call_reasons|body|[string]|false|none|
|» documents|body|[[Document](#schemadocument)]|false|Append-only supporting documents to attach while resolving the claim (e.g. authorization or licensing proof).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» certify_no_infringement|true|
|» certify_brand_is_accurate|true|
|» certify_no_shaft_content|true|
|» certify_ip_ownership|true|

## Contest an infringement claim

<a id="opIdcontestInfringementClaim"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/infringement_claims/e379fbc8-cd83-4bef-a280-a0ac9d00dcf8/contest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "contest_notes": "We own the trademark outright; our registration precedes the claimant by three years. See attached certificate.",
    "documents": [
      {
        "document_id": "2a7e8337-e803-4057-a4ae-26c40eb0bc6c",
        "document_type": "trademark_registration",
        "description": "USPTO trademark certificate."
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /infringement_claims/{claim_id}/contest`

Submit a written response and supporting documents disputing the claim. The first call moves the claim from `pending` to `contested`; subsequent calls append supplementary evidence without changing status. The `documents[]` you attach are aggregated across rounds in the claim's `contest_documents` field.

Only `pending` and `contested` claims accept new evidence. A `resolved` claim returns `400`.

Failure modes:
- `400` - the claim is `resolved` (terminal); cannot be contested further.
- `404` - the claim does not exist or is not against a DIR you own.
- `422` - `contest_notes` is too short (< 10 chars), too long (> 2000 chars), `documents` is > 20 entries, or a `document_id` is duplicated within the same submission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "contest_notes": "We own the trademark outright; our registration precedes the claimant by three years. See attached certificate.",
  "documents": [
    {
      "document_id": "2a7e8337-e803-4057-a4ae-26c40eb0bc6c",
      "document_type": "trademark_registration",
      "description": "USPTO trademark certificate."
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="contest-an-infringement-claim-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|claim_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier of the claim.|
|body|body|[InfringementClaimContest](#schemainfringementclaimcontest)|true|none|
|» contest_notes|body|string|true|Customer's response to the claim. 10–2000 characters.|
|» documents|body|[[Document](#schemadocument)]|false|Up to 20 supporting documents per submission. `document_id` must be unique within this submission. Documents are aggregated into the claim's `contest_documents` across all submissions.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "e379fbc8-cd83-4bef-a280-a0ac9d00dcf8",
    "dir_id": "42a3f554-7ce3-44c2-bfe9-6e1afe0d7991",
    "enterprise_id": "7eca8226-8081-4e11-abdc-437b5f53a81f",
    "claim_type": "trademark",
    "claim_description": "Alleged infringement on trademark XYZ.",
    "claimant_name": "Test Claimant LLC",
    "claimant_contact": "legal@testclaimant.example.com",
    "claim_date": "2026-04-22T02:12:54Z",
    "status": "pending",
    "resolution": "upheld",
    "resolution_date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "resolution_notes": "string",
    "contest_documents": [
      {
        "document_id": "2a7e8337-e803-4057-a4ae-26c40eb0bc6c",
        "document_type": "business_registration",
        "description": "Certificate of incorporation."
      }
    ],

      {
        "notes": "We own the trademark outright; our registration precedes the claimant by three years.",
        "submitted_at": "2026-04-22T02:13:06.629473Z",
        "document_count": 1
      }
    ],
    "dir": {

      "display_name": "Acme Plumbing",
      "enterprise_id": "7eca8226-8081-4e11-abdc-437b5f53a81f",

    },
```

## Create a secret

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /integration_secrets`

Create a new secret with an associated identifier that can be used to securely integrate with other services.

> Body parameter

```json

  "identifier": "my_secret",
  "type": "bearer",
  "token": "my_secret_value"
```

|» type|body|string|true|The type of secret.|
|» token|body|string|false|The token for the secret. Required for bearer type secrets, ignored otherwise.|
|» username|body|string|false|The username for the secret. Required for basic type secrets, ignored otherwise.|
|» password|body|string|false|The password for the secret. Required for basic type secrets, ignored otherwise.|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-machine-payments">Machine Payments</h1>

Machine payment (MPP) account-credit operations. Fund your Telnyx account programmatically from a machine or agent using the Machine Payment Protocol, an HTTP-402 flow settled via Stripe or Tempo.

## Create a machine payment account credit

<a id="opIdcreateMachinePaymentAccountCredit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/machine-payments/account-credit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "amount_usd": "10.00"
  }'
```

`POST /machine-payments/account-credit`

Creates an account credit using the Machine Payment Protocol (MPP), an HTTP-402 payment flow for machines and agents.

The flow has two steps. First, send an authenticated request with the `amount_usd` to credit; the response is `402 Payment Required` with one or more payment challenges (for example separate Tempo and Stripe challenges) in the `WWW-Authenticate` header. Second, retry the request with an `Authorization: Payment ...` credential constructed from the challenge; on success the response includes the credited transaction and a `Payment-Receipt` header.

The credited account is never chosen by the request body: the initial request credits the account of the authenticated user, and a paid retry credits the account bound to the verified payment credential. The amount must be within the configured bounds (by default between 5.00 and 500.00 USD).

Successful paid retries are idempotent — when Rails reaches its duplicate-transaction lookup for an already-recorded payment, it returns the existing transaction with `created: false` instead of crediting the account again. This deduplication applies to successful fulfillment: re-sending the same Stripe credential may instead be rejected by the upstream provider as an idempotent replay and return `402 Payment Required` rather than the existing transaction.

> **Warning: the payment credential is bound to a specific Telnyx account ID.** A payment is captured before the bound account is validated. If the credential names an account that is missing, suspended, blocked, cancelled, dormant, or ineligible for the tier, the payment is captured but **no account is credited**. If the credential names a different but eligible account, that account is credited — the service does not compare it against the payer's account. There is **no automatic refund**: if the captured payment does not credit the intended account, contact Telnyx support for remediation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount_usd": "10.00"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-machine-payment-account-credit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[MachinePaymentAccountCreditRequest](#schemamachinepaymentaccountcreditrequest)|true|none|
|» amount_usd|body|string|true|Amount to credit in USD, as a decimal string with up to two fractional digits (by default between 5.00 and 500.00). The request body is required on the initial challenge request and remains required on a paid retry, where you re-send the identical body plus the payment credential — the credential, not the body, selects the payment, and the retried body is not re-validated.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "de06811a-2e43-4561-af5a-7d0a26e20bbb",
    "record_type": "machine_payment_account_credit",
    "account_id": "123456789",
    "amount": "10.00",
    "currency": "USD",
    "payment_source": "machine_payment",
    "provider": "stripe",
    "payment_method": "stripe_spt",
    "payment_intent_id": "pi_3OrJx2eZvKYlo2C1234abcd",
    "receipt_reference": "pi_3OrJx2eZvKYlo2C1234abcd",
    "mpp_resource": "telnyx:account-credit:123456789:usd:10.00",
    "status": "settled",
    "created": false,
    "created_at": "2026-08-12T15:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "de06811a-2e43-4561-af5a-7d0a26e20bbb",
    "record_type": "machine_payment_account_credit",
    "account_id": "123456789",
    "amount": "10.00",
    "currency": "USD",
    "payment_source": "machine_payment",
    "provider": "stripe",
    "payment_method": "stripe_spt",
    "payment_intent_id": "pi_3OrJx2eZvKYlo2C1234abcd",
    "receipt_reference": "pi_3OrJx2eZvKYlo2C1234abcd",
    "mpp_resource": "telnyx:account-credit:123456789:usd:10.00",
    "status": "settled",
    "created": true,
    "created_at": "2026-08-12T15:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid Payment authorization credential"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10009",
      "title": "Authentication failed",
      "detail": "The required authentication headers were either invalid or not included in the request."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Machine payments are not currently enabled"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Not found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "machine payment account credit conflicts with existing transaction"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10027",
      "title": "Invalid request",
      "detail": "amount_usd must be at least 5.00"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 502 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Machine payment service failed"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-machine-payment-account-credit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful duplicate paid retry — the existing account-credit transaction is returned and the account is not credited again. This applies when Rails reaches its duplicate-transaction lookup; re-sending the same Stripe credential may instead be rejected by the upstream provider as an idempotent replay and return `402 Payment Required`.|[MachinePaymentAccountCreditResponse](#schemamachinepaymentaccountcreditresponse)|
|201|Created|Account credit created from a verified machine payment|[MachinePaymentAccountCreditResponse](#schemamachinepaymentaccountcreditresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request — proxied verbatim from the upstream machine payment service when it rejects the request: a malformed or undeserializable `Authorization: Payment ...` credential, a payment credential whose amount violates the upstream amount policy, or a request that fails upstream schema validation. The body is the upstream singular `error` envelope, not the standard Telnyx `errors` array.|[MachinePaymentUpstreamError](#schemamachinepaymentupstreamerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized — the request carried neither valid Telnyx API credentials nor an `Authorization: Payment ...` credential|[machine-payments_ErrorResponse](#schemamachine-payments_errorresponse)|
|402|Payment Required|Payment required. One or more Machine Payment Protocol challenges (for example separate Tempo and Stripe challenges) are returned in the `WWW-Authenticate` header. Construct a payment credential from a challenge and retry the request with an `Authorization: Payment ...` header.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden — machine payments are not enabled for the account, the account tier is ineligible, the account is suspended, or the request origin is not permitted. Note: when the account is suspended the failure is returned via `render_failure` as `{"success": false, "message": "You must verify your identity before you may perform this action.", "reasons": []}` rather than the standard `errors` envelope.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found — proxied verbatim from the upstream machine payment service when the machine payment provider is disabled. The body is the upstream singular `error` envelope, not the standard Telnyx `errors` array.|[MachinePaymentUpstreamError](#schemamachinepaymentupstreamerror)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict — the payment maps to an already-recorded account credit with different fulfillment metadata, so the account is not credited again|[machine-payments_ErrorResponse](#schemamachine-payments_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity — missing or invalid `amount_usd`, or the request fails account-credit policy checks|[machine-payments_ErrorResponse](#schemamachine-payments_errorresponse)|
|502|Bad Gateway|Bad gateway — the upstream machine payment service failed to process the request. Other upstream failure statuses (for example 404 when the machine payment provider is disabled, or 400 for schema validation failures) may be proxied verbatim to the client.|[machine-payments_ErrorResponse](#schemamachine-payments_errorresponse)|

<h3 id="create-a-machine-payment-account-credit-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **403**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[machine-payments_ErrorResponse](#schemamachine-payments_errorresponse)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[MachinePaymentSuspendedAccountFailure](#schemamachinepaymentsuspendedaccountfailure)|false|none|Legacy failure envelope returned when the account is suspended.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Payment-Receipt|string||Machine Payment Protocol receipt returned on successful paid responses. Contains the receipt token identifying the settled payment; keep it for audit and reconciliation alongside the credited transaction.|
|201|Payment-Receipt|string||Machine Payment Protocol receipt returned on successful paid responses. Contains the receipt token identifying the settled payment; keep it for audit and reconciliation alongside the credited transaction.|
|402|WWW-Authenticate|string||Machine Payment Protocol challenge(s) returned on a 402 response, following the HTTP WWW-Authenticate format (RFC 9110). Construct a payment credential from a challenge and retry the same request with an `Authorization: Payment ...` header carrying it.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth, Payment
</aside>

<h1 id="telnyx-api-managed-accounts">Managed Accounts</h1>

## Lists accounts managed by the current user.

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/managed_accounts \

```

`GET /managed_accounts`

Lists the accounts managed by the current user. Users need to be explictly approved by Telnyx in order to become manager accounts.

<h3 id="lists-accounts-managed-by-the-current-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|object|false|Consolidated filter parameter (deepObject style). Originally: filter[email][contains], filter[email][eq], filter[organization_name][contains], filter[organization_name][eq], filter[status][eq]|
|page|query|object|false|Consolidated page parameter (deepObject style). Originally: page[number], page[size]|
|sort|query|string|false|Specifies the sort order for results. By default sorting direction is ascending. To have the results sorted in descending order add the <code> -</code> prefix.<br/><br/><br>That is: <ul><br>  <li><br>    <code>email</code>: sorts the result by the<br>    <code>email</code> field in ascending order.<br>  </li><br><br>  <li><br>    <code>-email</code>: sorts the result by the<br>    <code>email</code> field in descending order.<br>  </li><br></ul> <br/> If not given, results are sorted by <code>created_at</code> in descending order.|
|include_cancelled_accounts|query|boolean|false|Specifies if cancelled accounts should be included in the results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created_at|
|sort|email|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateManagedAccountRequest](#schemacreatemanagedaccountrequest)|true|Parameters that define the managed account to be created|
|» email|body|string|false|The email address for the managed account. If not provided, the email address will be generated based on the email address of the manager account.|
|» password|body|string|false|Password for the managed account. If a password is not supplied, the account will not be able to be signed into directly. (A password reset may still be performed later to enable sign-in via password.)|
|» business_name|body|string|true|The name of the business for which the new managed account is being created, that will be used as the managed accounts's organization's name.|
|» managed_account_allow_custom_pricing|body|boolean|false|Boolean value that indicates if the managed account is able to have custom pricing set for it or not. If false, uses the pricing of the manager account. Defaults to false. This value may be changed after creation, but there may be time lag between when the value is changed and pricing changes take effect.|
|» rollup_billing|body|boolean|false|Boolean value that indicates if the billing information and charges to the managed account "roll up" to the manager account. If true, the managed account will not have its own balance and will use the shared balance with the manager account. This value cannot be changed after account creation without going through Telnyx support as changes require manual updates to the account ledger. Defaults to false.|

## Upload media

<a id="opIdCreateMediaStorage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/media \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
```

`POST /media`

Upload media file to Telnyx so it can be used with other Telnyx services

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "media_url": "http://www.example.com/audio.mp3",
  "ttl_secs": 86400,
  "media_name": "my-file"
```

|body|body|[UploadMediaRequest](#schemauploadmediarequest)|true|Upload media request|

## Speak in a meeting session

<a id="opIdspeakMeetingSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/meeting_sessions/mtgsess_a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/actions/speak \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Here are the three decisions from this call.",
    "interrupt": false
  }'
```

`POST /meeting_sessions/{id}/actions/speak`

Sends audio / text-to-speech into a meeting session. With a Telnyx AI Assistant attached, the bot is a webpage-output bot: the speak audio routes through the assistant's output page rather than the bot mic and plays once the assistant is connected -- it is not refused. If that page cannot be reached, delivery fails with the 502 below, which may arrive without an error envelope, so branch on the status code before parsing a body. The assistant is designed to own the conversation, so prefer letting it speak or use `send_chat`. With a digital avatar (`assistant.avatar: true`), speak is refused with 409 `invalid_state` (message prefix `avatar_requires_assistant_speech:`): the avatar renders only the assistant's own speech.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "Here are the three decisions from this call.",
  "interrupt": false
}
```

<h3 id="speak-in-a-meeting-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the meeting session.|
|body|body|[SpeakMeetingSessionRequest](#schemaspeakmeetingsessionrequest)|true|none|
|» text|body|string|true|Text for the bot to speak.|
|» voice|body|string|false|Voice identifier to use for this utterance. When supplied, it overrides the session-default voice configured at creation; otherwise the speak action uses that session default.|
|» interrupt|body|boolean|false|If true, interrupt any currently playing audio to speak this text immediately.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "accepted": true
  }
}
```

```json
    "code": "invalid_request",

  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

```json
  }
```

## Create a meeting session artifact

<a id="opIdcreateMeetingSessionArtifact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/meeting_sessions/mtgsess_a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/artifacts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "summary"
  }'
```

`POST /meeting_sessions/{id}/artifacts`

Requests asynchronous generation of one artifact: `summary`, `action_items`, `decisions`, `topics`, `open_questions`, or `custom`. Each request produces one artifact. `custom` is answered from a `prompt` you supply, which is required for `custom` and rejected on the five named types. Generation requires transcript content and configured inference and currently reads at most the first 10,000 segments, so exceptionally long transcripts may produce incomplete artifacts or fail model limits. **Not idempotent, and every call is billed**: each request is a separate inference run, so a retry or a duplicate POST produces a second artifact and a second charge. Guard the call rather than relying on the service to collapse it. The automatic `summarize_on_end` attempt is billed on the same basis.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "summary"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-meeting-session-artifact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the meeting session.|
|body|body|[CreateMeetingSessionArtifactRequest](#schemacreatemeetingsessionartifactrequest)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|What to generate from the transcript. `custom` is answered from a `prompt` you supply; the five named types need none.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|Answered from the `prompt` below rather than a fixed question.|
|» prompt|body|string|true|An open-ended request answered from the transcript. Required when `type` is `custom`, and rejected with 400 on any named type. Trimmed before storage and echoed back in artifact responses and the `artifact.completed` webhook.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|summary|
|» type|action_items|
|» type|decisions|
|» type|topics|
|» type|open_questions|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-meeting-session-data">Meeting Session Data</h1>

`GET /meeting_sessions/{id}/events`

## Delete meeting session recording media

<a id="opIddeleteMeetingSessionRecordingMedia"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/meeting_sessions/mtgsess_a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/recording_media \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /meeting_sessions/{id}/recording_media`

Irreversibly requests deletion of the aggregate recording media for the session. The operation retains the Telnyx-local Meeting session, transcript segments, events, artifacts, and usage records. It is separate from `DELETE /meeting_sessions/{id}`, which stops or cancels participation without deleting the persisted session. A missing/foreign session returns 404; a deletion request whose outcome is unknown returns 502.

<h3 id="delete-meeting-session-recording-media-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the meeting session.|

## List meeting session transcript

<a id="opIdlistMeetingSessionTranscript"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/meeting_sessions/mtgsess_a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/transcript \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /meeting_sessions/{id}/transcript`

Returns transcript segments ordered by ascending `seq`. Default `limit` is 100 and maximum is 1,000. Continue with `after=meta.next_after`. A long-poll timeout returns 200 with empty `data` and `meta.next_after: null`; retain the cursor supplied to that request because null is not a replacement cursor.

<h3 id="list-meeting-session-transcript-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the meeting session.|
|after|query|integer|false|Return results with a cursor position after this value.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of results to return per page.|
|wait_seconds|query|integer|false|Long-poll duration in seconds. The server holds the connection open for up to this many seconds, waiting for new or updated results before returning an empty response. Set to 0 for an immediate response.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Create a meeting session

<a id="opIdcreateMeetingSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/meeting_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "meeting_url": "https://zoom.us/j/1234567890",
    "bot_name": "Notetaker"
  }'
```

`POST /meeting_sessions`

Creates a new meeting session. When an idempotency_key is supplied in the request body, replay lookup is scoped to the authenticated account and compares only the key; the request payload is not fingerprinted or compared. If a session with that key already exists for the account, the existing session is replayed (200); otherwise a new session is created (201). The session may enter asynchronous states (e.g. joining, waiting_for_admission) before becoming active. Optional `camera_image` input is write-only and applies only when no avatar or Assistant webpage output takes precedence. An ignored URL is not fetched. An effective URL source is resolved before bot creation; neither the source URL nor image bytes are persisted, returned, or logged. Treat signed URLs as credentials. With `assistant.avatar: true`, the assistant is read before the bot is created: an assistant without a Telnyx avatar configured is rejected with 400 `invalid_request` (message prefix `assistant_avatar_not_configured:`), an unknown assistant with 400 `invalid_request` (prefix `assistant_not_found:`), and a failed lookup with 503 `assistant_lookup_unavailable`; no bot is created in any of these cases.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "meeting_url": "https://zoom.us/j/1234567890",
  "bot_name": "Notetaker"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-meeting-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateMeetingSessionRequest](#schemacreatemeetingsessionrequest)|true|none|
|» meeting_url|body|string(uri)|true|The meeting URL the bot should join.|
|» bot_name|body|string|false|Display name for the bot in the meeting. Defaults to "Meeting Bot".|
|» join_at|body|string(date-time)|false|ISO-8601 timestamp in the future at which the bot should join. If omitted, the bot joins immediately.|
|» voice|body|string|false|Session-default voice identifier used for `speak_on_enter` and ordinary speak actions. A voice supplied on an individual speak action overrides this default for that utterance.|
|» speak_on_enter|body|string|false|Text the bot speaks when it enters the meeting. **Not spoken when an `assistant` is attached**: the value is accepted and echoed back on the session, but the assistant owns the voice and the line is never delivered, with no event reporting the omission. Use `chat_on_enter` to announce an assistant-backed bot. Rejected with 400 `invalid_request` when `assistant.avatar` is `true`.|
|» chat_on_enter|body|string|false|A message the bot posts to the meeting's chat as soon as it becomes active — typically a recording disclosure. Delivered at most once. Independent of `speak_on_enter`: both may be set, and the chat message posts first because it does not wait for text-to-speech or avatar startup. Rejected with 422 `unsupported_capability` on platforms without meeting chat.|
|» barge_in|body|boolean|false|When enabled, a human participant `speech_on` event interrupts and stops the current bot audio; it does not bypass admission or initiate speech. Assistant sessions reject `barge_in: true`.|
|» summarize_on_end|body|boolean|false|If true, generate a summary artifact when the session ends.|
|» camera_image|body|[MeetingSessionCameraImage](#schemameetingsessioncameraimage)|false|Write-only static camera-tile image for this session, not a native account or participant profile photo. Supply exactly one JPEG source. When effective, the image is used as the bot's static camera/video output; presentation varies by meeting platform and recording configuration and is not guaranteed in recordings. An effective Avatar or Assistant webpage output takes precedence, so this input is ignored and a URL source is not fetched.|
|» webhook_url|body|string(uri)|false|HTTPS endpoint to receive session lifecycle callbacks. Static validation requires HTTPS, rejects embedded credentials and blocked hosts, and enforces egress policy. Validation makes no network request to the endpoint.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to the session. The serialized JSON representation must not exceed 16384 characters at runtime.|
|» idempotency_key|body|string|false|Client-supplied idempotency key to safely retry creation requests without duplicating sessions. Lookup is scoped to the authenticated account and compares the key only; the request payload is not fingerprinted or compared.|
|» assistant|body|[MeetingSessionAssistantRequest](#schemameetingsessionassistantrequest)|false|Attach a Telnyx AI Assistant to the session. Supply the Assistant's ID; the Meeting service connects it to the meeting directly. The Call Control connection, caller ID and loopback SIP URI previously required here have been removed and are now rejected as unknown fields.|

> Example responses

## Delete a meeting session

<a id="opIddeleteMeetingSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/meeting_sessions/mtgsess_a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`DELETE /meeting_sessions/{id}`

Stops a meeting session without deleting its persisted record. Scheduled bots are cancelled, while bots that are joining or active are asked to leave. The persisted meeting session record remains available.
