## Request Private Wireless Gateway assignment for SIM card group

<a id="opIdSetPrivateWirelessGatewayForSimCardGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/sim_card_groups/6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58/actions/set_private_wireless_gateway \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "private_wireless_gateway_id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58"
  }'
```

`POST /sim_card_groups/{id}/actions/set_private_wireless_gateway`

This action will asynchronously assign a provisioned Private Wireless Gateway to the SIM card group. Completing this operation defines that all SIM cards in the SIM card group will get their traffic controlled by the associated Private Wireless Gateway. This operation will also imply that new SIM cards assigned to a group will inherit its network definitions. If it's moved to a different group that doesn't have a Private Wireless Gateway, it'll use Telnyx's default mobile network configuration.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "private_wireless_gateway_id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58"
}
```

|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Identifies the SIM group.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-sim-cards">SIM Cards</h1>

SIM Cards operations

## Purchase eSIMs

<a id="opIdPurchaseESim"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/actions/purchase/esims \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sim_card_group_id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
    "tags": [
      "personal",
      "customers",
      "active-customers"
    ],
    "product": "whitelabel",
    "whitelabel_name": "Custom SPN",
    "amount": 10,
    "status": "standby"
  }'
```

`POST /actions/purchase/esims`

Purchases and registers the specified amount of eSIMs to the current user's account.<br/><br/>
If <code>sim_card_group_id</code> is provided, the eSIMs will be associated with that group. Otherwise, the default group for the current user will be used.<br/><br/>


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sim_card_group_id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
  "tags": [
    "personal",
    "customers",
    "active-customers"
  ],
  "product": "whitelabel",
  "whitelabel_name": "Custom SPN",
  "amount": 10,
  "status": "standby"
}
```

<h3 id="purchase-esims-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ESimPurchase](#schemaesimpurchase)|true|none|
|» sim_card_group_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The group SIMCardGroup identification. This attribute can be <code>null</code> when it's present in an associated resource.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Searchable tags associated with the SIM cards|
|» product|body|string|false|Type of product to be purchased, specify "whitelabel" to use a custom SPN|
|» whitelabel_name|body|string|false|Service Provider Name (SPN) for the Whitelabel eSIM product. It will be displayed as the mobile service name by operating systems of smartphones. This parameter must only contain letters, numbers and whitespaces.|
|» amount|body|integer|true|The amount of eSIMs to be purchased.|
|» status|body|string|false|Status on which the SIM cards will be set after being successfully registered.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|enabled|
|» status|disabled|
|» status|standby|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
      "record_type": "sim_card",
      "status": {
        "value": "enabled",
```

## Register SIM cards

<a id="opIdRegisterSimCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/actions/register/sim_cards \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sim_card_group_id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
    "tags": [
      "personal",
      "customers",
      "active-customers"
    ],
    "registration_codes": [
      "0000000001",
      "0000000002",
      "0000000003"
    ],
    "status": "standby"
  }'
```

`POST /actions/register/sim_cards`

Register the SIM cards associated with the provided registration codes to the current user's account.<br/><br/>
If <code>sim_card_group_id</code> is provided, the SIM cards will be associated with that group. Otherwise, the default group for the current user will be used.<br/><br/>


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sim_card_group_id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
  "tags": [
    "personal",
    "customers",
    "active-customers"
  ],
  "registration_codes": [
    "0000000001",
    "0000000002",
    "0000000003"
  ],
  "status": "standby"
}
```

<h3 id="register-sim-cards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SIMCardRegistration](#schemasimcardregistration)|true|none|
|» sim_card_group_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The group SIMCardGroup identification. This attribute can be <code>null</code> when it's present in an associated resource.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Searchable tags associated with the SIM card|
|» registration_codes|body|[string]|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|Status on which the SIM card will be set after being successful registered.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|enabled|
|» status|disabled|
|» status|standby|

## Deletes a SIM card

<a id="opIdDeleteSimCard"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/sim_cards/6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /sim_cards/{id}`

The SIM card will be decommissioned, removed from your account and you will stop being charged.<br />The SIM card won't be able to connect to the network after the deletion is completed, thus making it impossible to consume data.<br/>
Transitioning to the disabled state may take a period of time.
Until the transition is completed, the SIM card status will be disabling <code>disabling</code>.<br />In order to re-enable the SIM card, you will need to re-register it.

<h3 id="deletes-a-sim-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Identifies the SIM.|
|report_lost|query|boolean|false|Enables deletion of disabled eSIMs that can't be uninstalled from a device. This is irreversible and the eSIM cannot be re-registered.|

`POST /sim_cards/{id}/actions/disable`

This API disables a SIM card, disconnecting it from the network and making it impossible to consume data.<br/>
The API will trigger an asynchronous operation called a SIM Card Action. Transitioning to the disabled state may take a period of time. The status of the SIM Card Action can be followed through the [List SIM Card Action](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/sim-card-actions/list-sim-card-actions) API.

## Request enabling voice on a SIM card

<a id="opIdEnableVoiceSimCard"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/sim_cards/6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58/actions/enable_voice \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "connection_id": "123456789"
  }'
```

`POST /sim_cards/{id}/actions/enable_voice`

This API enables voice calling on a SIM card. When a <code>connection_id</code> is provided, the SIM is associated with the specified Mobile Voice Connection. The connection must be owned by the same user and of type <code>mobile_voice</code>.<br/>
The API will trigger an asynchronous operation called a SIM Card Action. The status of the SIM Card Action can be followed through the [List SIM Card Action](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/sim-card-actions/list-sim-card-actions) API.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "connection_id": "123456789"
}
```

<h3 id="request-enabling-voice-on-a-sim-card-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Identifies the SIM.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» connection_id|body|string|false|The identifier of the Mobile Voice Connection to associate with this SIM card. The connection must be owned by the same user and of type <code>mobile_voice</code>. If omitted, voice is enabled without a connection association.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
    "record_type": "sim_card_action",
    "sim_card_id": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
    "action_type": "enable",
    "status": {

      "reason": "The data limit was exceeded."
    },

      }

}
```

`GET /session_analysis/{record_type}/{event_id}`

Retrieves a full session analysis tree for a given event, including costs, child events, and product linkages.

<h3 id="get-session-analysis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|path|string|true|The record type identifier.|
|event_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The event identifier (UUID).|
|include_children|query|boolean|false|Whether to include child events in the response.|
|max_depth|query|integer|false|Maximum traversal depth for the event tree.|
|expand|query|string|false|Controls what data to expand on each event node.|
|date_time|query|string(date-time)|false|ISO 8601 timestamp or date to narrow index selection for faster lookups. Accepts full datetime (e.g., 2026-03-17T10:00:00Z) or date-only format (e.g., 2026-03-17).|

</aside>

## Change a namespace's settings

<a id="opIdUpdateNamespaceSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/memory/namespaces/string/settings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "summary": {
      "instructions": "Lead with the customer'\''s plan tier. Keep it under 100 words."
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /ai/memory/namespaces/{namespace}/settings`

Only the fields you send are changed; anything omitted is left as it is, so `{}` changes nothing. Sending `instructions: null`, or an empty or whitespace-only string, clears them and returns summaries to the neutral default.

Instructions are capped at 2000 characters. A longer note is refused rather than truncated, because a note cut mid-sentence is a worse steer than none. A change reaches each summary the next time that summary is regenerated, not immediately.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "summary": {
    "instructions": "Lead with the customer's plan tier. Keep it under 100 words."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="change-a-namespaces-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace. `default` exists for every organization.|
|body|body|[NamespaceSettingsPatch](#schemanamespacesettingspatch)|true|none|
|» summary|body|[SummarySettingsPatch](#schemasummarysettingspatch) \| null|false|Summary settings to change. Omit to change nothing.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[SummarySettingsPatch](#schemasummarysettingspatch)|false|A partial update to a namespace's summary settings.<br><br>Only the fields present in the request are changed; the rest are left as<br>they are. Sending `instructions: null` (or empty) clears the instructions.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "summary": {
      "instructions": "Lead with the customer's plan tier. Keep it under 100 words."
    }
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10009",
      "title": "Authentication failed",
      "detail": "Could not find any usable credentials in the request.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/"
      },
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10009"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "namespace_not_found",
      "detail": "no such namespace"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "invalid_instructions",
      "detail": "instructions must be at most 2000 characters"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 502 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "upstream_error",
      "detail": "the memory dataplane is unavailable"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="change-a-namespaces-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|The settings as stored|[NamespaceSettingsResponse](#schemanamespacesettingsresponse)|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-sources">Sources</h1>

What a profile stored, and what its memories came from.

## List a profile's sources, most recently written first

<a id="opIdListMemorySources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/memory/namespaces/string/profiles/string/sources \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ai/memory/namespaces/{namespace}/profiles/{profile_id}/sources`

Everything a profile has stored and extracts memories from: each ingested session, and each remembered fact, which has no session. Content is not listed; read one source for it. A source whose ingest is still queued is not here yet. Re-ingesting a session moves it to the front, so a listing paged while sessions are written can repeat or miss one at a page boundary. A `session_id` narrows the listing to the source that session was stored as: one source or none, and none -- an empty page, not a 404 -- for a session never ingested, still queued, or another profile's.

<h3 id="list-a-profiles-sources-most-recently-written-first-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|profile_id|path|string|true|none|
|session_id|query|string \| null|false|An ingested session, by the `session_id` it was ingested with. Narrows the request to the source that session was stored as.|
|page[number]|query|integer|false|The page to return, counting from 1. Bounded in depth: (page[number] - 1) * page[size] may be at most 10000.|
|page[size]|query|integer|false|How many results a page holds.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "data": [
    {

    },

      "session_id": null,

}
```

## Forget one source

<a id="opIdForgetSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/memory/namespaces/string/profiles/string/sources/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /ai/memory/namespaces/{namespace}/profiles/{profile_id}/sources/{source_id}`

Deletes one source -- an ingested session or a remembered fact -- together with the memories derived from it. A memory derived from this source and others is deleted too, and derived again from what remains in the background. It answers only once the source is gone. A source that is not there -- never stored, another profile's, or already deleted -- answers 404, so on a `502` or a `504` repeat the identical request and read a 404 as done. An ingest of the same session that is still queued is not cancelled, and stores the session again when it runs. Nothing here can be undone.

<h3 id="forget-one-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace. `default` exists for every organization.|
|profile_id|path|string|true|The profile: your identifier for the user, caller or agent this memory is about.|
|source_id|path|string|true|Identifies one source within its profile: an ingested session, or one remembered fact. Returned by `ingest` and `remember` when the write is accepted. Re-ingesting a session keeps its source id.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
    "source_id": "b1e6c0a2-4f3d-4a2e-9c7b-8e1f2a3b4c5d",
    "memories_deleted": 3
  }
}
```

```json
      "code": "source_not_found",
```

```json

  "errors": [
```

<h1 id="telnyx-api-speech-to-text-capabilities">Speech To Text Capabilities</h1>

Discover available speech-to-text providers, models, and supported languages.

## List supported STT providers

<a id="opIdlistSttProviders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/speech-to-text/providers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /speech-to-text/providers`

Retrieve the canonical list of supported speech-to-text providers, models, accepted language codes, and the service types each model supports.

Service types:
  * `streaming` — standalone WebSocket transcription via `/speech-to-text/transcription`.
  * `file_based` — file-based transcription via `/ai/audio/transcriptions`.
  * `in_call` — live call transcription via Call Control `transcription_start`.
  * `ai_assistant` — STT configured on a Call Control AI Assistant via voice-assistant `TranscriptionConfig` (covers both live-streaming and non-streaming/batch models).

Use this endpoint to discover which (provider, model) combinations are available for the surface you need, and which language codes each accepts. `auto` in a `languages` array indicates the provider performs language detection.

<h3 id="list-supported-stt-providers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|service_type|query|[STTServiceType](#schemasttservicetype)|false|Filter to entries that support the given service type. For backward compatibility with the values that briefly shipped before the product-aligned rename, the legacy aliases `file_transcription`, `in_call_transcription`, and `ai_assistant_transcription` are silently accepted and normalized to `file_based`, `in_call`, and `ai_assistant` respectively. The response always emits the canonical (post-rename) values.|
|provider|query|string|false|Filter to entries for a specific STT provider. The enum mirrors the providers advertised across the speech-to-text spec (including `google` and `telnyx`, which are accepted as WebSocket transcription engines). A provider that has no models currently registered for any service type will return an empty `data` array rather than an error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|service_type|streaming|
|service_type|file_based|
|service_type|in_call|
|service_type|ai_assistant|
|provider|deepgram|
|provider|speechmatics|
|provider|assemblyai|
|provider|xai|
|provider|soniox|
|provider|parakeet|
|provider|humain|
|provider|reson8|
|provider|cohere|
|provider|azure|
|provider|openai|
|provider|google|
|provider|telnyx|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "provider": "deepgram",
      "model": "deepgram/nova-3",
      "hosted": true,
      "service_types": [
        {
          "type": "streaming",
          "languages": [
            "en",
            "es",
            "fr"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
```

<h1 id="telnyx-api-speech-to-text-over-websockets">Speech To Text over WebSockets</h1>

Speech to text command operations

## Speech to text over WebSocket

<a id="opIdTranscriptionOverWs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.telnyx.com/v2/speech-to-text/transcription?transcription_engine=Telnyx&input_format=mp3' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`GET /speech-to-text/transcription`

Open a WebSocket connection to stream audio and receive transcriptions in real-time. Authentication is provided via the standard `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` header.

Supported engines: `Azure`, `Deepgram`, `Google`, `Telnyx`, `xAI`, `Speechmatics`, `Soniox`, `Parakeet`, `Humain`, `Reson8`, `Cohere`.

**Connection flow:**
1. Open WebSocket with query parameters specifying engine, input format, and language.
2. Send binary audio frames (mp3, wav, linear16, or linear32 format, per `input_format`).
3. Receive JSON transcript frames with `transcript`, `is_final`, and `confidence` fields.
4. Close connection when done.

<h3 id="speech-to-text-over-websocket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transcription_engine|query|string|true|The transcription engine to use for processing the audio stream.|
|input_format|query|string|true|The format of input audio stream.|
|sample_rate|query|integer|false|Audio sample rate in Hz. Required when `input_format` is a raw encoding (`linear16`, `linear32`) — those formats carry no header metadata. Ignored for container formats (`mp3`, `wav`), which self-describe their rate. `speechmatics/linden-1` accepts only `16000`.|
|language|query|string|false|The language spoken in the audio stream. For `cohere/ar-stt`, this must be `ar` or `en` — unlike other engines, Cohere does not auto-detect the language, and rejects unsupported values including `auto`; omitting it defaults to `ar`. For `speechmatics/linden-1`, omitting it defaults to `en`; `auto`, `auto_beta`, `multi`, or a language outside its supported list is rejected when the connection is established. `speechmatics/linden-1` also accepts `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-AU`, `cmn-Hans`, and `cmn-Hant`, which select the spelling or script variant (`en` alone uses the default spelling).|
|interim_results|query|boolean|false|Whether to receive interim transcription results.|
|model|query|[azure_models](#schemaazure_models) \| [deepgram_models](#schemadeepgram_models) \| [google_models](#schemagoogle_models) \| [telnyx_models](#schematelnyx_models) \| [xai_models](#schemaxai_models) \| [speechmatics_models](#schemaspeechmatics_models) \| [soniox_models](#schemasoniox_models) \| [parakeet_models](#schemaparakeet_models) \| [humain_models](#schemahumain_models) \| [reson8_models](#schemareson8_models) \| [cohere_ar_stt_models](#schemacohere_ar_stt_models)|false|The specific model to use within the selected transcription engine.|
|endpointing|query|integer|false|Silence duration (in milliseconds) that triggers end-of-speech detection. When set, the engine uses this value to determine when a speaker has stopped talking. Supported by `xAI`, `Deepgram`, `Google`, `Speechmatics` (`speechmatics/standard` only; `speechmatics/linden-1` uses fixed service-side voice activity detection and ignores it), and `Soniox`. `Soniox` accepts values between 500 and 3000. Other engines may not support this parameter.|
|redact|query|string|false|Enable redaction of sensitive information (e.g., PCI data, SSN) from transcription results. Supported values depend on the transcription engine.|
|keyterm|query|string|false|A key term to boost in the transcription. The engine will be more likely to recognize this term. Can be specified multiple times for multiple terms.|
|keywords|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of keywords to boost in the transcription. The engine will prioritize recognition of these words.|
|body|body|[SttClientEvent](#schemasttclientevent)|false|Client sends binary audio frames (mp3, wav, linear16, or linear32 format, per `input_format`) over the WebSocket. See `SttClientEvent` schema.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|transcription_engine|Azure|
|transcription_engine|Deepgram|
|transcription_engine|Google|
|transcription_engine|Telnyx|
|transcription_engine|xAI|
|transcription_engine|Speechmatics|
|transcription_engine|Soniox|
|transcription_engine|Parakeet|
|transcription_engine|Humain|
|transcription_engine|Reson8|
|transcription_engine|Cohere|
|input_format|mp3|
|input_format|wav|
|input_format|linear16|
|input_format|linear32|

> Example responses

> 101 Response

```json
{
  "type": "transcript",
  "transcript": "string",
  "is_final": true,
  "confidence": 0
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10004",
      "title": "Missing required parameter",
      "detail": "The 'transcription_engine' parameter is required and cannot be blank.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/transcription_engine"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="speech-to-text-over-websocket-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|101|Switching Protocols|WebSocket connection established. Communication proceeds via binary audio frames (client) and JSON transcript frames (server).<br><br>**Client → Server:** Binary audio data (mp3, wav, linear16, or linear32, per `input_format`).<br>**Server → Client:** See `TranscriptFrame` and `SttErrorFrame` schemas.|[SttServerEvent](#schemasttserverevent)|
|200|OK|WebSocket upgrade successful — this response is not returned directly. See 101 for frame documentation.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid parameters — engine not supported or missing required fields.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication failed — missing or invalid Authorization header.|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity. The request was well-formed but could not be processed due to semantic errors. This includes validation errors, invalid parameter values and business logic violations.|[speech-to-text_Errors](#schemaspeech-to-text_errors)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

<h1 id="telnyx-api-spend-limits">Spend Limits</h1>

Daily and monthly spend limits per product. A limit applies to the organization of the authenticated user, or to the user's own account when they belong to no organization; every user of the organization sees and changes the same limits.

- **Periods.** `daily` covers the current UTC day and `monthly` the current UTC calendar month. The two limits are independent: you can set either, both or neither.
- **Blocking.** When spend in a period goes above the limit (strictly greater), the product is blocked until the period ends: 00:00 UTC the next day for `daily`, 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the next month for `monthly`. A block appears within about 2 minutes (daily) or 10 minutes (monthly) of the spend being recorded.
- **Changes apply immediately.** Creating, updating or deleting a limit checks the period's spend in the same request: raising the limit above the spend, or removing it, lifts that period's block, and lowering it below the spend blocks the product at once. The `evaluation` object in the response says what happened.
- **Supported products.** Today only `inference` supports spend limits. A blocked account gets HTTP 403 with the error title `Inference spend limit reached` (code `10039`) on new billable chat completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages and classification requests; requests already running finish normally. Take the list of products from the list operation.
- **API key limits.** For `inference`, a limit can also apply to one API key, named by `credential_id`: the key's identifier as recorded on usage, never its secret. When the key's spend goes above its own limit, only that key is blocked, with the error title `API key spend limit reached` (code `10039`); the account's other keys keep working. The API key limits of a period cannot add up to more than the total limit when the total has an amount. Only language-model requests authenticated with an API key count toward its limit.
- **Limits set by Telnyx.** Telnyx support can also set a limit on your account. It is listed with `origin: operator` and you can update or delete it like your own.

## List spend limits

<a id="opIdlistSpendLimits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/spend_limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /spend_limits`

Returns one entry per product and period you can set a limit on, with the limit, the spend so far in the period and whether the product is blocked. An entry without a limit is still listed (`limit: null`). When the spend cannot be read, the entry is returned with `spend_usd: null` and `spend_error` set. The list is not paginated. Each entry also lists the API key limits of its product and period in `credential_limits`, with each key's spend and block. Each API key limit can be at most the total limit; together they may add up to more than it.

## Create a spend limit

<a id="opIdcreateSpendLimit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/spend_limits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "product": "inference",
    "period": "daily",
    "amount": 100,
    "reason": "Team budget"
  }'
```

`POST /spend_limits`

Sets a limit for a product and period that has none. Send exactly one of `amount` and `unlimited: true`. The period's spend is checked at once: if it is already above the new limit, the product is blocked immediately (`evaluation.blocked_now`). Returns 409 when a limit already exists for the product and period; update it instead. With `credential_id`, the limit applies to that API key only: it needs an `amount`, and the period's API key limits cannot add up to more than the total limit when the total has an amount.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "product": "inference",
  "period": "daily",
  "amount": 100,
  "reason": "Team budget"
}
```

|» *oneOf*|body|[CreateSpendLimitUnlimited](#schemacreatespendlimitunlimited)|false|Explicitly no cap. Not available for API key limits.|

## Delete a spend limit

<a id="opIddeleteSpendLimit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/spend_limits/inference \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /spend_limits/{product}`

Removes the limit for the product and period. For `inference`, which has no default limit, the product becomes unlimited for the period and the period's block is lifted (`evaluation.released`). The response carries `limit: null` and the `effective_limit_usd` that applies after the removal. Returns 404 when no limit is set. With the `credential_id` query parameter, the request removes that API key's limit for the period and lifts the key's block in that period at once. A block under the key's limit in the other period stays (`evaluation.still_blocked_other_period`). Removing the total limit leaves the API key limits in place.

<h3 id="delete-a-spend-limit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|product|path|string|true|Product the limit applies to, as returned in `product` by the list operation.|
|period|query|[SpendLimitPeriod](#schemaspendlimitperiod)|false|Limit period. Defaults to `daily`; send it explicitly.|
|credential_id|query|string|false|Identifier of one API key as recorded on usage, never the key's secret, percent-encoded: the request is then about that key's limit. Absent means the total limit; present but blank is refused.|
|reason|query|string|false|Why the limit is removed, kept for audit. At most 500 characters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|period|daily|
|period|monthly|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
    "record_type": "spend_limit",

    "product_name": "Inference",
    "period": "daily",

    "period_end": "2026-09-25",
    "limit": null,
    "effective_limit_usd": null,
    "spend_usd": "12.80",
    "spend_error": null,
    "blocked": false,
    "block": null,
    "evaluation": {
      "spend_usd": null,
      "released": true,
      "blocked_now": false,
      "still_over_limit": false,
      "still_blocked_other_period": false,
      "evaluation_deferred": false
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10015",
      "title": "Product does not support self-service spend limits",
      "detail": "Spend limits for this product cannot be managed through the API; contact support"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10009",
      "title": "Authentication failed",
      "detail": "The required authentication headers were either invalid or not included in the request."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10010",
      "title": "Authorization failed",
      "detail": "You do not have permission to perform the requested action on the specified resource or resources."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

## Update a spend limit

<a id="opIdupdateSpendLimit"></a>

```bash

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    "amount": 250
  }'
```

`PATCH /spend_limits/{product}`

Replaces the value of the existing limit for the product and period. Send exactly one of `amount` and `unlimited: true`. The period's spend is checked at once: raising the limit above the spend lifts the period's block (`evaluation.released`), and lowering it below the spend blocks the product (`evaluation.blocked_now`). Returns 404 when no limit is set; create it instead. With the `credential_id` query parameter, the request changes that API key's limit; it needs an `amount`, and it can be at most the period's total limit. Lowering the total limit below the period's highest API key limit is refused.

## Create a Tailscale Subnet Router

<a id="opIdCreateTailscaleSubnetRouter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/tailscale_subnet_routers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "tailnet-ashburn",
    "network_id": "0de011ae-ee53-4df4-ba96-754728eb5aad",
    "region_code": "ashburn-va",
    "advertised_routes": [
      "172.27.0.0/24"
    ],
    "auth_key": "tskey-auth-k1AbCdEfGh2IjKlMnOpQrStUv"
  }'
```

`POST /tailscale_subnet_routers`

Creates a Tailscale Subnet Router on a Network and enrolls it in the user's tailnet with the auth key. The response returns the router with `status` `provisioning`. Poll `GET /tailscale_subnet_routers/{id}` until it is `provisioned`. Then approve its routes in the tailnet, unless an auto-approver covers them.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "tailnet-ashburn",
  "network_id": "0de011ae-ee53-4df4-ba96-754728eb5aad",
  "region_code": "ashburn-va",
  "advertised_routes": [
    "172.27.0.0/24"
  ],
  "auth_key": "tskey-auth-k1AbCdEfGh2IjKlMnOpQrStUv"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-tailscale-subnet-router-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TailscaleSubnetRouterCreate](#schematailscalesubnetroutercreate)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A user specified name for the router.|
|» network_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The id of the Network to attach the router to.|
|» region_code|body|string|true|The code of the region to create the router in. `GET /network_coverage` lists the regions whose `available_services` include `tailscale_subnet_router`.|
|» advertised_routes|body|[string]|true|IPv4 subnets of the Network that the router advertises to the tailnet. Each entry is a canonical CIDR that the Network routes. Default, loopback, link-local, multicast, and Tailscale (`100.64.0.0/10`) ranges are rejected. So are ranges that overlap the router's own, `172.27.254.0/24` and `198.18.0.0/20`.|
|» auth_key|body|string(password)|true|A Tailscale auth key that enrolls the router in the user's tailnet: reusable, pre-approved, tagged, and not ephemeral. Telnyx stores it encrypted until enrollment succeeds, then discards it. It is never returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "data": {
    "id": "5c6f0a7e-6c7b-4d7f-9f2e-3b1e4e9a8c21",
    "record_type": "tailscale_subnet_router",
    "name": "tailnet-ashburn",
    "network_id": "0de011ae-ee53-4df4-ba96-754728eb5aad",
    "region_code": "ashburn-va",
    "advertised_routes": [
      "172.27.0.0/24"
    ],
    "status": "provisioning",
    "customer_address": "172.27.254.1",
    "device_id": null,
    "tailnet_name": null,
    "tailscale_ips": [],
    "created_at": "2026-10-13T15:04:05.123456Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-10-13T15:04:05.123456Z"
  }
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10015",

        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10015"
      }
    }
```

`DELETE /tailscale_subnet_routers/{id}`

## Update a Tailscale Subnet Router

<a id="opIdUpdateTailscaleSubnetRouter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/tailscale_subnet_routers/6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "advertised_routes": [
      "172.27.0.0/24",
      "172.27.1.0/24"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /tailscale_subnet_routers/{id}`

Renames the router, changes its advertised routes, or retries a failed enrollment. Any change queues a new provisioning run and returns the router with `status` `provisioning`. The router keeps its machine identity on the tailnet. Send an empty object to retry a `failed` router with its stored auth key. Include a new `auth_key` only while the router has never enrolled. The router's Network and region cannot change: create a new router instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "advertised_routes": [
    "172.27.0.0/24",
    "172.27.1.0/24"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-tailscale-subnet-router-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Identifies the resource.|
|body|body|[TailscaleSubnetRouterUpdate](#schematailscalesubnetrouterupdate)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A user specified name for the router.|
|» advertised_routes|body|[string]|false|IPv4 subnets of the Network that the router advertises to the tailnet. Each entry is a canonical CIDR that the Network routes. Default, loopback, link-local, multicast, and Tailscale (`100.64.0.0/10`) ranges are rejected. So are ranges that overlap the router's own, `172.27.254.0/24` and `198.18.0.0/20`.|
|» auth_key|body|string(password)|false|A replacement Tailscale auth key. Accepted only while the router has never enrolled, for example after a `failed` enrollment. Never returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "5c6f0a7e-6c7b-4d7f-9f2e-3b1e4e9a8c21",

    "name": "tailnet-ashburn",

    "advertised_routes": [
      "172.27.0.0/24",
      "172.27.1.0/24"
    ],
    "status": "provisioning",
    "customer_address": "172.27.254.1",
    "device_id": "n5c6f0a7e1CNTRL",
    "tailnet_name": "acme.example",
    "tailscale_ips": [
      "100.101.2.30",
      "fd7a:115c:a1e0::2a"
    ],
    "created_at": "2026-10-13T15:04:05.123456Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-10-14T09:12:00.000000Z"
  }
}
```

<a id="opIdCreateTexmlApplication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/texml_applications \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "friendly_name": "call-router",
    "active": false,
    "anchorsite_override": "Amsterdam, Netherlands",
    "dtmf_type": "Inband",
    "first_command_timeout": true,
    "first_command_timeout_secs": 10,
    "voice_url": "https://example.com",
    "voice_fallback_url": "https://fallback.example.com",
    "call_cost_in_webhooks": false,
    "voice_method": "get",
    "status_callback": "https://example.com",
    "status_callback_method": "get",
    "tags": [
      "tag1",
      "tag2"
    ],
    "inbound": {
      "channel_limit": 10,
      "shaken_stir_enabled": true,
      "sip_subdomain": "example",
      "sip_subdomain_receive_settings": "only_my_connections"
    },
    "outbound": {
      "channel_limit": 10,
      "outbound_voice_profile_id": "1293384261075731499"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /texml_applications`

Creates a TeXML application, which defines the voice URLs and settings used to serve TeXML instructions for calls, and returns the created application.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "friendly_name": "call-router",
  "active": false,
  "anchorsite_override": "Amsterdam, Netherlands",
  "dtmf_type": "Inband",
  "first_command_timeout": true,
  "first_command_timeout_secs": 10,
  "voice_url": "https://example.com",
  "voice_fallback_url": "https://fallback.example.com",
  "call_cost_in_webhooks": false,
  "voice_method": "get",
  "status_callback": "https://example.com",
  "status_callback_method": "get",
  "tags": [
    "tag1",
    "tag2"
  ],
  "inbound": {
    "channel_limit": 10,
    "shaken_stir_enabled": true,
    "sip_subdomain": "example",
    "sip_subdomain_receive_settings": "only_my_connections"
  },
  "outbound": {
    "channel_limit": 10,
    "outbound_voice_profile_id": "1293384261075731499"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-texml-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateTexmlApplicationRequest](#schemacreatetexmlapplicationrequest)|true|Parameters that can be set when creating a TeXML Application|
|» friendly_name|body|[ApplicationName](#schemaapplicationname)|true|A user-assigned name to help manage the application.|
|» active|body|[ConnectionActive](#schemaconnectionactive)|false|Specifies whether the connection can be used.|
|» anchorsite_override|body|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|» dtmf_type|body|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|» first_command_timeout|body|[FirstCommandTimeout](#schemafirstcommandtimeout)|false|Specifies whether calls to phone numbers associated with this connection should hangup after timing out.|
|» first_command_timeout_secs|body|[FirstCommandTimeoutSecs](#schemafirstcommandtimeoutsecs)|false|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a dial command.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with the Texml Application.|
|» voice_url|body|string(uri)|true|URL to which Telnyx will deliver your XML Translator webhooks.|
|» voice_fallback_url|body|string(uri)|false|URL to which Telnyx will deliver your XML Translator webhooks if we get an error response from your voice_url.|
|» call_cost_in_webhooks|body|boolean|false|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this TeXML Application.|
|» voice_method|body|string|false|HTTP request method Telnyx will use to interact with your XML Translator webhooks. Either 'get' or 'post'.|
|» status_callback|body|string(uri)|false|URL for Telnyx to send requests to containing information about call progress events.|
|» status_callback_method|body|string|false|HTTP request method Telnyx should use when requesting the status_callback URL.|
|» inbound|body|object|false|none|
|» » channel_limit|body|integer|false|When set, this will limit the total number of inbound calls to phone numbers associated with this connection.|
|» » shaken_stir_enabled|body|boolean|false|When enabled Telnyx will include Shaken/Stir data in the Webhook for new inbound calls.|
|» » sip_subdomain|body|string|false|Specifies a subdomain that can be used to receive Inbound calls to a Connection, in the same way a phone number is used, from a SIP endpoint. Example: the subdomain "example.sip.telnyx.com" can be called from any SIP endpoint by using the SIP URI "sip:@example.sip.telnyx.com" where the user part can be any alphanumeric value. TLS signaling is supported. SRTP media encryption requires TLS transport.|
|» » sip_subdomain_receive_settings|body|string|false|This option can be enabled to receive calls from: "Anyone" (any SIP endpoint in the public Internet) or "Only my connections" (any connection assigned to the same Telnyx user).|
|» outbound|body|object|false|none|
|» » channel_limit|body|integer|false|When set, this will limit the total number of outbound calls to phone numbers associated with this connection.|
|» » outbound_voice_profile_id|body|[OutboundVoiceProfileId](#schemaoutboundvoiceprofileid)|false|Identifies the associated outbound voice profile.|

<h1 id="telnyx-api-texml-rest-commands">TeXML REST Commands</h1>

TeXML REST Commands

## Fetch multiple call resources

<a id="opIdGetTexmlCalls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/texml/Accounts/f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9/Calls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /texml/Accounts/{account_sid}/Calls`

Returns multiple call resouces for an account. This endpoint is eventually consistent.

<h3 id="fetch-multiple-call-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_sid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Telnyx account that owns the resource, for example `f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9`. The `account_sid` path segment is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is a Telnyx account UUID, not a Twilio `AC...` SID. It must match the account that owns the API key used to authenticate the request, otherwise the endpoint returns `404`. The same value is sent as `AccountSid` in TeXML webhooks.|
|Page|query|integer|false|The number of the page to be displayed, zero-indexed, should be used in conjuction with PageToken.|
|PageSize|query|integer|false|The number of records to be displayed on a page|
|PageToken|query|string|false|Used to request the next page of results.|
|To|query|string|false|Filters calls by the to number.|
|From|query|string|false|Filters calls by the from number.|
|Status|query|string|false|Filters calls by status.|
|StartTime|query|string|false|Filters calls by their start date. Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD.|
|StartTime>|query|string|false|Filters calls by their start date (after). Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD|
|StartTime<|query|string|false|Filters calls by their start date (before). Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD|
|EndTime|query|string|false|Filters calls by their end date. Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD|
|EndTime>|query|string|false|Filters calls by their end date (after). Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD|
|EndTime<|query|string|false|Filters calls by their end date (before). Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Status|canceled|
|Status|completed|
|Status|failed|
|Status|busy|
|Status|no-answer|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "calls": [],
  "end": 0,
  "first_page_uri": "/v2/texml/Accounts/61bf923e-5e4d-4595-a110-56190ea18a1b/Calls.json?Page=0&PageSize=1",
  "next_page_uri": "/v2/texml/Accounts/61bf923e-5e4d-4595-a110-56190ea18a1b/Calls.json?Page=1&PageSize=1&PageToken=MTY4AjgyNDkwNzIxMQ",
  "page": 0,
  "page_size": 1,
  "start": 0,
  "uri": "/v2/texml/Accounts/61bf923e-5e4d-4595-a110-56190ea18a1b/Calls.json?Page=0&PageSize=1"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Resource not found"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Multiple call resources.|[CallResourceIndex](#schemacallresourceindex)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[call-scripting_ResourceNotFoundError_c75353cb83](#schemacall-scripting_resourcenotfounderror_c75353cb83)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth

## Initiate an outbound call

<a id="opIdInitiateTexmlCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/texml/Accounts/f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9/Calls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "To": "+13121230000",
    "From": "+13120001234",
    "Url": "https://www.example.com/texml.xml",
    "StatusCallback": "https://www.example.com/statuscallback-listener",
    "ApplicationSid": "1293384261075731499"
  }'
```

`POST /texml/Accounts/{account_sid}/Calls`

Initiate an outbound TeXML call. Telnyx will request TeXML from the XML Request URL configured for the TeXML Application in the Mission Control Portal.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "To": "+13121230000",
  "From": "+13120001234",
  "Url": "https://www.example.com/texml.xml",
  "StatusCallback": "https://www.example.com/statuscallback-listener",
  "ApplicationSid": "1293384261075731499"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-an-outbound-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_sid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Telnyx account that owns the resource, for example `f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9`. The `account_sid` path segment is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is a Telnyx account UUID, not a Twilio `AC...` SID. It must match the account that owns the API key used to authenticate the request, otherwise the endpoint returns `404`. The same value is sent as `AccountSid` in TeXML webhooks.|
|body|body|[InitiateCallRequest](#schemainitiatecallrequest)|true|Initiate Call request object|
|» ApplicationSid|body|string|true|The ID of the TeXML Application that will handle the call, for example `1293384261075731499`. The `ApplicationSid` name is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is the numeric ID of one of your TeXML Applications (see the TeXML Applications API or the Mission Control Portal), not a Twilio `AP...` SID. If `Url` and `Texml` are omitted, Telnyx fetches instructions from the XML Request URL configured on this application.|
|» To|body|string|true|The phone number of the called party. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|» From|body|string|true|The phone number of the party that initiated the call. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|» CallerId|body|string|false|To be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`To` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and `-_~!.+` special characters. If ommited, the display name will be the same as the number in the `From` field.|
|» Url|body|string|false|The URL from which Telnyx will retrieve the TeXML call instructions.|
|» UrlMethod|body|string|false|HTTP request type used for `Url`. The default value is inherited from TeXML Application setting.|
|» FallbackUrl|body|string|false|A failover URL for which Telnyx will retrieve the TeXML call instructions if the `Url` is not responding.|
|» StatusCallback|body|string|false|URL destination for Telnyx to send status callback events to for the call.|
|» StatusCallbackMethod|body|string|false|HTTP request type used for `StatusCallback`.|
|» StatusCallbackEvent|body|string|false|The call events for which Telnyx should send a webhook. Multiple events can be defined when separated by a space.|
|» MachineDetection|body|string|false|Enables Answering Machine Detection.|
|» DetectionMode|body|string|false|Allows you to choose between Regular, Premium, and PremiumCallScreening detections. See https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/voice/programmable-voice/answering-machine-detection|
|» AsyncAmd|body|boolean|false|Select whether to perform answering machine detection in the background. By default execution is blocked until Answering Machine Detection is completed.|
|» AsyncAmdStatusCallback|body|string|false|URL destination for Telnyx to send AMD callback events to for the call.|
|» AsyncAmdStatusCallbackMethod|body|string|false|HTTP request type used for `AsyncAmdStatusCallback`. The default value is inherited from TeXML Application setting.|
|» MachineDetectionTimeout|body|integer|false|Maximum timeout threshold in milliseconds for overall detection.|
|» MachineDetectionPromptEndTimeout|body|integer|false|Silence duration threshold after a call screening prompt before ending prompt detection, in milliseconds. Used when `DetectionMode` is `PremiumCallScreening`.|
|» MachineDetectionSpeechThreshold|body|integer|false|Maximum threshold of a human greeting. If greeting longer than this value, considered machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|» MachineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold|body|integer|false|Silence duration threshold after a greeting message or voice for it be considered human. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|» MachineDetectionSilenceTimeout|body|integer|false|If initial silence duration is greater than this value, consider it a machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepProfile|body|string|false|Selects which detectors must validate a beep. `both` requires the amplitude and frequency detectors to agree. `freq_only` uses the frequency detector alone, for beeps whose volume is too unsteady for the default profile. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepMinFrequency|body|integer(int32)|false|Lowest frequency, in Hz, that a tone must reach to be treated as a beep. Raising it above 480 excludes North American ringback (440 + 480 Hz), which can otherwise be reported as a beep when the `freq_only` profile is in use. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepMaxFrequency|body|integer(int32)|false|Highest frequency, in Hz, that a tone can reach and still be treated as a beep. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepMinToneDuration|body|integer(int32)|false|Shortest tone, in milliseconds, that can be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects brief tones such as call-progress blips. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepSpectralConfirmation|body|boolean|false|When enabled, a candidate beep must pass an additional spectral check before it is reported. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepSpectralWindow|body|integer(int32)|false|Length of the spectral confirmation window, in milliseconds. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepSpectralMinPurity|body|number|false|Minimum spectral purity, from 0 to 1, for a tone to be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects mixed tones such as ringback, which combines two frequencies. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» MachineDetectionBeepSpectralRejectFaxCng|body|boolean|false|When enabled, the fax CNG tone is rejected rather than reported as a beep. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|» CancelPlaybackOnMachineDetection|body|boolean|false|Whether to cancel ongoing playback on `machine` detection. Defaults to `true`.|
|» CancelPlaybackOnDetectMessageEnd|body|boolean|false|Whether to cancel ongoing playback on `greeting ended` detection. Defaults to `true`.|
|» DeepfakeDetection|body|string|false|Enables Deepfake Detection on the dialed call. When enabled, audio from the remote party is analyzed to determine whether the voice is AI-generated. Results are delivered asynchronously via a callback.|
|» DeepfakeDetectionCallbackUrl|body|string|false|URL destination for Telnyx to send deepfake detection callback events to for the call.|
|» DeepfakeDetectionCallbackMethod|body|string|false|HTTP request type used for `DeepfakeDetectionCallbackUrl`.|
|» PreferredCodecs|body|string|false|The list of comma-separated codecs to be offered on a call.|
|» Record|body|boolean|false|Whether to record the entire participant's call leg. Defaults to `false`.|
|» RecordingChannels|body|string|false|The number of channels in the final recording. Defaults to `mono`.|
|» RecordingStatusCallback|body|string|false|The URL the recording callbacks will be sent to.|
|» RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|body|string|false|HTTP request type used for `RecordingStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|» RecordingStatusCallbackEvent|body|string|false|The changes to the recording's state that should generate a call to `RecoridngStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`.|
|» RecordingTimeout|body|integer|false|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that the transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite)|
|» RecordingTrack|body|string|false|The audio track to record for the call. The default is `both`.|
|» SendRecordingUrl|body|[SendRecordingUrl](#schemasendrecordingurl)|false|Whether to send RecordingUrl in webhooks.|
|» SipAuthPassword|body|string|false|The password to use for SIP authentication.|
|» SipAuthUsername|body|string|false|The username to use for SIP authentication.|
|» Trim|body|string|false|Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the recording. Defaults to `trim-silence`.|
|» CustomHeaders|body|[object]|false|Custom HTTP headers to be sent with the call. Each header should be an object with 'name' and 'value' properties.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the custom header|
|» » value|body|string|true|The value of the custom header|
|» SipRegion|body|string|false|Defines the SIP region to be used for the call.|
|» MediaEncryption|body|string|false|Defines whether media should be encrypted on the call. When set to `SRTP`, the call will use Secure Real-time Transport Protocol for media encryption. When set to `DTLS`, the call will use DTLS for media encryption. Only supported for SIP destinations.|
|» SuperviseCallSid|body|string|false|The call control ID of the existing call to supervise. When provided, the created leg will be added to the specified call in supervising mode. Status callbacks and action callbacks will NOT be sent for the supervising leg.|
|» SupervisingRole|body|string|false|The supervising role for the new leg. Determines the audio behavior: barge (hear both sides), whisper (only hear supervisor), monitor (hear both sides but supervisor muted). Default: barge|
|» Timeout|body|integer|false|The number of seconds to wait for the called party to answer the call before the call is canceled. The minimum value is 5 and the maximum value is 120. Default is 30 seconds.|
|» TimeLimit|body|integer|false|The maximum duration of the call in seconds. The minimum value is 30 and the maximum value is 14400 (4 hours). Default is 14400 seconds.|
|» Texml|body|string|false|TeXML to be used as instructions for the call. If provided, the call will execute these instructions instead of fetching from the Url.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» Texml|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» Url|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» Url|body|object|false|none|
|» Texml|body|object|false|none|

## Update call

<a id="opIdUpdateTexmlCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/texml/Accounts/f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9/Calls/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d 'Status=completed'
```

`POST /texml/Accounts/{account_sid}/Calls/{call_sid}`

Update TeXML call. Please note that the keys present in the payload MUST BE formatted in CamelCase as specified in the example.

> Body parameter

```yaml
Status: completed
```

<h3 id="update-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_sid|path|string|true|The CallSid that identifies the call to update.|
|account_sid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Telnyx account that owns the resource, for example `f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9`. The `account_sid` path segment is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is a Telnyx account UUID, not a Twilio `AC...` SID. It must match the account that owns the API key used to authenticate the request, otherwise the endpoint returns `404`. The same value is sent as `AccountSid` in TeXML webhooks.|
|body|body|[UpdateCallRequest](#schemaupdatecallrequest)|true|Update Call request object|
|» Status|body|string|false|The value to set the call status to. Setting the status to completed ends the call.|

## Request recording for a call

<a id="opIdStartTeXMLCallRecording"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/texml/Accounts/f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9/Calls/string/Recordings.json \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d 'PlayBeep=false&RecordingStatusCallbackEvent=in-progress%20completed%20absent&RecordingStatusCallback=http%3A%2F%2Fwebhook.com%2Fcallback&RecordingStatusCallbackMethod=GET&RecordingChannels=single&RecordingTrack=inbound&SendRecordingUrl=false'
```

`POST /texml/Accounts/{account_sid}/Calls/{call_sid}/Recordings.json`

Starts recording with specified parameters for call idientified by call_sid.

> Body parameter

```yaml
PlayBeep: false
RecordingStatusCallbackEvent: in-progress completed absent
RecordingStatusCallback: "http://webhook.com/callback"
RecordingStatusCallbackMethod: GET
RecordingChannels: single
RecordingTrack: inbound
SendRecordingUrl: false
```

<h3 id="request-recording-for-a-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_sid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Telnyx account that owns the resource, for example `f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9`. The `account_sid` path segment is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is a Telnyx account UUID, not a Twilio `AC...` SID. It must match the account that owns the API key used to authenticate the request, otherwise the endpoint returns `404`. The same value is sent as `AccountSid` in TeXML webhooks.|
|call_sid|path|string|true|The CallSid that identifies the call to update.|
|body|body|[TexmlCreateCallRecordingRequestBody](#schematexmlcreatecallrecordingrequestbody)|false|Starts call recording on a call.|
|» PlayBeep|body|[PlayBeep](#schemaplaybeep)|false|Whether to play a beep when recording is started.|
|» RecordingStatusCallbackEvent|body|[RecordingStatusCallbackEvent](#schemarecordingstatuscallbackevent)|false|The changes to the recording's state that should generate a call to `RecoridngStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`.|
|» RecordingStatusCallback|body|[TexmlStatusCallback](#schematexmlstatuscallback)|false|Url where status callbacks will be sent.|
|» RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|body|[TexmlStatusCallbackMethod](#schematexmlstatuscallbackmethod)|false|HTTP method used to send status callbacks.|
|» RecordingChannels|body|[TexmlRecordingChannels](#schematexmlrecordingchannels)|false|When `dual`, final audio file has the first leg on channel A, and the rest on channel B. `single` mixes both tracks into a single channel.|
|» RecordingTrack|body|[RecordingTrack](#schemarecordingtrack)|false|The audio track to record for the call. The default is `both`.|
|» SendRecordingUrl|body|[SendRecordingUrl](#schemasendrecordingurl)|false|Whether to send RecordingUrl in webhooks.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|GET|
|» RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|POST|
|» RecordingChannels|single|
|» RecordingChannels|dual|
|» RecordingTrack|inbound|
|» RecordingTrack|outbound|
|» RecordingTrack|both|

## Request siprec session for a call

<a id="opIdStartTeXMLSiprecSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/texml/Accounts/f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9/Calls/string/Siprec.json \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d 'ConnectorName=my_connector&Name=my_siprec_session&Track=both_tracks&IncludeMetadataCustomHeaders=true&Secure=true&SessionTimeoutSecs=900&SipTransport=tcp&StatusCallback=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.example.com%2Fcallback&StatusCallbackMethod=GET'
```

`POST /texml/Accounts/{account_sid}/Calls/{call_sid}/Siprec.json`

Starts siprec session with specified parameters for call idientified by call_sid.

> Body parameter

```yaml
ConnectorName: my_connector
Name: my_siprec_session
Track: both_tracks
IncludeMetadataCustomHeaders: true
Secure: true
SessionTimeoutSecs: 900
SipTransport: tcp
StatusCallback: "https://www.example.com/callback"
StatusCallbackMethod: GET
```

<h3 id="request-siprec-session-for-a-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_sid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Telnyx account that owns the resource, for example `f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9`. The `account_sid` path segment is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is a Telnyx account UUID, not a Twilio `AC...` SID. It must match the account that owns the API key used to authenticate the request, otherwise the endpoint returns `404`. The same value is sent as `AccountSid` in TeXML webhooks.|
|call_sid|path|string|true|The CallSid that identifies the call to update.|
|body|body|[TexmlCreateSiprecSessionRequestBody](#schematexmlcreatesiprecsessionrequestbody)|false|Starts a SIPREC session.|
|» ConnectorName|body|string|false|The name of the connector to use for the SIPREC session.|
|» Name|body|string|false|Name of the SIPREC session. May be used to stop the SIPREC session from TeXML instruction.|
|» Track|body|string|false|The track to be used for siprec session. Can be `both_tracks`, `inbound_track` or `outbound_track`. Defaults to `both_tracks`.|
|» IncludeMetadataCustomHeaders|body|boolean|false|When set, custom parameters will be added as metadata (recording.session.ExtensionParameters). Otherwise, they’ll be added to sip headers.|
|» Secure|body|boolean|false|Controls whether to encrypt media sent to your SRS using SRTP and TLS. When set you need to configure SRS port in your connector to 5061.|
|» SessionTimeoutSecs|body|integer|false|Sets `Session-Expires` header to the INVITE. A reinvite is sent every half the value set. Usefull for session keep alive. Minimum value is 90, set to 0 to disable.|
|» SipTransport|body|string|false|Specifies SIP transport protocol.|
|» StatusCallback|body|string|false|URL destination for Telnyx to send status callback events to for the siprec session.|
|» StatusCallbackMethod|body|string|false|HTTP request type used for `StatusCallback`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» Track|both_tracks|
|» Track|inbound_track|
|» Track|outbound_track|
|» IncludeMetadataCustomHeaders|true|
|» IncludeMetadataCustomHeaders|false|
|» Secure|true|
|» Secure|false|
|» SipTransport|udp|
|» SipTransport|tcp|
|» SipTransport|tls|
|» StatusCallbackMethod|GET|
|» StatusCallbackMethod|POST|

```bash
  -d 'StatusCallback=http%3A%2F%2Fwebhook.com%2Fcallback&StatusCallbackMethod=GET&Track=both_tracks&Name=My%20stream&BidirectionalMode=rtp&BidirectionalCodec=G722&Url=wss%3A%2F%2Fwww.example.com%2Fwebsocket'
```

`POST /texml/Accounts/{account_sid}/Calls/{call_sid}/Streams.json`

Starts streaming media from a call to a specific WebSocket address.

> Body parameter

```yaml
StatusCallback: "http://webhook.com/callback"
StatusCallbackMethod: GET
Track: both_tracks
Name: My stream
BidirectionalMode: rtp
BidirectionalCodec: G722
Url: "wss://www.example.com/websocket"
```

<h3 id="start-streaming-media-from-a-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_sid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Telnyx account that owns the resource, for example `f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9`. The `account_sid` path segment is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is a Telnyx account UUID, not a Twilio `AC...` SID. It must match the account that owns the API key used to authenticate the request, otherwise the endpoint returns `404`. The same value is sent as `AccountSid` in TeXML webhooks.|
|call_sid|path|string|true|The CallSid that identifies the call to update.|
|body|body|[TexmlCreateCallStreamingRequestBody](#schematexmlcreatecallstreamingrequestbody)|false|Start streaming media from a call|
|» StatusCallback|body|[TexmlStatusCallback](#schematexmlstatuscallback)|false|Url where status callbacks will be sent.|
|» StatusCallbackMethod|body|[TexmlStatusCallbackMethod](#schematexmlstatuscallbackmethod)|false|HTTP method used to send status callbacks.|
|» Track|body|[StreamTrack](#schemastreamtrack)|false|Tracks to be included in the stream|
|» Name|body|[StreamName](#schemastreamname)|false|The user specified name of Stream.|
|» BidirectionalMode|body|[TexmlBidirectionalStreamMode](#schematexmlbidirectionalstreammode)|false|Configures method of bidirectional streaming (mp3, rtp).|
|» BidirectionalCodec|body|[TexmlBidirectionalStreamCodec](#schematexmlbidirectionalstreamcodec)|false|Indicates codec for bidirectional streaming RTP payloads. Used only with stream_bidirectional_mode=rtp. Case sensitive.|
|» Url|body|[TexmlStreamUrl](#schematexmlstreamurl)|false|The destination WebSocket address where the stream is going to be delivered.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» StatusCallbackMethod|GET|
|» StatusCallbackMethod|POST|
|» Track|inbound_track|
|» Track|outbound_track|
|» Track|both_tracks|
|» BidirectionalMode|mp3|
|» BidirectionalMode|rtp|
|» BidirectionalCodec|PCMU|
|» BidirectionalCodec|PCMA|
|» BidirectionalCodec|G722|

## List conference resources

<a id="opIdGetTexmlConferences"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/texml/Accounts/f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9/Conferences \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /texml/Accounts/{account_sid}/Conferences`

Returns a paginated list of conference resources for the account, with support for filtering by friendly name, status, and creation or update dates.

<h3 id="list-conference-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_sid|path|string|true|The UUID of the Telnyx account that owns the resource, for example `f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9`. The `account_sid` path segment is kept for Twilio API compatibility, but the value is a Telnyx account UUID, not a Twilio `AC...` SID. It must match the account that owns the API key used to authenticate the request, otherwise the endpoint returns `404`. The same value is sent as `AccountSid` in TeXML webhooks.|
|Page|query|integer|false|The number of the page to be displayed, zero-indexed, should be used in conjuction with PageToken.|
|PageSize|query|integer|false|The number of records to be displayed on a page|
|PageToken|query|string|false|Used to request the next page of results.|
|FriendlyName|query|string|false|Filters conferences by their friendly name.|
|Status|query|string|false|Filters conferences by status.|
|DateCreated|query|string|false|Filters conferences by the creation date. Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD. Also accepts inequality operators, e.g. DateCreated>=2023-05-22.|
|DateUpdated|query|string|false|Filters conferences by the time they were last updated. Expected format is YYYY-MM-DD. Also accepts inequality operators, e.g. DateUpdated>=2023-05-22.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Status|init|
|Status|in-progress|
|Status|completed|

```json
  "end": 0,

  "next_page_uri": "/v2/texml/Accounts/61bf923e-5e4d-4595-a110-56190ea18a1b/Conferences.json?Page=1&PageSize=1&PageToken=MTY4AjgyNDkwNzIxMQ",

  "page_size": 1,
  "start": 0,
  "uri": "/v2/texml/Accounts/61bf923e-5e4d-4595-a110-56190ea18a1b/Conferences.json?Page=0&PageSize=1"
}
```

```json
    {
      "detail": "Resource not found"
    }
  ]
}
```
