<h1 id="telnyx-api-audio">Audio</h1>

## Transcribe speech to text

<a id="opIdaudio_public_audio_transcriptions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/audio/transcriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'file_url=https://example.com/file.mp3' \
  -F 'model=distil-whisper/distil-large-v2' \
  -F 'response_format=json' \
  -F 'timestamp_granularities[]=segment' \
  -F 'language=en-US' \
  -F 'model_config={"smart_format":true,"punctuate":true}'
```

`POST /ai/audio/transcriptions`

Transcribe speech to text. This endpoint is consistent with the [OpenAI Transcription API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/audio/createTranscription) and may be used with the OpenAI JS or Python SDK.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
file_url: "https://example.com/file.mp3"
model: distil-whisper/distil-large-v2
response_format: json
"timestamp_granularities[]": segment
language: en-US
model_config:
  smart_format: true
  punctuate: true
```

<h3 id="transcribe-speech-to-text-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AudioTranscriptionRequest](#schemaaudiotranscriptionrequest)|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|false|The audio file object to transcribe, in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm. File uploads are limited to 100 MB. Cannot be used together with `file_url`. Note: the `deepgram/*` models only support mp3 and wav formats.|
|» file_url|body|string|false|Link to audio file in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm. Support for hosted files is limited to 100MB. Cannot be used together with `file`. Note: the `deepgram/*` models only support mp3 and wav formats.|
|» model|body|string|true|ID of the model to use. `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` is lower latency but English-only. `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` is multi-lingual but slightly higher latency. The `deepgram/*` models only accept mp3/wav files: `deepgram/nova-3` covers ~49 languages plus `multi` and `deepgram/nova-2` covers ~33, while the `-medical` variants are tuned for clinical vocabulary and accept English only (`en` and its regional variants, e.g. `en-US`, `en-GB`). `nvidia/parakeet-v3` is multilingual with automatic language detection; `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1` is a medical model, English only. `reson8/prerecorded` covers 10 languages, returns word timestamps, and labels speakers via `model_config`.|
|» response_format|body|string|false|The format of the transcript output. Use `verbose_json` to take advantage of timestamps.|
|» timestamp_granularities[]|body|string|false|The timestamp granularities to populate for this transcription. `response_format` must be set verbose_json to use timestamp granularities. Currently `segment` is supported.|
|» language|body|string|false|The language of the audio to be transcribed. `deepgram/nova-3` supports ~49 languages plus `multi`, and `deepgram/nova-2` supports ~33 plus `multi`; the `-medical` variants are English only (`en` and its regional variants, e.g. `en-US`, `en-GB`). Deepgram models validate on the base language and forward the full tag, so regional variants such as `de-CH` and `pt-BR` are accepted where the base language is supported; an unsupported language returns a 400. For `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, supports multiple languages. `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` does not support language parameter. `nvidia/parakeet-v3` detects the language automatically; `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1` is English only. `reson8/prerecorded` accepts `nl`, `en`, `fr`, `fy`, `de`, `it`, `pl`, `pt`, `es` and `sv` (regional variants are transcribed as the base language) and detects the language when it is omitted.|
|» model_config|body|object|false|Additional model-specific configuration parameters. Only allowed with the `deepgram/*` models and `reson8/prerecorded`. Sent as a JSON string in multipart requests; for the `deepgram/*` models it is passed through to Deepgram as query parameters, while `reson8/prerecorded` accepts only `diarize` (speaker labels) and `max_speakers` (1 to 8). Any other model with `model_config` returns 400. Can include Deepgram-specific options such as `smart_format`, `punctuate`, `diarize` (speaker labels), `multichannel` (transcribe each channel independently; billed duration is file duration multiplied by the number of channels), `utterances`, `numerals`, and `language`. If `language` is provided both as a top-level parameter and in `model_config`, the top-level parameter takes precedence.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» model|distil-whisper/distil-large-v2|
|» model|openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo|
|» model|deepgram/nova-2|
|» model|deepgram/nova-2-medical|
|» model|deepgram/nova-3|
|» model|deepgram/nova-3-medical|
|» model|nvidia/parakeet-v3|
|» model|omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1|
|» model|reson8/prerecorded|
|» response_format|json|
|» response_format|verbose_json|
|» timestamp_granularities[]|segment|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "duration": 0,
  "segments": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "text": "string"
    }
  ],
  "words": [
    {
      "word": "string",
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "confidence": 0,
      "speaker": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[AudioTranscriptionResponse](#schemaaudiotranscriptionresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth

`POST /ai/mcp_servers`

Creates a new MCP server configuration on your account and returns the created server.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Name",
  "type": "Type",
  "url": "Url"
}
```

<h3 id="create-mcp-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same logical request. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each operation and reuse it only when retrying that operation with the same request. Invalid headers—including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—return 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.|
|body|body|[CreateMCPServerRequest](#schemacreatemcpserverrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» url|body|string|true|none|
|» api_key_ref|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» allowed_tools|body|[string]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "Id",
  "name": "Name",
  "type": "Type",
  "url": "Url",
  "created_at": "2024-01-23T18:10:02.574Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10036",
      "detail": "A request with this Idempotency-Key is already being processed.",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/header/Idempotency-Key"
      },
      "title": "Resource is being processed"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "body",
        "name"
      ],
      "msg": "Field required",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-mcp-server-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful Response|[MCPServer](#schemamcpserver)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request / Validation Failed (10015). Invalid, duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong Idempotency-Key headers are rejected by Edge with HTTP 400 and error code 10015.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|409|Conflict|A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still being processed (10036). Retry later with the same key and request.|[email_ErrorResponse](#schemaemail_errorresponse)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large. A request sent with an Idempotency-Key whose body exceeds the endpoint's Edge replay-protection limit (256 KB) is rejected before it reaches the service. Requests sent without the header are not subject to this limit.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error. Reusing an Idempotency-Key with a different request body also returns 422 with error code 10027.|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable (10016), including unavailable Edge idempotency protection for a keyed request.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|

<h3 id="create-mcp-server-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Idempotent-Replayed|boolean||Present with value `true` when Edge replayed a stored successful response for the supplied Idempotency-Key. Omitted for first-time requests and error responses.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

`DELETE /ai/mcp_servers/{mcp_server_id}`

Permanently deletes the specified MCP server configuration from your account.

<h3 id="delete-mcp-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mcp_server_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the mcp server.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10007",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": [
        "string"
      ],
      "msg": "Message",
      "type": "Error Type"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-mcp-server-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|MCP server deleted successfully. No content is returned.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request (10015). The MCP server cannot be deleted because it is still in use by an active assistant. A server counts as in use when it is referenced by an active assistant's live configuration or by any of its retained version snapshots — so deletion can be refused even when the assistant's current configuration (`mcp_servers`) no longer lists the server. The `detail` names the blocking assistant(s) and their IDs. Remove the server from the assistant's configuration and delete any retained assistant versions that still reference it (see DELETE /ai/assistants/{assistant_id}/versions/{version_id}), then retry.|[inference-embedding_ErrorResponse](#schemainference-embedding_errorresponse)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Error|[HTTPValidationError](#schemahttpvalidationerror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="telnyx-api-openai-chat">OpenAI Chat</h1>

## Create a chat completion (OpenAI-compatible)

<a id="opIdcreate_openai_chat_completion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/openai/chat/completions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "system",
        "content": "You are a friendly chatbot."
      },
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Hello, world!"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /ai/openai/chat/completions`

Chat with a language model. This endpoint is consistent with the [OpenAI Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat) and may be used with the OpenAI JS or Python SDK by setting the base URL to `https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/openai`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "You are a friendly chatbot."
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Hello, world!"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-chat-completion-openai-compatible-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ChatCompletionRequest](#schemachatcompletionrequest)|true|none|
|» messages|body|[[ChatCompletionSystemMessageParam](#schemachatcompletionsystemmessageparam)]|true|A list of the previous chat messages for context.|
|» model|body|string|false|The language model to chat with.|
|» service_tier|body|string|false|The service tier to use for this request. Supported values vary by model; use `GET /v2/ai/openai/models` and inspect the model's `service_tiers` field. If omitted, Telnyx-hosted models use `default`.|
|» region|body|string|false|Optional data-residency region the request should be served from, using the same vocabulary as your account's Data Locality setting. Behavior depends on `mode`. Supported for Telnyx-hosted models only: a request routed to an external provider never passes through Telnyx model routing, so a region cannot be enforced for it. Omit for today's latency-based routing.|
|» mode|body|string|false|How strictly `region` is applied. `preferred` (the default when `region` is set) tries that region first and falls back to another when the model cannot be served there, so a request that would have succeeded still succeeds. `strict` pins the request: it is served from that region or it fails with a 422, never redirected to another region. Requires `region`.|
|» api_key_ref|body|string|false|If you are using an external inference provider like xAI or OpenAI, this field allows you to pass along a reference to your API key. After creating an [integration secret](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) for you API key, pass the secret's `identifier` in this field.|
|» stream|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to stream data-only server-sent events as they become available.|
|» temperature|body|number|false|Adjusts the "creativity" of the model. Lower values make the model more deterministic and repetitive, while higher values make the model more random and creative.|
|» max_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|Maximum number of completion (output) tokens, including reasoning and answer tokens combined. An omitted or null limit defaults to 8192 unless the model is excluded from that default; excluded models leave the limit to the serving engine. Explicit values and applied defaults are clamped to the model's max_completion_tokens metadata when that ceiling is set (see GET /v2/ai/openai/models). An omitted limit on an excluded model remains unset even when metadata declares a ceiling. Input and output together must fit the model's context window. Set an explicit limit when a bounded generation budget is required. For example, omitted or null limits default to 8192 for `zai-org/GLM-5.3` and `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. Hosted exclusions include `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5`, `zai-org/GLM-5.2`, `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B`, `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct`, `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` and `google/gemma-2b-it`. Legacy external and fine-tuned model IDs can also bypass the default; model discovery reports completion ceilings, not whether this default applies. Set an explicit limit for predictable behavior across models.|
|» tools|body|[[ChatCompletionToolParam](#schemachatcompletiontoolparam) \| [Retrieval](#schemaretrieval)]|false|The `function` tool type follows the same schema as the [OpenAI Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat). The `retrieval` tool type is unique to Telnyx. You may pass a list of [embedded storage buckets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/embeddings/embed-documents) for retrieval-augmented generation.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ChatCompletionToolParam](#schemachatcompletiontoolparam)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[Retrieval](#schemaretrieval)|false|none|
|» tool_choice|body|string|false|none|
|» response_format|body|[ChatCompletionResponseFormatParam](#schemachatcompletionresponseformatparam)|false|Controls the format of the model output. `json_object` guarantees valid JSON output without defining a schema; `json_schema` constrains the output to the JSON schema you supply via the `json_schema` property and is the supported way to get guaranteed structured output on Telnyx-hosted models.|
|» min_p|body|number|false|This is an alternative to `top_p` that [many prefer](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/27670). Must be in [0, 1].|
|» n|body|number|false|This will return multiple choices for you instead of a single chat completion.|
|» use_beam_search|body|boolean|false|Setting this to `true` will allow the model to [explore more completion options](https://huggingface.co/blog/how-to-generate#beam-search). This is not supported by OpenAI.|
|» best_of|body|integer|false|This is used with `use_beam_search` to determine how many candidate beams to explore.|
|» length_penalty|body|number|false|This is used with `use_beam_search` to prefer shorter or longer completions.|
|» early_stopping|body|boolean|false|This is used with `use_beam_search`. If `true`, generation stops as soon as there are `best_of` complete candidates; if `false`, a heuristic is applied and the generation stops when is it very unlikely to find better candidates.|
|» logprobs|body|boolean|false|Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token returned in the `content` of `message`.|
|» top_logprobs|body|integer|false|This is used with `logprobs`. An integer between 0 and 20 specifying the number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log probability.|
|» frequency_penalty|body|number|false|Higher values will penalize the model from repeating the same output tokens.|
|» presence_penalty|body|number|false|Higher values will penalize the model from repeating the same output tokens.|
|» top_p|body|number|false|An alternative or complement to `temperature`. This adjusts how many of the top possibilities to consider.|
|» stop|body|string \| [string]|false|Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. The returned text will not contain the stop sequence.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» seed|body|integer|false|If specified, the system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same `seed` and parameters should return the same result.|
|» enable_thinking|body|boolean|false|Whether to enable the thinking/reasoning phase for models that support it (e.g., QwQ, Qwen3). When set to false, the model will skip the internal reasoning step and respond directly, which can reduce latency. Defaults to true.|
|» reasoning_effort|body|string|false|Controls the reasoning effort for models that support it. When set, the model spends more or less compute on internal reasoning before generating its response. Supported values: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Not all models support all values; unsupported values are rejected with a 400 error. When omitted, reasoning models use their default effort level.|

|» region|USA|
|» region|EU|
|» region|AUS|
|» region|UAE|
|» mode|preferred|
|» mode|strict|
|» tool_choice|none|
|» tool_choice|auto|
|» tool_choice|required|
|» reasoning_effort|none|
|» reasoning_effort|minimal|
|» reasoning_effort|low|
|» reasoning_effort|medium|
|» reasoning_effort|high|
|» reasoning_effort|xhigh|
|» reasoning_effort|max|

## Get available models (OpenAI-compatible)

<a id="opIdlist_openai_models"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/openai/models \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ai/openai/models`

Lists every model currently available to your account on Telnyx Inference, including SOTA open-source LLMs hosted on Telnyx GPUs (for example `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`, `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8`, and `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`), embedding models, and any fine-tuned models you have created.

Each entry is a `ModelMetadata` object describing the model id, owner, task, context length, supported languages, billing tier, pricing per 1M tokens, deployment regions, and whether the model supports vision or fine-tuning. Use this endpoint to discover model ids you can pass to `POST /v2/ai/openai/chat/completions`.

Model ids follow the `{organization}/{model_name}` convention from Hugging Face (for example `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`). This endpoint is OpenAI-compatible: clients pointed at `https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/openai` can call `client.models.list()` to retrieve the same payload.

```json
      },

}
```

## Create an OpenAI-compatible response

<a id="opIdchat_public_openai_responses_completions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/openai/responses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8",
    "conversation": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
    "instructions": "You are a friendly chatbot.",
    "input": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "input_text",
            "text": "Hello, world!"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "stream": false
  }'
```

`POST /ai/openai/responses`

Create a response using Telnyx's OpenAI-compatible Responses API. This endpoint is compatible with the [OpenAI Responses API](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/responses/overview) and may be used with the OpenAI JS or Python SDK by setting the base URL to `https://api.telnyx.com/v2/ai/openai`.

The `conversation` parameter refers to a Telnyx Conversation rather than an OpenAI-hosted conversation object. To persist a thread across turns, first [create a conversation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/create-a-conversation) with `POST /ai/conversations`, then pass that conversation's `id` in the Responses request as `conversation`. The endpoint appends the new input, assistant output, reasoning, and tool-call messages to that conversation. Reuse the same `conversation` id on subsequent Responses requests, including tool-result followups, so the model receives the prior context.

If `conversation` is omitted, the request is processed without persisting messages to a Telnyx conversation. Use the Conversations API to manage history: [list conversations](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/list-conversations) (optionally filtered by metadata), [fetch messages](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/get-conversation-messages) for a conversation, and optionally [add messages](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/conversations/create-message) outside the Responses flow.

You can attach arbitrary metadata when creating a conversation (for example to tag the conversation's source, channel, or user) and later filter by it when listing conversations.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8",
  "conversation": "6a09cdc3-8948-47f0-aa62-74ac943d6c58",
  "instructions": "You are a friendly chatbot.",
  "input": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "Hello, world!"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "stream": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-openai-compatible-response-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» model|body|string|false|Model identifier to use for the response, for example `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` or another model available from the Telnyx OpenAI-compatible models endpoint.|
|» service_tier|body|string|false|The service tier to use for this request. Supported values vary by model; use `GET /v2/ai/openai/models` and inspect the model's `service_tiers` field. If omitted, Telnyx-hosted models use `default`.|
|» region|body|string|false|Optional data-residency region the request should be served from, using the same vocabulary as your account's Data Locality setting. Behavior depends on `mode`. Supported for Telnyx-hosted models only: a request routed to an external provider never passes through Telnyx model routing, so a region cannot be enforced for it. Omit for today's latency-based routing.|
|» mode|body|string|false|How strictly `region` is applied. `preferred` (the default when `region` is set) tries that region first and falls back to another when the model cannot be served there, so a request that would have succeeded still succeeds. `strict` pins the request: it is served from that region or it fails with a 422, never redirected to another region. Requires `region`.|
|» input|body|object|false|The input items for this turn, using the OpenAI Responses API input format.|
|» conversation|body|string(uuid)|false|Optional Telnyx Conversation ID from `POST /ai/conversations`. When provided, Telnyx stores this turn on that conversation and uses the conversation's prior messages as context. Reuse the same ID for subsequent turns and tool-result followups. Omit it for a non-persisted, stateless response.|
|» instructions|body|string|false|Optional system/developer instructions for the model. When used with a persisted `conversation`, send these on the first request that creates the thread; subsequent turns can rely on the stored history.|
|» stream|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to stream Server-Sent Events, matching OpenAI's Responses streaming format.|
|» reasoning|body|object|false|none|
|» » effort|body|string|false|Controls the reasoning effort for models that support it. Same values and semantics as reasoning_effort on Chat Completions.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» region|USA|
|» region|EU|
|» region|AUS|
|» region|UAE|
|» mode|preferred|
|» mode|strict|
|» » effort|none|
|» » effort|minimal|
|» » effort|low|
|» » effort|medium|
|» » effort|high|
|» » effort|xhigh|
|» » effort|max|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "id": "resp_8b1f2a3c9d4e5f6a",
  "object": "response",
  "created_at": 1706011802,
  "status": "completed",

  "output": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "id": "msg_8b1f2a3c9d4e5f6a",
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "output_text",

        }
```

## Creates an authentication provider

<a id="opIdCreateAuthenticationProvider"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/authentication_providers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Okta",
    "short_name": "myorg",
    "active": true,
    "settings": {
      "idp_entity_id": "https://myorg.myidp.com/saml/metadata",
      "idp_sso_target_url": "https://myorg.myidp.com/trust/saml2/http-post/sso",
      "idp_cert_fingerprint": "13:38:C7:BB:C9:FF:4A:70:38:3A:E3:D9:5C:CD:DB:2E:50:1E:80:A7",
      "idp_cert_fingerprint_algorithm": "sha256"
    },
    "settings_url": "https://myorg.myidp.com/saml/metadata"
  }'
```

`POST /authentication_providers`

Creates a new authentication provider for single sign-on, configured from the provided identity provider details, and returns the created resource.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Okta",
  "short_name": "myorg",
  "active": true,
  "settings": {
    "idp_entity_id": "https://myorg.myidp.com/saml/metadata",
    "idp_sso_target_url": "https://myorg.myidp.com/trust/saml2/http-post/sso",
    "idp_cert_fingerprint": "13:38:C7:BB:C9:FF:4A:70:38:3A:E3:D9:5C:CD:DB:2E:50:1E:80:A7",
    "idp_cert_fingerprint_algorithm": "sha256"
  },
  "settings_url": "https://myorg.myidp.com/saml/metadata"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-an-authentication-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AuthenticationProviderCreate](#schemaauthenticationprovidercreate)|true|none|
|» name|body|[name](#schemaname)|true|The name associated with the authentication provider.|
|» short_name|body|[short_name](#schemashort_name)|true|The short name associated with the authentication provider. This must be unique and URL-friendly, as it's going to be part of the login URL.|
|» active|body|[active](#schemaactive)|false|The active status of the authentication provider|
|» settings|body|[settings](#schemasettings)|true|The settings associated with the authentication provider.|
|» settings_url|body|[settings_url](#schemasettings_url)|false|The URL for the identity provider metadata file to populate the settings automatically. If the settings attribute is provided, that will be used instead.|

|200|OK|Successful response|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request, the request was unacceptable, often due to missing a required parameter.|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity. Check the 'detail' field in response for details.|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Unexpected error|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|

<h3 id="retrieve-the-features-for-a-list-of-numbers-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|false|none|none|
|» phone_number|string|true|none|none|
|» features|[string]|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="telnyx-api-oauth-protocol">OAuth Protocol</h1>

## OAuth authorization endpoint

<a id="opIdAuthorizeOAuth"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.telnyx.com/v2/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=string&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Fexample.com'
```

`GET /oauth/authorize`

OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint for the authorization code flow

<h3 id="oauth-authorization-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|response_type|query|string|true|OAuth response type|
|client_id|query|string|true|OAuth client identifier|
|redirect_uri|query|string(uri)|true|Redirect URI|
|scope|query|string|false|Space-separated list of requested scopes|
|state|query|string|false|State parameter for CSRF protection|
|code_challenge|query|string|false|PKCE code challenge|
|code_challenge_method|query|string|false|PKCE code challenge method|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|response_type|code|
|code_challenge_method|plain|
|code_challenge_method|S256|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>Authorize application</title></head><body><h1>Authorize My App</h1><p>My App is requesting access to your Telnyx account.</p><button>Allow</button> <button>Deny</button></body></html>
```

> 400 Response

```text
<html><body>Authorization consent page</body></html>
```

<h3 id="oauth-authorization-endpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Consent page displayed (when consent UI is embedded)|Inline|
|302|Found|Redirect to consent page or client with authorization code/error|None|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Client not found|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid redirect URI|Inline|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Dynamic client registration

<a id="opIdRegisterOAuthClient"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/oauth/register \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "redirect_uris": [
      "https://example.com/callback"
    ],
    "client_name": "My OAuth Application",
    "grant_types": [
      "authorization_code"
    ],
    "response_types": [
      "code"
    ],
    "scope": "admin",
    "token_endpoint_auth_method": "client_secret_basic",
    "logo_uri": "http://example.com",
    "tos_uri": "http://example.com",
    "policy_uri": "http://example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /oauth/register`

Register a new OAuth client dynamically (RFC 7591)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "redirect_uris": [
    "https://example.com/callback"
  ],
  "client_name": "My OAuth Application",
  "grant_types": [
    "authorization_code"
  ],
  "response_types": [
    "code"
  ],
  "scope": "admin",
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "client_secret_basic",
  "logo_uri": "http://example.com",
  "tos_uri": "http://example.com",
  "policy_uri": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="dynamic-client-registration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OAuthDynamicRegistrationRequest](#schemaoauthdynamicregistrationrequest)|true|none|
|» redirect_uris|body|[string(uri)]|false|Array of redirection URI strings for use in redirect-based flows|
|» client_name|body|string|false|Human-readable string name of the client to be presented to the end-user|
|» grant_types|body|[string]|false|Array of OAuth 2.0 grant type strings that the client may use|
|» response_types|body|[string]|false|Array of the OAuth 2.0 response type strings that the client may use|
|» scope|body|string|false|Space-separated string of scope values that the client may use|
|» token_endpoint_auth_method|body|string|false|Authentication method for the token endpoint|
|» logo_uri|body|string(uri)|false|URL of the client logo|
|» tos_uri|body|string(uri)|false|URL of the client's terms of service|
|» policy_uri|body|string(uri)|false|URL of the client's privacy policy|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_types|authorization_code|
|» grant_types|client_credentials|
|» grant_types|refresh_token|
|» token_endpoint_auth_method|none|
|» token_endpoint_auth_method|client_secret_basic|
|» token_endpoint_auth_method|client_secret_post|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "client_id": "abc123def456",
  "client_secret": "string",
  "redirect_uris": [
    "http://example.com"
  ],
  "client_name": "string",
  "grant_types": [
    "string"
  ],
  "response_types": [
    "string"
  ],
  "scope": "string",
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "string",
  "client_id_issued_at": 0,
  "logo_uri": "http://example.com",
  "tos_uri": "http://example.com",
  "policy_uri": "http://example.com"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client_metadata",
  "error_description": "The client metadata was invalid",
  "invalid_fields": {
    "property1": [
      "string"
    ],
    "property2": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="dynamic-client-registration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Client registered successfully|[OAuthDynamicRegistrationResponse](#schemaoauthdynamicregistrationresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid client metadata|Inline|

<h3 id="dynamic-client-registration-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|false|none|none|
|error_description|string|false|none|none|
|invalid_fields|object|false|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|[string]|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## OAuth token endpoint

<a id="opIdExchangeOAuthToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/oauth/token \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "grant_type": "client_credentials",
    "scope": "admin",
    "code": "string",
    "redirect_uri": "http://example.com",
    "code_verifier": "string",
    "refresh_token": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /oauth/token`

Exchange authorization code, client credentials, or refresh token for access token

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "grant_type": "client_credentials",
  "scope": "admin",
  "code": "string",
  "redirect_uri": "http://example.com",
  "code_verifier": "string",
  "refresh_token": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="oauth-token-endpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TokenRequest](#schematokenrequest)|true|none|
|» grant_type|body|string|true|OAuth 2.0 grant type|
|» scope|body|string|false|Space-separated list of requested scopes (for client_credentials)|
|» code|body|string|false|Authorization code (for authorization_code flow)|
|» redirect_uri|body|string(uri)|false|Redirect URI (for authorization_code flow)|
|» code_verifier|body|string|false|PKCE code verifier (for authorization_code flow)|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|Refresh token (for refresh_token flow)|
|» client_id|body|string|false|OAuth client ID (if not using HTTP Basic auth)|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|OAuth client secret (if not using HTTP Basic auth)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_type|client_credentials|
|» grant_type|authorization_code|
|» grant_type|refresh_token|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 0,
  "scope": "string",
  "refresh_token": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_request"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client"
}
```

<h3 id="oauth-token-endpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Token response|[TokenResponse](#schematokenresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request|[oauth_oauth_Error](#schemaoauth_oauth_error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Invalid client credentials|[oauth_oauth_Error](#schemaoauth_oauth_error)|

Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
oauthClientAuth
</aside>

## Create a CSV download

<a id="opIdCreateCsvDownload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/phone_numbers/csv_downloads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /phone_numbers/csv_downloads`

Starts generation of a CSV export for phone numbers matching the supplied filters. The `csv_format` parameter selects the output format, and the response contains the resulting download record.

<h3 id="create-a-csv-download-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|csv_format|query|string|false|Which format to use when generating the CSV file. The default for backwards compatibility is 'V1'|
|filter|query|object|false|Consolidated filter parameter (deepObject style). Originally: filter[has_bundle], filter[tag], filter[connection_id], filter[phone_number], filter[status], filter[voice.connection_name], filter[voice.usage_payment_method], filter[billing_group_id], filter[emergency_address_id], filter[customer_reference]|
|include_managed_accounts|query|boolean|false|When true, the CSV includes phone numbers from all managed accounts in addition to the requesting account's own numbers. Only applies to V2 format; ignored for V1. The export appends `user_id` and `email` columns identifying the account that owns each number. When a filter is provided, it applies to the combined set of numbers. Requires access to managed accounts; requests without that access are rejected.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|csv_format|V1|
|csv_format|V2|

```json
      "url": "https://www.telnyx.com/sample/42587e44-3a3e-46de-9255-0c9a7a1d1ec7",
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create a Whatsapp hosted signup

<a id="opIdCreateWhatsappHostedSignup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.telnyx.com/v2/whatsapp/hosted_signups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "app_id": "123456789012345",
    "signup_type": "coexistence"
  }'
```

`POST /whatsapp/hosted_signups`

Create a time-limited onboarding URL on the Telnyx-hosted Embedded Signup page for a Tech Provider's end customer. Set `signup_type` to `coexistence` to launch Meta's WhatsApp Business app coexistence flow instead of standard Cloud API onboarding.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app_id": "123456789012345",
  "signup_type": "coexistence"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-whatsapp-hosted-signup-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WhatsappHostedSignupCreateRequest](#schemawhatsapphostedsignupcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» app_id|body|string|true|Meta App ID linked to the Telnyx account or its manager account. The app must be enabled.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|When the onboarding URL expires, in RFC 3339 format. Must be in the future and at most 3 days ahead. Defaults to 24 hours after creation.|
|» signup_type|body|string|false|Onboarding flow the hosted page launches. Use `coexistence` for a number that remains active in the WhatsApp Business app.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» signup_type|standard|
|» signup_type|coexistence|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "0192345a-7b8c-7d9e-0f12-3456789abcde",
    "record_type": "whatsapp_jwt",
    "app_id": "123456789012345",
    "created_at": "2026-07-08T12:00:00Z",
    "expires_at": "2026-07-09T12:00:00Z",
    "jwt": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
    "url": "https://acct.fyi?token=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
    "solution_id": "987654321098765"
  }
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10015",
      "title": "Bad request",
      "detail": "expires_at must be at most 3 days in the future"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "string",
      "title": "string",
      "detail": "string",
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/data/attributes/phone_number",
        "parameter": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="telnyx-api-webhooks-1">Webhooks</h1>

## Call AI Gather Ended

<a id="opIdCallAIGatherEnded"></a>

`POST CallAIGatherEnded`



This webhook uses Telnyx headers (telnyx-timestamp, telnyx-signature-ed25519) that are compatible with Standard Webhooks specification for SDK generation. Custom validation logic can map these to standard webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature equivalents. See https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks for details.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "event",
    "event_type": "call.ai_gather.ended",
    "id": "0ccc7b54-4df3-4bca-a65a-3da1ecc777f0",
    "occurred_at": "2018-02-02T22:25:27.521992Z",
    "payload": {
      "call_control_id": "v2:T02llQxIyaRkhfRKxgAP8nY511EhFLizdvdUKJiSw8d6A9BborherQ",
      "connection_id": "7267xxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
      "call_leg_id": "428c31b6-7af4-4bcb-b7f5-5013ef9657c1",
      "call_session_id": "428c31b6-7af4-4bcb-b7f5-5013ef9657c1",
      "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
      "from": "+35319605860",
      "to": "+35319605860",
      "status": "valid",
      "message_history": [
        {
          "content": "Hello, can you tell me your age and where you live?",
          "role": "assistant"
        },
        {
          "content": "Hello, I'm 29 and I live in Paris?",
          "role": "user"
        }
      ],
      "result": {
        "age": 29,
        "city": "Paris"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="call-ai-gather-ended-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|telnyx-timestamp|header|integer(int64)|true|Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) of when the webhook was sent - compatible with webhook-timestamp|
|telnyx-signature-ed25519|header|string|true|Base64 encoded Ed25519 signature for webhook verification - compatible with webhook-signature|
|body|body|[CallAIGatherEndedEvent](#schemacallaigatherendedevent)|true|none|
|» data|body|[CallAIGatherEnded](#schemacallaigatherended)|false|none|

<h3 id="call-ai-gather-ended-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The server must return an HTTP 200, otherwise we will reattempt delivery at the failover webhook URL.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## TeXML AI Gather

<a id="opIdTexmlAiGather"></a>

`POST TexmlAiGatherWebhook`

Webhook sent when AI Gather completes with transcription results.
This webhook uses Telnyx headers (telnyx-timestamp, telnyx-signature-ed25519) that are compatible with Standard Webhooks specification for SDK generation. Custom validation logic can map these to standard webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature equivalents. See https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks for details.

> Body parameter

```yaml
AccountSid: f5586561-8ff0-4291-a51b-c7dfe4139ff9
Base64MessageHistory: "W3sicm9sZSI6InVzZXIiLCJjb250ZW50IjoiSGVsbG8ifV0="
Base64Result: eyJzdGF0dXMiOiJ2YWxpZCIsInJlc3VsdCI6eyJ0ZXh0IjoiSSB3b3VsZCBsaWtlIHRvIHNjaGVkdWxlIGFuIGFwcG9pbnRtZW50In19
CallSid: "v3:9X2vxPDFY2RHSJ1EdMS0RHRksMTg7ldNxdjWbVr9zBjbGjGsSe-aiQ"
CallSidLegacy: "v3:9X2vxPDFY2RHSJ1EdMS0RHRksMTg7ldNxdjWbVr9zBjbGjGsSe-aiQ"
ConnectionId: "1234567890"
From: "+35319605860"
Status: valid
To: "+13129457420"
```

<h3 id="texml-ai-gather-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|telnyx-timestamp|header|integer(int64)|true|Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) of when the webhook was sent - compatible with webhook-timestamp|
|telnyx-signature-ed25519|header|string|true|Base64 encoded Ed25519 signature for webhook verification - compatible with webhook-signature|
|body|body|[TexmlAiGatherWebhookSchema](#schematexmlaigatherwebhookschema)|true|none|
|» AccountSid|body|string|true|The unique identifier of the account (user_id).|
|» Base64MessageHistory|body|string|false|Base64-encoded JSON array of message history (conditional).|

## artifact.completed

<a id="opIdMeetingArtifactCompletedWebhook"></a>

`POST artifactCompleted`

Sent when an artifact finishes generating -- `summary`, `action_items`, `decisions`, `topics`, `open_questions` or `custom`. Deliveries are best effort and not guaranteed: up to 5 attempts with backoff that starts around 60 seconds and roughly doubles per retry, and a 10-second delivery timeout, so respond with a 2xx promptly. Retries can produce duplicates; deduplicate on envelope `id`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "whdel_9f2c...",
  "event": "artifact.completed",
  "version": "1",
  "occurred_at": "2026-06-16T09:06:00Z",
  "data": {
    "session_id": "mtgsess_9b2f...",
    "artifact_id": "mtgart_4e7c...",
    "type": "summary",
    "content": {
      "text": "Decisions: hold pricing flat through Q3. Actions: Casey to send the summary."
    },
    "model_provenance": {
      "model": "example-model",
      "provider": "telnyx"
    },
    "prompt": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="artifactcompleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Meeting-Bot-Signature|header|string|true|Signature header `t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<hex>`. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with the webhook secret over the timestamp ASCII bytes, a literal `.` byte, and the exact raw request-body bytes; hex-encode and compare `v1` in constant time. Reject timestamps outside your accepted skew. No bearer token is sent.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|string|true|Unique event id; deduplicate deliveries on it.|
|» event|body|string|true|Event type.|
|» version|body|string|true|Envelope version.|
|» occurred_at|body|string(date-time)|true|When the event occurred.|
|» data|body|object|true|Completed artifact, including its generated content.|
|» » session_id|body|string|true|The meeting session this event belongs to.|
|» » artifact_id|body|string|true|Id of the completed artifact.|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of the completed artifact.|
|» » content|body|object|true|Generated artifact content.|
|» » » text|body|string|true|Generated artifact text.|
|» » model_provenance|body|object|true|Model that generated the artifact.|
|» » » model|body|string|true|none|
|» » » provider|body|string|true|none|
|» » prompt|body|string \| null|true|The prompt that produced this artifact, or null for a named type. Non-null only when `type` is `custom`; the five named types always return `null`.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event|artifact.completed|
|» » type|summary|
|» » type|action_items|
|» » type|decisions|
|» » type|topics|
|» » type|open_questions|
|» » type|custom|

<h3 id="artifactcompleted-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return any 2xx status promptly to acknowledge the delivery; non-2xx responses and timeouts are retried.|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Call analyzed

<a id="opIdCallAnalyzed"></a>

`POST callAnalyzed`



This webhook uses Telnyx headers (telnyx-timestamp, telnyx-signature-ed25519) that are compatible with Standard Webhooks specification for SDK generation. Custom validation logic can map these to standard webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature equivalents. See https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks for details.

Delivered after an AI assistant conversation ends and post-call processing completes. The payload consolidates the conversation's generated insights, its recordings, and the call's full cost breakdown (AI Voice Assistant engine minutes, LLM inference, call control, SIP trunking, recording).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "event",
    "event_type": "call.analyzed",
    "id": "afa6f4ac-f569-575b-9127-75a2746cf0ab",
    "occurred_at": "2026-10-15T20:38:46.308491Z",
```

## Call Conversation Created

<a id="opIdCallConversationCreated"></a>

`POST callConversationCreated`

Emitted when a conversation is created for a call, including when an AI assistant starts automatically after an `answer` command with `assistant.id` or a `dial` command with `assistant.id`, or through `ai_assistant_start` or `gather_using_ai`. Read `data.payload.conversation_id` and correlate it with `data.payload.call_control_id`.

For the answer-with-assistant flow, the `answer` response does not include the conversation ID. This webhook supplies it during assistant startup without waiting for `call.conversation.ended` or polling the Conversations API. It is delivered to the configured Call Control webhook URL and does not require `send_message_history_updates`.

The event indicates that the conversation was created; it does not confirm that the assistant is ready to speak or that greeting audio has started.

This webhook uses Telnyx headers (telnyx-timestamp, telnyx-signature-ed25519) that are compatible with Standard Webhooks specification for SDK generation. Custom validation logic can map these to standard webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature equivalents. See https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks for details.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "event",
    "event_type": "call.conversation.created",
    "id": "eb8775a6-634f-48b0-b177-d5465a8a8e9f",
    "occurred_at": "2025-05-29T13:35:38.817785Z",
    "created_at": "2025-05-29T13:35:38.927621Z",

      "call_control_id": "v3:HDR1vQHx697hpP9xZ0bhlbUOWPFPDtPcxw-nuSMuC6mGVpb0euoklQ",
      "call_leg_id": "cc29cce6-3c91-11f0-a8e5-02420aef3d20",
      "call_session_id": "cc29c8d6-3c91-11f0-aa7c-02420aef3d20",
      "client_state": "g3QAAAACbQAAAAtkYXRhX2NlbnRlcm0AAAADY2gxbQAAAApkZXBsb3ltZW50bQAAAARiYXNl",
      "connection_id": "2694492062593582591",
      "conversation_id": "0424805b-adc1-4ff8-9f95-e1de6883ecbe",
      "from": "+13124287921",
      "to": "+13125550100"
    }
  }
}
```

## Call Conversation Start Failed

<a id="opIdCallConversationStartFailed"></a>

`POST callConversationStartFailed`

Emitted when an AI assistant requested with an `answer` or `dial` command (`assistant.id`) could not be started after the call was answered, for example because the assistant ID does not exist. No conversation is created, so neither `call.conversation.created` nor `call.conversation.ended` is sent for this attempt. The call stays answered: use this event to continue the call, for example by transferring it, playing a message, or hanging up. `data.payload.reason` is `invalid_request` when the request was rejected and `service_error` otherwise.

This webhook uses Telnyx headers (telnyx-timestamp, telnyx-signature-ed25519) that are compatible with Standard Webhooks specification for SDK generation. Custom validation logic can map these to standard webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature equivalents. See https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks for details.

## session.status_changed

<a id="opIdMeetingSessionStatusChangedWebhook"></a>

`POST sessionStatusChanged`

Sent when the session moves to a new lifecycle status. Deliveries are best effort and not guaranteed: up to 5 attempts with backoff that starts around 60 seconds and roughly doubles per retry, and a 10-second delivery timeout, so respond with a 2xx promptly. Retries can produce duplicates; deduplicate on envelope `id`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "whdel_9f2c...",
  "event": "session.status_changed",
  "version": "1",
  "occurred_at": "2026-06-16T09:00:05Z",
  "data": {
    "session_id": "mtgsess_9b2f...",
    "status": "active",
    "status_detail": null,
    "recording": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="sessionstatuschanged-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Meeting-Bot-Signature|header|string|true|Signature header `t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<hex>`. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with the webhook secret over the timestamp ASCII bytes, a literal `.` byte, and the exact raw request-body bytes; hex-encode and compare `v1` in constant time. Reject timestamps outside your accepted skew. No bearer token is sent.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|string|true|Unique event id; deduplicate deliveries on it.|
|» event|body|string|true|Event type.|
|» version|body|string|true|Envelope version.|
|» occurred_at|body|string(date-time)|true|When the event occurred.|
|» data|body|object|true|Status transition details.|
|» » session_id|body|string|true|The meeting session this event belongs to.|
|» » status|body|string|true|The new session status.|
|» » status_detail|body|string \| null|true|Additional detail about the status (for example `cancelled`), or null.|
|» » recording|body|boolean|true|Whether the session is recording at this lifecycle edge.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event|session.status_changed|

<h3 id="sessionstatuschanged-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return any 2xx status promptly to acknowledge the delivery; non-2xx responses and timeouts are retried.|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## transcript.completed

<a id="opIdMeetingTranscriptCompletedWebhook"></a>

## WhatsApp WABA Added

<a id="opIdWhatsappWabaAdded"></a>

`POST whatsappWabaAdded`

Reports the outcome of a WhatsApp Embedded Signup session. Telnyx sends it to the `webhook_url` set with `PATCH /v2/whatsapp/user_data` when the session succeeds or fails.

This webhook uses Telnyx headers (telnyx-timestamp, telnyx-signature-ed25519) that are compatible with Standard Webhooks specification for SDK generation. Custom validation logic can map these to standard webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature equivalents. See https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks for details.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": {
    "record_type": "event",
    "id": "5d4f8c1a-6b2e-4f3a-9c7d-2e1b0a9f8e7d",
    "event_type": "whatsapp.waba_added",
    "occurred_at": "2026-10-01T10:02:11.000Z",
    "payload": {
      "record_type": "waba_account_added",
      "waba_id": "123456789012345",
      "phone_numbers": [
        "+15551234567"
      ],
      "status": "SUCCESS",
      "event_id": "019f4253-e09a-7622-bc6f-625378711d78"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="whatsapp-waba-added-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|telnyx-timestamp|header|integer(int64)|true|Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) of when the webhook was sent - compatible with webhook-timestamp|
|telnyx-signature-ed25519|header|string|true|Base64 encoded Ed25519 signature for webhook verification - compatible with webhook-signature|
|body|body|[WhatsappWabaAddedEvent](#schemawhatsappwabaaddedevent)|true|none|
|» data|body|[WhatsappWabaAdded](#schemawhatsappwabaadded)|true|none|

<h3 id="whatsapp-waba-added-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return an HTTP 200 to acknowledge the webhook.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

```json
  "value": "{{#integration_secret}}my_agent_api_key{{/integration_secret}}"
}
```

A header sent when fetching an A2A agent's card and on every call made to that agent.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|HTTP header name. May only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores, or a `{{dynamic_variable}}` placeholder surrounded by those characters.|
|value|string|true|none|Header value, stored exactly as written. It may be a literal, a `{{dynamic_variable}}`, or an `{{#integration_secret}}identifier{{/integration_secret}}` section that resolves to a stored integration secret when the conversation starts. Control characters are not allowed. The encrypted `{{variable \| encryption_secret_ref}}` form used for per-caller credentials is not resolved here and is rejected when the assistant is saved.|

|send_message_history_updates|boolean|false|none|When `true`, a `call.ai_gather.message_history_updated` webhook carrying the full message history is sent each time the conversation message history is updated. |participants|[[AIAssistantJoinParticipant](#schemaaiassistantjoinparticipant)]|false|none|A list of participants to add to the conversation when it starts.|

<h2 id="tocS_AccountEmailEvent">AccountEmailEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccountemailevent"></a>
<a id="schema_AccountEmailEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSaccountemailevent"></a>
<a id="tocsaccountemailevent"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "event_type": "email.delivered",
  "canonical_event_type": "email.delivered",
  "occurred_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "recipient_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "payload": {
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "recipient_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "status": "queued",
    "occurred_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "from": {
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "to": {
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "name": "string",
      "kind": "to"
    },
    "cc": {
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "name": "string",
      "kind": "to"
    },
    "bcc": {
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "name": "string",
      "kind": "to"
    },
    "subject": "string"
  }
}
```

An account-polling event. The envelope is webhook-shaped, but polling preserves stored-event cardinality: queued, sending, sandbox, cancelled, and daily_limit_exceeded message events fan out per recipient; scheduled remains one message-scoped row. Payload fields vary among recipient-scoped, message-scoped, and minimal fallback rows.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|Event UUID.|
|event_type|string|true|none|Legacy customer-visible event name, prefixed with `email.`. Gateway rejections render `email.failed`; MTA expirations render `email.bounced`. Webhook subscription allowlists match the legacy name.|
|canonical_event_type|string|true|none|Additive canonical outcome name, prefixed with `email.`. Gateway rejection is `email.gw_reject`, ambiguous injection timeout is `email.injection_timeout`, and MTA expiration is `email.expired`. Unchanged outcomes retain their names. Existing stored rows are translated only when recorded payload evidence proves the outcome; a legacy failed row is not guessed or sharpened.|
|occurred_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|recipient_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Durable email recipient UUID. Present for recipient-scoped events, including each queued, sending, sandbox, cancelled, and daily_limit_exceeded fan-out event.|
|payload|[AccountEmailEventPayload](#schemaaccountemaileventpayload)|true|none|Payload returned by GET /email_events. Every row includes id, status, and occurred_at. Recipient-scoped rows also include recipient_id, from, subject, and exactly one object-valued to, cc, or bcc field. Legacy or message-scoped rows can omit recipient_id and use object-valued or string-valued to/cc fields, including an empty string when no address exists; bcc is redacted. If the related message or recipient cannot be loaded, the minimal fallback can omit from, subject, and recipient fields. Additional persisted public evidence can be present.|

```json
{
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "recipient_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
```

Payload returned by GET /email_events. Every row includes id, status, and occurred_at. Recipient-scoped rows also include recipient_id, from, subject, and exactly one object-valued to, cc, or bcc field. Legacy or message-scoped rows can omit recipient_id and use object-valued or string-valued to/cc fields, including an empty string when no address exists; bcc is redacted. If the related message or recipient cannot be loaded, the minimal fallback can omit from, subject, and recipient fields. Additional persisted public evidence can be present.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|Email message UUID.|
|recipient_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Durable email recipient UUID. Present for recipient-scoped events.|
|status|string|true|none|Stored event outcome slug, not the authoritative recipient status. Account polling returns the stored name, including suppression, scan, and quarantine lifecycle names. Webhooks retain legacy payload names: gateway rejections use failed and MTA expirations use bounced. New sharp stored rows can expose gw_reject, injection_timeout, or expired. Use the envelope canonical_event_type to identify the outcome across surfaces.|
|occurred_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|from|[AccountEmailEventSender](#schemaaccountemaileventsender)|false|none|Sender projection in account event polling. The display name is explicitly null when the message has no sender name.|
|to|[EmailWebhookRecipient](#schemaemailwebhookrecipient) \| string|false|none|none|
|cc|[EmailWebhookRecipient](#schemaemailwebhookrecipient) \| string|false|none|none|
|bcc|[EmailWebhookRecipient](#schemaemailwebhookrecipient) \| string|false|none|none|
|subject|string|false|none|none|

```json
  "idempotency_key": "string"
}
```

Discriminated union on type. Variants are strict: unknown fields are rejected with 400. Reusing an idempotency_key with an identical request replays the original resource; with a different request it returns 409 idempotency_conflict.

### Properties

|*oneOf*|[ClickAction](#schemaclickaction)|false|none|Click an element identified by observation_id + ref.|
|*oneOf*|[FillAction](#schemafillaction)|false|none|Type text into the element identified by observation_id + ref.|
|*oneOf*|[SelectAction](#schemaselectaction)|false|none|Select an option on the element identified by observation_id + ref.|
|*oneOf*|[PressAction](#schemapressaction)|false|none|Press a keyboard key.|
|*oneOf*|[ScrollAction](#schemascrollaction)|false|none|Scroll the page.|
|*oneOf*|[ScreenshotAction](#schemascreenshotaction)|false|none|Capture a screenshot of the current page.|
|*oneOf*|[WaitForAction](#schemawaitforaction)|false|none|Wait for a condition before continuing.|
|*oneOf*|[BatchAction](#schemabatchaction)|false|none|Execute 1-50 sub-actions sequentially. Non-recursive: a batch inside a batch is rejected (400). An empty array is rejected (400). A failed sub-action stops the batch; earlier browser mutations are not rolled back, but partial sub-action results are not returned.|

This should be left with the default value of `true` unless you have used the `/addresses/actions/validate` endpoint to validate the address separately prior to creation. If an address is not validated for emergency use upon creation and it is not valid, it will not be able to be used for emergency services. In an address record, this flag indicates whether emergency validation was performed at creation: `true` means the record passed emergency validation before it was created; `false` means validation was skipped during this creation request, and the address may have been validated separately. This flag is not a current validity status; emergency use still requires a valid address.|

|assistant|[CallAssistantRequest](#schemacallassistantrequest)|false|none|AI Assistant configuration and per-call overrides. All fields except `id` are optional. Omitted assistant fields use the stored configuration. Supplied `voice_settings` and `transcription` objects replace their stored objects rather than merging individual settings; include every setting you want to retain. `dynamic_variables` are merged, with request values taking precedence.|
|conversation_relay_config|[ConversationRelayEmbeddedConfig](#schemaconversationrelayembeddedconfig)|false|none|Starts a Conversation Relay session automatically when the answered/dialed call is answered. This embedded shape is supported on `answer` and `dial`. It uses public field names (`url`, `dtmf_detection`, `greeting`, `voice`, `language`, etc.) and maps them to the underlying Conversation Relay action. `client_state`, `tts_language`, and `transcription_language` inside this object are ignored; use the parent command's `client_state` and `command_id` fields instead.|
|billing_group_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Use this field to set the Billing Group ID for the call. Must be a valid and existing Billing Group ID.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|custom_headers|[[CustomSipHeader](#schemacustomsipheader)]|false|none|Custom headers to be added to the SIP INVITE response.|
|preferred_codecs|string|false|none|The list of comma-separated codecs in a preferred order for the forked media to be received.|
|sip_headers|[[SipHeader](#schemasipheader)]|false|none|SIP headers to be added to the SIP INVITE response. Currently only User-to-User header is supported.|
|sound_modifications|[SoundModifications](#schemasoundmodifications)|false|none|Use this field to modify sound effects, for example adjust the pitch.|
|stream_url|string|false|none|The destination WebSocket address where the stream is going to be delivered.|
|stream_track|string|false|none|Specifies which track should be streamed.|
|stream_codec|[StreamCodec](#schemastreamcodec)|false|none|Specifies the codec to be used for the streamed audio. When set to 'default' or when transcoding is not possible, the codec from the call will be used.|
|stream_bidirectional_mode|[StreamBidirectionalMode](#schemastreambidirectionalmode)|false|none|Configures method of bidirectional streaming (mp3, rtp).|
|stream_bidirectional_codec|[StreamBidirectionalCodec](#schemastreambidirectionalcodec)|false|none|Indicates codec for bidirectional streaming RTP payloads. Used only with stream_bidirectional_mode=rtp. Case sensitive.|
|stream_bidirectional_target_legs|[StreamBidirectionalTargetLegs](#schemastreambidirectionaltargetlegs)|false|none|Specifies which call legs should receive the bidirectional stream audio.|
|send_silence_when_idle|boolean|false|none|Generate silence RTP packets when no transmission available.|
|webhook_url|string|false|none|Use this field to override the URL for which Telnyx will send subsequent webhooks to for this call.|
|webhook_url_method|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `webhook_url`.|
|transcription|boolean|false|none|Enable standalone call transcription upon call answer. The default value is false. Configure this feature with `transcription_config`. To configure speech recognition for an AI assistant, use `assistant.transcription` instead.|
|transcription_config|[TranscriptionStartRequest](#schematranscriptionstartrequest)|false|none|none|
|record|string|false|none|Start recording automatically after an event. Disabled by default.|
|record_channels|string|false|none|Defines which channel should be recorded ('single' or 'dual') when `record` is specified.|
|record_format|string|false|none|Defines the format of the recording ('wav' or 'mp3') when `record` is specified.|
|record_max_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Defines the maximum length for the recording in seconds when `record` is specified. The minimum value is 0. The maximum value is 43200. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_timeout_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected when `record` is specified. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that call transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_track|string|false|none|The audio track to be recorded. Can be either `both`, `inbound` or `outbound`. If only single track is specified (`inbound`, `outbound`), `channels` configuration is ignored and it will be recorded as mono (single channel).|
|record_trim|string|false|none|When set to `trim-silence`, silence will be removed from the beginning and end of the recording.|
|record_custom_file_name|string|false|none|The custom recording file name to be used instead of the default `call_leg_id`. Telnyx will still add a Unix timestamp suffix.|
|webhook_urls|object|false|none|A map of event types to arrays of webhook URLs. When an event of the specified type occurs, the webhook URLs associated with that event type will be called instead of `webhook_url`. Events not mapped here will use the default `webhook_url`.|
|webhook_urls_method|string|false|none|HTTP request method to invoke `webhook_urls`.|
|webhook_retries_policies|object|false|none|A map of event types to retry policies. Each retry policy contains an array of `retries_ms` specifying the delays between retry attempts in milliseconds. Maximum 5 retries, total delay cannot exceed 60 seconds.|
|deepfake_detection|object|false|none|Enables deepfake detection on the call. When enabled, audio from the remote party is streamed to a detection service that analyzes whether the voice is AI-generated. Results are delivered via the `call.deepfake_detection.result` webhook.|

```json
  ],

  "mode": "preferred"

```

Anthropic Messages-compatible request with Telnyx extensions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|The model to use for generating the response, for example `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` or another model available from the Telnyx models endpoint.|
|messages|[object]|true|none|The messages to send to the model, following the [Anthropic Messages API](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/messages) format.|
|max_tokens|integer|true|none|The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.|
|system|string \| [object]|false|none|System prompt. Can be a string or an array of content blocks following the Anthropic API format.|
|stream|boolean|false|none|Whether to stream the response as Anthropic-format Server-Sent Events.|
|temperature|number|false|none|Amount of randomness injected into the response. Ranges from 0 to 1.|
|top_p|number|false|none|Nucleus sampling parameter. Use temperature or top_p, but not both.|
|top_k|integer|false|none|Top-k sampling parameter. Only sample from the top K options for each subsequent token.|
|stop_sequences|[string]|false|none|Custom sequences that will cause the model to stop generating.|
|metadata|object|false|none|An object describing metadata about the request.|
|tools|[object]|false|none|Definitions of tools that the model may use, following the Anthropic API format.|
|tool_choice|object|false|none|Controls how the model uses tools, following the Anthropic API format.|
|thinking|object|false|none|Extended thinking configuration for models that support it. Set `type` to `enabled` to turn on extended thinking.|
|api_key_ref|string|false|none|If you are using an external inference provider, this field allows you to pass along a reference to your API key. After creating an [integration secret](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) for your API key, pass the secret's `identifier` in this field.|
|mcp_servers|[object]|false|none|List of MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to make available to the model.|
|fallback_config|object|false|none|Configuration for model fallback behavior when the primary model is unavailable.|
|billing_group_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The billing group ID to associate with this request.|
|timeout|number|false|none|Request timeout in seconds.|
|max_retries|integer|false|none|Maximum number of retries for the request.|
|service_tier|string|false|none|The service tier to use for this request. Supported values vary by model; use the Telnyx models endpoint and inspect the model's `service_tiers` field. If omitted, Telnyx-hosted models use `default`.|
|region|string|false|none|Optional data-residency region the request should be served from, using the same vocabulary as your account's Data Locality setting. Behavior depends on `mode`. Supported for Telnyx-hosted models only: a request routed to an external provider never passes through Telnyx model routing, so a region cannot be enforced for it. Omit for today's latency-based routing.|
|mode|string|false|none|How strictly `region` is applied. `preferred` (the default when `region` is set) tries that region first and falls back to another when the model cannot be served there, so a request that would have succeeded still succeeds. `strict` pins the request: it is served from that region or it fails with a 422, never redirected to another region. Requires `region`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|region|USA|
|region|EU|
|region|AUS|
|region|UAE|
|mode|preferred|
|mode|strict|

<h2 id="tocS_ArithmeticExpression">ArithmeticExpression</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaarithmeticexpression"></a>

<a id="tocSarithmeticexpression"></a>
<a id="tocsarithmeticexpression"></a>

```json
{
  "left": {
    "name": "cart_total",
    "type": "variable"
  },
  "op": "+",
  "right": {
    "name": "shipping_cost",
    "type": "variable"
  },
  "type": "arithmetic"
}
```

Numeric expression: applies an arithmetic operator to two sub-expressions.

Useful for derived numeric checks, e.g. `cart_total + shipping > 50`.
Both operands should resolve to numbers at runtime.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|left|[Expression](#schemaexpression)|true|none|A node in a deterministic expression AST. Exactly one variant is selected by the `type` discriminator. Terminal variants (`number_literal`, `string_literal`, `bool_literal`, `variable`) bottom out the recursion; `arithmetic`, `bool_op`, and `comparison` nest further sub-expressions.<br><br>Extracted into a single named schema so the recursive union is defined once (was previously inlined at every operand site).|
|op|string|true|none|Arithmetic operator applied to `left` and `right`.|
|right|[Expression](#schemaexpression)|true|none|A node in a deterministic expression AST. Exactly one variant is selected by the `type` discriminator. Terminal variants (`number_literal`, `string_literal`, `bool_literal`, `variable`) bottom out the recursion; `arithmetic`, `bool_op`, and `comparison` nest further sub-expressions.<br><br>Extracted into a single named schema so the recursive union is defined once (was previously inlined at every operand site).|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|op|+|
|op|-|
|op|*|
|op|/|
|op|%|
