<h2 id="tocS_AssistantA2AAgent">AssistantA2AAgent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistanta2aagent"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantA2AAgent"></a>
<a id="tocSassistanta2aagent"></a>
<a id="tocsassistanta2aagent"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "billing_agent",
  "url": "https://agents.example.com",
  "headers": [
    {
      "name": "X-Api-Key",
      "value": "{{#integration_secret}}my_agent_api_key{{/integration_secret}}"
    }
  ],
  "async": false,
  "timeout_ms": 30000,
  "poll_interval_ms": 500,
  "messages": [
    {
      "type": "request_start",
      "content": "string",
      "timing_ms": 100
    }
  ]
}
```

A remote agent, reachable over the A2A (Agent2Agent) protocol, that an assistant can delegate to. Tools are not configured here: at the start of every conversation the agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|Identifies the agent and seeds the names of the tools derived from its card (`a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`). Characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` are replaced with `_` before the tool name is built, so two agents whose names differ only in punctuation collide and are rejected.|
|url|string|true|none|The agent's base URL, or the URL of its agent card. At most 2,048 bytes once UTF-8 encoded. `/.well-known/agent-card.json` is appended to the path unless it already ends in `.json`. Must be an `http://` or `https://` URL for an externally reachable host: internal destinations (`localhost`, private and reserved IP ranges, `.local` domains) are rejected, and the hostname may not contain a `{{...}}` placeholder. Placeholders in the path are allowed.|
|headers|[[A2AAgentHeader](#schemaa2aagentheader)]|false|none|Headers sent when fetching this agent's card and on every call made to it. Use them to authenticate to the agent.|
|async|boolean|false|none|When `true`, the assistant hands the turn straight back to the model and the agent's answer is delivered into the conversation once it arrives, instead of the caller waiting for it in silence.|
|timeout_ms|integer|false|none|Total budget, in milliseconds, for one call to this agent, including any time spent polling a task that is still running. Omit to inherit the assistant's tool timeout.|
|poll_interval_ms|integer|false|none|How often, in milliseconds, to poll an agent task that has not finished yet. Defaults to 500.|
|messages|[object]|false|none|Filler messages spoken while a call to this agent is in progress. `request_start` messages are spoken immediately when the call begins. `request_response_delayed` messages are spoken after `timing_ms` has elapsed only if the agent has not answered yet. Filler messages are not used when `async` is `true`.|

<h2 id="tocS_AssistantTarget">AssistantTarget</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistanttarget"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantTarget"></a>
<a id="tocSassistanttarget"></a>
<a id="tocsassistanttarget"></a>

```json
{
  "assistant_id": "assistant-billing",
  "position": {
    "x": 600,
    "y": 80
  },
  "type": "assistant",
  "voice_mode": "unified"
}
```

Edge target referencing a different assistant.

When the edge fires, the conversation hands off to `assistant_id`: the
active assistant on the conversation row is rewritten and the new
assistant's flow starts at its own `start_node_id`. The current turn's
LLM response is delivered to the user as-is; subsequent turns route
to the new assistant.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant_id|string|true|none|ID of the assistant the conversation transitions to.|
|position|[NodePosition](#schemanodeposition)|false|none|Optional canvas coordinates for rendering the target assistant as a node in authoring UIs. Pure presentation — the runtime ignores it; round-trips so frontends can persist graph layout across reloads. When multiple edges target the same assistant, each edge's `position` is independent (frontends typically use the first non-null one).|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|voice_mode|string|false|none|Voice behavior when handing off to the target assistant, mirroring the handoff tool's `voice_mode`. `unified` (default) keeps the current voice across the handoff; `distinct` lets the target assistant speak with its own configured voice. Only applies to assistant targets — node targets override voice via the node's own `voice_settings`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|voice_mode|unified|
|voice_mode|distinct|

```json
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "parameters": {}
    }
  }
]
```

Deprecated for new integrations. Inline tool definitions available to the assistant. Prefer `tool_ids` to attach shared tools created with the AI Tools endpoints. On update, a sent `tools` array fully replaces the assistant's inline tools; omit the field to leave them unchanged. Each tool type except `function`, `webhook`, and `client_side_tool` allows at most one instance per assistant, counted across inline `tools` and shared `tool_ids` combined.

<h2 id="tocS_AudioTranscriptionRequest">AudioTranscriptionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaudiotranscriptionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_AudioTranscriptionRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSaudiotranscriptionrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsaudiotranscriptionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "file": "string",
  "file_url": "https://example.com/file.mp3",
  "model": "distil-whisper/distil-large-v2",
  "response_format": "json",
  "timestamp_granularities[]": "segment",
  "language": "en-US",
  "model_config": {
    "smart_format": true,
    "punctuate": true
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file|string(binary)|false|none|The audio file object to transcribe, in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm. File uploads are limited to 100 MB. Cannot be used together with `file_url`. Note: the `deepgram/*` models only support mp3 and wav formats.|
|file_url|string|false|none|Link to audio file in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm. Support for hosted files is limited to 100MB. Cannot be used together with `file`. Note: the `deepgram/*` models only support mp3 and wav formats.|
|model|string|true|none|ID of the model to use. `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` is lower latency but English-only. `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` is multi-lingual but slightly higher latency. The `deepgram/*` models only accept mp3/wav files: `deepgram/nova-3` covers ~49 languages plus `multi` and `deepgram/nova-2` covers ~33, while the `-medical` variants are tuned for clinical vocabulary and accept English only (`en` and its regional variants, e.g. `en-US`, `en-GB`). `nvidia/parakeet-v3` is multilingual with automatic language detection; `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1` is a medical model, English only. `reson8/prerecorded` covers 10 languages, returns word timestamps, and labels speakers via `model_config`.|
|response_format|string|false|none|The format of the transcript output. Use `verbose_json` to take advantage of timestamps.|
|timestamp_granularities[]|string|false|none|The timestamp granularities to populate for this transcription. `response_format` must be set verbose_json to use timestamp granularities. Currently `segment` is supported.|
|language|string|false|none|The language of the audio to be transcribed. `deepgram/nova-3` supports ~49 languages plus `multi`, and `deepgram/nova-2` supports ~33 plus `multi`; the `-medical` variants are English only (`en` and its regional variants, e.g. `en-US`, `en-GB`). Deepgram models validate on the base language and forward the full tag, so regional variants such as `de-CH` and `pt-BR` are accepted where the base language is supported; an unsupported language returns a 400. For `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, supports multiple languages. `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` does not support language parameter. `nvidia/parakeet-v3` detects the language automatically; `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1` is English only. `reson8/prerecorded` accepts `nl`, `en`, `fr`, `fy`, `de`, `it`, `pl`, `pt`, `es` and `sv` (regional variants are transcribed as the base language) and detects the language when it is omitted.|
|model_config|object|false|none|Additional model-specific configuration parameters. Only allowed with the `deepgram/*` models and `reson8/prerecorded`. Sent as a JSON string in multipart requests; for the `deepgram/*` models it is passed through to Deepgram as query parameters, while `reson8/prerecorded` accepts only `diarize` (speaker labels) and `max_speakers` (1 to 8). Any other model with `model_config` returns 400. Can include Deepgram-specific options such as `smart_format`, `punctuate`, `diarize` (speaker labels), `multichannel` (transcribe each channel independently; billed duration is file duration multiplied by the number of channels), `utterances`, `numerals`, and `language`. If `language` is provided both as a top-level parameter and in `model_config`, the top-level parameter takes precedence.|

|model|deepgram/nova-2-medical|
|model|deepgram/nova-3|

|model|nvidia/parakeet-v3|
|model|omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1|
|model|reson8/prerecorded|
|response_format|json|
|response_format|verbose_json|
|timestamp_granularities[]|segment|

<h2 id="tocS_AudioTranscriptionResponse">AudioTranscriptionResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaudiotranscriptionresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_AudioTranscriptionResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSaudiotranscriptionresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsaudiotranscriptionresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "text": "string",
  "duration": 0,
  "segments": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "text": "string",
      "words": [
        {
          "word": "string",
          "start": 0,
          "end": 0,
          "confidence": 0,
          "speaker": 0,
          "speaker_confidence": 0,
          "punctuated_word": "string"
        }
      ],
      "speakers": [
        0
      ],
      "channel": 0
    }
  ],
  "words": [
    {
      "word": "string",
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "confidence": 0,
      "speaker": 0,
      "speaker_confidence": 0,
      "punctuated_word": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

Response fields vary by model. `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` returns `text`, `duration`, and `segments` in `verbose_json` mode. `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` returns `text` only. The `deepgram/*` models return `text` and, depending on `model_config`, may include `words` with per-word timestamps and speaker labels. The Parakeet models (`nvidia/parakeet-v3`, `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1`) return `text` only. `reson8/prerecorded` returns `text` and, in `verbose_json` mode, `duration` and `segments` with `words`; with `diarize`, one segment per speaker turn with speaker labels.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|text|string|true|none|The transcribed text for the audio file.|
|duration|number|false|none|The duration of the audio file in seconds. Returned by `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` and the `deepgram/*` models when `response_format` is `verbose_json`. Not returned by `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`.|
|segments|[[AudioTranscriptionResponseSegments](#schemaaudiotranscriptionresponsesegments)]|false|none|Segments of the transcribed text and their corresponding details. Returned by `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` and the `deepgram/*` models when `response_format` is `verbose_json`; Deepgram segments also carry nested `words` and `speakers`. Not returned by `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`.|
|words|[[AudioTranscriptionResponseWord](#schemaaudiotranscriptionresponseword)]|false|none|Word-level timestamps and optional speaker labels. Only returned by the `deepgram/*` models when word-level output is enabled via `model_config`.|

<a id="tocsaudiotranscriptionresponsesegments"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,

  "words": [

      "word": "string",
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "confidence": 0,
      "speaker": 0,
      "speaker_confidence": 0,
      "punctuated_word": "string"
    }
  ],
  "speakers": [
    0
  ],
  "channel": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|number|true|none|Unique identifier of the segment.|
|start|number|true|none|Start time of the segment in seconds.|
|end|number|true|none|End time of the segment in seconds.|
|text|string|true|none|Text content of the segment.|
|words|[[AudioTranscriptionResponseWord](#schemaaudiotranscriptionresponseword)]|false|none|Word-level timing detail for this segment. Returned by the `deepgram/*` models when word-level output is enabled via `model_config`, and by `reson8/prerecorded`.|
|speakers|[integer]|false|none|Speaker indices heard in this segment. Returned by the `deepgram/*` models and `reson8/prerecorded` when `diarize` is enabled via `model_config`. With `multichannel`, speakers are numbered per channel from 0, so identify a speaker by (`channel`, speaker).|
|channel|integer|false|none|Zero-indexed audio channel of this segment. Returned by the `deepgram/*` models when `multichannel` is enabled via `model_config` and the file has more than one channel. Segments from all channels are merged in one list ordered by start time.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[AvatarId](#schemaavatarid)|true|none|Stable identifier returned by the Avatars API. Discover available stock IDs with GET /v2/ai/avatars and filter[avatar_type]=stock rather than maintaining a fixed list. Custom avatar IDs use the `avatar_` prefix and must belong to the authenticated organization. The service validates that the selected avatar is available.|
|name|string|true|none|Customer-facing avatar name.|
|provider|string|true|none|Avatar provider. The first release supports Telnyx avatars.|
|avatar_type|[AvatarType](#schemaavatartype)|true|none|Whether the avatar is provided by Telnyx or was uploaded by the authenticated organization.|
|hosted|boolean|true|none|Indicates that avatar rendering runs on Telnyx-operated infrastructure.|
|image_url|string(uri)|true|none|HTTPS image URL suitable for an avatar selection thumbnail. If the URL expires, list or retrieve the avatar again to refresh it.|
|image_url_expires_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Expiration time of `image_url`. Omitted when the URL does not expire.|
|suggested_voice_id|string|false|read-only|Optional recommended Telnyx text-to-speech voice for this avatar. An omitted field or empty string means no recommendation is available. Custom avatars have no suggested voice. It is informational and selecting the avatar does not automatically change the AI Assistant's configured voice.|
|content_type|[AvatarContentType](#schemaavatarcontenttype)|false|none|MIME type of a custom avatar image.|
|size_bytes|integer|false|none|Size of a custom avatar image in bytes.|
|width_px|integer|false|none|Decoded width of a custom avatar image.|
|height_px|integer|false|none|Decoded height of a custom avatar image.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Time when the custom avatar was created.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Time when the custom avatar was last updated.|

```json

  "type": "batch",
  "actions": [
    {
      "type": "navigate",
      "url": "http://example.com",
      "wait_until": "load",
      "include_observation": false,

    }
  ],
  "include_observation": false,

}
```

Execute 1-50 sub-actions sequentially. Non-recursive: a batch inside a batch is rejected (400). An empty array is rejected (400). A failed sub-action stops the batch; earlier browser mutations are not rolled back, but partial sub-action results are not returned.

<h2 id="tocS_BooleanOpExpression">BooleanOpExpression</h2>

```json
{
  "op": "and",
  "operands": [
    {
      "name": "is_premium",
      "type": "variable"
    },
    {
      "left": {
        "name": "user_age",
        "type": "variable"
      },
      "op": ">=",
      "right": {
        "type": "number_literal",
        "value": 18
      },
      "type": "comparison"
    }
  ],
  "type": "bool_op"
}
```

Combine sub-expressions with a logical operator (`and` / `or` / `not`).

`and` and `or` accept two or more operands; `not` accepts exactly one.

|type|string|true|none|none|

|op|or|
|op|not|

<a id="tocSbpoauthorization"></a>
<a id="tocsbpoauthorization"></a>

```json
{
  "record_type": "bpo_authorization",
  "bpo_enterprise_id": "4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6",
  "status": "pending",
  "loa_document_id": "2a7e8337-e803-4057-a4ae-26c40eb0bc6c",
  "rejection_reason": "Letter of Authorization is unsigned"
}
```

A single authorization of a BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) account on a DIR.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|string|true|read-only|Always `bpo_authorization`.|
|bpo_enterprise_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The authorized BPO account's enterprise id.|
|status|string|true|none|Review state of this authorization. `pending` when the authorization is first added, or when you send a different `loa_document_id` for this BPO in `bpo_authorizations` (uploading a document alone changes nothing). Approving the DIR approves its pending authorizations; an admin can also approve or reject one on its own. Only an `approved` authorization adds the BPO to this DIR's authorized callers in the branded calling registry.|
|loa_document_id|string(uuid)|true|none|Id of the signed Letter of Authorization document submitted for this BPO. Send it back unchanged in `bpo_authorizations` when updating the DIR to keep this authorization and its review state.|
|rejection_reason|string \| null|false|none|Why the authorization was rejected. `null` unless `status` is `rejected`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|record_type|bpo_authorization|
|status|pending|
|status|approved|
|status|rejected|

|loa_document_id|string(uuid)|true|none|Id of the signed Letter of Authorization document (uploaded via the Telnyx Documents API) in which the Brand Owner authorizes this BPO.|

<h2 id="tocS_BridgeRequest">BridgeRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabridgerequest"></a>
<a id="schema_BridgeRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSbridgerequest"></a>
<a id="tocsbridgerequest"></a>

```json
{
  "call_control_id": "v3:MdI91X4lWFEs7IgbBEOT9M4AigoY08M0WWZFISt1Yw2axZ_IiE4pqg",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
  "park_after_unbridge": "self"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|string|true|none|The Call Control ID of the call you want to bridge with, can't be used together with queue parameter or video_room_id parameter.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|queue|string|false|none|The name of the queue you want to bridge with, can't be used together with call_control_id parameter or video_room_id parameter. Bridging with a queue means bridging with the first call in the queue. The call will always be removed from the queue regardless of whether bridging succeeds. Returns an error when the queue is empty.|
|video_room_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ID of the video room you want to bridge with, can't be used together with call_control_id parameter or queue parameter.|
|video_room_context|string|false|none|The additional parameter that will be passed to the video conference. It is a text field and the user can decide how to use it. For example, you can set the participant name or pass JSON text. It can be used only with video_room_id parameter.|
|prevent_double_bridge|boolean|false|none|When set to `true`, it prevents bridging if the target call is already bridged to another call. Disabled by default.|
|park_after_unbridge|string|false|none|Specifies behavior after the bridge ends (i.e. the opposite leg either hangs up or is transferred). If supplied with the value `self`, the current leg will be parked after unbridge. If not set, the default behavior is to hang up the leg.|
|play_ringtone|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether to play a ringtone if the call you want to bridge with has not yet been answered.|
|ringtone|string|false|none|Specifies which country ringtone to play when `play_ringtone` is set to `true`. If not set, the US ringtone will be played.|
|record|string|false|none|Start recording automatically after an event. Disabled by default.|
|record_channels|string|false|none|Defines which channel should be recorded ('single' or 'dual') when `record` is specified.|
|record_format|string|false|none|Defines the format of the recording ('wav' or 'mp3') when `record` is specified.|
|record_max_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Defines the maximum length for the recording in seconds when `record` is specified. The minimum value is 0. The maximum value is 43200. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_timeout_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected when `record` is specified. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that call transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_track|string|false|none|The audio track to be recorded. Can be either `both`, `inbound` or `outbound`. If only single track is specified (`inbound`, `outbound`), `channels` configuration is ignored and it will be recorded as mono (single channel).|
|record_trim|string|false|none|When set to `trim-silence`, silence will be removed from the beginning and end of the recording.|
|record_custom_file_name|string|false|none|The custom recording file name to be used instead of the default `call_leg_id`. Telnyx will still add a Unix timestamp suffix.|
|mute_dtmf|string|false|none|When enabled, DTMF tones are not passed to the call participant. The webhooks containing the DTMF information will be sent.|
|hold_after_unbridge|boolean|false|none|Specifies behavior after the bridge ends. If set to `true`, the current leg will be put on hold after unbridge instead of being hung up.|

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "model": "gpt-4o",
  "name": "string",
  "instructions": "You are a friendly voice assistant.",
  "greeting": "string",
  "voice_settings": {
    "voice": "string",
    "voice_speed": 1,
    "api_key_ref": "string",
    "temperature": 0.5,
    "similarity_boost": 0.75,
    "use_speaker_boost": true,
    "style": 0,
    "speed": 1,
    "language_boost": null,
    "expressive_mode": false,
    "background_audio": {
      "type": "predefined_media",
      "value": "silence",
      "volume": 1
    }
  },
  "transcription": {
    "model": "distil-whisper/distil-large-v2",
    "language": "string"
  },
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "book_appointment",
      "book_appointment": {
        "event_type_id": 0,
        "api_key_ref": "my_calcom_api_key",
        "attendee_name": "string",
        "attendee_timezone": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "llm_api_key_ref": "my_llm_api_key",
  "openai_api_key_ref": "my_openai_api_key",
  "dynamic_variables": {
    "customer_name": "John",
    "account_id": "ACC-12345"
  },
  "fallback_config": {
    "model": "string",
    "llm_api_key_ref": "string",
    "external_llm": {
      "model": "string",
      "base_url": "string",
      "llm_api_key_ref": "string",
      "authentication_method": "token",
      "certificate_ref": "string",
      "token_retrieval_url": "string",
      "forward_metadata": false
    }
  },
  "external_llm": {
    "model": "string",
    "base_url": "string",
    "llm_api_key_ref": "string",
    "authentication_method": "token",
    "certificate_ref": "string",
    "token_retrieval_url": "string",
    "forward_metadata": false
  },
  "mcp_servers": [
    {}
  ],
  "observability_settings": {}
}
```

AI Assistant configuration and per-call overrides. All fields except `id` are optional. Omitted assistant fields use the stored configuration. Supplied `voice_settings` and `transcription` objects replace their stored objects rather than merging individual settings; include every setting you want to retain. `dynamic_variables` are merged, with request values taking precedence.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The identifier of the AI assistant to use.|
|model|string|false|none|LLM model override for this call. If omitted, the assistant's configured model is used.|
|name|string|false|none|Assistant name override for this call.|
|instructions|string|false|none|System instructions for the voice assistant. Can be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables). This will overwrite the instructions set in the assistant configuration.|
|greeting|string|false|none|Initial greeting text spoken when the assistant starts. Can be plain text for any voice or SSML for `AWS.Polly.<voice_id>` voices. There is a 3,000 character limit.|
|voice_settings|[VoiceSettings](#schemavoicesettings)|false|none|Per-call voice configuration. Set the voice identifier in `voice_settings.voice`, not in `assistant.voice`. If supplied, this object replaces the stored voice settings.|
|transcription|[TranscriptionConfig](#schematranscriptionconfig)|false|none|Per-call speech-to-text configuration for the assistant. If omitted, the stored assistant transcription configuration is used. If supplied, this object replaces the stored transcription settings. This is separate from the top-level `transcription` boolean on answer and dial commands.|
|tools|[[BookAppointmentTool](#schemabookappointmenttool) \| [CheckAvailabilityTool](#schemacheckavailabilitytool) \| [WebhookTool](#schemawebhooktool) \| [HangupTool](#schemahanguptool) \| [TransferTool](#schematransfertool) \| [CallControlRetrievalTool](#schemacallcontrolretrievaltool)]|false|none|Inline tool definitions available to the assistant (webhook, retrieval, transfer, hangup, etc.). Overrides the assistant's stored tools if provided.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|Integration secret identifier for the LLM provider API key. Use this field to reference an [integration secret](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) containing your LLM provider API key. Supports any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.).|
|openai_api_key_ref|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated — use `llm_api_key_ref` instead. Integration secret identifier for the OpenAI API key. This field is maintained for backward compatibility; `llm_api_key_ref` is the canonical field name and supports all LLM providers.|
|dynamic_variables|object|false|none|Map of dynamic variables and their default values. Dynamic variables can be referenced in instructions, greeting, and tool definitions using the `{{variable_name}}` syntax. Call-control-agent automatically merges in `telnyx_call_*` variables (telnyx_call_to, telnyx_call_from, telnyx_conversation_channel, telnyx_agent_target, telnyx_end_user_target, telnyx_call_caller_id_name) and custom header variables.|
|fallback_config|object|false|none|Fallback LLM configuration used when the primary LLM provider is unavailable.|
|external_llm|object|false|none|External LLM configuration for bringing your own LLM endpoint.|
|mcp_servers|[object]|false|none|MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configurations for extending the assistant's capabilities with external tools and data sources.|
|observability_settings|object|false|none|Observability configuration for the assistant session, including Langfuse integration for tracing and monitoring.|

TLS signaling is supported. SRTP media encryption requires TLS transport.|
|sip_subdomain_receive_settings|string|false|none|This option can be enabled to receive calls from: "Anyone" (any SIP endpoint in the public Internet) or "Only my connections" (any connection assigned to the same Telnyx user).|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant|[CallAssistantRequest](#schemacallassistantrequest)|false|none|AI Assistant configuration and per-call overrides. All fields except `id` are optional. Omitted assistant fields use the stored configuration. Supplied `voice_settings` and `transcription` objects replace their stored objects rather than merging individual settings; include every setting you want to retain. `dynamic_variables` are merged, with request values taking precedence.|
|conversation_relay_config|[ConversationRelayEmbeddedConfig](#schemaconversationrelayembeddedconfig)|false|none|Starts a Conversation Relay session automatically when the answered/dialed call is answered. This embedded shape is supported on `answer` and `dial`. It uses public field names (`url`, `dtmf_detection`, `greeting`, `voice`, `language`, etc.) and maps them to the underlying Conversation Relay action. `client_state`, `tts_language`, and `transcription_language` inside this object are ignored; use the parent command's `client_state` and `command_id` fields instead.|
|to|string \| [string]|true|none|The DID or SIP URI to dial out to. Multiple DID or SIP URIs can be provided using an array of strings. For SIP URI destinations, append `;secure=true` or `;secure=srtp` to enable SRTP media encryption for that endpoint, or `;secure=dtls` to enable DTLS media encryption for that endpoint. If `media_encryption` is set to `SRTP` or `DTLS`, it takes precedence over any per-endpoint `secure` URI parameter. For a single string destination, you may append a comma followed by DTMF digits (e.g. `+18004247767,200`) to play those digits as DTMF once the called party answers — equivalent to setting `send_digits_on_answer` separately. If both are present, the explicit `send_digits_on_answer` parameter takes precedence. This shorthand is not supported when `to` is an array.|
|from|string|true|none|The `from` number to be used as the caller id presented to the destination (`to` number). The number should be in +E164 format.|
|diversion|string|false|none|The `to` number of an active inbound call, in +E164 format. Telnyx checks whether there is currently an active inbound call where `to` matches this `diversion` value and `from` matches the `from` number supplied for this request. If such a call exists, the `from` number is treated as verified (since it is already on an active inbound call to you) and can be used as the caller id for this outbound call.|
|from_display_name|string|false|none|The `from_display_name` string to be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`to` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and -_~!.+ special characters. If ommited, the display name will be the same as the number in the `from` field.|
|privacy|string|false|none|Indicates the privacy level to be used for the call. When set to `id`, caller ID information (name and number) will be hidden from the called party. When set to `none` or omitted, caller ID will be shown normally.|
|connection_id|string|true|none|The ID of the Call Control App (formerly ID of the connection) to be used when dialing the destination.|
|audio_url|string|false|none|The URL of a file to be played back to the callee when the call is answered. The URL can point to either a WAV or MP3 file. media_name and audio_url cannot be used together in one request.|
|send_digits_on_answer|string|false|none|DTMF digits to send automatically after the called party answers. Useful for reaching an extension behind an IVR (e.g. `"200"` to dial extension 200 once the called party picks up). Allowed characters: `0-9`, `A-D`, `w` (0.5s pause), `W` (1s pause), `*`, `#`. Maximum 64 characters. When omitted, no automatic DTMF is sent. May also be supplied inline by appending `,<digits>` to `to` (e.g. `to=+18004247767,200`); if both forms are present, this explicit field takes precedence.|
|media_name|string|false|none|The media_name of a file to be played back to the callee when the call is answered. The media_name must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. The file must either be a WAV or MP3 file.|
|preferred_codecs|string|false|none|The list of comma-separated codecs in a preferred order for the forked media to be received.|
|timeout_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the call to be answered by the destination to which it is being called. If the timeout is reached before an answer is received, the call will hangup and a `call.hangup` webhook with a `hangup_cause` of `timeout` will be sent. Minimum value is 5 seconds. Maximum value is 600 seconds.|
|retry_on_timeout|boolean|false|none|Whether to keep trying the remaining routing paths (e.g. alternate providers/gateways) for the same destination after `timeout_secs` is reached for the current attempt. When set to `false`, reaching `timeout_secs` aborts the entire dial attempt and the `call.hangup` webhook reports a `hangup_cause` of `no_answer` instead of `timeout`.|
|time_limit_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|Sets the maximum duration of a Call Control Leg in seconds. If the time limit is reached, the call will hangup and a `call.hangup` webhook with a `hangup_cause` of `time_limit` will be sent. For example, by setting a time limit of 120 seconds, a Call Leg will be automatically terminated two minutes after being answered. The default time limit is 14400 seconds or 4 hours and this is also the maximum allowed call length.|
|answering_machine_detection|string|false|none|Enables Answering Machine Detection. Telnyx offers Premium and Standard detections. With Premium detection, when a call is answered, Telnyx runs real-time detection and sends a `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` webhook with one of the following results: `human_residence`, `human_business`, `machine`, `silence` or `fax_detected`. If we detect a beep, we also send a `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended` webhook with the result of `beep_detected`. If we detect a beep before `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` we only send `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended`, and if we detect a beep after `call.machine.premium.detection.ended`, we send both webhooks. With Standard detection, when a call is answered, Telnyx runs real-time detection to determine if it was picked up by a human or a machine and sends an `call.machine.detection.ended` webhook with the analysis result. If `greeting_end` or `detect_words` is used and a `machine` is detected, you will receive another `call.machine.greeting.ended` webhook when the answering machine greeting ends with a beep or silence. If `detect_beep` is used, you will only receive `call.machine.greeting.ended` if a beep is detected. If `answering_machine_detection` is set to `premium_ios_call_screening_detection`, Premium AMD runs with iOS Call Screening support: after an initial `machine` result, Telnyx listens for the iOS call-screening prompt to end or for an Apple Call Screening tone, sends `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended` with `result=prompt_ended` or `call.machine.premium.call_screening.detected` with `result=screening` respectively. When the Apple Call Screening tone is detected, Premium AMD is restarted on the screened call and a `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` webhook with the post-screening classification follows.|
|answering_machine_detection_config|object|false|none|Optional configuration parameters to modify 'answering_machine_detection' performance. Only `total_analysis_time_millis` and `greeting_duration_millis` parameters are applicable when `premium` is selected as answering_machine_detection. `prompt_end_timeout_millis` is additionally applicable when `premium_ios_call_screening_detection` is selected.|
|deepfake_detection|object|false|none|Enables deepfake detection on the call. When enabled, audio from the remote party is streamed to a detection service that analyzes whether the voice is AI-generated. Results are delivered via the `call.deepfake_detection.result` webhook.|
|conference_config|object|false|none|Optional configuration parameters to dial new participant into a conference.|
|custom_headers|[[CustomSipHeader](#schemacustomsipheader)]|false|none|Custom headers to be added to the SIP INVITE.|
|billing_group_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Use this field to set the Billing Group ID for the call. Must be a valid and existing Billing Group ID.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore others Dial commands with the same `command_id`.|
|link_to|string|false|none|Use another call's control id for sharing the same call session id|
|bridge_intent|boolean|false|none|Indicates the intent to bridge this call with the call specified in link_to. When bridge_intent is true, link_to becomes required and the from number will be overwritten by the from number from the linked call.|
|bridge_on_answer|boolean|false|none|Whether to automatically bridge answered call to the call specified in link_to. When bridge_on_answer is true, link_to becomes required.|
|prevent_double_bridge|boolean|false|none|Prevents bridging and hangs up the call if the target is already bridged. Disabled by default.|
|park_after_unbridge|string|false|none|If supplied with the value `self`, the current leg will be parked after unbridge. If not set, the default behavior is to hang up the leg. When park_after_unbridge is set, link_to becomes required.|
|media_encryption|string|false|none|Defines whether media should be encrypted on the call. For SIP URI destinations, media encryption can also be requested per endpoint with the `secure` URI parameter: `;secure=true` or `;secure=srtp` enables SRTP, and `;secure=dtls` enables DTLS. This parameter, when set to `SRTP` or `DTLS`, takes precedence over the per-endpoint `secure` value.|
|sip_auth_username|string|false|none|SIP Authentication username used for SIP challenges.|
|sip_auth_password|string|false|none|SIP Authentication password used for SIP challenges.|
|sip_headers|[[SipHeader](#schemasipheader)]|false|none|SIP headers to be added to the SIP INVITE request. Currently only User-to-User header is supported.|
|sip_transport_protocol|string|false|none|Defines SIP transport protocol to be used on the call.|
|sound_modifications|[SoundModifications](#schemasoundmodifications)|false|none|Use this field to modify sound effects, for example adjust the pitch.|
|stream_url|string|false|none|The destination WebSocket address where the stream is going to be delivered.|
|stream_track|string|false|none|Specifies which track should be streamed.|
|stream_codec|[StreamCodec](#schemastreamcodec)|false|none|Specifies the codec to be used for the streamed audio. When set to 'default' or when transcoding is not possible, the codec from the call will be used.|
|stream_bidirectional_mode|[StreamBidirectionalMode](#schemastreambidirectionalmode)|false|none|Configures method of bidirectional streaming (mp3, rtp).|
|stream_bidirectional_codec|[StreamBidirectionalCodec](#schemastreambidirectionalcodec)|false|none|Indicates codec for bidirectional streaming RTP payloads. Used only with stream_bidirectional_mode=rtp. Case sensitive.|
|stream_bidirectional_target_legs|[StreamBidirectionalTargetLegs](#schemastreambidirectionaltargetlegs)|false|none|Specifies which call legs should receive the bidirectional stream audio.|
|stream_bidirectional_sampling_rate|[StreamBidirectionalSamplingRate](#schemastreambidirectionalsamplingrate)|false|none|Audio sampling rate.|
|stream_establish_before_call_originate|boolean|false|none|Establish websocket connection before dialing the destination. This is useful for cases where the websocket connection takes a long time to establish.|
|send_silence_when_idle|boolean|false|none|Generate silence RTP packets when no transmission available.|
|webhook_url|string|false|none|Use this field to override the URL for which Telnyx will send subsequent webhooks to for this call.|
|webhook_url_method|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `webhook_url`.|
|webhook_urls|object|false|none|A map of event types to arrays of webhook URLs. When an event of the specified type occurs, the webhook URLs associated with that event type will be called instead of the default webhook URL. Events not mapped here will use the default webhook URL.|
|webhook_urls_method|string|false|none|HTTP request method to invoke `webhook_urls`.|
|webhook_retries_policies|object|false|none|A map of event types to retry policies. Each retry policy contains an array of `retries_ms` specifying the delays between retry attempts in milliseconds. Maximum 5 retries, total delay cannot exceed 60 seconds.|
|record|string|false|none|Start recording automatically after an event. Disabled by default.|
|record_channels|string|false|none|Defines which channel should be recorded ('single' or 'dual') when `record` is specified.|
|record_format|string|false|none|Defines the format of the recording ('wav' or 'mp3') when `record` is specified.|
|record_max_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Defines the maximum length for the recording in seconds when `record` is specified. The minimum value is 0. The maximum value is 43200. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_timeout_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected when `record` is specified. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that call transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_track|string|false|none|The audio track to be recorded. Can be either `both`, `inbound` or `outbound`. If only single track is specified (`inbound`, `outbound`), `channels` configuration is ignored and it will be recorded as mono (single channel).|
|record_trim|string|false|none|When set to `trim-silence`, silence will be removed from the beginning and end of the recording.|
|record_custom_file_name|string|false|none|The custom recording file name to be used instead of the default `call_leg_id`. Telnyx will still add a Unix timestamp suffix.|
|supervise_call_control_id|string|false|none|The call leg which will be supervised by the new call.|
|supervisor_role|string|false|none|The role of the supervisor call. 'barge' means that supervisor call hears and is being heard by both ends of the call (caller & callee). 'whisper' means that only supervised_call_control_id hears supervisor but supervisor can hear everything. 'monitor' means that nobody can hear supervisor call, but supervisor can hear everything on the call.|
|enable_dialogflow|boolean|false|none|Enables Dialogflow for the current call. The default value is false.|
|dialogflow_config|[DialogflowConfig](#schemadialogflowconfig)|false|none|none|
|transcription|boolean|false|none|Enable transcription upon call answer. The default value is false.|
|transcription_config|[TranscriptionStartRequest](#schematranscriptionstartrequest)|false|none|none|
|sip_region|string|false|none|Defines the SIP region to be used for the call.|
|stream_auth_token|string|false|none|An authentication token to be sent as part of the WebSocket connection when using streaming. Maximum length is 4000 characters.|
|route_to_mobile|boolean|false|none|When set to true, routes the call directly to the mobile device associated with the destination Telnyx Mobile number, bypassing Inbound Calls Interception configured in the Telnyx Portal under Mobile Numbers → select the number → Voice → Call Interception. Use this when transferring an intercepted call to the mobile device to prevent the call from being intercepted again. Defaults to false.|

```json
    "city": "Anytown",
    "state_code": "CA",

    "zip4": "1234",
    "country_code": "US"
  },
  "confidence_score": 80,
  "error_code": null
}
```

Identity information for the phone number's owner, including name and postal address. Populated when `type=caller-identity` is requested.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The name associated with the phone number.|
|address|[number-lookup_Address](#schemanumber-lookup_address)|false|none|Postal address associated with the phone number's owner.|
|confidence_score|number \| null|false|none|How strongly the phone number is linked to the returned name, on a scale of 50 to 90 (higher means more supporting signals). Reflects signal strength, not probability: 70 indicates stronger, more consistent evidence than 60, not a 70% chance of being correct. As a guide, 70+ is high confidence, 60 moderate, and 50 limited. Below 50 no name is returned, so scores under 50 are never present.|
|error_code|string \| null|false|none|A lookup-specific error code if the identity could not be resolved; otherwise null.|

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "You are a friendly chatbot."
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Hello, world!"
    }
  ],
  "model": "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
  "service_tier": "string",
  "region": "USA",
  "mode": "preferred",
  "api_key_ref": "string",
  "stream": false,
  "temperature": 0.1,
  "max_tokens": 0,
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {}
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "none",
  "response_format": {
    "type": "text"
  },
  "min_p": 0,
  "n": 0,
  "use_beam_search": false,
  "best_of": 0,
  "length_penalty": 1,
  "early_stopping": false,
  "logprobs": false,
  "top_logprobs": 0,
  "frequency_penalty": 0,
  "presence_penalty": 0,
  "top_p": 0,
  "stop": "string",
  "seed": 0,
  "enable_thinking": true,
  "reasoning_effort": "none"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[[ChatCompletionSystemMessageParam](#schemachatcompletionsystemmessageparam)]|true|none|A list of the previous chat messages for context.|
|model|string|false|none|The language model to chat with.|
|service_tier|string|false|none|The service tier to use for this request. Supported values vary by model; use `GET /v2/ai/openai/models` and inspect the model's `service_tiers` field. If omitted, Telnyx-hosted models use `default`.|
|region|string|false|none|Optional data-residency region the request should be served from, using the same vocabulary as your account's Data Locality setting. Behavior depends on `mode`. Supported for Telnyx-hosted models only: a request routed to an external provider never passes through Telnyx model routing, so a region cannot be enforced for it. Omit for today's latency-based routing.|
|mode|string|false|none|How strictly `region` is applied. `preferred` (the default when `region` is set) tries that region first and falls back to another when the model cannot be served there, so a request that would have succeeded still succeeds. `strict` pins the request: it is served from that region or it fails with a 422, never redirected to another region. Requires `region`.|
|api_key_ref|string|false|none|If you are using an external inference provider like xAI or OpenAI, this field allows you to pass along a reference to your API key. After creating an [integration secret](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) for you API key, pass the secret's `identifier` in this field.|
|stream|boolean|false|none|Whether or not to stream data-only server-sent events as they become available.|
|temperature|number|false|none|Adjusts the "creativity" of the model. Lower values make the model more deterministic and repetitive, while higher values make the model more random and creative.|
|max_tokens|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of completion (output) tokens, including reasoning and answer tokens combined. An omitted or null limit defaults to 8192 unless the model is excluded from that default; excluded models leave the limit to the serving engine. Explicit values and applied defaults are clamped to the model's max_completion_tokens metadata when that ceiling is set (see GET /v2/ai/openai/models). An omitted limit on an excluded model remains unset even when metadata declares a ceiling. Input and output together must fit the model's context window. Set an explicit limit when a bounded generation budget is required. For example, omitted or null limits default to 8192 for `zai-org/GLM-5.3` and `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. Hosted exclusions include `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5`, `zai-org/GLM-5.2`, `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B`, `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct`, `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` and `google/gemma-2b-it`. Legacy external and fine-tuned model IDs can also bypass the default; model discovery reports completion ceilings, not whether this default applies. Set an explicit limit for predictable behavior across models.|
|tools|[[ChatCompletionToolParam](#schemachatcompletiontoolparam) \| [Retrieval](#schemaretrieval)]|false|none|The `function` tool type follows the same schema as the [OpenAI Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat). The `retrieval` tool type is unique to Telnyx. You may pass a list of [embedded storage buckets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/embeddings/embed-documents) for retrieval-augmented generation.|
|tool_choice|string|false|none|none|
|response_format|[ChatCompletionResponseFormatParam](#schemachatcompletionresponseformatparam)|false|none|Controls the format of the model output. `json_object` guarantees valid JSON output without defining a schema; `json_schema` constrains the output to the JSON schema you supply via the `json_schema` property and is the supported way to get guaranteed structured output on Telnyx-hosted models.|
|min_p|number|false|none|This is an alternative to `top_p` that [many prefer](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/27670). Must be in [0, 1].|
|n|number|false|none|This will return multiple choices for you instead of a single chat completion.|
|use_beam_search|boolean|false|none|Setting this to `true` will allow the model to [explore more completion options](https://huggingface.co/blog/how-to-generate#beam-search). This is not supported by OpenAI.|
|best_of|integer|false|none|This is used with `use_beam_search` to determine how many candidate beams to explore.|
|length_penalty|number|false|none|This is used with `use_beam_search` to prefer shorter or longer completions.|
|early_stopping|boolean|false|none|This is used with `use_beam_search`. If `true`, generation stops as soon as there are `best_of` complete candidates; if `false`, a heuristic is applied and the generation stops when is it very unlikely to find better candidates.|
|logprobs|boolean|false|none|Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token returned in the `content` of `message`.|
|top_logprobs|integer|false|none|This is used with `logprobs`. An integer between 0 and 20 specifying the number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log probability.|
|frequency_penalty|number|false|none|Higher values will penalize the model from repeating the same output tokens.|

<h2 id="tocS_CloudfsFilesystemStatus">CloudfsFilesystemStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacloudfsfilesystemstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_CloudfsFilesystemStatus"></a>
<a id="tocScloudfsfilesystemstatus"></a>
<a id="tocscloudfsfilesystemstatus"></a>

```json
"ready"
```

Lifecycle status of the filesystem. `ready` means it is fully provisioned and usable. `needs_format` means the storage bucket and metadata database were provisioned but the filesystem has not yet been formatted — run `juicefs format` with the filesystem's `meta_url` before mounting. `failed` means the last lifecycle action failed — see the filesystem's `error` message. `deleted` appears only in the delete response: deleted filesystems are excluded from list results and return a `404` on retrieval.

<h2 id="tocS_ComparisonExpression">ComparisonExpression</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacomparisonexpression"></a>
<a id="schema_ComparisonExpression"></a>
<a id="tocScomparisonexpression"></a>
<a id="tocscomparisonexpression"></a>

```json
{
  "left": {
    "name": "user_age",
    "type": "variable"
  },
  "op": ">=",
  "right": {
    "type": "number_literal",
    "value": 18
  },
  "type": "comparison"
}
```

Compare two sub-expressions with a relational or membership operator.

Evaluates to a boolean. Used in edge conditions to gate transitions on
runtime values, e.g. `user_age >= 18` or `tier == "gold"`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|left|[Expression](#schemaexpression)|true|none|A node in a deterministic expression AST. Exactly one variant is selected by the `type` discriminator. Terminal variants (`number_literal`, `string_literal`, `bool_literal`, `variable`) bottom out the recursion; `arithmetic`, `bool_op`, and `comparison` nest further sub-expressions.<br><br>Extracted into a single named schema so the recursive union is defined once (was previously inlined at every operand site).|
|op|string|true|none|Relational/membership operator. `contains` / `not_contains` apply to strings (substring) and arrays (membership).|
|right|[Expression](#schemaexpression)|true|none|A node in a deterministic expression AST. Exactly one variant is selected by the `type` discriminator. Terminal variants (`number_literal`, `string_literal`, `bool_literal`, `variable`) bottom out the recursion; `arithmetic`, `bool_op`, and `comparison` nest further sub-expressions.<br><br>Extracted into a single named schema so the recursive union is defined once (was previously inlined at every operand site).|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|op|==|
|op|!=|
|op|<|
|op|<=|
|op|>|
|op|>=|
|op|contains|
|op|not_contains|

```json
{
  "call_control_id": "v3:MdI91X4lWFEs7IgbBEOT9M4AigoY08M0WWZFISt1Yw2axZ_IiE4pqg",
  "audio_url": "http://example.com/gather_prompt.wav",
  "minimum_digits": 1,
  "maximum_digits": 4,
  "timeout_millis": 30000
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call leg that will receive the gather prompt.|
|audio_url|string|false|none|The URL of the audio file to play as the gather prompt. Must be WAV or MP3 format.|
|media_name|string|false|none|The name of the media file uploaded to the Media Storage API to play as the gather prompt.|
|minimum_digits|integer|false|none|Minimum number of digits to gather.|
|maximum_digits|integer|false|none|Maximum number of digits to gather.|
|maximum_tries|integer|false|none|Maximum number of times to play the prompt if no input is received.|
|timeout_millis|integer|false|none|Duration in milliseconds to wait for input before timing out.|
|terminating_digit|string|false|none|Digit that terminates gathering. Set to an empty string to disable the terminating digit entirely, so that a digit such as `#` can be collected as input per `valid_digits`.|
|valid_digits|string|false|none|Digits that are valid for gathering. All other digits will be ignored.|
|inter_digit_timeout_millis|integer|false|none|Duration in milliseconds to wait between digits.|
|initial_timeout_millis|integer|false|none|Duration in milliseconds to wait for the first digit before timing out.|
|stop_playback_on_dtmf|boolean|false|none|Whether to stop the audio playback when a DTMF digit is received.|
|invalid_audio_url|string|false|none|URL of audio file to play when invalid input is received.|
|invalid_media_name|string|false|none|Name of media file to play when invalid input is received.|
|gather_id|string|false|none|Identifier for this gather command. Will be included in the gather ended webhook. Maximum 100 characters.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. Must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audio_url|string|false|none|The URL of a file to be played back in the conference. media_name and audio_url cannot be used together in one request.|
|media_name|string|false|none|The media_name of a file to be played back in the conference. The media_name must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. The file must either be a WAV or MP3 file.|
|loop|[Loopcount](#schemaloopcount)|false|none|The number of times the audio file should be played. If supplied, the value must be an integer between 1 and 100, or the special string `infinity` for an endless loop.|
|call_control_ids|[string]|false|none|List of call control ids identifying participants the audio file should be played to. If not given, the audio file will be played to the entire conference.|
|region|[ConferenceRegion](#schemaconferenceregion)|false|none|Region where the conference data is located. Defaults to the region defined in user's data locality settings (Europe or US).|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|region|Europe|
|region|Middle East|
|region|US|

```json
  ],
  "payload": "Say this to participants",
  "payload_type": "text",

  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_ids|[string]|false|none|Call Control IDs of participants who will hear the spoken text. When empty all participants will hear the spoken text.|
|payload|string|true|none|The text or SSML to be converted into speech. There is a 3,000 character limit.|
|payload_type|string|false|none|The type of the provided payload. The payload can either be plain text, or Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML).|
|voice|string|true|none|Specifies the voice used in speech synthesis.<br><br>- Define voices using the format `<Provider>.<Model>.<VoiceId>`. Specifying only the provider will give default values for voice_id and model_id.<br><br> **Supported Providers:**<br>- **AWS:** Use `AWS.Polly.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna`). For neural voices, which provide more realistic, human-like speech, append `-Neural` to the `VoiceId` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna-Neural`). Check the [available voices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/available-voices.html) for compatibility.<br>- **Azure:** Use `Azure.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Azure.en-CA-ClaraNeural`, `Azure.en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural`, `Azure.en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural`). For a complete list of voices, go to [Azure Voice Gallery](https://speech.microsoft.com/portal/voicegallery). Use `voice_settings` to configure custom deployments, regions, or API keys.<br>- **ElevenLabs:** Use `ElevenLabs.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `ElevenLabs.eleven_multilingual_v2.21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM`). The `ModelId` part is optional. To use ElevenLabs, you must provide your ElevenLabs API key as an integration identifier secret in `"voice_settings": {"api_key_ref": "<secret_identifier>"}`. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) for details. Check [available voices](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/get-voices).<br>- **Telnyx:** Use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>` (e.g., `Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af`). Use `voice_settings` to configure voice_speed and other synthesis parameters. `Bayan` provides Arabic (multiple dialects) and English voices (e.g., `Telnyx.Bayan.Ahmed`, `Telnyx.Bayan.Amanda`). `Sukhan` provides Urdu voices (e.g., `Telnyx.Sukhan.urdu-professor`); `voice_speed` is not supported.<br>- **Minimax:** Use `Minimax.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Minimax.speech-02-hd.Wise_Woman`). Supported models: `speech-02-turbo`, `speech-02-hd`, `speech-2.6-turbo`, `speech-2.8-turbo`. Use `voice_settings` to configure speed, volume, pitch, and language_boost.<br>- **Resemble:** Use `Resemble.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Resemble.Turbo.Aaron_en-US`). Supported models: `Pro`, `Turbo`, `Urdu`. `<VoiceId>` is a stock voice name or the ID of a Resemble voice clone. Use `voice_settings` to configure precision, sample_rate, and format.<br>- **Inworld:** Use `Inworld.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Inworld.Mini.Loretta`, `Inworld.Max.Oliver`, `Inworld.TTS2.Loretta`). Supported models: `Mini`, `Max`, `TTS2`. Use `voice_settings` to configure `delivery_mode` (`STABLE`, `BALANCED`, `CREATIVE`), supported by `TTS2` only.<br>- **Fish Audio:** Use `FishAudio.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `FishAudio.s2.1-pro.<reference_id>`). Supported models: `s2.1-pro`, `s2-pro`, `s1`. `VoiceId` is a Fish Voice-Library reference ID.<br>- **Soniox:** Use `Soniox.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma`). Supported model: `tts-rt-v2`. Browse the catalog via the [Voices API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/text-to-speech-commands/list-available-voices). Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the text, for example `it`. SSML is not supported. Use `voice_settings` to configure `speed` (0.7 to 1.3) and `reduce_silence`.<br>- **xAI:** Use `xAI.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `xAI.eve`). Available voices: `eve`, `ara`, `rex`, `sal`, `leo`.<br>- **Humain:** Use `Humain.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Humain.sara-ar`). Available voices: `sara-en`, `abdulaziz-en`, `sara-ar`, `abdulaziz-ar`, `nourah-ar`, `abdullah-ar`. Native Arabic (Saudi dialect) and English voices only — no `ModelId` segment.<br><br>For service_level basic, you may define the gender of the speaker (male or female).|
|voice_settings|[ElevenLabsVoiceSettings](#schemaelevenlabsvoicesettings) \| [TelnyxVoiceSettings](#schematelnyxvoicesettings) \| [AWSVoiceSettings](#schemaawsvoicesettings) \| [MinimaxVoiceSettings](#schemaminimaxvoicesettings) \| [AzureVoiceSettings](#schemaazurevoicesettings) \| [ResembleVoiceSettings](#schemaresemblevoicesettings) \| [InworldVoiceSettings](#schemainworldvoicesettings) \| [XAIVoiceSettings](#schemaxaivoicesettings) \| [SonioxVoiceSettings](#schemasonioxvoicesettings) \| [AssemblyAIVoiceSettings](#schemaassemblyaivoicesettings)|false|none|The settings associated with the voice selected|
|language|string|false|none|The language you want spoken. This parameter is ignored when a `Polly.*` voice is specified.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid execution of duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore subsequent commands with the same `command_id` as one that has already been executed.|
|region|[ConferenceRegion](#schemaconferenceregion)|false|none|Region where the conference data is located. Defaults to the region defined in user's data locality settings (Europe or US).|

<a id="tocSconnectionjitterbuffer"></a>
<a id="tocsconnectionjitterbuffer"></a>

```json
{
  "enable_jitter_buffer": true,
  "jitterbuffer_msec_min": 60,
  "jitterbuffer_msec_max": 200
}
```

Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enable_jitter_buffer|boolean|false|none|Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled.|
|jitterbuffer_msec_min|integer|false|none|The minimum jitter buffer size in milliseconds. Must be between 40 and 400. Has no effect if enable_jitter_buffer is not true.|
|jitterbuffer_msec_max|integer|false|none|The maximum jitter buffer size in milliseconds. Must be between 40 and 400. Has no effect if enable_jitter_buffer is not true.|

<h2 id="tocS_ConnectionNoiseSuppression">ConnectionNoiseSuppression</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconnectionnoisesuppression"></a>
<a id="schema_ConnectionNoiseSuppression"></a>
<a id="tocSconnectionnoisesuppression"></a>
<a id="tocsconnectionnoisesuppression"></a>

```json
"both"
```

Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.

<h2 id="tocS_ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails">ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails"></a>
<a id="schema_ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails"></a>
<a id="tocSconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails"></a>
<a id="tocsconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails"></a>

```json
{
  "engine": "deep_filter_net",
  "attenuation_limit": 80
}
```

Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|engine|string|false|none|The noise suppression engine to use. 'denoiser' is the default engine. 'deep_filter_net' and 'deep_filter_net_large' are alternative engines with different performance characteristics. Krisp engines ('krisp_viva_tel', 'krisp_viva_tel_lite', 'krisp_viva_promodel', 'krisp_viva_ss') provide advanced noise suppression capabilities. 'quail_voice_focus' provides Quail-based voice focus noise suppression.|
|attenuation_limit|integer|false|none|The attenuation limit value for the selected engine. Default values vary by engine: 0 for 'denoiser', 80 for 'deep_filter_net', 'deep_filter_net_large', and all Krisp engines ('krisp_viva_tel', 'krisp_viva_tel_lite', 'krisp_viva_promodel', 'krisp_viva_ss'), 100 for 'quail_voice_focus'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|engine|denoiser|
|engine|deep_filter_net|
|engine|deep_filter_net_large|
|engine|krisp_viva_tel|
|engine|krisp_viva_tel_lite|
|engine|krisp_viva_promodel|
|engine|krisp_viva_ss|
|engine|quail_voice_focus|

```json
    "language": "en"
  }
}
```

A single search result representing one chunk of a conversation history record. Records are split into chunks of up to 480 tokens with 64-token overlap at ingestion time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique chunk identifier.|
|record_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the parent record. Multiple chunks from the same record share this ID.|
|chunk_index|integer|true|none|Zero-based index of this chunk within the parent record.|
|chunk_total|integer|true|none|Total number of chunks the parent record was split into.|
|text|string|true|none|The text content of this chunk (up to 480 tokens).|
|score|number(float)|true|none|Cosine similarity score between the query vector and this chunk's vector. Higher values indicate greater semantic relevance.|
|region|string|true|none|The region where this record is stored.|
|user_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the user who owns this record.|
|organization_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the organization that owns this record.|
|record_created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When the original record was created (ISO 8601).|
|ingested_at|string(date-time)|true|none|When the record was chunked, embedded, and indexed (ISO 8601).|
|metadata|object|false|none|Arbitrary metadata attached to the record at ingestion time. Filterable via filter[field]=value query parameters.|

<h2 id="tocS_ConversationRelayEmbeddedConfig">ConversationRelayEmbeddedConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconversationrelayembeddedconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_ConversationRelayEmbeddedConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSconversationrelayembeddedconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsconversationrelayembeddedconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "url": "wss://example.com/conversation-relay",
  "dtmf_detection": true,
  "greeting": "Hi! Ask me anything!",
  "voice": "Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af",
  "tts_provider": "telnyx",
  "voice_settings": {
    "type": "telnyx"
  },
  "language": "en-US",
  "languages": [
    {
      "language": "en-US",
      "voice": "Telnyx.Ultra.alloy",
      "tts_provider": "telnyx",
      "transcription_engine": "Deepgram",
      "transcription_engine_config": {
        "transcription_model": "deepgram/nova-3"
      }
    }
  ],
  "interruptible": "speech",
  "interruptible_greeting": "dtmf",
  "custom_parameters": {
    "customer_id": "12345"
  }
}
```

Starts a Conversation Relay session automatically when the answered/dialed call is answered. This embedded shape is supported on `answer` and `dial`. It uses public field names (`url`, `dtmf_detection`, `greeting`, `voice`, `language`, etc.) and maps them to the underlying Conversation Relay action. `client_state`, `tts_language`, and `transcription_language` inside this object are ignored; use the parent command's `client_state` and `command_id` fields instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|url|string|true|none|WebSocket URL for your Conversation Relay server. Must start with `ws://` or `wss://`.|
|dtmf_detection|boolean|false|none|Enable DTMF detection for the relay session.|
|greeting|string|false|none|Text played when the relay session starts.|
|voice|[VoiceConfig](#schemavoiceconfig)|false|none|The voice to be used by the voice assistant. Currently we support ElevenLabs, Telnyx and AWS voices.<br><br> **Supported Providers:**<br>- **AWS:** Use `AWS.Polly.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna`). For neural voices, which provide more realistic, human-like speech, append `-Neural` to the `VoiceId` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna-Neural`). Check the [available voices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/available-voices.html) for compatibility.<br>- **Azure:** Use `Azure.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Azure.en-CA-ClaraNeural`, `Azure.en-CA-LiamNeural`, `Azure.en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural`, `Azure.en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural`). For a complete list of voices, go to [Azure Voice Gallery](https://speech.microsoft.com/portal/voicegallery).<br>- **ElevenLabs:** Use `ElevenLabs.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `ElevenLabs.BaseModel.John`). The `ModelId` part is optional. To use ElevenLabs, you must provide your ElevenLabs API key as an integration secret under `"voice_settings": {"api_key_ref": "<secret_id>"}`. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) for details. Check [available voices](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/get-voices).<br> - **Telnyx:** Use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>`<br>- **Inworld:** Use `Inworld.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Inworld.Mini.Loretta`, `Inworld.Max.Oliver`, `Inworld.TTS2.Loretta`). Supported models: `Mini`, `Max`, `TTS2`.<br>- **Fish Audio:** Use `FishAudio.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `FishAudio.s2.1-pro.<reference_id>`). Supported models: `s2.1-pro`, `s2-pro`, `s1`. `VoiceId` is a Fish Voice-Library reference ID.<br>- **Soniox:** Use `Soniox.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma`). Supported model: `tts-rt-v2`. Browse the catalog via the [Voices API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/text-to-speech-commands/list-available-voices). Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the text, for example `it`. SSML is not supported. Use `voice_settings` to configure `speed` (0.7 to 1.3) and `reduce_silence`.<br>- **xAI:** Use `xAI.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `xAI.eve`). Available voices: `eve`, `ara`, `rex`, `sal`, `leo`.<br>- **Humain:** Use `Humain.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Humain.sara-ar`). Available voices: `sara-en`, `abdulaziz-en`, `sara-ar`, `abdulaziz-ar`, `nourah-ar`, `abdullah-ar`. Native Arabic (Saudi dialect) and English voices only — no `ModelId` segment.|
|voice_settings|[ElevenLabsVoiceSettings](#schemaelevenlabsvoicesettings) \| [TelnyxVoiceSettings](#schematelnyxvoicesettings) \| [AWSVoiceSettings](#schemaawsvoicesettings) \| [MinimaxVoiceSettings](#schemaminimaxvoicesettings) \| [AzureVoiceSettings](#schemaazurevoicesettings) \| [ResembleVoiceSettings](#schemaresemblevoicesettings) \| [InworldVoiceSettings](#schemainworldvoicesettings) \| [XAIVoiceSettings](#schemaxaivoicesettings) \| [SonioxVoiceSettings](#schemasonioxvoicesettings) \| [AssemblyAIVoiceSettings](#schemaassemblyaivoicesettings)|false|none|The settings associated with the voice selected|
|tts_provider|string|false|none|Text-to-speech provider. If omitted, Telnyx derives it from `voice` or `provider`.|
|provider|string|false|none|Structured voice provider. Must be supplied together with `structured_provider`.|
|structured_provider|[ConversationRelayStructuredProvider](#schemaconversationrelaystructuredprovider)|false|none|Provider-specific structured voice settings. Must be supplied together with `provider`; Telnyx sends the value as the nested provider configuration for Conversation Relay.|
|language|string|false|none|Default language for both text-to-speech and speech recognition.|
|languages|[[ConversationRelayLanguage](#schemaconversationrelaylanguage)]|false|none|Per-language TTS and transcription settings.|
|interruptible|[ConversationRelayInterruptible](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptible)|false|none|Controls when caller input can interrupt assistant speech. `any` allows speech or DTMF interruptions; `none` disables interruptions; `speech` allows speech only; `dtmf` allows DTMF only.|
|interruptible_greeting|[ConversationRelayInterruptible](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptible)|false|none|Controls when caller input can interrupt assistant speech. `any` allows speech or DTMF interruptions; `none` disables interruptions; `speech` allows speech only; `dtmf` allows DTMF only.|
|interruption_settings|[ConversationRelayInterruptionSettings](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptionsettings)|false|none|Settings for handling caller interruptions during Conversation Relay speech.|
|transcription_engine|string|false|none|Engine to use for speech recognition. Legacy values `A` - `Google`, `B` - `Telnyx` are supported for backward compatibility. For Conversation Relay, use this field with `transcription_engine_config`; the `transcription` object is not supported.|
|transcription_engine_config|[ConversationRelayTranscriptionEngineConfig](#schemaconversationrelaytranscriptionengineconfig)|false|none|Engine-specific transcription settings for Conversation Relay. This accepts the same provider-specific options used by the Call Transcription Start command, such as `transcription_model`, without requiring the engine discriminator to be repeated inside this object. With Deepgram Flux (`deepgram/flux`), `interim_results`, `eot_threshold` and `eager_eot_threshold` control the interim prompts and the `eagerEndOfTurn` and `turnResumed` frames sent to your WebSocket server.|
|custom_parameters|object|false|none|Custom key-value parameters forwarded to the relay session as assistant dynamic variables.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|interruptible|any|

|interruptible|dtmf|
|interruptible_greeting|none|
|interruptible_greeting|any|

|interruptible_greeting|dtmf|

|interruption_settings|[ConversationRelayInterruptionSettings](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptionsettings)|false|none|Settings for handling caller interruptions during Conversation Relay speech.|
|transcription|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** Not supported for Conversation Relay start requests. Use `transcription_engine` and `transcription_engine_config` instead.|
|assistant|[ConversationRelayAssistant](#schemaconversationrelayassistant)|false|none|Custom parameters for the Conversation Relay session. Pass key-value data as `assistant.dynamic_variables` to make it available to the relay session.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to subsequent webhooks. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|tts_provider|string|false|none|Text-to-speech provider. If omitted, Telnyx derives it from `voice` or `provider`.|
|provider|string|false|none|Structured voice provider. Must be supplied together with `structured_provider`.|
|structured_provider|[ConversationRelayStructuredProvider](#schemaconversationrelaystructuredprovider)|false|none|Provider-specific structured voice settings. Must be supplied together with `provider`; Telnyx sends the value as the nested provider configuration for Conversation Relay.|
|transcription_engine|string|false|none|Engine to use for speech recognition. Legacy values `A` - `Google`, `B` - `Telnyx` are supported for backward compatibility. For Conversation Relay, use this field with `transcription_engine_config`; the `transcription` object is not supported.|
|transcription_engine_config|[ConversationRelayTranscriptionEngineConfig](#schemaconversationrelaytranscriptionengineconfig)|false|none|Engine-specific transcription settings for Conversation Relay. This accepts the same provider-specific options used by the Call Transcription Start command, such as `transcription_model`, without requiring the engine discriminator to be repeated inside this object. With Deepgram Flux (`deepgram/flux`), `interim_results`, `eot_threshold` and `eager_eot_threshold` control the interim prompts and the `eagerEndOfTurn` and `turnResumed` frames sent to your WebSocket server.|
|interruptible|[ConversationRelayInterruptible](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptible)|false|none|Controls when caller input can interrupt assistant speech. `any` allows speech or DTMF interruptions; `none` disables interruptions; `speech` allows speech only; `dtmf` allows DTMF only.|
|interruptible_greeting|[ConversationRelayInterruptible](#schemaconversationrelayinterruptible)|false|none|Controls when caller input can interrupt assistant speech. `any` allows speech or DTMF interruptions; `none` disables interruptions; `speech` allows speech only; `dtmf` allows DTMF only.|
|custom_parameters|object|false|none|Custom key-value parameters forwarded to the relay session as `assistant.dynamic_variables`. If `assistant.dynamic_variables` is also present, these values are merged in.|
