<h2 id="tocS_ConversationRelayTranscriptionEngineConfig">ConversationRelayTranscriptionEngineConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconversationrelaytranscriptionengineconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_ConversationRelayTranscriptionEngineConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSconversationrelaytranscriptionengineconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsconversationrelaytranscriptionengineconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "transcription_model": "deepgram/flux",
  "interim_results": true,
  "eager_eot_threshold": 0.5
}
```

Engine-specific transcription settings for Conversation Relay. This accepts the same provider-specific options used by the Call Transcription Start command, such as `transcription_model`, without requiring the engine discriminator to be repeated inside this object. With Deepgram Flux (`deepgram/flux`), `interim_results`, `eot_threshold` and `eager_eot_threshold` control the interim prompts and the `eagerEndOfTurn` and `turnResumed` frames sent to your WebSocket server.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|interim_results|boolean|false|none|Deepgram Flux: send interim transcripts as `prompt` frames with `last: false`.|
|eot_threshold|number|false|none|Deepgram Flux: confidence required to end the caller's turn.|
|eager_eot_threshold|number|false|none|Deepgram Flux: confidence at which an `eagerEndOfTurn` frame is sent before the final prompt, followed by `turnResumed` if the caller keeps talking. When omitted, these frames are not sent.|

```json
        "instructions": "Focus on billing questions. Look up the caller's latest invoice with the billing tool before answering.",
        "instructions_mode": "append",
        "model": "moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6",
        "name": "Billing",
        "position": {
          "x": 420,
          "y": 80
        },
        "shared_tool_ids": [
          "tool-billing-lookup"
        ],
        "tools_mode": "append"
      }
    ],
    "start_node_id": "n_intake"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|model|string|false|none|ID of the model to use when `external_llm` is not set. You can use the [Get models API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/openai-chat/get-available-models-openai-compatible) to see available models. If `external_llm` is provided, the assistant uses `external_llm` instead of this field. If neither `model` nor `external_llm` is provided, Telnyx applies the default model.|
|instructions|string|true|none|System instructions for the assistant. These may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables)|
|tools|[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)|false|none|Deprecated for new integrations. Inline tool definitions available to the assistant. Prefer `tool_ids` to attach shared tools created with the AI Tools endpoints.|
|mcp_servers|[[AssistantMCPServer](#schemaassistantmcpserver)]|false|none|MCP servers attached to the assistant. Create MCP servers with `/ai/mcp_servers`, then reference them by `id` here.|
|a2a_agents|[[AssistantA2AAgent](#schemaassistanta2aagent)]|false|none|A2A agents this assistant can delegate to. Tools are not stored here: at the start of every conversation each agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises, named `a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`. The following limits are not enforced when the assistant is saved, and anything past them is dropped when the conversation starts: 64 agents per assistant, 64 skills per card, 128 derived tools per assistant, and a 6 second budget for all card fetches combined. An agent whose card cannot be fetched costs the assistant that capability for the conversation; it does not fail the call.|
|tool_ids|[string]|false|none|IDs of shared tools to attach to the assistant. New integrations should prefer `tool_ids` over inline `tools`.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|greeting|string|false|none|Text that the assistant will use to start the conversation. This may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables). Use an empty string to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. Use the special value `<assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message>` to have the assistant generate the greeting based on the system instructions.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|This is only needed when using third-party inference providers selected by `model`. The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your LLM provider's API key. For bring-your-own endpoint authentication, use `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.|
|external_llm|[ExternalLLMReq](#schemaexternalllmreq)|false|none|none|
|fallback_config|[FallbackConfigReq](#schemafallbackconfigreq)|false|none|none|
|voice_settings|[inference-embedding_VoiceSettings](#schemainference-embedding_voicesettings)|false|none|none|
|avatar_settings|[AvatarSettingsRequest](#schemaavatarsettingsrequest) \| null|false|none|**Beta:** Optional avatar configuration for supported realtime browser conversations. Omit or set to `null` to create the assistant without an avatar.|
|transcription|[TranscriptionSettings](#schematranscriptionsettings)|false|none|none|
|telephony_settings|[TelephonySettings](#schematelephonysettings)|false|none|none|
|messaging_settings|[MessagingSettings](#schemamessagingsettings)|false|none|none|
|enabled_features|[[EnabledFeatures](#schemaenabledfeatures)]|false|none|none|
|insight_settings|[InsightSettings](#schemainsightsettings)|false|none|none|
|privacy_settings|[PrivacySettings](#schemaprivacysettings)|false|none|none|
|dynamic_variables_webhook_url|string|false|none|If `dynamic_variables_webhook_url` is set, Telnyx sends a POST request to this URL at the start of the conversation to resolve dynamic variables. **Gotcha:** the webhook response must wrap variables under a top-level `dynamic_variables` object, e.g. `{"dynamic_variables": {"customer_name": "Jane"}}`. Returning a flat object will be ignored and variables will fall back to their defaults. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) for the full request/response format and timeout behavior.|
|dynamic_variables_webhook_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|Timeout in milliseconds for the dynamic variables webhook. Must be between 1 and 10000 ms. If the webhook does not respond within this timeout, the call proceeds with default values. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables).|
|dynamic_variables|object|false|none|Map of dynamic variables and their default values|
|widget_settings|[WidgetSettings](#schemawidgetsettings)|false|none|Configuration settings for the assistant's web widget.|
|interruption_settings|[inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings](#schemainference-embedding_interruptionsettings)|false|none|Settings for interruptions and how the assistant decides the user has finished speaking. These timings are most relevant when using non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn behavior is controlled by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` (`eot_threshold`, `eot_timeout_ms`, `eager_eot_threshold`).|
|integrations|[[AssistantIntegration](#schemaassistantintegration)]|false|none|Connected integrations attached to the assistant. The catalog of available integrations is at `/ai/integrations`; the user's connected integrations are at `/ai/integrations/connections`. Each item references a catalog integration by `integration_id`.|
|observability_settings|[ObservabilityReq](#schemaobservabilityreq)|false|none|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the assistant. Tags can also be managed with the assistant tag endpoints.|
|post_conversation_settings|[PostConversationSettingsReq](#schemapostconversationsettingsreq)|false|none|Configuration for post-conversation processing. When enabled, the assistant receives one additional LLM turn after the conversation ends, allowing it to execute final tool calls such as sending a summary or updating a record via webhook or function tools. Integration and MCP server tools are not available post-conversation; call-control tools (e.g. hangup, transfer) are also unavailable. Beta feature.|
|delegation_settings|[DelegationSettings](#schemadelegationsettings)|false|none|Splits the conversation between a frontend model that talks to the caller and a backend model that does the work. On the GPT-Live route the frontend model cannot call tools at all — when it needs something done it raises a delegation and waits. On the chat completion route the frontend keeps a single `delegate` tool that returns immediately, so the conversation carries on while the backend works. Either way the backend's answer is spoken as commentary or kept as silent context, depending on `speak_results`. Beta feature.|
|websocket_settings|[WebsocketSettings](#schemawebsocketsettings)|false|none|Streams conversation and telephony events to a WebSocket server you host, and accepts messages injected back into the conversation. Telnyx opens the connection as a client, once per conversation. Delivery is best effort throughout: while the connection is down events are dropped rather than queued, and no socket failure is ever allowed to affect the call. Beta feature.|
|conversation_flow|[ConversationFlowReq](#schemaconversationflowreq)|false|none|Conversation flow as supplied by API clients (create / update).<br><br>A directed graph of `FlowNodeReq` connected by `FlowEdge`s. Validation<br>enforces unique node/edge IDs, that `start_node_id` references a real<br>node, and that every edge's endpoints reference real nodes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|enabled_features|telephony|
|enabled_features|messaging|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateAssistantTestRequest">CreateAssistantTestRequest</h2>

```json
{
  "name": "Customer Support Bot Test",
  "description": "string",
  "telnyx_conversation_channel": "web_chat",
  "destination": "+15551234567",
  "max_duration_seconds": 1,
  "test_suite": "string",
  "instructions": "Act as a frustrated customer who received a damaged product. Ask for a refund and escalate if not satisfied with the initial response.",
  "rubric": [
    {
      "criteria": "Assistant responds within 30 seconds",

    },

    }
  ]
```

Request model for creating a new assistant test.

This model defines all the required and optional parameters needed to create
a comprehensive test for an AI assistant, including test configuration,
evaluation criteria, and scheduling options.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|A descriptive name for the assistant test. This will be used to identify the test in the UI and reports.|
|description|string|false|none|Optional detailed description of what this test evaluates and its purpose. Helps team members understand the test's objectives.|
|telnyx_conversation_channel|object|false|none|The communication channel through which the test will be conducted. Determines how the assistant will receive and respond to test messages.|
|destination|string|true|none|The target destination for the test conversation. Format depends on the channel: phone number for SMS/voice, webhook URL for web chat, etc.|
|max_duration_seconds|integer|false|none|Maximum duration in seconds that the test conversation should run before timing out. If not specified, uses system default timeout.|
|test_suite|string|false|none|Optional test suite name to group related tests together. Useful for organizing tests by feature, team, or release cycle.|
|instructions|string|true|none|Detailed instructions that define the test scenario and what the assistant should accomplish. This guides the test execution and evaluation.|
|rubric|[object]|true|none|Evaluation criteria used to assess the assistant's performance. Each rubric item contains a name and specific criteria for evaluation.|

|user_name|string|true|none|The user name to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 4-32 characters long and alphanumeric values only (no spaces or special characters).|
|password|string|true|none|The password to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 8 to 128 characters long.|
|anchorsite_override|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|none|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|[ConnectionName](#schemaconnectionname)|true|none|A user-assigned name to help manage the connection.|
|sip_uri_calling_preference|string|false|none|This feature enables inbound SIP URI calls to your Credential Auth Connection. If enabled for all (unrestricted) then anyone who calls the SIP URI <your-username>@telnyx.com will be connected to your Connection. You can also choose to allow only calls that are originated on any Connections under your account (internal).|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; defaults to false when omitted on creation. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|ios_push_credential_id|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|android_push_credential_id|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1, v2 or texml. Note - texml can only be set when the outbound object parameter call_parking_enabled is included and set to true.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|inbound|[CredentialInbound](#schemacredentialinbound)|false|none|none|
|outbound|[CredentialOutbound](#schemacredentialoutbound)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateEmailBatchItemRequest">CreateEmailBatchItemRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreateemailbatchitemrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateEmailBatchItemRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScreateemailbatchitemrequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreateemailbatchitemrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "from": "string",
  "from_name": "string",
  "to": [
    "string"
  ],
  "cc": [
    "string"
  ],
  "bcc": [
    "string"
  ],
  "reply_to": "string",
  "subject": "string",
  "html_body": "string",
  "text_body": "string",
  "headers": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "attachments": [
    {
      "filename": "string",
      "content_type": "string",
      "content": "string",
      "disposition": "attachment",
      "content_id": "string"
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "group_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "ignore_suppression": false,
  "metadata": {},
  "tracking_settings": {
    "open_tracking": true,
    "click_tracking": true
  },
  "template_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "template_variables": {},
  "scheduled_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "send_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "inline_css": false,
  "sandbox_mode": false
}
```

A single message in a batch create request. This schema mirrors
`CreateEmailRequest` EXCEPT it does not accept the reply/forward
threading parameters (`in_reply_to_message_id`, `reply_to_all`,
`forward_of_message_id`) — those are single-send-only in Phase 1
(MSG-1491) and are not yet implemented on the batch endpoint. Recipient
email addresses must be unique across `to`, `cc`, and `bcc` after
case-insensitive normalization. Duplicate recipients return `400`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)|true|none|none|
|from_name|string|false|none|Optional display name for string `from`; overrides `from.name` when provided.|
|to|[EmailAddressArrayInput](#schemaemailaddressarrayinput)|true|none|none|
|cc|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|none|
|bcc|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|none|
|reply_to|[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)|false|none|Reply-to address. If provided as an object with a name, only the email is stored; the name is ignored.|
|subject|string|false|none|Required unless `template_id` is supplied. When using a template, the template's subject is rendered; if the template has no subject or renders empty, the request returns 400.|
|html_body|string|false|none|HTML email body. Returned only by `GET /email_messages/{id}`; omitted from create and list responses.|
|text_body|string|false|none|Plain text email body. Returned only by `GET /email_messages/{id}`; omitted from create and list responses.|
|headers|object|false|none|Custom email headers. Write-only; not returned in responses.|
|attachments|[[AttachmentRequest](#schemaattachmentrequest)]|false|none|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags for categorization and filtering. Stored on the message, returned on message responses, and propagated to Email Detail Records. Usable in `filter[tags]` when listing messages.|
|group_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Optional unsubscribe-group UUID used for group-scoped suppression checks and unsubscribe handling.|
|ignore_suppression|boolean|false|none|When true, allows delivery to recipients whose suppressions explicitly<br>permit an override. Hard bounces, spam complaints, and invalid-address<br>suppressions cannot be overridden. Requires the `email:override` API scope.<br>|
|metadata|object|false|none|Custom metadata key/value pairs. Stored on the message, returned on message responses, and propagated to Email Detail Records. Usable in `filter[metadata]` when listing messages.|
|tracking_settings|[TrackingSettings](#schematrackingsettings)|false|none|Per-send open and click tracking overrides. Omitted properties inherit the sender domain's tracking settings.|
|template_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|template_variables|object|false|none|Variables for Liquid template rendering. Non-object values may cause a 422 validation error on message creation, but are silently treated as an empty object for template rendering. When the template enables `strict_variables`, a missing required variable fails the request with 422 (single send) or a per-item `unprocessable_entity` error (batch) naming the variable; no message is persisted for the failed item.|
|scheduled_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Future ISO 8601 delivery time. Invalid or non-future timestamps are rejected. Single sends return HTTP 422; in batch sends the invalid item is reported in the 207 per-item errors while other items continue. `send_at` remains a deprecated request alias. A non-null `scheduled_at` takes precedence over `send_at`; when `scheduled_at` is omitted or null, `send_at` is used.|
|send_at|string(date-time)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated alias for `scheduled_at`.|
|inline_css|boolean|false|none|none|
|sandbox_mode|boolean|false|none|Per-message sandbox flag. The batch-level `sandbox_mode` envelope value is authoritative: it overwrites every message's `sandbox_mode` before processing, including the `false` default when the envelope omits the field. A per-item `sandbox_mode: true` inside a non-sandbox batch is therefore a real send. Set the envelope field to run any batch item in sandbox mode.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

Reserved recipients at `test.telnyx.com` produce the deterministic event chains documented on CreateEmailRequest.sandbox_mode; no batch item is injected into the MTA or outbound Kafka path. Sandbox batch items are non-billable, consume no daily-send-limit quota, and feed no delivery-reputation signals.|

```json
  },

    }
```

Recipient email addresses must be unique across `to`, `cc`, and `bcc` after case-insensitive normalization. Duplicate recipients return `400 Bad Request`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)|true|none|none|
|from_name|string|false|none|Optional display name for string `from`; overrides `from.name` when provided.|
|to|[EmailAddressArrayInput](#schemaemailaddressarrayinput)|true|none|none|
|cc|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|none|
|bcc|[[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)]|false|none|none|
|reply_to|[EmailAddressInput](#schemaemailaddressinput)|false|none|Reply-to address. If provided as an object with a name, only the email is stored; the name is ignored.|
|subject|string|false|none|Required unless `template_id` is supplied. When using a template, the template's subject is rendered; if the template has no subject or renders empty, the request returns 400.|
|html_body|string|false|none|HTML email body. Returned only by `GET /email_messages/{id}`; omitted from create and list responses.|
|text_body|string|false|none|Plain text email body. Returned only by `GET /email_messages/{id}`; omitted from create and list responses.|
|headers|object|false|none|Custom email headers. Write-only; not returned in responses.|
|attachments|[[AttachmentRequest](#schemaattachmentrequest)]|false|none|none|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags for categorization and filtering. Stored on the message, returned on message responses, and propagated to Email Detail Records. Usable in `filter[tags]` when listing messages.|
|group_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Optional unsubscribe-group UUID used for group-scoped suppression checks and unsubscribe handling.|
|ignore_suppression|boolean|false|none|When true, allows delivery to recipients whose suppressions explicitly<br>permit an override. Hard bounces, spam complaints, and invalid-address<br>suppressions cannot be overridden. Requires the `email:override` API scope.<br>|
|metadata|object|false|none|Custom metadata key/value pairs. Stored on the message, returned on message responses, and propagated to Email Detail Records. Usable in `filter[metadata]` when listing messages.|
|tracking_settings|[TrackingSettings](#schematrackingsettings)|false|none|Per-send open and click tracking overrides. Omitted properties inherit the sender domain's tracking settings.|
|template_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|template_variables|object|false|none|Variables for Liquid template rendering. Non-object values may cause a 422 validation error on message creation, but are silently treated as an empty object for template rendering. When the template enables `strict_variables`, a missing required variable fails the request with 422 (single send) or a per-item `unprocessable_entity` error (batch) naming the variable; no message is persisted for the failed item.|
|scheduled_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Future ISO 8601 delivery time. Invalid or non-future timestamps are rejected. Single sends return HTTP 422; in batch sends the invalid item is reported in the 207 per-item errors while other items continue. `send_at` remains a deprecated request alias. A non-null `scheduled_at` takes precedence over `send_at`; when `scheduled_at` is omitted or null, `send_at` is used.|
|send_at|string(date-time)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated alias for `scheduled_at`.|
|inline_css|boolean|false|none|none|
|sandbox_mode|boolean|false|none|Validates and accepts the message without injecting it into the MTA or outbound Kafka path. Nothing is delivered: sandbox records are non-billable, consume no daily-send-limit quota, and feed no delivery-reputation signals.<br><br>The reserved sandbox test-recipient domain is `test.telnyx.com`. In sandbox mode, these addresses produce deterministic recipient-scoped lifecycle events:<br><br>- `delivered@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> delivered<br>- `hard-bounce@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> bounced (permanent)<br>- `soft-bounce@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> bounced (transient)<br>- `complaint@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> sent -> complained<br>- `suppressed@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> suppressed<br>- `invalid@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> failed (invalid recipient)<br>- `dkim-fail@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> failed (DKIM unavailable)<br>- `rate-limit@test.telnyx.com`: queued -> sending -> failed (rate limit exceeded)<br><br>Matching is case-insensitive for both the local part and the domain and requires the exact domain `test.telnyx.com` — subdomains and other domains do not match. Mixed sandbox sends simulate only reserved test recipients; other recipients retain ordinary sandbox behavior (accepted, no delivery attempted). Hard-bounce and complaint outcomes also use the normal automatic-suppression pipeline. Non-sandbox sends to these addresses use the normal delivery path.|
|in_reply_to_message_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Telnyx message UUID of the message this send replies to. When provided,<br>the API sets RFC 5322 `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers on the<br>outbound MIME so the recipient's mailbox (Gmail/Outlook) threads it<br>correctly. The parent is looked up under the caller's account scope;<br>a UUID belonging to another account yields a non-enumerating 404.<br><br>Wire-only (Phase 1): the API sets the headers and does NOT resolve or<br>mutate `thread_id` on the server side. Messages sent without this<br>parameter are standalone (no threading headers injected).<br><br>Cannot be combined with `forward_of_message_id` (422).|
|reply_to_all|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates a reply-all intent. In Phase 1 (wire-only) this does not<br>change the threading headers — recipient selection is customer-<br>controlled (`to`/`cc`), and a thread is not defined by its audience.<br>When the referenced message has no thread context, reply-all<br>degrades to a plain reply (parent ID only in `References`). The<br>resolution engine (separate work) will expand the ancestor chain<br>at a later phase with no API change.<br><br>Only meaningful alongside `in_reply_to_message_id`.|
|forward_of_message_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Telnyx message UUID of the message this send forwards. Forwarded<br>messages start a NEW thread per RFC 5322 — NO `In-Reply-To` or<br>`References` headers are set on the outbound MIME. The id is<br>recorded in the message's metadata for EDR provenance only.<br><br>The id is validated as a UUID but is NOT looked up against the<br>message store — existence is the caller's responsibility (the<br>forward is pure metadata; it does not affect delivery). Cannot be<br>combined with `in_reply_to_message_id` (422).|

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "subject": "string",
  "html_body": "string",
  "text_body": "string",
  "variables": [
    "string"
  ],
  "variables_mode": "automatic",
  "strict_variables": false,
  "autoescape": false,
  "variable_schema": {
    "property1": {
      "required": true,
      "default": "string"
    },
    "property2": {
      "required": true,
      "default": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|Letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and underscores only.|
|subject|string \| null|false|none|Liquid template subject.|
|html_body|string \| null|false|none|Liquid template HTML body.|
|text_body|string \| null|false|none|Liquid template text body.|
|variables|[string]|false|none|Persisted variable names. In `automatic` mode a non-null array is rejected; in `explicit` mode this is the exact manual array and each item is limited to 255 Unicode code points.|
|variables_mode|string|false|none|Controls how `variables` is maintained. If both fields are omitted (or `variables` is null), the template uses `automatic` mode and extracts variable names from the effective subject, HTML body, and text body. A non-null `variables` array with no mode selects `explicit`. `automatic` rejects a simultaneous non-null array; `explicit` requires a non-null array, including valid `[]`, and preserves its exact order, duplicates, and string contents.|
|strict_variables|boolean|false|none|Per-template strict variable-validation setting. Defaults to `false` for backward compatibility. When `true`, a send or render that is missing a variable marked `required: true` in `variable_schema` fails with 422 naming the variable. Missing optional variables never fail; their schema `default` (when set) is applied to the render.|
|autoescape|boolean|false|none|Per-template HTML autoescaping setting. Defaults to `false` for backward compatibility. When `true`, the rendered `html_body` HTML-escapes each Liquid expression's output at the output boundary (after its filters run, before concatenation with literal template markup). Input values are never mutated and `subject`/`text_body` are never autoescaped. The boundary escape is idempotent: HTML entities already present in the output (e.g. from an explicit `escape` filter) are preserved, so an explicit `escape`/`escape_once` is never double-escaped, and markup introduced by any later filter in the chain is still escaped.|
|variable_schema|object \| null|false|none|Structured variable requirements. Required variables cannot define defaults; invalid combinations return 422. This is independent of the legacy `variables` array. On render with `strict_variables` enabled: `required` variables must be supplied as non-empty values — absent, `null`, empty string, empty object `{}`, and empty array `[]` all fail with 422 naming the variable, while present values such as `false` and `0` pass (they are present, not empty). Optional variables fall back to their `default` when absent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|variables_mode|automatic|
|variables_mode|explicit|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateInboundIpRequest">CreateInboundIpRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreateinboundiprequest"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateInboundIpRequest"></a>
<a id="tocScreateinboundiprequest"></a>
<a id="tocscreateinboundiprequest"></a>

```json
{
  "ani_number_format": "+E.164",
  "dnis_number_format": "+e164",
  "codecs": [
    "G722"
  ],
  "default_routing_method": "sequential",
  "channel_limit": 10,
  "generate_ringback_tone": true,
  "isup_headers_enabled": true,
  "prack_enabled": true,
  "sip_compact_headers_enabled": true,
  "sip_region": "US",
  "sip_subdomain": "test",
  "sip_subdomain_receive_settings": "only_my_connections",
  "timeout_1xx_secs": 10,
  "timeout_2xx_secs": 20,
  "shaken_stir_enabled": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ani_number_format|string|false|none|This setting allows you to set the format with which the caller's number (ANI) is sent for inbound phone calls.|
|dnis_number_format|string|false|none|none|
|codecs|[string]|false|none|Defines the list of codecs that Telnyx will send for inbound calls to a specific number on your portal account, in priority order. This only works when the Connection the number is assigned to uses Media Handling mode: default. OPUS and H.264 codecs are available only when using TCP or TLS transport for SIP.|
|default_routing_method|string|false|none|Default routing method to be used when a number is associated with the connection. Must be one of the routing method types or left blank, other values are not allowed.|
|channel_limit|integer|false|none|When set, this will limit the total number of inbound calls to phone numbers associated with this connection.|
|generate_ringback_tone|boolean|false|none|Generate ringback tone through 183 session progress message with early media.|
|isup_headers_enabled|boolean|false|none|When set, inbound phone calls will receive ISUP parameters via SIP headers. (Only when available and only when using TCP or TLS transport.)|
|prack_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable PRACK messages as defined in RFC3262.|
|sip_compact_headers_enabled|boolean|false|none|Defaults to true.|
|sip_region|string|false|none|Selects which `sip_region` to receive inbound calls from. If null, the default region (US) will be used.|
|sip_subdomain|string|false|none|Specifies a subdomain that can be used to receive Inbound calls to a Connection, in the same way a phone number is used, from a SIP endpoint. Example: the subdomain "example.sip.telnyx.com" can be called from any SIP endpoint by using the SIP URI "sip:@example.sip.telnyx.com" where the user part can be any alphanumeric value. TLS signaling is supported. SRTP media encryption requires TLS transport.|
|sip_subdomain_receive_settings|string|false|none|This option can be enabled to receive calls from: "Anyone" (any SIP endpoint in the public Internet) or "Only my connections" (any connection assigned to the same Telnyx user).|
|timeout_1xx_secs|integer|false|none|Time(sec) before aborting if connection is not made.|
|timeout_2xx_secs|integer|false|none|Time(sec) before aborting if call is unanswered (min: 1, max: 600).|
|shaken_stir_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled the SIP Connection will receive the Identity header with Shaken/Stir data in the SIP INVITE message of inbound calls, even when using UDP transport.|

Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|string|false|none|none|
|transport_protocol|string|false|none|One of UDP, TLS, or TCP. Applies only to connections with IP authentication or FQDN authentication.|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; defaults to false when omitted on creation. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|ios_push_credential_id|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|android_push_credential_id|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|inbound|[CreateInboundIpRequest](#schemacreateinboundiprequest)|false|none|none|
|outbound|[OutboundIp](#schemaoutboundip)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|


Request body for creating a new meeting session.

Cross-field rules:
- `assistant` cannot be combined with `join_at`; it is available only for sessions that join immediately.
- `assistant` cannot be combined with `barge_in: true`.
- `assistant.avatar: true` cannot be combined with `speak_on_enter`; the assistant greets through its avatar.
- The `assistant` options, including `avatar`, take effect at session creation and cannot be modified later.
- A digital avatar or Assistant webpage output takes precedence over `camera_image`; the static image is ignored and a URL source is not fetched.
- The former top-level `avatar` object (bring-your-own-key avatar) has been removed and is rejected with 400 `invalid_request`; use `assistant.avatar` instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|meeting_url|string(uri)|true|none|The meeting URL the bot should join.|
|bot_name|string|false|none|Display name for the bot in the meeting. Defaults to "Meeting Bot".|
|join_at|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO-8601 timestamp in the future at which the bot should join. If omitted, the bot joins immediately.|
|voice|string|false|none|Session-default voice identifier used for `speak_on_enter` and ordinary speak actions. A voice supplied on an individual speak action overrides this default for that utterance.|
|speak_on_enter|string|false|none|Text the bot speaks when it enters the meeting. **Not spoken when an `assistant` is attached**: the value is accepted and echoed back on the session, but the assistant owns the voice and the line is never delivered, with no event reporting the omission. Use `chat_on_enter` to announce an assistant-backed bot. Rejected with 400 `invalid_request` when `assistant.avatar` is `true`.|
|chat_on_enter|string|false|none|A message the bot posts to the meeting's chat as soon as it becomes active — typically a recording disclosure. Delivered at most once. Independent of `speak_on_enter`: both may be set, and the chat message posts first because it does not wait for text-to-speech or avatar startup. Rejected with 422 `unsupported_capability` on platforms without meeting chat.|
|barge_in|boolean|false|none|When enabled, a human participant `speech_on` event interrupts and stops the current bot audio; it does not bypass admission or initiate speech. Assistant sessions reject `barge_in: true`.|
|summarize_on_end|boolean|false|none|If true, generate a summary artifact when the session ends.|
|camera_image|[MeetingSessionCameraImage](#schemameetingsessioncameraimage)|false|write-only|Write-only static camera-tile image for this session, not a native account or participant profile photo. Supply exactly one JPEG source. When effective, the image is used as the bot's static camera/video output; presentation varies by meeting platform and recording configuration and is not guaranteed in recordings. An effective Avatar or Assistant webpage output takes precedence, so this input is ignored and a URL source is not fetched.|
|webhook_url|string(uri)|false|none|HTTPS endpoint to receive session lifecycle callbacks. Static validation requires HTTPS, rejects embedded credentials and blocked hosts, and enforces egress policy. Validation makes no network request to the endpoint.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to the session. The serialized JSON representation must not exceed 16384 characters at runtime.|
|idempotency_key|string|false|none|Client-supplied idempotency key to safely retry creation requests without duplicating sessions. Lookup is scoped to the authenticated account and compares the key only; the request payload is not fingerprinted or compared.|
|assistant|[MeetingSessionAssistantRequest](#schemameetingsessionassistantrequest)|false|none|Attach a Telnyx AI Assistant to the session. Supply the Assistant's ID; the Meeting service connects it to the meeting directly. The Call Control connection, caller ID and loopback SIP URI previously required here have been removed and are now rejected as unknown fields.|

When set, this overrides the messaging profile's `smart_encoding` setting.|

|number_pool_settings|[NumberPoolSettings](#schemanumberpoolsettings)|false|none|Number Pool allows you to send messages from a pool of numbers of different types, assigning<br>weights to each type. The pool consists of all the long code and toll free numbers<br>assigned to the messaging profile.<br><br>To disable this feature, set the object field to `null`.<br>|
|url_shortener_settings|[UrlShortenerSettings](#schemaurlshortenersettings)|false|none|The URL shortener feature allows automatic replacement of URLs that were generated using<br>a public URL shortener service. Some examples include bit.do, bit.ly, goo.gl, ht.ly,<br>is.gd, ow.ly, rebrand.ly, t.co, tiny.cc, and tinyurl.com. Such URLs are replaced with<br>with links generated by Telnyx. The use of custom links can improve branding and message<br>deliverability.<br><br>To disable this feature, set the object field to `null`.<br>|
|alpha_sender|string \| null|false|none|The alphanumeric sender ID to use when sending to destinations that require an alphanumeric sender ID.|
|daily_spend_limit|string|false|none|The maximum amount of money (in USD) that can be spent by this profile before midnight UTC.|
|daily_spend_limit_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to enforce the value configured by `daily_spend_limit`.|
|mms_fall_back_to_sms|boolean|false|none|enables SMS fallback for MMS messages.|
|mms_transcoding|boolean|false|none|enables automated resizing of MMS media.|
|mobile_only|boolean|false|none|Send messages only to mobile phone numbers.|
|smart_encoding|boolean|false|none|Enables automatic character encoding optimization for SMS messages. When enabled, the system automatically selects the most efficient encoding (GSM-7 or UCS-2) based on message content to maximize character limits and minimize costs.|
|resource_group_id|string \| null|false|none|The resource group ID to associate with this messaging profile.|
|health_webhook_url|string \| null(url)|false|none|A URL to receive health check webhooks for numbers in this profile.|
|ai_assistant_id|string \| null|false|none|The AI assistant ID to associate with this messaging profile.|

```json
  },
```

A UAC (User Agent Client) Connection registers Telnyx to your PBX — the opposite of a standard SIP trunk, where the PBX registers to Telnyx. Use UAC when your PBX doesn’t support outbound SIP registration or you need Telnyx to maintain the registration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|Defaults to true|
|user_name|string|false|none|The user name to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 4-32 characters long and alphanumeric values only (no spaces or special characters).|
|password|string|false|none|The password to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 8 to 128 characters long.|
|anchorsite_override|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|none|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|[ConnectionName](#schemaconnectionname)|true|none|A user-assigned name to help manage the connection.|
|sip_uri_calling_preference|string|false|none|This feature enables inbound SIP URI calls to your Credential Auth Connection. If enabled for all (unrestricted) then anyone who calls the SIP URI <your-username>@telnyx.com will be connected to your Connection. You can also choose to allow only calls that are originated on any Connections under your account (internal).|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; defaults to false when omitted on creation. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|ios_push_credential_id|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|android_push_credential_id|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1, v2 or texml. Note - texml can only be set when the outbound object parameter call_parking_enabled is included and set to true.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|inbound|[UacInboundRequest](#schemauacinboundrequest)|false|none|Inbound settings that can be supplied when creating or updating a UAC connection. The SIP subdomain fields returned in UAC connection responses are generated by Telnyx and are not accepted as request parameters.|
|outbound|[UacOutbound](#schemauacoutbound)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|
|internal_uac_settings|[UacInternalSettings](#schemauacinternalsettings)|false|none|Internal Telnyx-side settings for a UAC connection.|
|external_uac_settings|[UacExternalSettings](#schemauacexternalsettings)|false|none|External SIP peer settings used by Telnyx when registering to your PBX and routing outbound calls.|

|sip_uri_calling_preference|string|false|none|This feature enables inbound SIP URI calls to your Credential Auth Connection. If enabled for all (unrestricted) then anyone who calls the SIP URI <your-username>@telnyx.com will be connected to your Connection. You can also choose to allow only calls that are originated on any Connections under your account (internal).|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|

Defaults to false and returns the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|

|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|

|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

|generate_ringback_tone|boolean|false|none|Generate ringback tone through 183 session progress message with early media.|
|localization|string|false|none|A 2-character country code specifying the country whose national dialing rules should be used. For example, if set to `US` then any US number can be dialed without preprending +1 to the number. When left blank, Telnyx will try US and GB dialing rules, in that order, by default.|
|t38_reinvite_source|string|false|none|This setting only affects connections with Fax-type Outbound Voice Profiles. The setting dictates whether or not Telnyx sends a t.38 reinvite.<br/><br/> By default, Telnyx will send the re-invite. If set to `customer`, the caller is expected to send the t.38 reinvite.|

<h2 id="tocS_DecisionModelRequest">DecisionModelRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadecisionmodelrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_DecisionModelRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSdecisionmodelrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsdecisionmodelrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "telnyx/decision-flash",
  "state": "Our production calls are failing. Every customer is affected.",
  "questions": {
    "team": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Choose the team that should handle this incident.",
      "criteria": {
        "billing": "Payments and refunds",
        "technical_support": "Service faults and technical problems",
        "sales": "New purchases"
      }
    },
    "production_incident": {
      "type": "noul",
      "instructions": "Does the message describe an active production incident?"
    },
    "urgency": {
      "type": "score",
      "instructions": "Rate operational urgency.",
      "criteria": [
        "Low",
        "Normal",
        "High",
        "Critical"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Decision Models beta request. Choose a public model alias; omitted model defaults to telnyx/decision-flash. Telnyx manages the underlying models behind these aliases.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|false|none|Public model alias. telnyx/decision-flash offers the lowest cost and latency; telnyx/decision-pro supports decisions that require long context, including inputs beyond Jev’s 32k per-decision limit. Applies to every question in the request. Other values are rejected.|
|state|[DecisionModelContent](#schemadecisionmodelcontent)|true|none|Shared context evaluated by every question.|
|questions|object|true|none|Between 1 and 64 named questions. Each key identifies the corresponding answer.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|model|telnyx/decision-flash|
|model|telnyx/decision-pro|

<h2 id="tocS_DecisionModelScoreAnswer">DecisionModelScoreAnswer</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadecisionmodelscoreanswer"></a>
<a id="schema_DecisionModelScoreAnswer"></a>
<a id="tocSdecisionmodelscoreanswer"></a>
<a id="tocsdecisionmodelscoreanswer"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "score",
  "score": 2.9974242859177265,
  "legend": {
    "0": "Low",
    "1": "Normal",
    "2": "High",
    "3": "Critical"
  },
  "probabilities": {
    "0": 0.0003348349100603869,
    "1": 0.00003529133987660637,
    "2": 0.0015006266723396524,
    "3": 0.9981292470777234
  },
  "confidence": 0.9894200002646713
}
```

An expected rating over the ordered criteria.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Answer type.|
|score|number|true|none|Expected zero-based criterion index: sum(index * probability). Ranges from 0 to N-1 for N criteria; fractional values are valid.|
|legend|object|true|none|Criterion descriptions keyed by stringified zero-based indices, such as "0", "1", and "2".|
|probabilities|[DecisionModelProbabilities](#schemadecisionmodelprobabilities)|true|none|Relative scores keyed by the same stringified indices as legend.|
|confidence|[DecisionModelConfidence](#schemadecisionmodelconfidence)|true|none|Normalized entropy confidence: 1 - H(p) / ln(N), where H(p) = -sum(p * ln(p)) and N is the number of options. Zero indicates a uniform distribution; one indicates concentration on one option. This is neither the winning probability nor calibrated correctness.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|score|


A dedicated sending IP address owned by the account.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|record_type|string|false|none|none|
|ip_address|string|false|none|The allocated IPv4/IPv6 address.|
|ip_version|string|false|none|none|
|pool_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|none|
|region|string|false|none|Region label of the allocated IP (for example, `ewr-nj1`).|
|status|string|false|none|Lifecycle status. `provisioning`: purchased and billed, carries no mail until `start_warmup`. `warming_up`: warm-up ramp in progress. `active`: ramp complete. `suspended`: suspended by Telnyx; carries no mail and is still billed. `released`: returned to Telnyx; carries no mail.|
|warmup|[DedicatedIpWarmup](#schemadedicatedipwarmup)|false|none|Warmup ramp state for a dedicated IP.|
|billing|[DedicatedIpBilling](#schemadedicatedipbilling)|false|none|Monthly recurring charge (MRC) state for the IP's current allocation.|
|provisioning_status|string|false|none|Same value as `provisioning.dns_status`.|
|provisioning|[DedicatedIpProvisioning](#schemadedicatedipprovisioning)|false|none|Read-only status of the Telnyx-managed PTR record. No customer action is required to complete it.|
|ptr_hostname|string \| null|false|none|Telnyx-managed reverse DNS (PTR) hostname of the IP, in the form `mta-<a-b-c-d>.msgtelnyx.com`. Also used as the EHLO hostname when sending from the IP. Managed by Telnyx and cannot be changed through the API.|
|dns_confirmed_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the PTR hostname was forward-confirmed (PTR → hostname → A record → this IP). The IP carries mail only while this is set.|
|quarantine_until|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Set on release to 30 days after `released_at`. The address is not returned to stock before this time.|
|released_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the IP was released. Null until release.|
|suspension_reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason Telnyx recorded when suspending the IP. Null unless `status` is `suspended`.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

Monthly recurring charge (MRC) state for the IP's current allocation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|string|false|none|`not_started`: no charge recorded for the current allocation. `pending`: the charge is queued. `in_progress`: the charge is being created. `active`: the MRC is active. `stopping`: release requested; the MRC stop is being processed. `stopped`: the MRC has stopped. `stop_failed`: the MRC stop failed and the charge remains. `failed`: the charge could not be created.|
|charged|boolean|false|none|True when `status` is `active`, `stopping`, or `stop_failed`. An IP carries mail only after its charge has been created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|not_started|
|status|pending|
|status|in_progress|
|status|active|
|status|stopping|
|status|stopped|
|status|stop_failed|
|status|failed|

|dns_status|string|false|none|`dns_confirmed`: the PTR is forward-confirmed and `dns_confirmed_at` is set. `pending_ptr`: the PTR record is not yet in place. `pending_dns`: the PTR record is waiting for forward confirmation. `dns_lost`: a previously confirmed PTR no longer confirms, or the PTR request was abandoned before it ever confirmed (`ptr_request_state` is `abandoned`); the IP carries no mail until DNS is confirmed. `not_applicable`: the IP is released or has no PTR record on file.|
|ptr_request_state|string \| null|false|none|State of the Telnyx PTR change: `pending`, `pr_open`, `merged`, `confirmed`, `failed`, or `abandoned`. Informational.|
|ptr_request_pr_url|string \| null|false|none|Reference to the Telnyx PTR change request, when one exists. Informational.|
|checklist|object|false|none|Informational progress flags for the Telnyx-managed PTR. They do not gate `start_warmup`; use `dns_status` to check whether the IP can carry mail.|

<h2 id="tocS_DedicatedIpUpdateRequest">DedicatedIpUpdateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadedicatedipupdaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_DedicatedIpUpdateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSdedicatedipupdaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocsdedicatedipupdaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "pool_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "weight": 100,
  "force": false,
  "drain": false,
  "warmup_paused": true,
  "warmup": {
    "paused": true
  }
}
```

Applies one change per request. `pool_id` takes precedence over warm-up changes: when it is present, the IP moves to that pool (with `weight`, `force`, and `drain`) and other fields are ignored. Otherwise, use `warmup_paused` or `warmup.paused`; a Boolean `warmup_paused` takes precedence. The PTR hostname is managed by Telnyx and cannot be changed: when neither `pool_id` nor a warm-up field is present, a body that includes `ptr_hostname` (including `null`) returns `422` and the IP is unchanged. A body with none of these fields returns the IP unchanged.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pool_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Move the IP to this pool, replacing its current membership. Use the IP's current pool to change only its weight. To take an IP out of a pool, use `DELETE /email/ip_pools/{id}/ips/{ip_id}`.|
|weight|integer|false|none|Routing weight in the target pool. Used only with `pool_id`.|
|force|boolean|false|none|Set together with `drain: true` to move the last IP out of its current pool. Used only with `pool_id`.|
|drain|boolean|false|none|Set together with `force: true` to move the last IP out of its current pool. Acknowledges that mail routed to the emptied pool is held. Used only with `pool_id`.|
|warmup_paused|boolean|false|none|Pause (`true`) or resume (`false`) the warm-up ramp; equivalent to the `pause_warmup` and `resume_warmup` actions. A Boolean value takes precedence over `warmup.paused`. When a pause field is present and `pool_id` is absent, supplying neither pause field as a Boolean invokes resume.|
|warmup|object|false|none|Alias for `warmup_paused`.|

<h2 id="tocS_DedicatedIpWarmup">DedicatedIpWarmup</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadedicatedipwarmup"></a>
<a id="schema_DedicatedIpWarmup"></a>
<a id="tocSdedicatedipwarmup"></a>
<a id="tocsdedicatedipwarmup"></a>

```json
{
  "started_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "progress": 0,
  "daily_cap": 1,
  "paused": true,
  "paused_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "today": {
    "day": "1970-01-01",
    "cap": 0,
    "granted": 0,
    "remaining": 0
  }
}
```

Warmup ramp state for a dedicated IP.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|started_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When `start_warmup` was called. Null before warm-up starts and after release.|
|progress|integer|false|none|Ramp progress (0-100): the share of the 28 send-day schedule completed. Only UTC days on which the IP sent mail count. Set to 100 when the ramp completes, automatically or through `complete_warmup`. On an `active` IP this value is informational and can keep an earlier value after a suspension is lifted.|
|daily_cap|integer \| null|false|none|Daily cap of the current ramp stage. Null until the scheduler arms the first stage, and cleared when the ramp completes, automatically or through `complete_warmup`. On an `active` IP this value is informational and can keep an earlier stage cap after a suspension is lifted; it does not limit sending.|
|paused|boolean|false|none|True while the ramp is paused.|
|paused_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the ramp was paused. Null when not paused.|
|today|object \| null|false|none|Today's warmup allowance report card (current UTC day). Null outside the warmup window (before start_warmup, after release/suspension). `active` IPs report the ramp-complete allowance, except as described for `cap`.|

<h2 id="tocS_DefaultCondition">DefaultCondition</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadefaultcondition"></a>
<a id="schema_DefaultCondition"></a>
<a id="tocSdefaultcondition"></a>
<a id="tocsdefaultcondition"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "default"
}
```

Fallback edge condition: fires only when no other edge's condition is true.

Evaluated after every conditioned (`llm` / `expression`) edge regardless
of declaration order, so it routes the flow whenever none of the node's
other outgoing edges match. Valid **only** on edges leaving a `tool` or
`speak` node, where the deterministic step auto-advances and must always
have somewhere to go. A tool/speak node with any outgoing edge is required
to carry exactly one `default` edge so it never dead-ends; a tool/speak
node with no outgoing edges is a valid terminal step. Carries no parameters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_DelegationSettings">DelegationSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadelegationsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_DelegationSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSdelegationsettings"></a>
<a id="tocsdelegationsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "mode": "telnyx",
  "model": "string",
  "llm_api_key_ref": "string",
  "instructions": "string",
  "speak_results": true,
  "external_llm": {
    "model": "string",
    "base_url": "string",
    "llm_api_key_ref": "string",
    "authentication_method": "token",
    "certificate_ref": "string",
    "token_retrieval_url": "string",
    "forward_metadata": false,
    "extra_headers": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

Splits the conversation between a frontend model that talks to the caller and a backend model that does the work. On the GPT-Live route the frontend model cannot call tools at all — when it needs something done it raises a delegation and waits. On the chat completion route the frontend keeps a single `delegate` tool that returns immediately, so the conversation carries on while the backend works. Either way the backend's answer is spoken as commentary or kept as silent context, depending on `speak_results`. Beta feature.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the assistant delegates work to a backend model. Defaults to `true`: a GPT-Live assistant with delegation disabled can hold a conversation but can never look anything up or run a tool.|
|mode|string|false|none|Who answers a delegation. `telnyx` runs the backend model on Telnyx with the assistant's own tools, MCP servers and observability. `client` relays the delegation to a server you host over the WebSocket configured in `websocket_settings`: Telnyx sends a `session.delegation.created` frame and waits for your `session.delegation.completed` answer. That answer is text only, since the socket offers no tool vocabulary. If no socket is connected the delegation is refused and the assistant tells the caller it cannot look things up right now. Defaults to `telnyx`.|
|model|string|false|none|The backend model that answers delegations. Must be a model available for AI Assistants. When enabling `telnyx` delegation, explicitly set this field or `external_llm.model`; a configuration without either backend model is rejected. Only applies when `mode` is `telnyx`.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|Integration secret identifier for the backend model's API key. Required for models from providers other than Telnyx, OpenAI and Anthropic. A raw `api_key` is rejected rather than ignored, so that no plaintext credential is stored on the assistant.|
|instructions|string|false|none|Extra instructions for the backend model, in addition to the assistant's own. Use this for the business rules the backend needs and the talking model does not.|
|speak_results|boolean|false|none|Whether the backend's answer is spoken to the caller. When `true` the result is appended as commentary and paraphrased aloud; when `false` it is kept as silent context that informs later answers without being read out. Defaults to `true`.|
|external_llm|object|false|none|Run the backend on your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of a Telnyx-hosted model. As above, a raw `api_key` here is rejected — reference an integration secret with `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|telnyx|
|mode|client|
