A soft-deleted assistant in the Recently Deleted list: the full assistant configuration plus deletion metadata.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|version_id|string|false|none|Identifier for the assistant version returned by version-aware assistant endpoints.|
|version_created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when this assistant version was created.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|model|string|true|none|ID of the model to use when `external_llm` is not set. You can use the [Get models API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/openai-chat/get-available-models-openai-compatible) to see available models. If `external_llm` is provided, the assistant uses `external_llm` instead of this field. If neither `model` nor `external_llm` is provided, Telnyx applies the default model.|
|instructions|string|true|none|System instructions for the assistant. These may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables)|
|tools|[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)|false|none|The assistant's tools. Responses merge the assistant's shared Tools Library tools into this array alongside inline tools, each flagged `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. On update, a sent `tools` array fully replaces the inline tools only — shared tools stay attached unless `tool_ids` changes. Each tool type except `function`, `webhook`, and `client_side_tool` allows at most one instance per assistant across both sources.|
|mcp_servers|[[AssistantMCPServer](#schemaassistantmcpserver)]|false|none|MCP servers attached to the assistant. Create MCP servers with `/ai/mcp_servers`, then reference them by `id` here.|
|a2a_agents|[[AssistantA2AAgent](#schemaassistanta2aagent)]|false|none|A2A agents this assistant can delegate to. Tools are not stored here: at the start of every conversation each agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises, named `a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`. The following limits are not enforced when the assistant is saved, and anything past them is dropped when the conversation starts: 64 agents per assistant, 64 skills per card, 128 derived tools per assistant, and a 6 second budget for all card fetches combined. An agent whose card cannot be fetched costs the assistant that capability for the conversation; it does not fail the call.|
|greeting|string|false|none|Text that the assistant will use to start the conversation. This may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables). Use an empty string to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. Use the special value `<assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message>` to have the assistant generate the greeting based on the system instructions.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|This is only needed when using third-party inference providers selected by `model`. The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your LLM provider's API key. For bring-your-own endpoint authentication, use `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.|
|external_llm|[ExternalLLM](#schemaexternalllm)|false|none|none|
|fallback_config|[FallbackConfig](#schemafallbackconfig)|false|none|none|
|voice_settings|[inference-embedding_VoiceSettings](#schemainference-embedding_voicesettings)|false|none|none|
|avatar_settings|[AvatarSettings](#schemaavatarsettings) \| null|false|none|**Beta:** Saved avatar configuration for supported realtime browser conversations. `null` means that no avatar is configured.|
|transcription|[TranscriptionSettings](#schematranscriptionsettings)|false|none|none|
|telephony_settings|[TelephonySettings](#schematelephonysettings)|false|none|none|
|messaging_settings|[MessagingSettings](#schemamessagingsettings)|false|none|none|
|enabled_features|[[EnabledFeatures](#schemaenabledfeatures)]|false|none|none|
|insight_settings|[InsightSettings](#schemainsightsettings)|false|none|none|
|privacy_settings|[PrivacySettings](#schemaprivacysettings)|false|none|none|
|dynamic_variables_webhook_url|string|false|none|If `dynamic_variables_webhook_url` is set, Telnyx sends a POST request to this URL at the start of the conversation to resolve dynamic variables. **Gotcha:** the webhook response must wrap variables under a top-level `dynamic_variables` object, e.g. `{"dynamic_variables": {"customer_name": "Jane"}}`. Returning a flat object will be ignored and variables will fall back to their defaults. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) for the full request/response format and timeout behavior.|
|dynamic_variables_webhook_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|Timeout in milliseconds for the dynamic variables webhook. Must be between 1 and 10000 ms. If the webhook does not respond within this timeout, the call proceeds with default values. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables).|
|dynamic_variables|object|false|none|Map of dynamic variables and their values|
|import_metadata|[ImportMetadata](#schemaimportmetadata)|false|none|none|
|widget_settings|[WidgetSettings](#schemawidgetsettings)|false|none|Configuration settings for the assistant's web widget.|
|interruption_settings|[inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings](#schemainference-embedding_interruptionsettings)|false|none|Settings for interruptions and how the assistant decides the user has finished speaking. These timings are most relevant when using non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn behavior is controlled by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` (`eot_threshold`, `eot_timeout_ms`, `eager_eot_threshold`).|
|integrations|[[AssistantIntegration](#schemaassistantintegration)]|false|none|Connected integrations attached to the assistant. The catalog of available integrations is at `/ai/integrations`; the user's connected integrations are at `/ai/integrations/connections`. Each item references a catalog integration by `integration_id`.|
|observability_settings|[Observability](#schemaobservability)|false|none|none|
|version_name|string|false|none|Human-readable name for the assistant version.|
|related_mission_ids|[string]|false|none|IDs of missions related to this assistant.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the assistant. Tags can also be managed with the assistant tag endpoints.|
|post_conversation_settings|[PostConversationSettings](#schemapostconversationsettings)|false|none|Configuration for post-conversation processing. When enabled, the assistant receives one additional LLM turn after the conversation ends, allowing it to execute final tool calls such as sending a summary or updating a record via webhook or function tools. Integration and MCP server tools are not available post-conversation; call-control tools (e.g. hangup, transfer) are also unavailable. Beta feature.|
|delegation_settings|[DelegationSettings](#schemadelegationsettings)|false|none|Splits the conversation between a frontend model that talks to the caller and a backend model that does the work. On the GPT-Live route the frontend model cannot call tools at all — when it needs something done it raises a delegation and waits. On the chat completion route the frontend keeps a single `delegate` tool that returns immediately, so the conversation carries on while the backend works. Either way the backend's answer is spoken as commentary or kept as silent context, depending on `speak_results`. Beta feature.|
|websocket_settings|[WebsocketSettings](#schemawebsocketsettings)|false|none|Streams conversation and telephony events to a WebSocket server you host, and accepts messages injected back into the conversation. Telnyx opens the connection as a client, once per conversation. Delivery is best effort throughout: while the connection is down events are dropped rather than queued, and no socket failure is ever allowed to affect the call. Beta feature.|
|conversation_flow|[ConversationFlow](#schemaconversationflow)|false|none|Conversation flow as returned by the API.|
|deleted_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the soft delete.|
|permanently_deleted_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Point after which the assistant is permanently deleted automatically and can no longer be restored.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|enabled_features|telephony|
|enabled_features|messaging|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "To": "+12065550100",
  "From": "+12065550200"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Beep|string|false|none|Whether to play a notification beep to the conference when the participant enters and exits.|
|StatusCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send status callback events to for the call.|
|StatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `StatusCallback`.|
|StatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the call's state that should generate a call to `StatusCallback`. Can be: `initiated`, `ringing`, `answered`, and `completed`. Separate multiple values with a space. The default value is `completed`.|
|To|string|false|none|The phone number of the called party. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|From|string|false|none|The phone number of the party that initiated the call. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|Timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that we should allow the phone to ring before assuming there is no answer. Can be an integer between 5 and 120, inclusive. The default value is 30.|
|Muted|boolean|false|none|Whether the participant should be muted.|
|StartConferenceOnEnter|boolean|false|none|Whether to start the conference when the participant enters. Defaults to `true`.|
|EndConferenceOnExit|boolean|false|none|Whether to end the conference when the participant leaves. Defaults to `false`.|
|Label|string|false|none|A unique label for the participant that will be added to the conference. The label can be used to reference the participant for updates via the TeXML REST API.|
|EarlyMedia|boolean|false|none|Whether participant shall be bridged to conference before the participant answers (from early media if available). Defaults to `false`.|
|ConferenceStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the conference callbacks will be sent to.|
|ConferenceStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `ConferenceStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|ConferenceStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the conference's state that should generate a call to `ConferenceStatusCallback`. Can be: `start`, `end`, `join` and `leave`. Separate multiple values with a space. By default no callbacks are sent.|
|WaitUrl|string|false|none|The URL to call for an audio file to play while the participant is waiting for the conference to start.|
|MaxParticipants|integer|false|none|The maximum number of participants in the conference. Can be a positive integer from 2 to 800. The default value is 250.|
|Coaching|boolean|false|none|Whether the participant is coaching another call. When `true`, `CallSidToCoach` has to be given.|
|CallSidToCoach|string|false|none|The SID of the participant who is being coached. The participant being coached is the only participant who can hear the participant who is coaching.|
|CallerId|string|false|none|To be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`To` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and `-_~!.+` special characters. If ommited, the display name will be the same as the number in the `From` field.|
|TimeLimit|integer|false|none|The maximum duration of the call in seconds.|
|MachineDetection|string|false|none|Whether to detect if a human or an answering machine picked up the call. Use `Enable` if you would like to ne notified as soon as the called party is identified. Use `DetectMessageEnd`, if you would like to leave a message on an answering machine.|
|MachineDetectionTimeout|integer|false|none|How long answering machine detection should go on for before sending an `Unknown` result. Given in milliseconds.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechThreshold|integer|false|none|Maximum threshold of a human greeting. If greeting longer than this value, considered machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold|integer|false|none|Silence duration threshold after a greeting message or voice for it be considered human. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSilenceTimeout|integer|false|none|If initial silence duration is greater than this value, consider it a machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionBeepProfile|string|false|none|Selects which detectors must validate a beep. `both` requires the amplitude and frequency detectors to agree. `freq_only` uses the frequency detector alone, for beeps whose volume is too unsteady for the default profile. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepMinFrequency|integer(int32)|false|none|Lowest frequency, in Hz, that a tone must reach to be treated as a beep. Raising it above 480 excludes North American ringback (440 + 480 Hz), which can otherwise be reported as a beep when the `freq_only` profile is in use. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepMaxFrequency|integer(int32)|false|none|Highest frequency, in Hz, that a tone can reach and still be treated as a beep. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepMinToneDuration|integer(int32)|false|none|Shortest tone, in milliseconds, that can be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects brief tones such as call-progress blips. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralConfirmation|boolean|false|none|When enabled, a candidate beep must pass an additional spectral check before it is reported. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralWindow|integer(int32)|false|none|Length of the spectral confirmation window, in milliseconds. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralMinPurity|number|false|none|Minimum spectral purity, from 0 to 1, for a tone to be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects mixed tones such as ringback, which combines two frequencies. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralRejectFaxCng|boolean|false|none|When enabled, the fax CNG tone is rejected rather than reported as a beep. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|AmdStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the result of answering machine detection will be sent to.|
|AmdStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `AmdStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|ApplicationSid|string|false|none|The SID of the TeXML application that will handle the new participant's call. Required unless joining an existing conference by its ConferenceSid.|
|CancelPlaybackOnMachineDetection|boolean|false|none|Whether to cancel ongoing playback on `machine` detection. Defaults to `true`.|
|CancelPlaybackOnDetectMessageEnd|boolean|false|none|Whether to cancel ongoing playback on `greeting ended` detection. Defaults to `true`.|
|PreferredCodecs|string|false|none|The list of comma-separated codecs to be offered on a call.|
|Record|boolean|false|none|Whether to record the entire participant's call leg. Defaults to `false`.|
|RecordingChannels|string|false|none|The number of channels in the final recording. Defaults to `mono`.|
|RecordingStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the recording callbacks will be sent to.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `RecordingStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the recording's state that should generate a call to `RecoridngStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`.|
|RecordingTrack|string|false|none|The audio track to record for the call. The default is `both`.|
|SipAuthPassword|string|false|none|The password to use for SIP authentication.|
|SipAuthUsername|string|false|none|The username to use for SIP authentication.|
|Trim|string|false|none|Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the recording. Defaults to `trim-silence`.|
|ConferenceRecord|string|false|none|Whether to record the conference the participant is joining. Defualts to `do-not-record`. The boolean values `true` and `false` are synonymous with `record-from-start` and `do-not-record` respectively.|
|ConferenceRecordingStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the conference recording callbacks will be sent to.|
|ConferenceRecordingStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `ConferenceRecordingStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|ConferenceRecordingStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the conference recording's state that should generate a call to `RecoridngStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`. `failed` and `absent` are synonymous.|
|ConferenceRecordingTimeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that the transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite)|
|ConferenceTrim|string|false|none|Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the conference recording. Defaults to `trim-silence`.|
|CustomHeaders|[object]|false|none|Custom HTTP headers to be sent with the call. Each header should be an object with 'name' and 'value' properties.|

<h2 id="tocS_DialMetric">DialMetric</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadialmetric"></a>
<a id="schema_DialMetric"></a>
<a id="tocSdialmetric"></a>
<a id="tocsdialmetric"></a>

```json
{
  "record_type": "dial_metric",
  "region": "us",
  "start_time": "2026-09-29T12:00:00.000Z",
  "end_time": "2026-09-29T13:00:00.000Z",
  "dials": {
    "total": 85600,
    "accepted": 85240,
    "rejected": {
      "dps_limit": 360,
      "hourly_limit": 0,
      "daily_limit": 0
    }
  },
  "average_dps": 23.7778,
  "peak_dps": 104,
  "dps_limit": 100
}
```

Dial counts and rates for one region in one time bucket. One record per region per bucket.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|string|false|none|none|
|region|string|false|none|Region where the dials were handled. Current values are `us`, `eu`, `australia`, `middle_east`, `canada` and `india`. New values can be added, so clients must tolerate values not listed here. Buckets of different regions are separate records.|
|start_time|string(date-time)|false|none|Start of the bucket (inclusive), UTC.|
|end_time|string(date-time)|false|none|End of the bucket (exclusive), UTC. Five seconds, one minute or one hour after `start_time`, depending on `granularity`.|
|dials|object|false|none|Dial attempt counts in the bucket.|
|average_dps|number|false|none|`dials.total` divided by the bucket duration in seconds, rounded to 4 decimal places. Counts every dial attempt, rejected ones included.|
|peak_dps|number|false|none|Dials per second, rounded to 4 decimal places, in the busiest 5-second window of the bucket, summed across all call-processing nodes of the region. Counts every dial attempt, rejected ones included, so `peak_dps` above `dps_limit` is expected when dials were rejected. For `granularity=second` it equals `average_dps`.|
|dps_limit|integer \| null|false|none|DPS limit in force during the busiest 5-second window, so it compares directly with `peak_dps`. `null` means unlimited. Enforcement near the limit is approximate; `dials.rejected.dps_limit` is the authoritative signal that the limit was reached.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|record_type|dial_metric|

<h2 id="tocS_DirStatus">DirStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadirstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_DirStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSdirstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsdirstatus"></a>

```json
"draft"
```

DIR lifecycle status.
- `draft` - newly created; editable; not yet submitted.
- `submitted` / `in_review` - Telnyx is reviewing.
- `verified` - approved; phone numbers may be attached.
- `rejected` - Telnyx rejected this submission; `rejection_reasons` is populated; customer can edit and resubmit.
- `unsuccessful` - system-side error during processing; customer can edit and resubmit.
- `suspended` - temporarily disabled (e.g. by an active infringement claim).
- `expired` - verification expired; customer must resubmit.
- `infringement_claimed` - a trademark/impersonation claim is open against this DIR.
- `permanently_rejected` - terminal; cannot be resubmitted.
- `delete_requested` - you have requested deletion; the DIR still exists and Telnyx is completing the removal (de-registration and cleanup). A verified DIR keeps serving its branded identity, and keeps billing, until the removal finishes.

|display_name|string|false|none|Name shown to call recipients. 1–35 characters, no emoji, not whitespace-only.|
|reselling|boolean|false|none|Set to true if your organization places calls on behalf of other enterprises (BPO/reseller). Updating this triggers re-vetting on next submit.|
|authorizer_name|string|false|none|Name of the person at your enterprise authorizing this DIR. Must be a real individual.|
|authorizer_email|string(email)|false|none|Contact email of the authorizer. Telnyx may send verification or infringement notices here.|
|logo_url|string(uri)|false|none|Publicly accessible HTTPS URL (max 128 chars) to a 256x256 BMP logo (max 1 MB).|
|call_reasons|[string]|false|none|1–10 reasons your business calls customers. Validate phrasing against `POST /call_reasons/validate`.|
|certify_brand_is_accurate|boolean|false|none|Certification that the DIR information is accurate. Must be `true` for the DIR to be submitted for vetting.|
|certify_no_shaft_content|boolean|false|none|Certification that this DIR is not used for SHAFT content (Sex, Hate, Alcohol, Firearms, Tobacco) where prohibited. Must be `true` for the DIR to be submitted for vetting.|
|certify_ip_ownership|boolean|false|none|Certification of ownership of any logos/trademarks shown. Must be `true` for the DIR to be submitted for vetting.|
|documents|[[Document](#schemadocument)]|false|none|Additional supporting documents to attach. Append-only: existing documents are never removed or replaced, and an empty or omitted list is a no-op. Each `document_id` may appear at most once on a DIR.|
|webhook_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|Optional `https://` URL that receives webhook notifications when this DIR's compliance review completes. Send `null` to clear. Changing only this field on a `verified` DIR does not re-vet it. Maximum 2048 characters.|
|bpo_authorizations|[[BpoAuthorizationInput](#schemabpoauthorizationinput)]|false|none|Optional. Replace this DIR's authorized BPO (Business Process Outsourcer) accounts with these, each with its signed Letter of Authorization. The supplied list replaces the current one: a BPO left out has its authorization removed, and a new BPO (or a changed Letter of Authorization) is created `pending` admin review. Send an empty list to clear all authorizations; omit the field to leave them unchanged. Editing this list does not re-vet the DIR. Maximum 10.|

Suppression record. Schema fields hidden by the view:
`account_id`, `bounce_category`, `dsn_code`, `meta`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|record_type|string|true|none|View-only discriminator.|
|domain_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|`null` ⇒ account scope. Stored on the row; exposed here.|
|group_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|`null` ⇒ global; set ⇒ group-scoped opt-out.|
|from|string \| null|false|none|`null` ⇒ not address-scope. (schema: from_address)|
|to|string|true|none|Normalized recipient. (schema: to_address)|
|reason|[Reason](#schemareason)|true|none|none|
|source|[email_Source](#schemaemail_source)|true|none|none|
|scope|[Scope](#schemascope)|true|none|Derived server-side from `domain_id`/`from`; never trusted from the caller.|
|status|[Status](#schemastatus)|true|none|none|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Optional expiration time. An active row stops matching<br>send-time suppression checks as soon as `expires_at <= now()`.<br>A maintenance worker later transitions the row to `status: expired`<br>and appends an `expired` audit event (normally within 15 minutes).<br>|

|source|manual|
|source|import|
|source|system|
|scope|account|

|scope|address|

|status|expired|

<h2 id="tocS_EmailDMARCPolicy">EmailDMARCPolicy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemaildmarcpolicy"></a>
<a id="schema_EmailDMARCPolicy"></a>
<a id="tocSemaildmarcpolicy"></a>
<a id="tocsemaildmarcpolicy"></a>

```json
{
  "p": "none",
  "pct": 100,
  "rua": "string",
  "sp": "none"
}
```

DMARC policy for a sending domain. Drives the recommended _dmarc.<domain> TXT record. DMARC is advisory and never blocks sending. When omitted or null, the domain uses the advisory default (v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@telnyx.com).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|p|string|false|none|Policy applied to messages that fail alignment.|
|pct|integer|false|none|Percentage of messages the policy applies to. Omitted from the record when 100.|
|rua|string \| null|false|none|URI for aggregate reports. Defaults to the Telnyx address when absent; null omits it.|
|sp|string \| null|false|none|Policy for subdomains. Omitted from the record when null.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|p|none|
|p|quarantine|
|p|reject|
|sp|none|
|sp|quarantine|
|sp|reject|

<h2 id="tocS_EmailDomainDKIMRotation">EmailDomainDKIMRotation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemaildomaindkimrotation"></a>
<a id="schema_EmailDomainDKIMRotation"></a>
<a id="tocSemaildomaindkimrotation"></a>
<a id="tocsemaildomaindkimrotation"></a>

```json
{
  "record_type": "email_domain_dkim_rotation",
  "domain_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174002",
  "domain": "example.com",
  "dkim": {
    "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-42661417400a",
    "selector": "telnyx1",
    "algorithm": "rsa-sha256",
    "key_length": 2048,
    "version": 2,
    "status": "active",
    "activated_at": "2026-09-11T12:00:00Z"
  },
  "previous_dkim_key": {
    "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174009",
    "selector": "telnyx1",
    "version": 1,
    "status": "retiring"
  },
  "old_selector_retained": false,
  "dns_records": [
    {
      "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-42661417400b",
      "purpose": "dkim",
      "record_type": "TXT",
      "host": "telnyx1._domainkey.example.com",
      "value": "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkqh...",
      "actual_value": null,
      "priority": null,
      "required": true,
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ]
}
```

Result of rotating a domain's DKIM key. The new key is active and signing switches to it immediately; the previous key is retired to a `retiring` state (retained, not revoked) so it can be revoked after the DNS propagation grace period. Selectors are fixed, so the DKIM DNS record's TXT value is replaced in place at the shared `<selector>._domainkey.<domain>` host — `old_selector_retained` is false and the returned dns_records carry the new value the customer must publish promptly.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|string|true|none|none|
|domain_id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|domain|string|true|none|none|
|dkim|object|true|none|The new active DKIM key.|
|previous_dkim_key|object \| null|true|none|The retired previous key, or null when the domain had no active key before rotation. Retained in a `retiring` state so it can be revoked after the DNS propagation grace period.<br>|
|old_selector_retained|boolean|true|none|False for this service: one selector is fixed per domain, so rotation replaces the TXT value at the existing _domainkey host. There is no dual-selector overlap; publish the replacement TXT promptly because signing switches immediately.|
|dns_records|[[DNSRecord](#schemadnsrecord)]|true|none|The DKIM DNS records the customer must publish, carrying the new key's TXT value with verification reset to pending.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|record_type|email_domain_dkim_rotation|

<h2 id="tocS_EmailEventCounts">EmailEventCounts</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemaileventcounts"></a>
<a id="schema_EmailEventCounts"></a>
<a id="tocSemaileventcounts"></a>
<a id="tocsemaileventcounts"></a>

```json
{
  "queued": 0,
  "sent": 0,
  "delivered": 0,
  "deferred": 0,
  "bounced": 0,
  "opened": 0,
  "clicked": 0,
  "complained": 0,
  "unsubscribed": 0,
  "failed": 0
}
```

Recipient-level outcome counts for the queried time range. Each to, cc, and bcc recipient counts separately; repeated events of the same type for the same message and recipient count once. Partial MTA injection results count successful recipients as sent and unsuccessful recipients as failed. Only the ten listed event types are counted; other valid event types (scheduled, cancelled, sandbox, sending, rejected) are not included in stats.

|bounced|integer|true|none|none|

|clicked|integer|true|none|none|

|unsubscribed|integer|true|none|none|
|failed|integer|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_EmailEventType">EmailEventType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemaileventtype"></a>
<a id="schema_EmailEventType"></a>
<a id="tocSemaileventtype"></a>
<a id="tocsemaileventtype"></a>

```json
"queued"
```

Bare stored event names returned by message history. In addition to the normal send and delivery lifecycle, polling can expose suppression, scan, and quarantine lifecycle rows. Sharp canonical names gw_reject, injection_timeout, and expired distinguish gateway rejection, ambiguous injection timeout, and MTA expiration. The failed and bounced names remain valid for system/admin failures and hard bounces respectively. Existing stored rows retain their original names.

|professional_license_number|string \| null|false|none|If your business operates under a professional license (for example legal, medical, or financial services), enter the license number issued by the licensing authority. Leave blank if it does not apply.|

<h2 id="tocS_Expression">Expression</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaexpression"></a>
<a id="schema_Expression"></a>
<a id="tocSexpression"></a>
<a id="tocsexpression"></a>

```json
{
  "left": {
    "name": "user_age",
    "type": "variable"
  },
  "op": ">=",
  "right": {
    "type": "number_literal",
    "value": 18
  },
  "type": "comparison"
}
```

A node in a deterministic expression AST. Exactly one variant is selected by the `type` discriminator. Terminal variants (`number_literal`, `string_literal`, `bool_literal`, `variable`) bottom out the recursion; `arithmetic`, `bool_op`, and `comparison` nest further sub-expressions.

Extracted into a single named schema so the recursive union is defined once (was previously inlined at every operand site).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[ComparisonExpression](#schemacomparisonexpression)|false|none|Compare two sub-expressions with a relational or membership operator.<br><br>Evaluates to a boolean. Used in edge conditions to gate transitions on<br>runtime values, e.g. `user_age >= 18` or `tier == "gold"`.|
|*oneOf*|[BooleanOpExpression](#schemabooleanopexpression)|false|none|Combine sub-expressions with a logical operator (`and` / `or` / `not`).<br><br>`and` and `or` accept two or more operands; `not` accepts exactly one.|
|*oneOf*|[ArithmeticExpression](#schemaarithmeticexpression)|false|none|Numeric expression: applies an arithmetic operator to two sub-expressions.<br><br>Useful for derived numeric checks, e.g. `cart_total + shipping > 50`.<br>Both operands should resolve to numbers at runtime.|
|*oneOf*|[DynamicVariableExpression](#schemadynamicvariableexpression)|false|none|Reference a dynamic variable by name.<br><br>Resolved at runtime from the assistant's dynamic-variables context (see<br>`Assistant.dynamic_variables` and the dynamic-variables webhook).|
|*oneOf*|[StringLiteralExpression](#schemastringliteralexpression)|false|none|Constant string value.|
|*oneOf*|[NumberLiteralExpression](#schemanumberliteralexpression)|false|none|Constant numeric value (float; integers are accepted and stored as float).|
|*oneOf*|[BooleanLiteralExpression](#schemabooleanliteralexpression)|false|none|Constant boolean value. Useful for unconditional ('always') edges.|

<h2 id="tocS_ExpressionCondition">ExpressionCondition</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaexpressioncondition"></a>
<a id="schema_ExpressionCondition"></a>
<a id="tocSexpressioncondition"></a>
<a id="tocsexpressioncondition"></a>

```json
{
  "expression": {
    "left": {
      "name": "user_age",
      "type": "variable"
    },
    "op": ">=",
    "right": {
      "type": "number_literal",
      "value": 18
    },
    "type": "comparison"
  },
  "type": "expression"
}
```

Edge condition evaluated as a deterministic expression AST.

The expression is computed against runtime dynamic variables and must
evaluate to a boolean. Prefer this over `LLMCondition` when the rule is
a clean function of known variables — it's cheaper and predictable.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expression|[Expression](#schemaexpression)|true|none|A node in a deterministic expression AST. Exactly one variant is selected by the `type` discriminator. Terminal variants (`number_literal`, `string_literal`, `bool_literal`, `variable`) bottom out the recursion; `arithmetic`, `bool_op`, and `comparison` nest further sub-expressions.<br><br>Extracted into a single named schema so the recursive union is defined once (was previously inlined at every operand site).|
|type|string|true|none|none|

```json
  "extra_headers": {

    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|Model identifier to use with the external LLM endpoint.|
|base_url|string|true|none|Base URL for the external LLM endpoint.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|Integration secret identifier for the external LLM API key.|
|authentication_method|[AuthenticationMethod](#schemaauthenticationmethod)|false|none|Authentication method used when connecting to the external LLM endpoint.|
|certificate_ref|string|false|none|Integration secret identifier for the client certificate used with certificate authentication.|
|token_retrieval_url|string|false|none|URL used to retrieve an access token when certificate authentication is enabled.|
|forward_metadata|boolean|false|none|When `true`, Telnyx forwards the assistant's dynamic variables to the external LLM endpoint as a top-level `extra_metadata` object on the chat completion request body. Defaults to `false`. Example payload sent to the external endpoint: `{"extra_metadata": {"customer_name": "Jane", "account_id": "acct_789", "telnyx_agent_target": "+13125550100", "telnyx_end_user_target": "+13125550123"}}`. Distinct from OpenAI's native `metadata` field, which has its own size and type limits.|
|extra_headers|object \| null|false|none|Custom HTTP headers Telnyx sets on every request to the external LLM endpoint, in addition to the authentication header. Keys are header names, values are static strings. At most 32 headers. Reserved names are rejected: accept-encoding, authorization, connection, content-encoding, content-length, content-type, cookie, expect, host, keep-alive, proxy-authenticate, proxy-authorization, proxy-connection, set-cookie, te, trailer, transfer-encoding, upgrade, x-host-rewrite, x-request-id, x-trace-id, and any x-telnyx-* or x-stainless-* header; '_' counts as '-' when names are compared. Names must be valid HTTP header names (RFC 7230 token, at most 128 characters) and must not repeat (case-insensitive). Values must be printable ASCII, at most 4096 characters, with no leading or trailing whitespace. Values are stored as plain text and returned when the assistant is retrieved.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|authentication_method|token|
|authentication_method|certificate|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|direction|[Direction](#schemadirection)|false|none|The direction of the fax.|
|media_url|[MediaUrl](#schemamediaurl)|false|none|The URL (or list of URLs) to the fax document. Supported formats: PDF, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, DOC, DOCX, RTF, and TXT. media_url and media_name/contents can't be submitted together.|
|media_name|[MediaName](#schemamedianame)|false|none|The media_name used for the fax's media. Must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. Supported formats: PDF, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, DOC, DOCX, RTF, and TXT. media_name and media_url/contents can't be submitted together.|
|to|[To](#schemato)|false|none|The phone number, in E.164 format, the fax will be sent to or SIP URI|
|from|[From](#schemafrom)|false|none|The phone number, in E.164 format, the fax will be sent from.|
|from_display_name|string|false|none|The string used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`to` number).|
|quality|[Quality](#schemaquality)|false|none|The quality of the fax. The `ultra` settings provides the highest quality available, but also present longer fax processing times. `ultra_light` is best suited for images, wihle `ultra_dark` is best suited for text.|
|status|string|false|none|Status of the fax|
|webhook_url|string|false|none|URL that will receive fax webhooks|
|webhook_failover_url|string|false|none|Optional failover URL that will receive fax webhooks if webhook_url doesn't return a 2XX response|
|store_media|boolean|false|none|Should fax media be stored on temporary URL. It does not support media_name.|
|stored_media_url|string|false|none|If store_media was set to true, this is a link to temporary location. Link expires after 10 minutes.|
|preview_url|string|false|none|If `store_preview` was set to `true`, this is a link to temporary location. Link expires after 10 minutes.|
|client_state|string|false|none|State received from a command.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO 8601 timestamp when resource was created|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO 8601 timestamp when resource was updated|
|failure_reason|string \| null|false|none|Customer-facing failure reason for the fax. Present on every fax object (null when the fax has not failed). Mapped from the more granular `internal_failure_reason`. Common values include: `receiver_call_dropped`, `sender_call_dropped`, `sender_canceled`, `carrier_lost`, `service_unavailable`, `fax_signaling_error`, `receiver_communication_error`, `sender_communication_error`, `receiver_decline`, `receiver_recovery_on_timer_expire`, `receiver_no_response`, `receiver_invalid_number_format`, `receiver_no_answer`, `receiver_incompatible_destination`, `receiver_unallocated_number`, `destination_unreachable`, `user_busy`, `invalid_ecm_response_from_receiver`, `fax_initial_communication_timeout`, `destination_not_in_service_plan`, `account_disabled`, `destination_invalid`, `no_outbound_profile`, `destination_not_in_countries_whitelist`, `user_channel_limit_exceeded`, `outbound_profile_channel_limit_exceeded`, `connection_channel_limit_exceeded`, `outbound_profile_daily_spend_limit_exceeded`, `unverified_origination_number`, `unverified_destination_not_allowed`, `file_format_invalid`, `file_download_failed`, `file_size_limit_exceeded`, `page_count_limit_exceeded`, `media_processing_exception`.|
|internal_failure_reason|string \| null|false|none|Internal, more granular failure reason for the fax. Present on every fax object (null when the fax has not failed). Useful for deeper debugging beyond the customer-facing `failure_reason`.|

<h2 id="tocS_FlowEdge">FlowEdge</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaflowedge"></a>
<a id="schema_FlowEdge"></a>
<a id="tocSflowedge"></a>
<a id="tocsflowedge"></a>

```json
{
  "condition": {
    "prompt": "The user has confirmed their booking details.",
    "type": "llm"
  },
  "id": "e_age_gate",
  "start_node_id": "string",
  "target": {
    "node_id": "n_billing",
    "type": "node"
  }
}
```

Directed transition from one node to a target, gated by a condition.

The target is either another node in the same flow (`NodeTarget`) or a
different assistant (`AssistantTarget`). Multiple edges may share a
`start_node_id`. On calls, `expression` conditions are evaluated before
the model turn and take precedence over `llm` conditions regardless of
declaration order, while `llm` conditions are offered to the assistant's
model as transition tools and fire when the model selects one. On chat
channels, an `expression` condition that is true when the turn begins
routes before the reply is generated; all conditioned edges that remain
are considered together in declaration order after the reply, and the
first true one wins.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|condition|[LLMCondition](#schemallmcondition) \| [ExpressionCondition](#schemaexpressioncondition) \| [DefaultCondition](#schemadefaultcondition)|true|none|Condition that gates the transition. Discriminated by `type`: `llm`, `expression`.|
|id|string|true|none|Caller-supplied unique identifier for this edge within the flow.|
|start_node_id|string|true|none|ID of the node this edge transitions away from.|
|target|[NodeTarget](#schemanodetarget) \| [AssistantTarget](#schemaassistanttarget)|true|none|Destination of the transition. Discriminated by `type`: `node` (jump to another node in this flow) or `assistant` (hand off to a different assistant).|

One step in a conversation flow, as returned by the API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_llm|[ExternalLLM](#schemaexternalllm)|false|none|Override for `Assistant.external_llm` while this node is active. Use this to route a node's turns to a different external LLM (different `model`, `base_url`, credentials). Part of the LLM bundle — see `model` for cascade semantics. Mutually exclusive with `model` on the node (a single LLM identity per node).|
|id|string|true|none|Caller-supplied unique identifier for this node within the flow.|
|instructions|string|true|none|Prompt that drives the LLM while this node is active. Required.|
|instructions_mode|string|false|none|How `instructions` combine with the assistant-level instructions. `replace` (default): the node's instructions are used alone. `append`: the node's instructions are concatenated after the assistant's instructions.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|Override for `Assistant.llm_api_key_ref` while this node is active. Part of the LLM bundle — see `model` for cascade semantics.|
|model|string|false|none|Override for `Assistant.model` while this node is active. Part of the LLM bundle (`model` + `llm_api_key_ref` + `external_llm`): when any of the three is set on the node, all three are taken from the node and the assistant-level LLM identity is not consulted. When none of the three is set, the assistant's bundle cascades unchanged.|
|name|string|false|none|Optional human-readable label, displayed in authoring UIs.|
|position|[NodePosition](#schemanodeposition)|false|none|Optional canvas coordinates used by authoring UIs to lay out the graph. Ignored by the runtime; round-trips so frontends can persist graph layout across reloads.|
|shared_tool_ids|[string]|false|none|IDs of shared (org-level) tools available at this node. Knowledge bases are attached the same way — via a shared retrieval tool. Tools not listed here are not callable while this node is active.|
|tools|[[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)]|false|none|Full tool definitions for this node, resolved from `shared_tool_ids` server-side.   ],


One step in a conversation flow, as supplied by API clients.

Each node carries the prompt, tool scope, and optional overrides for
model/voice/transcription. Unset overrides cascade from the assistant.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_llm|[ExternalLLMReq](#schemaexternalllmreq)|false|none|Override for `Assistant.external_llm` while this node is active. Use this to route a node's turns to a different external LLM (different `model`, `base_url`, credentials). Part of the LLM bundle — see `model` for cascade semantics. Mutually exclusive with `model` on the node (a single LLM identity per node).|
|id|string|true|none|Caller-supplied unique identifier for this node within the flow.|
|instructions|string|true|none|Prompt that drives the LLM while this node is active. Required.|
|instructions_mode|string|false|none|How `instructions` combine with the assistant-level instructions. `replace` (default): the node's instructions are used alone. `append`: the node's instructions are concatenated after the assistant's instructions.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|Override for `Assistant.llm_api_key_ref` while this node is active. Part of the LLM bundle — see `model` for cascade semantics.|
|model|string|false|none|Override for `Assistant.model` while this node is active. Part of the LLM bundle (`model` + `llm_api_key_ref` + `external_llm`): when any of the three is set on the node, all three are taken from the node and the assistant-level LLM identity is not consulted. When none of the three is set, the assistant's bundle cascades unchanged.|
|name|string|false|none|Optional human-readable label, displayed in authoring UIs.|
|position|[NodePosition](#schemanodeposition)|false|none|Optional canvas coordinates used by authoring UIs to lay out the graph. Ignored by the runtime; round-trips so frontends can persist graph layout across reloads.|
|shared_tool_ids|[string]|false|none|IDs of shared (org-level) tools available at this node. Knowledge bases are attached the same way — via a shared retrieval tool. Tools not listed here are not callable while this node is active.|
|tools_mode|string|false|none|How `shared_tool_ids` combine with the assistant-level tool set. `replace` (default): only the node's tools are callable. `append`: the node's tools are added to the assistant's tools. Ignored when `shared_tool_ids` is null.|
|transcription|[TranscriptionSettings](#schematranscriptionsettings)|false|none|Per-node transcription override (model/language/region). Unset fields cascade from the assistant-level transcription. A node that sets `model`, `fallback_models`, or `challenger` doesn't inherit the assistant's `fallback_models` or `challenger`; it uses only the ones it sets. Otherwise it inherits them, and they must fit the model and language the node runs; a change they no longer fit is rejected.|
|type|string|false|none|Node kind discriminator. `prompt` (default) is an LLM-driven step; `tool` is a standalone tool execution and `speak` a scripted message (see `ToolNodeReq` / `SpeakNodeReq`).|
|voice_settings|[inference-embedding_VoiceSettings](#schemainference-embedding_voicesettings)|false|none|Per-node voice override. Only fields set here override the assistant-level voice settings; unset fields cascade.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|instructions_mode|replace|
|instructions_mode|append|
|tools_mode|replace|
|tools_mode|append|

```json
{
```

```json
  "maximum_digits": 10,
  "timeout_millis": 60000,
  "inter_digit_timeout_millis": 10000,
  "initial_timeout_millis": 10000,
  "terminating_digit": "#",
  "valid_digits": "123",
  "gather_id": "my_gather_id",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|minimum_digits|integer(int32)|false|none|The minimum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a minimum value of 1.|
|maximum_digits|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a maximum value of 128.|
|timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of milliseconds to wait to complete the request.|
|inter_digit_timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of milliseconds to wait for input between digits.|
|initial_timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of milliseconds to wait for the first DTMF.|
|terminating_digit|string|false|none|The digit used to terminate input if fewer than `maximum_digits` digits have been gathered. Set to an empty string to disable the terminating digit entirely, so that a digit such as `#` can be collected as input per `valid_digits`.|
|valid_digits|string|false|none|A list of all digits accepted as valid.|
|gather_id|string|false|none|An id that will be sent back in the corresponding `call.gather.ended` webhook. Will be randomly generated if not specified.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|parameters|object|true|none|The parameters described as a JSON Schema object that needs to be gathered by the voice assistant. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format|
|assistant|[Assistant](#schemaassistant)|false|none|Assistant configuration including choice of LLM, custom instructions, and tools.|
|transcription|[TranscriptionConfig](#schematranscriptionconfig)|false|none|The settings associated with speech to text for the voice assistant. This is only relevant if the assistant uses a text-to-text language model. Any assistant using a model with native audio support (e.g. `fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_4`) will ignore this field.|
|language|[GoogleTranscriptionLanguage](#schemagoogletranscriptionlanguage)|false|none|none|
|voice|[VoiceConfig](#schemavoiceconfig)|false|none|The voice to be used by the voice assistant. Currently we support ElevenLabs, Telnyx and AWS voices.<br><br> **Supported Providers:**<br>- **AWS:** Use `AWS.Polly.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna`). For neural voices, which provide more realistic, human-like speech, append `-Neural` to the `VoiceId` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna-Neural`). Check the [available voices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/available-voices.html) for compatibility.<br>- **Azure:** Use `Azure.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Azure.en-CA-ClaraNeural`, `Azure.en-CA-LiamNeural`, `Azure.en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural`, `Azure.en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural`). For a complete list of voices, go to [Azure Voice Gallery](https://speech.microsoft.com/portal/voicegallery).<br>- **ElevenLabs:** Use `ElevenLabs.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `ElevenLabs.BaseModel.John`). The `ModelId` part is optional. To use ElevenLabs, you must provide your ElevenLabs API key as an integration secret under `"voice_settings": {"api_key_ref": "<secret_id>"}`. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) for details. Check [available voices](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/get-voices).<br> - **Telnyx:** Use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>`<br>- **Inworld:** Use `Inworld.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Inworld.Mini.Loretta`, `Inworld.Max.Oliver`, `Inworld.TTS2.Loretta`). Supported models: `Mini`, `Max`, `TTS2`.<br>- **Fish Audio:** Use `FishAudio.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `FishAudio.s2.1-pro.<reference_id>`). Supported models: `s2.1-pro`, `s2-pro`, `s1`. `VoiceId` is a Fish Voice-Library reference ID.<br>- **Soniox:** Use `Soniox.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma`). Supported model: `tts-rt-v2`. Browse the catalog via the [Voices API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/text-to-speech-commands/list-available-voices). Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the text, for example `it`. SSML is not supported. Use `voice_settings` to configure `speed` (0.7 to 1.3) and `reduce_silence`.<br>- **xAI:** Use `xAI.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `xAI.eve`). Available voices: `eve`, `ara`, `rex`, `sal`, `leo`.<br>- **Humain:** Use `Humain.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Humain.sara-ar`). Available voices: `sara-en`, `abdulaziz-en`, `sara-ar`, `abdulaziz-ar`, `nourah-ar`, `abdullah-ar`. Native Arabic (Saudi dialect) and English voices only — no `ModelId` segment.|
|voice_settings|[ElevenLabsVoiceSettings](#schemaelevenlabsvoicesettings) \| [TelnyxVoiceSettings](#schematelnyxvoicesettings) \| [AWSVoiceSettings](#schemaawsvoicesettings) \| [AzureVoiceSettings](#schemaazurevoicesettings) \| [ResembleVoiceSettings](#schemaresemblevoicesettings) \| [XAIVoiceSettings](#schemaxaivoicesettings) \| [SonioxVoiceSettings](#schemasonioxvoicesettings) \| [AssemblyAIVoiceSettings](#schemaassemblyaivoicesettings)|false|none|The settings associated with the voice selected|
|greeting|string|false|none|Text that will be played when the gathering starts, if none then nothing will be played when the gathering starts. The greeting can be text for any voice or SSML for `AWS.Polly.<voice_id>` voices. There is a 3,000 character limit.|
|send_partial_results|boolean|false|none|Default is `false`. If set to `true`, the voice assistant will send partial results via the `call.ai_gather.partial_results` callback in real time as individual fields are gathered. If set to `false`, the voice assistant will only send the final result via the `call.ai_gather.ended` callback.|
|send_message_history_updates|boolean|false|none|Default is `false`. If set to `true`, the voice assistant will send updates to the message history via the `call.ai_gather.message_history_updated` callback in real time as the message history is updated.|
|message_history|[object]|false|none|The message history you want the voice assistant to be aware of, this can be useful to keep the context of the conversation, or to pass additional information to the voice assistant.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|interruption_settings|[InterruptionSettings](#schemainterruptionsettings)|false|none|Settings for handling user interruptions during assistant speech|
|user_response_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum time in milliseconds to wait for user response before timing out.|
|gather_ended_speech|string|false|none|Text that will be played when the gathering has finished. There is a 3,000 character limit.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|audio_url|string|false|none|The URL of a file to be played back at the beginning of each prompt. The URL can point to either a WAV or MP3 file. media_name and audio_url cannot be used together in one request.|

The URL can point to either a WAV or MP3 file. invalid_media_name and invalid_audio_url cannot be used together in one request.|
|invalid_media_name|string|false|none|The media_name of a file to be played back when digits don't match the `valid_digits` parameter or the number of digits is not between `min` and `max`. The media_name must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. The file must either be a WAV or MP3 file.|
|minimum_digits|integer(int32)|false|none|The minimum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a minimum value of 1.|
|maximum_digits|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a maximum value of 128.|
|maximum_tries|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of times the file should be played if there is no input from the user on the call.|
|timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of milliseconds to wait for a DTMF response after file playback ends before a replaying the sound file.|

|valid_digits|string|false|none|A list of all digits accepted as valid.|
|inter_digit_timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of milliseconds to wait for input between digits.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|

```json
  "maximum_digits": 10,
  "terminating_digit": "#",
  "valid_digits": "123",
  "inter_digit_timeout_millis": 10000,
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payload|string|true|none|The text or SSML to be converted into speech. There is a 3,000 character limit.|
|invalid_payload|string|false|none|The text or SSML to be converted into speech when digits don't match the `valid_digits` parameter or the number of digits is not between `min` and `max`. There is a 3,000 character limit.|
|payload_type|string|false|none|The type of the provided payload. The payload can either be plain text, or Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML).|
|service_level|string|false|none|This parameter impacts speech quality, language options and payload types. When using `basic`, only the `en-US` language and payload type `text` are allowed.|
|voice|string|true|none|Specifies the voice used in speech synthesis.<br><br>- Define voices using the format `<Provider>.<Model>.<VoiceId>`. Specifying only the provider will give default values for voice_id and model_id.<br><br> **Supported Providers:**<br>- **AWS:** Use `AWS.Polly.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna`). For neural voices, which provide more realistic, human-like speech, append `-Neural` to the `VoiceId` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna-Neural`). Check the [available voices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/available-voices.html) for compatibility.<br>- **Azure:** Use `Azure.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Azure.en-CA-ClaraNeural`, `Azure.en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural`, `Azure.en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural`). For a complete list of voices, go to [Azure Voice Gallery](https://speech.microsoft.com/portal/voicegallery). Use `voice_settings` to configure custom deployments, regions, or API keys.<br>- **ElevenLabs:** Use `ElevenLabs.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `ElevenLabs.eleven_multilingual_v2.21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM`). The `ModelId` part is optional. To use ElevenLabs, you must provide your ElevenLabs API key as an integration identifier secret in `"voice_settings": {"api_key_ref": "<secret_identifier>"}`. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) for details. Check [available voices](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/get-voices).<br>- **Telnyx:** Use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>` (e.g., `Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af`). Use `voice_settings` to configure voice_speed and other synthesis parameters. `Bayan` provides Arabic (multiple dialects) and English voices (e.g., `Telnyx.Bayan.Ahmed`, `Telnyx.Bayan.Amanda`). `Sukhan` provides Urdu voices (e.g., `Telnyx.Sukhan.urdu-professor`); `voice_speed` is not supported.<br>- **Minimax:** Use `Minimax.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Minimax.speech-02-hd.Wise_Woman`). Supported models: `speech-02-turbo`, `speech-02-hd`, `speech-2.6-turbo`, `speech-2.8-turbo`. Use `voice_settings` to configure speed, volume, pitch, and language_boost.<br>- **Resemble:** Use `Resemble.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Resemble.Turbo.Aaron_en-US`). Supported models: `Pro`, `Turbo`, `Urdu`. `<VoiceId>` is a stock voice name or the ID of a Resemble voice clone. Use `voice_settings` to configure precision, sample_rate, and format.<br>- **Inworld:** Use `Inworld.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Inworld.Mini.Loretta`, `Inworld.Max.Oliver`, `Inworld.TTS2.Loretta`). Supported models: `Mini`, `Max`, `TTS2`. Use `voice_settings` to configure `delivery_mode` (`STABLE`, `BALANCED`, `CREATIVE`), supported by `TTS2` only.<br>- **Fish Audio:** Use `FishAudio.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `FishAudio.s2.1-pro.<reference_id>`). Supported models: `s2.1-pro`, `s2-pro`, `s1`. `VoiceId` is a Fish Voice-Library reference ID.<br>- **Soniox:** Use `Soniox.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma`). Supported model: `tts-rt-v2`. Browse the catalog via the [Voices API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/text-to-speech-commands/list-available-voices). Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the text, for example `it`. SSML is not supported. Use `voice_settings` to configure `speed` (0.7 to 1.3) and `reduce_silence`.<br>- **xAI:** Use `xAI.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `xAI.eve`). Available voices: `eve`, `ara`, `rex`, `sal`, `leo`.<br>- **Humain:** Use `Humain.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Humain.sara-ar`). Available voices: `sara-en`, `abdulaziz-en`, `sara-ar`, `abdulaziz-ar`, `nourah-ar`, `abdullah-ar`. Native Arabic (Saudi dialect) and English voices only — no `ModelId` segment.<br><br>For service_level basic, you may define the gender of the speaker (male or female).|
|voice_settings|[ElevenLabsVoiceSettings](#schemaelevenlabsvoicesettings) \| [TelnyxVoiceSettings](#schematelnyxvoicesettings) \| [AWSVoiceSettings](#schemaawsvoicesettings) \| [MinimaxVoiceSettings](#schemaminimaxvoicesettings) \| [AzureVoiceSettings](#schemaazurevoicesettings) \| [ResembleVoiceSettings](#schemaresemblevoicesettings) \| [InworldVoiceSettings](#schemainworldvoicesettings) \| [XAIVoiceSettings](#schemaxaivoicesettings) \| [SonioxVoiceSettings](#schemasonioxvoicesettings) \| [AssemblyAIVoiceSettings](#schemaassemblyaivoicesettings)|false|none|The settings associated with the voice selected|
|language|string|false|none|The language you want spoken. This parameter is ignored when a `Polly.*` voice is specified.|
|minimum_digits|integer(int32)|false|none|The minimum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a minimum value of 1.|
|maximum_digits|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of digits to fetch. This parameter has a maximum value of 128.|
|maximum_tries|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of times that a file should be played back if there is no input from the user on the call.|
|timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of milliseconds to wait for a DTMF response after speak ends before a replaying the sound file.|
|terminating_digit|string|false|none|The digit used to terminate input if fewer than `maximum_digits` digits have been gathered. Set to an empty string to disable the terminating digit entirely, so that a digit such as `#` can be collected as input per `valid_digits`.|
|valid_digits|string|false|none|A list of all digits accepted as valid.|
|inter_digit_timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of milliseconds to wait for input between digits.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice|string|false|none|Voice identifier in the format `provider.model_id.voice_id` or `provider.voice_id`. Examples: `Telnyx.Ultra.<voice_id>`, `Telnyx.Bayan.Ahmed`, `Telnyx.Sukhan.urdu-professor`, `azure.en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural`, `aws.Polly.Generative.Lucia`. When provided, `provider`, `model_id`, and `voice_id` are extracted automatically and take precedence over individual parameters.|
|text|string|false|none|The text to convert to speech.|
|provider|string|false|none|TTS provider. Required unless `voice` is provided.|
|language|string|false|none|Language code (e.g. `en-US`). Usage varies by provider.|
|text_type|string|false|none|Text type. Use `ssml` for SSML-formatted input (supported by AWS and Azure).|
|output_type|string|false|none|Determines the response format. `binary_output` returns raw audio bytes, `base64_output` returns base64-encoded audio in JSON.|
|disable_cache|boolean|false|none|When `true`, bypass the audio cache and generate fresh audio.|
|voice_settings|object|false|none|Provider-specific voice settings. Contents vary by provider — see provider-specific parameter objects below.|
|aws|[AwsProviderParams](#schemaawsproviderparams)|false|none|AWS Polly provider-specific parameters.|
|telnyx|[TelnyxProviderParams](#schematelnyxproviderparams)|false|none|Telnyx provider-specific parameters. For the `Ultra` model, use `voice_speed`, `volume`, and `emotion`. `Bayan` and `Sukhan` don't use `temperature`, `volume`, or `emotion`. `Bayan` accepts `voice_speed` from 0.5 to 2.0; `Sukhan` doesn't support it. `Bayan` synthesizes at a native 16 kHz: `sampling_rate` `8000`, `22050`, or `24000` is resampled, needs `response_format: pcm`, and isn't available with `output_type: audio_id`. `Sukhan`'s `response_format` is restricted to `mp3` or `pcm` (no `wav`).|
|azure|[AzureProviderParams](#schemaazureproviderparams)|false|none|Azure Cognitive Services provider-specific parameters.|
|elevenlabs|[ElevenLabsProviderParams](#schemaelevenlabsproviderparams)|false|none|ElevenLabs provider-specific parameters.|
|minimax|[MinimaxProviderParams](#schemaminimaxproviderparams)|false|none|Minimax provider-specific parameters.|
|resemble|[ResembleProviderParams](#schemaresembleproviderparams)|false|none|Resemble AI provider-specific parameters.|
|xai|[XAIProviderParams](#schemaxaiproviderparams)|false|none|xAI provider-specific parameters.|
|humain|[HumainProviderParams](#schemahumainproviderparams)|false|none|Humain provider-specific parameters. Unlike other providers, Humain has no format/sample-rate negotiation (output is always PCM16 24kHz mono) and no language parameter — language is fixed per voice.|
|soniox|[SonioxProviderParams](#schemasonioxproviderparams)|false|none|Soniox provider-specific parameters. Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the language of the text.|
|assemblyai|[AssemblyAIProviderParams](#schemaassemblyaiproviderparams)|false|none|AssemblyAI provider-specific parameters. Every voice speaks all six supported languages; set `language` to the language of the text.|

Values are strings (1-256 characters, no control or format characters), integers within +/-9007199254740991, or booleans; floats, null, objects and arrays are rejected. Values that look like credentials are rejected. Tags are attribution only: never forwarded upstream, never part of the response cache key, never used for budgets or routing. An untagged request reports {}.|

The handoff tool allows the assistant to hand off control of the conversation to another AI assistant. By default, this will happen transparently to the end user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|shared|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this tool comes from the shared Tools Library. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. Read-only: set by the server, not accepted in requests. When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).|
|handoff|[HandoffToolParams](#schemahandofftoolparams)|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_HangupRequest">HangupRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahanguprequest"></a>
<a id="schema_HangupRequest"></a>
<a id="tocShanguprequest"></a>
<a id="tocshanguprequest"></a>

```json
{
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|custom_headers|[[CustomSipHeader](#schemacustomsipheader)]|false|none|Custom headers to be added to the SIP BYE message.|
|reason|string|false|none|Text for the SIP `Reason` header (RFC 3326) sent when cancelling an unanswered outbound leg. The SIP CANCEL carries `Reason: SIP;cause=200;text="<reason>"`; phones such as Poly and Yealink use it to suppress the missed-call entry for a call answered elsewhere. Has no effect on an answered leg or an inbound leg. A hangup sent before the leg's `call.initiated` webhook still hangs up the leg, but without the `Reason` header. Must not contain `"`, `\`, control characters, or characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (such as emoji); invalid values are rejected with a 422.|

|default_tertiary_fqdn_id|string \| null|false|none|The default tertiary FQDN to use for the number. Only settable if the connection is<br>of FQDN type. Value must be the ID of an FQDN set on the connection.|
|channel_limit|integer \| null|false|none|When set, this will limit the total number of inbound calls to phone numbers associated with this connection.|
|generate_ringback_tone|boolean|false|none|Generate ringback tone through 183 session progress message with early media.|
|isup_headers_enabled|boolean|false|none|When set, inbound phone calls will receive ISUP parameters via SIP headers. (Only when available and only when using TCP or TLS transport.)|
|prack_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable PRACK messages as defined in RFC3262.|
|sip_compact_headers_enabled|boolean|false|none|Defaults to true.|
|sip_region|string|false|none|Selects which `sip_region` to receive inbound calls from. If null, the default region (US) will be used.|
|sip_subdomain|string \| null|false|none|Specifies a subdomain that can be used to receive Inbound calls to a Connection, in the same way a phone number is used, from a SIP endpoint. Example: the subdomain "example.sip.telnyx.com" can be called from any SIP endpoint by using the SIP URI "sip:@example.sip.telnyx.com" where the user part can be any alphanumeric value. TLS signaling is supported. SRTP media encryption requires TLS transport.|
|sip_subdomain_receive_settings|string|false|none|This option can be enabled to receive calls from: "Anyone" (any SIP endpoint in the public Internet) or "Only my connections" (any connection assigned to the same Telnyx user).|
|timeout_1xx_secs|integer|false|none|Time(sec) before aborting if connection is not made.|
|timeout_2xx_secs|integer|false|none|Time(sec) before aborting if call is unanswered (min: 1, max: 600).|
|shaken_stir_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled the SIP Connection will receive the Identity header with Shaken/Stir data in the SIP INVITE message of inbound calls, even when using UDP transport.|

<h2 id="tocS_InferenceEmbeddingTransferToolParams">InferenceEmbeddingTransferToolParams</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainferenceembeddingtransfertoolparams"></a>
<a id="schema_InferenceEmbeddingTransferToolParams"></a>
<a id="tocSinferenceembeddingtransfertoolparams"></a>
<a id="tocsinferenceembeddingtransfertoolparams"></a>

```json
{
  "targets": [
    {
      "name": "Support",
      "to": "+13129457420",
      "message": "I have a caller asking about a billing issue on invoice 4471.",
      "extension": "wwww200",
      "sip_auth_username": "sipuser",
      "sip_auth_password": "sippass"
    }
  ],
  "from": "+35319605860",
  "diversion": "{{telnyx_agent_target}}",
  "warm_transfer_instructions": "Briefly greet the transfer recipient and provide any relevant information from the call. Let them know you will bridge the call right after.",
  "warm_transfer_acceptance": {
    "enabled": false,
    "end_user_target_context_mode": "private",
    "require_acceptance": false,
    "timeout_secs": 60
  },
  "description": "Transfer the call to a human agent.",
  "bridge_beep": {
    "enabled": false,
    "target_legs": "self"
  },
  "warm_message_delay_ms": 2000,
  "custom_headers": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "voicemail_detection": {
    "detection_mode": "disabled",
    "on_voicemail_detected": {
      "action": "stop_transfer",
      "voicemail_message": {
        "type": "message",
        "message": "string"
      }
    },
    "detection_config": {
      "greeting_silence_duration_millis": 500,
      "greeting_total_analysis_time_millis": 500,
      "after_greeting_silence_millis": 100,
      "between_words_silence_millis": 10,
      "greeting_duration_millis": 100,
      "initial_silence_millis": 100,
      "maximum_number_of_words": 1,
      "maximum_word_length_millis": 50,
      "silence_threshold": 1,
      "total_analysis_time_millis": 500,
      "min_word_length_millis": 1
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|targets|[object] \| string|true|none|The different possible targets of the transfer. The assistant will be able to choose one of the targets to transfer the call to. This can also be a dynamic variable string like `{{ targets }}` where `targets` is returned by the dynamic variables webhook and resolves to an array of target objects at runtime.|
|from|string|true|none|Number or SIP URI placing the call.|
|diversion|string|false|none|The number the inbound call was received on, forwarded so an unverified non-Telnyx `from` can be used as the caller id -- typically to transfer out as the original caller by pairing `from: "{{telnyx_end_user_target}}"` with `diversion: "{{telnyx_agent_target}}"`. The caller id is only accepted while that number is still on an active inbound call to this `diversion` number, and the `diversion` number must be one you own or have verified.|
|warm_transfer_instructions|string|false|none|Natural language instructions for your agent for how to provide context for the transfer recipient.|
|warm_transfer_acceptance|object|false|none|Requires the transfer destination to accept the call before the caller is bridged. When enabled, the assistant speaks privately with the destination after they answer — delivering the warm transfer message and asking whether they take the call — while the caller keeps hearing ringback. The assistant then finalizes the transfer with the built-in `complete_transfer` tool: an accept bridges the calls, a decline hangs up the destination and returns the assistant to the caller with the reason the destination gave. Requires either `warm_transfer_instructions` or a `message` on every target, otherwise the assistant fails to save. Only available for calls started with `ai_assistant_start`; single-caller conversations only (a conference or additional invited participants fall back to a regular warm transfer).|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the transfer tool. By default, Telnyx generates this automatically based on the configured targets. Typically only set when importing an assistant from another provider that allowed a custom description; in that case the provided value is preserved. Most users should leave this empty and let Telnyx manage it.|
|bridge_beep|object|false|none|Plays a short beep once the transfer completes and the calls are bridged, so the transfer destination knows the caller is now on the line. The warm transfer message plays before the bridge; this marks the moment the caller actually joins. Works with and without `warm_transfer_acceptance`.|
|warm_message_delay_ms|integer \| null|false|none|Optional delay in milliseconds before playing the warm message audio when the transferred call is answered. When set, the audio_url is not included in the dial command; instead, playback starts after the specified delay. When not set, existing behavior (audio_url in dial) is preserved.|
|custom_headers|[object]|false|none|Custom headers to be added to the SIP INVITE for the transfer command.|
|voicemail_detection|object|false|none|Configuration for voicemail detection (AMD - Answering Machine Detection) on the transferred call. Allows the assistant to detect when a voicemail system answers the transferred call and take appropriate action.|

<h2 id="tocS_InitiateAICallRequest">InitiateAICallRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainitiateaicallrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_InitiateAICallRequest"></a>
