<a id="tocsinitiateaicallrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "From": "+13120001234",
  "To": "+13121230000",
  "AIAssistantId": "ai-assistant-id-123"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|From|string|true|none|The phone number of the party initiating the call. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|To|string|true|none|The phone number of the called party. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|AIAssistantId|string|true|none|The ID of the AI assistant to use for the call. Telnyx attempts to warm up this assistant before the call is placed and starts it automatically when the called party answers.|
|AIAssistantVersion|string|false|none|The version of the AI assistant to use.|
|AIAssistantDynamicVariables|object|false|none|Key-value map of dynamic variables to pass to the AI assistant.|
|CallerId|string|false|none|To be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`To` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and `-_~!.+` special characters. If omitted, the display name will be the same as the number in the `From` field.|
|StatusCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send status callback events for this AI call. When provided, this per-call value overrides the status callback URL configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|StatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The status callback events for which Telnyx should send a webhook for this AI call. Multiple events can be defined when separated by a space. Valid values: initiated, ringing, answered, completed, no-answer, busy, canceled, failed, analyzed. When provided, this per-call value overrides the status callback events configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|StatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `StatusCallback` and `StatusCallbacks` for this AI call. When provided, this per-call value overrides the status callback method configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|StatusCallbacks|[string]|false|none|Array of URL destinations for Telnyx to send status callback events for this AI call. When provided, these per-call values override the status callback URL configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|CustomHeaders|[object]|false|none|Custom HTTP headers to be sent with the call. Each header should be an object with 'name' and 'value' properties.|
|ConversationCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send AI conversation callback events for this call. Events include `conversation_created` and `conversation_ended`.|
|ConversationCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `ConversationCallback` and `ConversationCallbacks`.|
|ConversationCallbacks|[string]|false|none|Array of URL destinations for AI conversation callback events for this call. Events include `conversation_created` and `conversation_ended`.|
|MachineDetection|string|false|none|Enables Answering Machine Detection.|
|DetectionMode|string|false|none|Allows you to choose between Regular, Premium, and PremiumCallScreening detections. See https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/voice/programmable-voice/answering-machine-detection|
|AsyncAmd|boolean|false|none|Select whether to perform answering machine detection in the background. By default execution is blocked until Answering Machine Detection is completed.|
|AsyncAmdStatusCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send AMD callback events to for the call.|
|AsyncAmdStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `AsyncAmdStatusCallback`.|
|MachineDetectionTimeout|integer|false|none|Maximum timeout threshold in milliseconds for overall detection.|
|MachineDetectionPromptEndTimeout|integer|false|none|Silence duration threshold after a call screening prompt before ending prompt detection, in milliseconds. Used when `DetectionMode` is `PremiumCallScreening`.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechThreshold|integer|false|none|Maximum threshold of a human greeting. If greeting longer than this value, considered machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold|integer|false|none|Silence duration threshold after a greeting message or voice for it be considered human. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSilenceTimeout|integer|false|none|If initial silence duration is greater than this value, consider it a machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionBeepProfile|string|false|none|Selects which detectors must validate a beep. `both` requires the amplitude and frequency detectors to agree. `freq_only` uses the frequency detector alone, for beeps whose volume is too unsteady for the default profile. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepMinFrequency|integer(int32)|false|none|Lowest frequency, in Hz, that a tone must reach to be treated as a beep. Raising it above 480 excludes North American ringback (440 + 480 Hz), which can otherwise be reported as a beep when the `freq_only` profile is in use. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepMaxFrequency|integer(int32)|false|none|Highest frequency, in Hz, that a tone can reach and still be treated as a beep. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepMinToneDuration|integer(int32)|false|none|Shortest tone, in milliseconds, that can be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects brief tones such as call-progress blips. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralConfirmation|boolean|false|none|When enabled, a candidate beep must pass an additional spectral check before it is reported. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralWindow|integer(int32)|false|none|Length of the spectral confirmation window, in milliseconds. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralMinPurity|number|false|none|Minimum spectral purity, from 0 to 1, for a tone to be treated as a beep. Raising it rejects mixed tones such as ringback, which combines two frequencies. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|MachineDetectionBeepSpectralRejectFaxCng|boolean|false|none|When enabled, the fax CNG tone is rejected rather than reported as a beep. Only used when MachineDetection is enabled.|
|Passports|string|false|none|A string of passport identifiers to associate with the call.|
|TimeLimit|integer|false|none|The maximum duration of the call in seconds. The minimum value is 30 and the maximum value is 14400 (4 hours). Default is 14400 seconds.|
|Timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds to wait for the called party to answer the call before the call is canceled. The minimum value is 5 and the maximum value is 120. Default is 30 seconds.|
|Record|boolean|false|none|Whether to record the entire participant's call leg. Defaults to `false`.|
|RecordingChannels|string|false|none|The number of channels in the final recording. Defaults to `mono`.|
|RecordingStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the recording callbacks will be sent to.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `RecordingStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the recording's state that should generate a call to `RecordingStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`.|
|RecordingTimeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|RecordingTrack|string|false|none|The audio track to record for the call. The default is `both`.|
|Trim|string|false|none|Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the recording. Defaults to `trim-silence`.|
|SendRecordingUrl|[SendRecordingUrl](#schemasendrecordingurl)|false|none|Whether to send RecordingUrl in webhooks.|
|PreferredCodecs|string|false|none|The list of comma-separated codecs to be offered on a call.|
|SipAuthUsername|string|false|none|The username to use for SIP authentication.|
|SipAuthPassword|string|false|none|The password to use for SIP authentication.|
|SipRegion|string|false|none|Defines the SIP region to be used for the call.|

|MediaEncryption|string|false|none|Defines whether media should be encrypted on the call. When set to `SRTP`, the call will use Secure Real-time Transport Protocol for media encryption. When set to `DTLS`, the call will use DTLS for media encryption. Only supported for SIP destinations.|
|SuperviseCallSid|string|false|none|The call control ID of the existing call to supervise. When provided, the created leg will be added to the specified call in supervising mode. Status callbacks and action callbacks will NOT be sent for the supervising leg.|
|SupervisingRole|string|false|none|The supervising role for the new leg. Determines the audio behavior: barge (hear both sides), whisper (only hear supervisor), monitor (hear both sides but supervisor muted). Default: barge|
|Timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds to wait for the called party to answer the call before the call is canceled. The minimum value is 5 and the maximum value is 120. Default is 30 seconds.|
|TimeLimit|integer|false|none|The maximum duration of the call in seconds. The minimum value is 30 and the maximum value is 14400 (4 hours). Default is 14400 seconds.|
|Texml|string|false|none|TeXML to be used as instructions for the call. If provided, the call will execute these instructions instead of fetching from the Url.|

When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).|
|invite|[InviteToolConfig](#schemainvitetoolconfig)|true|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|anchorsite_override|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|none|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|string|false|none|none|
|transport_protocol|string|false|none|One of UDP, TLS, or TCP. Applies only to connections with IP authentication or FQDN authentication.|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Defaults to false and returns the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|ios_push_credential_id|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|android_push_credential_id|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|created_at|string|false|none|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was created.|
|updated_at|string|false|none|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was updated.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|inbound|[InboundIp](#schemainboundip)|false|none|none|
|outbound|[OutboundIp](#schemaoutboundip)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

An account-scoped pool of dedicated IPs. Mail uses a pool only when the pool is scoped to the sending domain (`domain_id`) or is the account default (`is_default`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|record_type|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|Pool name, unique within the account.|
|is_default|boolean|false|none|Whether this is the account's default pool. The default pool carries mail for sending domains that have no domain-scoped pool. At most one per account.|
|domain_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Email domain this pool is scoped to. The pool carries that domain's mail. Null when the pool is not domain-scoped.|
|ips|[[IpPoolMemberIp](#schemaippoolmemberip)]|false|none|Member IPs with their routing weights. Populated by Retrieve an IP pool; list, create, and update responses return an empty array.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|record_type|ip_pool|

A dedicated IP as a member of a pool, with its routing weight in this pool. Weight is a positive integer (default 100).

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|

|ip_version|string|false|none|none|
|pool_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|none|
|region|string|false|none|Region label of the allocated IP (for example, `ewr-nj1`).|
|status|string|false|none|Lifecycle status. `provisioning`: purchased and billed, carries no mail until `start_warmup`. `warming_up`: warm-up ramp in progress. `active`: ramp complete. `suspended`: suspended by Telnyx; carries no mail and is still billed. `released`: returned to Telnyx; carries no mail.|
|warmup|[DedicatedIpWarmup](#schemadedicatedipwarmup)|false|none|Warmup ramp state for a dedicated IP.|
|billing|[DedicatedIpBilling](#schemadedicatedipbilling)|false|none|Monthly recurring charge (MRC) state for the IP's current allocation.|
|provisioning_status|string|false|none|Same value as `provisioning.dns_status`.|
|provisioning|[DedicatedIpProvisioning](#schemadedicatedipprovisioning)|false|none|Read-only status of the Telnyx-managed PTR record. No customer action is required to complete it.|
|ptr_hostname|string \| null|false|none|Telnyx-managed reverse DNS (PTR) hostname of the IP, in the form `mta-<a-b-c-d>.msgtelnyx.com`. Also used as the EHLO hostname when sending from the IP. Managed by Telnyx and cannot be changed through the API.|

|released_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the IP was released. Null until release.|
|suspension_reason|string \| null|false|none|Reason Telnyx recorded when suspending the IP. Null unless `status` is `suspended`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_control_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier and token for controlling the call|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string. Please note that the client_state will be updated for the participient call leg and the change will not affect conferencing webhooks unless the participient is the owner of the conference.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid execution of duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore subsequent commands with the same `command_id` as one that has already been executed.|
|end_conference_on_exit|boolean|false|none|Whether the conference should end and all remaining participants be hung up after the participant leaves the conference. Defaults to "false".|
|soft_end_conference_on_exit|boolean|false|none|Whether the conference should end after the participant leaves the conference. NOTE this doesn't hang up the other participants. Defaults to "false".|
|hold|boolean|false|none|Whether the participant should be put on hold immediately after joining the conference. Defaults to "false".|
|hold_audio_url|string|false|none|The URL of a file to be played to the participant when they are put on hold after joining the conference. hold_media_name and hold_audio_url cannot be used together in one request. Takes effect only when "start_conference_on_create" is set to "false". This property takes effect only if "hold" is set to "true".|
|hold_media_name|string|false|none|The media_name of a file to be played to the participant when they are put on hold after joining the conference. The media_name must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. The file must either be a WAV or MP3 file. Takes effect only when "start_conference_on_create" is set to "false". This property takes effect only if "hold" is set to "true".|
|mute|boolean|false|none|Whether the participant should be muted immediately after joining the conference. Defaults to "false".|
|start_conference_on_enter|boolean|false|none|Whether the conference should be started after the participant joins the conference. Defaults to "false".|
|supervisor_role|string|false|none|Sets the joining participant as a supervisor for the conference. A conference can have multiple supervisors. "barge" means the supervisor enters the conference as a normal participant. This is the same as "none". "monitor" means the supervisor is muted but can hear all participants. "whisper" means that only the specified "whisper_call_control_ids" can hear the supervisor. Defaults to "none".|
|whisper_call_control_ids|[string]|false|none|Array of unique call_control_ids the joining supervisor can whisper to. If none provided, the supervisor will join the conference as a monitoring participant only.|
|beep_enabled|string|false|none|Whether a beep sound should be played when the participant joins and/or leaves the conference. Can be used to override the conference-level setting.|
|region|[ConferenceRegion](#schemaconferenceregion)|false|none|Region where the conference data is located. Defaults to the region defined in user's data locality settings (Europe or US).|

|beep_enabled|on_exit|

<h2 id="tocS_LLMCondition">LLMCondition</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemallmcondition"></a>
<a id="schema_LLMCondition"></a>
<a id="tocSllmcondition"></a>
<a id="tocsllmcondition"></a>

```json
{
  "prompt": "The user has confirmed their booking details.",
  "type": "llm"
}
```

Edge condition routed by the assistant's LLM from a natural-language
prompt.

How the edge is decided depends on the channel. On calls, each outgoing
`llm` condition is offered to the assistant's model as a transition tool
alongside the assistant's tools, and the edge fires when the model
selects it; the platform does not evaluate the prompt itself, and
instructions that forbid or discourage tool calls can stop these edges
from firing. On chat channels, the edge prompts are evaluated in a
separate model call after the reply, which does not use the assistant's
instructions. Use this for fuzzy intents that aren't expressible as a
deterministic expression (e.g. 'user wants to escalate to a human').

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|prompt|string|true|none|Natural-language criterion the model routes on. On calls this is offered to the model as the transition tool's description; on chat channels it is judged as a statement in the post-reply evaluation call.|
|type|string|true|none|none|

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "record_type": "machine_payment_account_credit",
  "account_id": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "currency": "string",
  "payment_source": "machine_payment",
  "provider": "stripe",
  "payment_method": "stripe_spt",
  "payment_intent_id": "string",
  "receipt_reference": "string",
  "mpp_resource": "string",
  "status": "new",
  "created": true,
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

An account-credit transaction settled through the Machine Payment Protocol.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier of the account-credit transaction.|
|record_type|string|true|none|Record type identifier.|
|account_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the credited Telnyx account. Derived from the authenticated user on the initial request and from the verified payment credential on a paid retry — never from the request body.|
|amount|string|true|none|Credited amount as a decimal string with two fractional digits.|
|currency|string|true|none|ISO 4217 currency code of the credited amount (currently always USD).|
|payment_source|string|true|none|Payment source identifier distinguishing machine payments from other account-credit sources.|
|provider|string \| null|false|none|Upstream payment provider that settled the payment.|
|payment_method|string \| null|false|none|Payment method used by the provider: `stripe_spt` for Stripe Shared Payment Token payments, `tempo_usdc` for Tempo USDC payments.|
|payment_intent_id|string \| null|false|none|Stripe PaymentIntent identifier for Stripe settlements. Absent for Tempo settlements.|
|receipt_reference|string \| null|false|none|Provider receipt reference: the Stripe PaymentIntent identifier for Stripe settlements, or the on-chain transaction hash for Tempo settlements.|
|mpp_resource|string \| null|false|none|Machine Payment Protocol resource identifier the payment credential was bound to.|
|status|string \| null|false|none|Status of the transaction. Successful machine payment credits are recorded as `settled`.|
|created|boolean|false|none|True when this response created a new account credit, false when an existing transaction was returned for a duplicate paid retry.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO 8601 timestamp when the transaction was created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|record_type|machine_payment_account_credit|
|payment_source|machine_payment|
|provider|stripe|
|provider|tempo|
|provider|null|
|payment_method|stripe_spt|
|payment_method|tempo_usdc|
|payment_method|null|
|status|new|
|status|processing|
|status|settled|
|status|expired|
|status|invalid|
|status|null|

|t38_fax_gateway_enabled|boolean|false|none|Controls whether Telnyx will accept a T.38 re-INVITE for this phone number. Note that Telnyx will not send a T.38 re-INVITE; this option only controls whether one will be accepted.|

Represents a meeting session. All serializer fields are present and required; nullable fields use null when absent. No actor, provider-bot, idempotency, routing, key, or internal fields are exposed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the meeting session.|
|account_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the owning account.|
|provider|string|true|none|Provider handling the meeting session.|
|status|string|true|none|Lifecycle status. `waiting_for_admission` means the bot reached the meeting lobby and may require host approval. `active` means the bot entered the meeting/media path. `ended` alone does not prove attendance; use non-null `joined_at` as positive evidence that the session became active. `admission_denied` is reserved for an explicit provider denial, while cancellation or another termination can end a never-admitted session as `ended`.|
|status_detail|string \| null|true|none|Additional human-readable detail about the status, or null.|
|recording|boolean|true|none|Whether the session is being recorded.|
|meeting_url|string(uri)|true|none|The meeting URL the bot joins.|
|platform|string|true|none|Detected meeting platform.|
|bot_name|string|true|none|Display name of the bot in the meeting.|
|config|[MeetingSessionConfig](#schemameetingsessionconfig)|true|none|none|
|avatar|[MeetingSessionAvatar](#schemameetingsessionavatar) \| null|true|none|The assistant's avatar when the session was created with `assistant.avatar: true`, otherwise null.|
|avatar_state|string \| null|true|none|Current state of the avatar, or null if the session has no avatar. `starting` until the avatar's video is playing, then `connected`; `degraded` when the session has fallen back to voice-only (the `avatar.degraded` event carries the reason); `disconnected` when the avatar has ended.|
|avatar_state_changed_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last avatar state change, or null.|
|assistant|[MeetingSessionAssistant](#schemameetingsessionassistant) \| null|true|none|Assistant configuration if an assistant is attached, otherwise null.|
|assistant_state|string \| null|true|none|Current state of the assistant, or null if no assistant is attached.|
|assistant_state_changed_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last assistant state change, or null.|
|webhook_url|string \| null(uri)|true|none|Webhook endpoint for session lifecycle callbacks, or null if not configured.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to the session.|
|failure_reason|string \| null|true|none|Human-readable failure reason if the session failed, or null.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the session was created.|
|join_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Scheduled join time, or null for immediate join.|
|joined_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the session first became `active`, or null if it never became active. This remains positive admission evidence after terminal transitions.|
|ended_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp when the session ended, or null if ongoing.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the last update to the session.|

<h2 id="tocS_MeetingSessionAssistantRequest">MeetingSessionAssistantRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemameetingsessionassistantrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_MeetingSessionAssistantRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSmeetingsessionassistantrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsmeetingsessionassistantrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "audio_gate": "half_duplex",
  "dynamic_variables": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "leave_on_end": false,
  "avatar": false
}
```

Attach a Telnyx AI Assistant to the session. Supply the Assistant's ID; the Meeting service connects it to the meeting directly. The Call Control connection, caller ID and loopback SIP URI previously required here have been removed and are now rejected as unknown fields.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Identifier of the assistant to attach.|
|audio_gate|string|false|none|Audio gating strategy for the assistant call leg. `half_duplex` (default) sends the assistant a single mixed meeting stream and mutes it while the assistant speaks, so the assistant cannot hear itself and cannot be interrupted. `full_duplex` sends a separate stream per participant, which allows barge-in and removes self-hearing, and COSTS SIGNIFICANTLY MORE: per-participant streams multiply the per-minute cost by the number of participants.|
|dynamic_variables|object|false|none|Per-conversation values for the [dynamic variables](/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) used in the Assistant's instructions, greeting, or tools. Delivered before the Assistant's first utterance, so they resolve for the opening line as well as the rest of the conversation. At most 63 entries; keys 1-128 characters; values must be strings. The map is budgeted in aggregate at 1,047,552 bytes (1023 KiB) rather than capped per value. `streaming_audio`, `ai_assistant_streaming_audio` and `meeting_session_id` are reserved and rejected with `400 invalid_request` -- they toggle provider infrastructure or are set by the service rather than fill a prompt template.|
|leave_on_end|boolean|false|none|Leave the meeting when the Assistant's conversation reaches a terminal state -- `ended` **or** `failed`. Off by default, which leaves the bot in the meeting after the Assistant stops. Fires once: a second terminal transition does not leave twice, and a leave the provider refuses is logged without changing how the session settles.|
|avatar|boolean|false|none|Beta. Show the avatar configured on the assistant (its `avatar_settings`; see [AI Assistant avatars](/docs/inference/ai-assistants/avatars)) as the bot's camera, lip-synced to the assistant's own speech. The request carries no avatar ID or key: the assistant is read at creation and the request is rejected with 400 `invalid_request` if it has no Telnyx avatar configured. Supported on Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Webex; other platforms return 422 `unsupported_capability`. REST-only. Not echoed back on `assistant`; the session's top-level `avatar` and `avatar_state` fields report it instead. If the avatar fails, the session continues voice-only and `avatar_state` becomes `degraded`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|audio_gate|half_duplex|
|audio_gate|full_duplex|

The encoded value is limited to 1,835,008 characters and the decoded JPEG to 1,363,148 bytes. The JPEG is limited to 4,096 pixels per dimension, 4 megapixels, and 128 MB of decoder memory. The service resolves the URL before bot creation and does not persist, return, or log the URL or image bytes.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uuid|string|false|none|Unique identifier of the message|
|user_id|string|false|none|Identifier of the Telnyx account who owns the message|
|completed_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Message completion time|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Message creation time|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Message updated time|
|sent_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Time when the message was sent|
|carrier|string|false|none|Country-specific carrier used to send or receive the message|
|carrier_fee|string|false|none|Fee charged by certain carriers in order to deliver certain message types. Telnyx passes this fee on to the customer according to our pricing table|
|cld|string|false|none|The recipient of the message (to parameter in the Messaging API)|
|cli|string|false|none|The sender of the message (from parameter in the Messaging API). For Alphanumeric ID messages, this is the sender ID value|
|country_code|string|false|none|Two-letter representation of the country of the cld property using the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format|
|delivery_status|string|false|none|Final webhook delivery status|
|delivery_status_failover_url|string|false|none|Failover customer-provided URL which Telnyx posts delivery status webhooks to|
|delivery_status_webhook_url|string|false|none|Primary customer-provided URL which Telnyx posts delivery status webhooks to|
|direction|string|false|none|Logical direction of the message from the Telnyx customer's perspective. It's inbound when the Telnyx customer receives the message, or outbound otherwise|
|fteu|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this is a Free-To-End-User (FTEU) short code message|
|mcc|string|false|none|Mobile country code. Only available for certain products, such as Global Outbound-Only from Alphanumeric Sender ID|
|mnc|string|false|none|Mobile network code. Only available for certain products, such as Global Outbound-Only from Alphanumeric Sender ID|
|message_type|string|false|none|Describes the Messaging service used to send the message. Available services are: Short Message Service (SMS), Multimedia Messaging Service (MMS), and Rich Communication Services (RCS)|
|on_net|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether both sender and recipient numbers are Telnyx-managed|
|profile_id|string|false|none|Unique identifier of the Messaging Profile used to send or receive the message|
|profile_name|string|false|none|Name of the Messaging Profile used to send or receive the message|
|source_country_code|string|false|none|Two-letter representation of the country of the cli property using the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format|
|status|string|false|none|Final status of the message after the delivery attempt|
|tags|string|false|none|Comma-separated tags assigned to the Telnyx number associated with the message|
|rate|string|false|none|Currency amount per billing unit used to calculate the Telnyx billing cost|
|currency|string|false|none|Telnyx account currency used to describe monetary values, including billing cost|
|cost|string|false|none|Amount, in the user currency, for the Telnyx billing cost|
|errors|[string]|false|none|Telnyx API error codes returned by the Telnyx gateway|
|parts|integer|false|none|Number of message parts. The message is broken down in multiple parts when its length surpasses the limit of 160 characters|
|record_type|string|true|none|Identifies the record schema|

|status|dlr_timeout|

<h2 id="tocS_MessageEvent">MessageEvent</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamessageevent"></a>
<a id="schema_MessageEvent"></a>
<a id="tocSmessageevent"></a>
<a id="tocsmessageevent"></a>

```json
{
  "type": {},
  "event_type": "email.delivered",
  "canonical_event_type": "email.delivered",
  "occurred_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "payload": {}
}
```

An event on the per-message events endpoint. The legacy event_type and additive canonical_event_type are email.-prefixed. The deprecated type preserves the bare stored event name for compatibility.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|object|true|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated name field retained for compatibility. Its value is the bare stored event name, never email.-prefixed. Use event_type for the legacy rendering or canonical_event_type for the canonical name.|
|event_type|string|true|none|Legacy customer-visible event name, prefixed with `email.`. Gateway rejections render `email.failed`; MTA expirations render `email.bounced`. Webhook subscription allowlists match the legacy name.|
|canonical_event_type|string|true|none|Additive canonical outcome name, prefixed with `email.`. Gateway rejection is `email.gw_reject`, ambiguous injection timeout is `email.injection_timeout`, and MTA expiration is `email.expired`. Unchanged outcomes retain their names. Existing stored rows are translated only when recorded payload evidence proves the outcome; a legacy failed row is not guessed or sharpened.|
|occurred_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|payload|object|false|none|none|

Telnyx product features the messaging customer can enable on the messaging profile. Keys map to individual feature flags; unknown keys are accepted and preserved for forward compatibility with rolling deployments.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ai_opt_out_detection_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enables AI detection of inbound opt-out messages that do not follow the standard STOP/UNSTOP/HELP opt-out keyword pattern. When enabled, the messaging platform applies an AI model to identify non-standard opt-out requests (e.g. natural-language phrases) and treats them as opt-outs.|
|auto_chunk_long_messages|boolean|false|none|Enables server-side chunking of outbound SMS. When enabled, an outbound message that exceeds the maximum number of segments allowed for its destination (10 segments by default; some aggregators accept up to 25) is automatically split into multiple child messages, each within the segment limit, and sent sequentially in order. Splitting is encoding-aware: GSM-7 bodies split at 153-character boundaries and UCS-2 bodies at 134-byte (67-character) boundaries. When disabled (the default), messages exceeding the segment limit are rejected with an error.|

<h2 id="tocS_ModelMetadata">ModelMetadata</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamodelmetadata"></a>
<a id="schema_ModelMetadata"></a>
<a id="tocSmodelmetadata"></a>
<a id="tocsmodelmetadata"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6",
  "object": "model",
  "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "base_model": "string",
  "owned_by": "Telnyx",
  "organization": "moonshotai",
  "task": "text-generation",
  "context_length": 262144,
  "max_completion_tokens": 0,
  "languages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "parameters": 1000000000000,
  "parameters_str": "1.0T",
  "tier": "small",
  "license": "string",
  "is_fine_tunable": false,
  "recommended_for_assistants": false,
  "is_vision_supported": false,
  "beta": false,
  "description": "string",
  "pricing": {
    "prompt": "0.300000",
    "completion": "1.200000",
    "cached_prompt": "0.060000",
    "currency": "USD",
    "unit": "1M_tokens"
  },
  "regions": [
    "us-central-1",
    "us-east-1"
  ],
  "service_tiers": [
    "default"
  ]
}
```

Metadata for a model available on Telnyx Inference. Returned by `GET /v2/ai/openai/models` (and the deprecated `GET /v2/ai/models`). Open-source models live under their Hugging Face organization (e.g. `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`, `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`); fine-tuned models are owned by the Telnyx organization that trained them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Model identifier. For open-source models, follows the `{organization}/{model_name}` convention from Hugging Face (e.g. `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`).|
|object|string|false|none|Object type. Always `model`.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp at which the model was registered on Telnyx Inference (ISO 8601).|
|base_model|string \| null|false|none|Base model the fine-tuned model was trained from. Only set for fine-tuned models.|
|owned_by|string|true|none|Owner of the model. `Telnyx` for Telnyx-hosted open-source models, the upstream provider name for proxied models, or the Telnyx organization id for fine-tuned models.|
|organization|string|true|none|Organization that originally published the model, matching the prefix of `id` for open-source models.|
|task|string|false|none|Primary task the model is intended for, e.g. `text-generation`, `audio-text-to-text`, `feature-extraction` (embeddings).|
|context_length|integer|true|none|Maximum total tokens (prompt + completion) supported by the model in a single request.|
|max_completion_tokens|integer \| null|false|none|Model-specific completion-token ceiling. For Chat Completions, this value clamps explicit output limits and the 8192 default when that default applies. Models excluded from the default leave an omitted or null output limit unset for the serving engine, even when this metadata declares a ceiling; see `ChatCompletionRequest.max_tokens` for the hosted default and exclusion lists. This field does not report the effective default. `null` means no separate completion ceiling is declared; input and output together must still fit `context_length`.|
|languages|[string]|true|none|ISO language codes the model supports (e.g. `en`, `es`).|
|parameters|integer|true|none|Total parameter count of the model.|
|parameters_str|string \| null|false|none|Human-readable parameter count, e.g. `1.0T`, `753.9B`, `8B`.|
|tier|string|true|none|Billing tier the model belongs to. Used together with `pricing` to determine cost per 1M tokens.|
|license|string|true|none|License the model is distributed under, e.g. `Apache 2.0`, `MIT`, `Llama 3 Community License`.|
|is_fine_tunable|boolean|false|none|Whether the model can be used as a base for a fine-tuning job via `POST /v2/ai/fine_tuning/jobs`.|
|recommended_for_assistants|boolean|false|none|Whether Telnyx currently recommends this model as the LLM powering a Telnyx AI Assistant.|
|is_vision_supported|boolean|false|none|Whether the model accepts image inputs in chat completions (multimodal vision support).|
|beta|boolean|false|none|Whether the model is in beta. New Telnyx-hosted models launch with `beta: true`; the label is removed once the model is established.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Short, human-readable summary of what the model is best suited for.|
|pricing|object|false|none|Mapping of token kind to price, as strings to preserve precision. Typical keys are `prompt`, `cached_prompt`, and `completion`. When pricing is available the block also includes `currency` (ISO 4217 code matching the account's configured billing currency) and `unit` (the denomination the prices are quoted in, currently always `1M_tokens` for token-priced models).|
|regions|[string]|false|none|Public region names where the model is currently deployed (e.g. `us-central-1`, `eu-central-1`).|
|service_tiers|[string]|false|none|Service tiers supported by this Telnyx-hosted model. Use one of these values as `service_tier` in Chat Completions or Responses requests. This field is omitted for externally hosted models.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|tier|small|
|tier|medium|
|tier|large|
|tier|unlisted|
|service_tiers|default|
|service_tiers|priority|
|service_tiers|flex|

<a id="schemanodetarget"></a>
<a id="schema_NodeTarget"></a>
<a id="tocSnodetarget"></a>
<a id="tocsnodetarget"></a>

```json
{
  "node_id": "n_billing",
  "type": "node"
}
```

Edge target referencing another node within the same flow.

The runtime transitions the active node to `node_id` and continues
processing within the current assistant's flow.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_id|string|true|none|ID of the node this edge transitions into.|
|type|string|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_NoiseSuppressionEngine">NoiseSuppressionEngine</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanoisesuppressionengine"></a>
<a id="schema_NoiseSuppressionEngine"></a>
<a id="tocSnoisesuppressionengine"></a>
<a id="tocsnoisesuppressionengine"></a>

```json
"Denoiser"
```

The engine to use for noise suppression.
For backward compatibility, engines A, B, C, and D are also supported, but are deprecated:
 A - Denoiser
 B - DeepFilterNet
 C - Krisp
 D - AiCoustics

<h2 id="tocS_NoiseSuppressionEngineConfig">NoiseSuppressionEngineConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanoisesuppressionengineconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_NoiseSuppressionEngineConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSnoisesuppressionengineconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsnoisesuppressionengineconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "attenuation_limit": 100,
  "mode": "standard",
  "model": "krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef",
  "suppression_level": 50,
  "family": "sparrow",
  "size": "l",
  "enhancement_level": 0.5,
  "voice_gain": 1
}
```

Configuration parameters for noise suppression engines. Different engines support different parameters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attenuation_limit|integer|false|none|The attenuation limit for noise suppression (0-100). Only applicable for DeepFilterNet.|
|mode|string|false|none|Processing mode. Only applicable for DeepFilterNet.|
|model|string|false|none|The Krisp model to use. Only applicable for Krisp.|
|suppression_level|number|false|none|Suppression level (0.0-100.0). Only applicable for Krisp.|
|family|string|false|none|AiCoustics model family. 'sparrow' optimized for human-to-human calls, 'quail' optimized for Voice AI/STT. Only applicable for AiCoustics.|
|size|string|false|none|AiCoustics model size. 's' and 'l' work with both families. 'xs' and 'xxs' are sparrow-only. 'vf_l' and 'vf_1_1_l' are quail-only. Only applicable for AiCoustics.|
|enhancement_level|number|false|none|Enhancement intensity (0.0-1.0). Only applicable for AiCoustics.|
|voice_gain|number|false|none|Voice gain multiplier (0.1-4.0). Only applicable for AiCoustics.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|standard|
|mode|advanced|
|model|krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef|
|model|krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef|
|model|krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef|
|model|krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef|
|family|sparrow|
|family|quail|
|size|s|
|size|l|
|size|xs|
|size|xxs|
|size|vf_l|
|size|vf_1_1_l|

```json
{
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
  "direction": "both",

  }
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|

|direction|[NoiseSuppressionDirection](#schemanoisesuppressiondirection)|false|none|The direction of the audio stream to be noise suppressed.|
|noise_suppression_engine|[NoiseSuppressionEngine](#schemanoisesuppressionengine)|false|none|The engine to use for noise suppression.<br>For backward compatibility, engines A, B, C, and D are also supported, but are deprecated:<br> A - Denoiser<br> B - DeepFilterNet<br> C - Krisp<br> D - AiCoustics|
|noise_suppression_engine_config|[NoiseSuppressionEngineConfig](#schemanoisesuppressionengineconfig)|false|none|Configuration parameters for noise suppression engines. Different engines support different parameters.|

<h2 id="tocS_NumberPoolSettings">NumberPoolSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanumberpoolsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_NumberPoolSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSnumberpoolsettings"></a>
<a id="tocsnumberpoolsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "toll_free_weight": 10,
  "long_code_weight": 1,
  "skip_unhealthy": true,
  "sticky_sender": false,
  "geomatch": false
}
```

Number Pool allows you to send messages from a pool of numbers of different types, assigning
weights to each type. The pool consists of all the long code and toll free numbers
assigned to the messaging profile.

To disable this feature, set the object field to `null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|toll_free_weight|number|true|none|Defines the probability weight for a Toll Free number to be selected when sending a message.<br>The higher the weight the higher the probability. The sum of the weights for all number types<br>does not necessarily need to add to 100. Weight must be a non-negative number, and when equal<br>to zero it will remove the number type from the pool.<br>|
|long_code_weight|number|true|none|Defines the probability weight for a Long Code number to be selected when sending a message.<br>The higher the weight the higher the probability. The sum of the weights for all number types<br>does not necessarily need to add to 100.  Weight must be a non-negative number, and when equal<br>to zero it will remove the number type from the pool.<br>|
|skip_unhealthy|boolean|true|none|If set to true all unhealthy numbers will be automatically excluded from the pool.<br>Health metrics per number are calculated on a regular basis, taking into account the deliverability<br>rate and the amount of messages marked as spam by upstream carriers.<br>Numbers with a deliverability rate below 25% or spam ratio over 75% will be considered unhealthy.<br>|
|sticky_sender|boolean|false|none|If set to true, Number Pool will try to choose the same sending number for all messages to a particular<br>recipient. If the sending number becomes unhealthy and `skip_unhealthy` is set to true, a new<br>number will be chosen.<br>|
|geomatch|boolean|false|none|If set to true, Number Pool will try to choose a sending number with the same area code as the destination<br>number. If there are no such numbers available, a nunber with a different area code will be chosen. Currently<br>only NANP numbers are supported.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_PageMeta">PageMeta</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapagemeta"></a>
<a id="schema_PageMeta"></a>
<a id="tocSpagemeta"></a>
<a id="tocspagemeta"></a>

```json
{
  "page_number": 0,
  "page_size": 0,
  "total_pages": 0,
  "total_results": 0
}
```

Where a listing's page sits in the whole.

A page is a snapshot: the counts it reports and the order it is drawn in
both move as writes land, so paging through a busy namespace can repeat or
miss an entry at a page boundary.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_number|integer|true|none|The page returned, counting from 1.|
|page_size|integer|true|none|How many results a page holds.|
|total_pages|integer|true|none|Pages that can be requested; 0 when nothing matched. Page until `page_number` reaches it rather than until a page comes back short: a page can hold fewer than `page_size` results without being the last. Capped at the deepest page served, so on a very large listing it covers fewer results than `total_results`.|
|total_results|integer|true|none|Results the request matched, including any past the deepest page.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapayrequest"></a>

<a id="tocspayrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "connector_name": "Default",
  "amount": 10.5,
  "currency": "USD",
  "payment_method": "credit-card",
  "transaction_type": "charge",
  "max_attempts": 3,
  "timeout_millis": 5000,
  "inter_digit_timeout_millis": 5000,
  "voice": "female",
  "language": "en-US",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_name|string|false|none|Name of the Pay connector used to process the transaction.|
|amount|number|false|none|Amount to charge. Required when `transaction_type` is `charge`.|
|currency|string|false|none|Currency used for the transaction. Pay currently supports USD only.|
|payment_token|string|false|none|Existing payment token. When supplied, payment-detail collection is skipped.|
|payment_method|string|false|none|Payment method to collect.|
|valid_card_types|[string]|false|none|Restricts accepted card numbers to the listed card types. When the caller enters a card number that does not match one of the listed types, Pay treats the input as invalid and re-prompts for the card number. Cannot be used together with `payment_token`.|
|postal_code|string \| boolean|false|none|Controls billing postal code collection for credit-card payments when no `payment_token` is supplied. Set to `true` or the string `"true"` (the default) to prompt the caller for a postal code. Set to `false` or the string `"false"` to skip the postal code prompt without supplying a postal code to the payment connector. Supply any other non-empty string, such as `"90210"`, to use that postal code without prompting. Empty or whitespace-only strings are rejected. This option does not affect ACH debit payments or payments using an existing token.|
|min_postal_code_length|integer|false|none|Minimum number of digits the caller must enter when collecting a credit-card billing postal code. Applies only when `postal_code` is `true` or `"true"` and no `payment_token` is supplied. The default is 1. The maximum number of digits collected is the greater of 10 and this value. This does not validate the length of a postal code supplied directly in `postal_code`.|
|transaction_type|string|false|none|Transaction to perform. If omitted, Pay infers `tokenize` when `amount` is absent or zero and `charge` when `amount` is positive.|
|description|string|false|none|Optional description forwarded with the payment transaction.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Base64-encoded state included in subsequent webhooks.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Metadata forwarded to the Pay connector.|
|parameters|object|false|none|Additional parameters forwarded to the Pay connector.|
|prompts|[PayPrompts](#schemapayprompts)|false|none|Custom text-to-speech prompts keyed by payment collection step.|
|max_attempts|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of attempts for each payment collection step.|
|timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|Time in milliseconds to wait for DTMF input for each collection step.|
|inter_digit_timeout_millis|integer(int32)|false|none|Time in milliseconds to wait between consecutive DTMF digits.|
|voice|string|false|none|Voice used for payment prompts. Accepts `male`, `female`, or a provider voice in `<Provider>.<Model>.<VoiceId>` format, for example `AWS.Polly.Joanna` or `Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af`.|
|language|string|false|none|Language used for payment prompts.|
|service_level|string|false|none|Speech synthesis service level used for payment prompts. Pay defaults to `premium`.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Idempotency key for the command. Telnyx ignores a duplicate command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|

```json
    "connector_name": "string",

      "bank-routing-number": "string",
      "bank-account-number": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

(BETA) The pay tool allows the assistant to collect card payments from the caller via DTMF during the conversation. Recording is automatically paused while the pay tool is active and resumes when the payment flow completes. The connector_name must reference a pay connector configured in the Telnyx API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|shared|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this tool comes from the shared Tools Library. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. Read-only: set by the server, not accepted in requests. When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).|
|pay|[PayToolParams](#schemapaytoolparams)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|pay|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connector_name|string|true|none|The name of the pay connector configured in the Telnyx API. Must reference an existing pay connector for this organization.|
|currency|string|false|none|Default currency for payments processed by this tool.|
|payment_method|string|false|none|Default payment method for payments processed by this tool.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Description of the pay tool shown to the assistant so it knows when to call the tool. Not sent to the payment connector — the per-call `description` argument the assistant passes is what reaches the processor.|
|connector_parameters|object|false|none|Custom key/value parameters forwarded to the pay connector as `parameters` in the processor request. String values may use `{{dynamic_variable}}` templating, resolved per call.|
|valid_card_types|[string]|false|none|Restricts accepted card numbers to the listed card types. When the caller enters a card number that does not match one of the listed types, Pay treats the input as invalid and re-prompts for the card number.|
|postal_code|string \| boolean|false|none|Controls billing postal code collection for credit-card payments. Set to `false` to skip the postal code prompt without supplying a postal code to the payment connector (non-US cards, e.g. Irish Eircodes). Set to `true` to prompt the caller. Supply a non-empty string, such as `"90210"`, to use that postal code without prompting. This option does not affect ACH debit payments or payments using an existing token.|
|min_postal_code_length|integer|false|none|Minimum number of digits the caller must enter when collecting a credit-card billing postal code. Applies only when `postal_code` prompts the caller. Omitted means the platform default (1) applies. The maximum number of digits collected is the greater of 10 and this value. This does not validate the length of a postal code supplied directly in `postal_code`.|
|max_attempts|integer|false|none|Maximum number of attempts for each payment collection step. Omitted means the platform default (3) applies.|
|timeout_millis|integer|false|none|Time in milliseconds to wait for DTMF input for each collection step. Omitted means the platform default (5000) applies. Increase this for slower entry, e.g. a 16-digit card number.|
|inter_digit_timeout_millis|integer|false|none|Time in milliseconds to wait between consecutive DTMF digits. Omitted means the platform default (5000) applies.|
|prompts|object|false|none|Custom text-to-speech prompts keyed by payment collection step. The AI assistant merges its own card-number prompt into this map, matching on the same step keys.|

A phone-number batch groups all numbers added in a single bulk-add request. Telnyx vets the batch as a unit. The response embeds the full `phone_numbers` array so you can read per-number status without a separate call, plus a batch-level `status` summarising the unit's progress.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|batch_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|dir_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|dir_display_name|string|false|read-only|The DIR's display name at the time the batch was read.|
|enterprise_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|status|[PhoneNumberStatus](#schemaphonenumberstatus)|false|none|Aggregate batch status. Mirrors the values used on individual phone numbers (`submitted`, `in_review`, `verified`, `unsuccessful`, `permanently_rejected`, etc.).|
|total_count|integer|false|read-only|Number of phone numbers in this batch (length of `phone_numbers`).|
|submitted_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When the batch was created (and implicitly submitted for vetting).|
|documents|[[Document](#schemadocument)]|false|none|Documents attached to this batch (e.g. a Letter of Authorization). Empty when none were supplied at add time.|
|phone_numbers|[[DirPhoneNumber](#schemadirphonenumber)]|false|none|All phone numbers in this batch, with per-number status.|

Bulk-delete partial-success response. `data` is the list of phone numbers that were soft-deleted. `meta.errors` holds per-number failures (e.g. number not associated with this DIR). When EVERY number in the request fails, the endpoint instead returns 400 with the canonical Telnyx error envelope and `data`/`meta` are absent.

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "1f56eb76-4078-4af7-ad4d-564b027256ee",
      "dir_id": "16635d38-75a6-4481-82e8-69af60e05011",
      "enterprise_id": "4a6192a4-573d-446d-b3ce-aff9117272a6",
      "phone_number": "+19493253498",
      "batch_id": "0a4b1f5e-2f12-4c0c-9a98-9b3a7d8b8e62",
      "loa_document_id": null,
      "status": "submitted",
      "rejection_reason": {
        "code": "documentation_incomplete",
        "title": "Documentation incomplete",
        "detail": "Provided documents do not establish business identity.",
        "message": "Please re-upload a clearer scan of the certificate."
      },
      "created_at": "2026-04-26T18:11:42.850928Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-04-26T18:12:11.123456Z",
      "verified_at": "2026-04-26T18:12:11.123456Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

Bulk-add success response (HTTP 201). All numbers in the request were accepted into a single new batch. Every entry in `data` shares the same `batch_id` - read it from any element to obtain the batch id for subsequent `GET .../phone_number_batches/{batch_id}` calls. If any number in the request fails (schema-invalid, not in inventory, already attached to another DIR, etc.) the entire request is rejected with HTTP 400 and the canonical Telnyx error envelope; the success body described here is therefore an all-or-nothing payload.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[DirPhoneNumber](#schemadirphonenumber)]|true|none|Phone numbers accepted into the new batch. List order mirrors the request order. Each element shares the same `batch_id`.|

<h2 id="tocS_PhoneNumberStatus">PhoneNumberStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaphonenumberstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_PhoneNumberStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSphonenumberstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsphonenumberstatus"></a>

```json
"submitted"
```

Phone-number lifecycle status.
- `submitted` / `in_review` - Telnyx is reviewing the batch this number belongs to.
- `verified` - approved; the DIR's display identity will be shown on outbound calls from this number.
- `unsuccessful` - Telnyx rejected this submission; the customer may re-add to retry.
- `suspended` - temporarily disabled (e.g. by an active infringement claim on the DIR).
- `expired` - verification expired; re-add to renew.
- `permanently_rejected` - terminal; cannot be re-added on this or any other DIR you own.

|---|---|---|---|---|

If you want to update specific numbers rather than all numbers matching a filter, you must use this parameter. Each item must be either a valid phone number ID or a phone number in E164 format (e.g., '+13127367254').|
|tags|[string]|false|none|A list of user-assigned tags to help organize phone numbers.|
|external_pin|string|false|none|If someone attempts to port your phone number away from Telnyx and your phone number has an external PIN set, we will attempt to verify that you provided the correct external PIN to the winning carrier. Note that not all carriers cooperate with this security mechanism.|
|customer_reference|string|false|none|A customer reference string for customer look ups.|
|connection_id|string|false|none|Identifies the connection associated with the phone number.|
|billing_group_id|string|false|none|Identifies the billing group associated with the phone number.|
|hd_voice_enabled|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether to enable or disable HD Voice on each phone number. HD Voice is a paid feature and may not be available for all phone numbers, more details about it can be found in the Telnyx support documentation.|
|deletion_lock_enabled|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether to enable or disable the deletion lock on each phone number. When enabled, this prevents the phone number from being deleted via the API or Telnyx portal.|
|voice|[UpdatePhoneNumberVoiceSettingsRequest](#schemaupdatephonenumbervoicesettingsrequest)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_PlayAudioUrlRequest">PlayAudioUrlRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaplayaudiourlrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_PlayAudioUrlRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSplayaudiourlrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsplayaudiourlrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "audio_url": "http://www.example.com/sounds/greeting.wav",
  "loop": "infinity",
  "overlay": true,
  "stop": "current",
  "target_legs": "self",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audio_url|string|false|none|The URL of a file to be played back on the call. The URL can point to either a WAV or MP3 file. media_name and audio_url cannot be used together in one request.|
|media_name|string|false|none|The media_name of a file to be played back on the call. The media_name must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. The file must either be a WAV or MP3 file.|
|loop|[Loopcount](#schemaloopcount)|false|none|The number of times the audio file should be played. If supplied, the value must be an integer between 1 and 100, or the special string `infinity` for an endless loop.|
|overlay|boolean|false|none|When enabled, audio will be mixed on top of any other audio that is actively being played back. Note that `overlay: true` will only work if there is another audio file already being played on the call.|
|stop|string|false|none|When specified, it stops the current audio being played. Specify `current` to stop the current audio being played, and to play the next file in the queue. Specify `all` to stop the current audio file being played and to also clear all audio files from the queue.|
|target_legs|string|false|none|Specifies the leg or legs on which audio will be played. If supplied, the value must be either `self`, `opposite` or `both`.|
|cache_audio|boolean|false|none|Caches the audio file. Useful when playing the same audio file multiple times during the call.|
|audio_type|string|false|none|Specifies the type of audio provided in `audio_url` or `playback_content`.|
|playback_content|string|false|none|Allows a user to provide base64 encoded mp3 or wav. Note: when using this parameter, `media_url` and `media_name` in the `playback_started` and `playback_ended` webhooks will be empty|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|audio_type|mp3|
|audio_type|wav|

<h2 id="tocS_PostConversationSettings">PostConversationSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapostconversationsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_PostConversationSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSpostconversationsettings"></a>
<a id="tocspostconversationsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": false
}
```

Configuration for post-conversation processing. When enabled, the assistant receives one additional LLM turn after the conversation ends, allowing it to execute final tool calls such as sending a summary or updating a record via webhook or function tools. Integration and MCP server tools are not available post-conversation; call-control tools (e.g. hangup, transfer) are also unavailable. Beta feature.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether post-conversation processing is enabled. When true, the assistant will be invoked after the conversation ends to perform any final tool calls. Defaults to false.|

```json
{
```

```json
  "rate": 0,
  "unit": "string",
  "currency": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "country_iso": "string",
  "direction": "string",

  "output_rate": "string",

    {

    }

      "max": 0,

    }

    {
      "min": 0,
      "max": 0,
      "rate": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

A single pricing entry. Standard products include rate, unit, currency, type, country_iso, direction, and tiers. Inference products include model, input_rate, output_rate, cached_input_rate, and their respective tier arrays. Rate-deck products include pricing_type and note fields with null rate and empty tiers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable name describing the pricing entry.|
|rate|number \| string \| null|false|none|Per-unit rate. Numeric for standard products, string for inference products. Null for rate-deck products.|
|unit|string|false|none|Unit of measurement (e.g., part, message, GB, per_1k_tokens).|
|currency|string|false|none|ISO currency code (e.g., USD).|
|type|string|false|none|Pricing type (e.g., usage).|
|country_iso|string \| null|false|none|ISO country code. Null for non-geographic products.|
|direction|string \| null|false|none|Direction (e.g., termination). Null for non-directional products.|
|tiers|[[PricingTier](#schemapricingtier)]|false|none|Volume-based tiered pricing. Empty for rate-deck products.|
|pricing_type|string \| null|false|none|Pricing type for non-standard products (e.g., rate_deck). Absent on standard products.|
|note|string \| null|false|none|Additional note for rate-deck products (e.g., "Pricing is determined by the WhatsApp rate deck.").|
|model|string|false|none|Model identifier. Present only on inference product entries.|
|input_rate|string|false|none|Input token rate. Present only on inference product entries.|
|cached_input_rate|string|false|none|Cached input token rate. Present only on inference product entries.|
|output_rate|string|false|none|Output token rate. Present only on inference product entries.|
|input_tiers|[[PricingTier](#schemapricingtier)]|false|none|Input token tiered pricing. Present only on inference product entries.|
|cached_input_tiers|[[PricingTier](#schemapricingtier)]|false|none|Cached input token tiered pricing. Present only on inference product entries.|
|output_tiers|[[PricingTier](#schemapricingtier)]|false|none|Output token tiered pricing. Present only on inference product entries.|

<h2 id="tocS_PrivacySettings">PrivacySettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprivacysettings"></a>
<a id="schema_PrivacySettings"></a>
<a id="tocSprivacysettings"></a>
<a id="tocsprivacysettings"></a>

```json
{
  "data_retention": true,
  "pii_redaction": "disabled",
  "in_transit_data_locality": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_retention|boolean|false|none|If true, conversation history and insights will be stored. If false, they will not be stored. This in‑tool toggle governs solely the retention of conversation history and insights via the AI assistant. It has no effect on any separate recording, transcription, or storage configuration that you have set at the account, number, or application level. All such external settings remain in force regardless of your selection here.|
|pii_redaction|string|false|none|Controls redaction of personally identifiable information (PII) from the conversation history that is stored for this assistant. `disabled` (default) stores content as-is. `redact` replaces detected PII with `<PII:type/>` placeholders (e.g. `<PII:name/>`, `<PII:phone/>`) as the stored copies are written: message content (user, assistant, and tool-result messages) and tool-call arguments are redacted when written to conversation history, so the stored transcript, its read-back via the history API, and any insights generated from the stored messages contain the placeholders instead of the PII; response bodies returned by webhook tools are redacted too, as stored in the webhook logs — a per-conversation record separate from the transcript. In the Mission Control Portal this field appears as a "PII Redaction" on/off toggle, where Enabled corresponds to `redact`. Redaction runs when the stored copy is written, after the LLM has generated its reply: the live conversation is not redacted, the assistant's tools keep receiving the full (unredacted) values during the call, and the LLM still sees full content in its context window. Call recordings (including any recording layout configured under telephony settings) and the payloads of messages/webhooks delivered during the call are never redacted by this setting. The set of detected PII types (names, street addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, government identifiers like SSN and driver's license numbers, credit card and bank account numbers, IP addresses, dates of birth, and other identifiers unique to a person) is fixed by Telnyx and cannot be configured or extended per assistant. Assistants with `redact` cannot be used for SMS/WhatsApp messaging (that combination is rejected with a 400 error); voice and web chat are unaffected.|
|in_transit_data_locality|boolean|false|none|Requires this assistant's conversations to be processed inside your organization's data-locality region, rather than only stored there, on every channel: for web chat, every model call of a turn; for voice, the call's model calls and the Telnyx-hosted speech services it uses; for SMS and WhatsApp, the model calls of each turn (how messages travel through carriers is not covered). Covered processing that cannot be handled in region fails rather than being served elsewhere. Enabling it requires a data-locality region with in-region inference (USA, EU, AUS, UAE; see [Inference regions](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/models/regions)), Telnyx-hosted models for the assistant, its fallback, and any conversation-flow node that overrides the model, and, when `insight_settings.model` is set, an insight model available in that region; the request is rejected otherwise. A voice call fails when it starts if its STT model or TTS voice is not self-hosted by Telnyx, if the assistant uses a speech-to-speech model, or if the call's media is anchored outside the region. Once enabled, send web chat requests and WebSocket or WebRTC conversations to your region's API hostname: one entering the platform in another region is refused rather than forwarded, because forwarding it would already have moved the content across the border. See [Data residency](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/data-residency#in-region-processing-for-ai-assistants). Defaults to false.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|pii_redaction|disabled|
|pii_redaction|redact|

<h2 id="tocS_PromptSyncStatus">PromptSyncStatus</h2>

```json
"enabled"
```

Whether to auto-publish the assistant's instructions as a Langfuse prompt.

When ENABLED + prompt_name set, every assistant create/update pushes
`instructions` to Langfuse via create_prompt and stores the returned
version in prompt_version.

<h2 id="tocS_RCSAction">RCSAction</h2>

<a id="tocsrcsaction"></a>

```json
{
  "text": "Hello world",
  "postback_data": "string",
  "fallback_url": "http://example.com",
  "dial_action": {
    "phone_number": "+13125551234"
  },
  "view_location_action": {
    "lat_long": {
      "latitude": 41.8,
      "longitude": -87.6
    },
    "label": "string",
    "query": "string"
  },
  "create_calendar_event_action": {
    "start_time": "2024-10-02T15:01:23Z",
    "end_time": "2024-10-02T15:02:31Z",
    "title": "string",
    "description": "string"
  },
  "open_url_action": {
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "application": "BROWSER",
    "webview_view_mode": "HALF",
    "description": "string"
  },
  "share_location_action": {}
}
```

When tapped, initiates the corresponding native action on the device.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|text|string|false|none|Text that is shown in the suggested action. Maximum 25 characters.|
|postback_data|string|false|none|Payload (base64 encoded) that will be sent to the agent in the user event that results when the user taps the suggested action. Maximum 2048 characters.|
|fallback_url|string(url)|false|none|Fallback URL to use if a client doesn't support a suggested action. Fallback URLs open in new browser windows. Maximum 2048 characters.|
|dial_action|[RCSDialAction](#schemarcsdialaction)|false|none|Opens the user's default dialer app with the agent-specified phone number filled in.|
|view_location_action|[RCSViewLocationAction](#schemarcsviewlocationaction)|false|none|Opens the user's default map app and selects the agent-specified location.|
|create_calendar_event_action|[RCSCreateCalendarEventAction](#schemarcscreatecalendareventaction)|false|none|Opens the user's default calendar app and starts the new calendar event flow with the agent-specified event data pre-filled.|
|open_url_action|[RCSOpenUrlAction](#schemarcsopenurlaction)|false|none|Opens the user's default web browser app to the specified URL.|
|share_location_action|[RCSShareLocationAction](#schemarcssharelocationaction)|false|none|Opens the RCS app's location chooser so the user can pick a location to send back to the agent.|

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|sip_address|string|true|none|The SIP URI to which the call will be referred to.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
