|sip_auth_username|string|false|none|SIP Authentication username used for SIP challenges.|
|sip_auth_password|string|false|none|SIP Authentication password used for SIP challenges.|
|sip_headers|[[SipHeader](#schemasipheader)]|false|none|SIP headers to be added to the request. Currently only User-to-User header is supported.|

<h2 id="tocS_Reference">Reference</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareference"></a>
<a id="schema_Reference"></a>
<a id="tocSreference"></a>
<a id="tocsreference"></a>

```json
{
  "record_type": "dir_reference",
  "ref_type": "business",
  "slot": 1,
  "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
  "job_title": "VP of Operations",
  "organization": "Acme Logistics",
  "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
  "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
  "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
  "timezone": "America/New_York"
}
```

A reference (business or financial) on a DIR, in the customer-facing shape. No internal identifiers are exposed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|string|true|read-only|Always `dir_reference`.|
|ref_type|string|true|none|Whether this is a business reference or the financial reference.|
|slot|integer|true|none|Position within the reference type, counting from 1. Business references occupy slots 1 and 2, in the order they were sent in the `business_references` array; the financial reference occupies slot 1. Use this value together with `ref_type` to address the reference when updating it.|
|full_name|string|true|none|Full name of the reference contact.|
|job_title|string \| null|false|none|Job title of the reference contact.|
|organization|string \| null|false|none|Organization the reference contact belongs to.|
|relationship_to_registrant|string \| null|false|none|How the reference contact is related to the registering business.|
|phone_e164|string|true|none|Reference phone number in E.164 format.|
|email|string(email) \| null|false|none|Reference contact email address.|
|timezone|string|true|none|IANA timezone id for the reference. Calls are only placed within the reference's local 8am-9pm window.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|record_type|dir_reference|
|ref_type|business|
|ref_type|financial|

<h2 id="tocS_ReferenceInput">ReferenceInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareferenceinput"></a>
<a id="schema_ReferenceInput"></a>
<a id="tocSreferenceinput"></a>
<a id="tocsreferenceinput"></a>

```json
{
  "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
  "job_title": "VP of Operations",
  "organization": "Acme Logistics",
  "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
  "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
  "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
  "timezone": "America/New_York"
}
```

One reference supplied at submit. The reference type is implied by the field that carries it (business_references vs financial_reference).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|full_name|string|true|none|Full name of the reference contact.|
|job_title|string \| null|false|none|Job title of the reference contact.|
|organization|string \| null|false|none|Organization the reference contact belongs to.|
|relationship_to_registrant|string \| null|false|none|How the reference contact is related to the registering business.|
|phone_e164|string|true|none|Reference phone number in E.164 format, e.g. +14155550123.|
|email|string(email)|true|none|Reference contact email address. Required: the reference is emailed scheduling and dial-in notices.|
|timezone|string|true|none|IANA timezone id for the reference (e.g. America/New_York). Required: calls are only placed within the reference's local 8am-9pm window.|

<h2 id="tocS_ReferenceSubmissionRequest">ReferenceSubmissionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareferencesubmissionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ReferenceSubmissionRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSreferencesubmissionrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsreferencesubmissionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "business_references": [
    {
      "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
      "job_title": "VP of Operations",
      "organization": "Acme Logistics",
      "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
      "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
      "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    },
    {
      "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
      "job_title": "VP of Operations",
      "organization": "Acme Logistics",
      "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
      "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
      "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    }
  ],
  "financial_reference": {
    "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
    "job_title": "VP of Operations",
    "organization": "Acme Logistics",
    "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
    "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
    "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
    "timezone": "America/New_York"
  }
}
```

Exactly two business references plus one financial reference.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|business_references|[[ReferenceInput](#schemareferenceinput)]|true|none|Exactly two business references. Array order determines each one's slot: the first entry becomes slot 1 and the second becomes slot 2. Those slots are what you pass when updating a single reference later. Each should be a senior contact who can speak to your company's reputation and operations: a C-suite executive (CEO, CFO, CTO, COO), an owner or founder as reflected in your corporate records, or a senior manager, director, or executive at an organization you work with, such as a vendor, partner, or client.|
|financial_reference|object|true|none|One financial reference who can confirm the company pays its bills: a licensed certified public accountant (CPA) the company uses, a contact at a bank or financial institution that has a relationship with the company, or a reasonable alternative banking or financial reference.|

<h2 id="tocS_ReferenceUpdateRequest">ReferenceUpdateRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareferenceupdaterequest"></a>
<a id="schema_ReferenceUpdateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSreferenceupdaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocsreferenceupdaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "full_name": "Dana Reyes",
  "job_title": "VP of Operations",
  "organization": "Acme Logistics",
  "relationship_to_registrant": "Supplier",
  "phone_e164": "+14155550123",
  "email": "dana.reyes@example.com",
  "timezone": "America/New_York"
}
```

Partial update for a single reference; supply at least one field. Cosmetic fields are always editable. phone_e164 and timezone may only be changed while a scheduled call has not yet been dialed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|full_name|string|false|none|The full name of the person we should contact as your reference.|
|job_title|string \| null|false|none|The reference contact's job title, for example CFO or Owner.|
|organization|string \| null|false|none|The name of the organization the reference contact works for.|
|relationship_to_registrant|string \| null|false|none|How the reference contact is related to the registering business.|
|phone_e164|string|false|none|The reference's phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550123. We call this number during their local business hours.|
|email|string(email)|false|none|The reference's email address. We email them scheduling and dial-in instructions before we call, so use an address they check.|
|timezone|string|false|none|The reference's IANA time zone, for example America/New_York. We only call during their local 8am to 9pm hours, which is why we need it.|

<h2 id="tocS_ReputationOwnershipStatus">ReputationOwnershipStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareputationownershipstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_ReputationOwnershipStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSreputationownershipstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsreputationownershipstatus"></a>

```json
"verified"
```

Result of ongoing ownership checks. `verified`: the number is with the carrier on record. `pending_confirmation`: the number's carrier changed, or a periodic ownership re-verification is due; confirm you still own it before `confirm_by`. `flagged`: a periodic re-verification went unanswered; the number stays monitored and is not removed, but confirm ownership (`POST .../ownership_confirm`) to return it to `verified`. `removed`: the number is no longer monitored; returned by `POST .../ownership_confirm` with `still_own: false`, and when listing numbers with `filter[ownership_status]=removed`.

|ownership_status|[ReputationOwnershipStatus](#schemareputationownershipstatus)|false|none|Result of ongoing ownership checks. `verified`: the number is with the carrier on record. `pending_confirmation`: the number's carrier changed, or a periodic ownership re-verification is due; confirm you still own it before `confirm_by`. `flagged`: a periodic re-verification went unanswered; the number stays monitored and is not removed, but confirm ownership (`POST .../ownership_confirm`) to return it to `verified`. `removed`: the number is no longer monitored; returned by `POST .../ownership_confirm` with `still_own: false`, and when listing numbers with `filter[ownership_status]=removed`.|

<h2 id="tocS_RequestMetadata">RequestMetadata</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarequestmetadata"></a>
<a id="schema_RequestMetadata"></a>
<a id="tocSrequestmetadata"></a>
<a id="tocsrequestmetadata"></a>

```json
{
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

Customer request tags from the x-ltg-metadata header: up to 5 entries. Keys are case-sensitive; keys starting with ltg_, telnyx_, litellm_ or cf_ (any case) are reserved. Values are strings (1-256 characters, no control or format characters), integers within +/-9007199254740991, or booleans; floats, null, objects and arrays are rejected. Values that look like credentials are rejected. Tags are attribution only: never forwarded upstream, never part of the response cache key, never used for budgets or routing. An untagged request reports {}.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|string \| integer \| boolean|false|none|none|

```json
  "label": "string",

```

Upload-based voice clone using the Resemble provider. The clone is `active` on creation. Use it as voice `Resemble.<model_id>.<clone_id>`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audio_file|string(binary)|true|none|Audio file to clone the voice from. Supported formats: WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A. Converted to WAV and trimmed to the first 10 seconds. For best quality, provide about 10 seconds of clean, single-speaker speech. Maximum size: 20MB.|
|name|string|true|none|Name for the voice clone.|
|language|string|false|none|Language of the reference audio, matched case-insensitively. Pro: required, one of `ar`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en-US`, `es`, `fi`, `fr-fr`, `he`, `hi`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `ms`, `nl`, `no`, `pl`, `pt`, `ru`, `sv`, `sw`, `tr`, `zh`. Turbo: `en` or `en-US` (default `en-US`). Urdu: `ur` (default). Other values return `422`.|
|gender|string|true|none|Gender of the voice clone.|
|label|string|false|none|Optional custom label describing the voice style.|
|model_id|string|true|none|Resemble model: `Pro`, `Turbo` (English only), or `Urdu`. A clone works only with this model.|

```json
  "store_preview": false,
  "preview_format": "tiff",
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connection_id|string|true|none|The connection ID to send the fax with.|
|media_url|[MediaUrl](#schemamediaurl)|false|none|The URL (or list of URLs) to the fax document. Supported formats: PDF, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, DOC, DOCX, RTF, and TXT. media_url and media_name/contents can't be submitted together.|
|media_name|[MediaName](#schemamedianame)|false|none|The media_name used for the fax's media. Must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. Supported formats: PDF, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, DOC, DOCX, RTF, and TXT. media_name and media_url/contents can't be submitted together.|
|to|[To](#schemato)|true|none|The phone number, in E.164 format, the fax will be sent to or SIP URI|
|from|[From](#schemafrom)|true|none|The phone number, in E.164 format, the fax will be sent from.|
|from_display_name|string|false|none|The `from_display_name` string to be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`to` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and -_~!.+ special characters. If ommited, the display name will be the same as the number in the `from` field.|
|quality|[Quality](#schemaquality)|false|none|The quality of the fax. The `ultra` settings provides the highest quality available, but also present longer fax processing times. `ultra_light` is best suited for images, wihle `ultra_dark` is best suited for text.|
|t38_enabled|boolean|false|none|The flag to disable the T.38 protocol.|
|monochrome|boolean|false|none|The flag to enable monochrome, true black and white fax results.|
|black_threshold|integer|false|none|The black threshold percentage for monochrome faxes. Only applicable if `monochrome` is set to `true`.|
|store_media|boolean|false|none|Should fax media be stored on temporary URL. It does not support media_name, they can't be submitted together.|

```json
{
  "type": "send_message",
  "shared": true,
  "send_message": {
    "message_template": "string"
  }
}
```

The send_message tool allows the assistant to send SMS or MMS messages to the end user. The 'to' and 'from' addresses are automatically determined from the conversation context, and the message text is generated by the assistant unless a message_template is provided for runtime variable substitution.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|shared|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this tool comes from the shared Tools Library. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. Read-only: set by the server, not accepted in requests. When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).|
|send_message|object|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|send_message|

<h2 id="tocS_SharedCampaign">SharedCampaign</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasharedcampaign"></a>
<a id="schema_SharedCampaign"></a>
<a id="tocSsharedcampaign"></a>
<a id="tocssharedcampaign"></a>

```json
{
  "brandId": "string",
  "campaignId": "string",
  "createDate": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "usecase": "string"
}
```

Campaign is generated by the 10DLC registry once the corresponding campaign request is approved. Each campaign is assigned a unique identifier - **campaignId**. Once a campaign is activated, limited information is published to the NetNumber OSR service for consumption by members of the ecosystem. When a campaign is suspended(reversible) or expired(non-reversible), campaign data is deleted from the OSR service. Most attributes of campaignare immutable, including **usecase**, **vertical**, **brandId** and **cspId**.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brandId|string|true|none|Alphanumeric identifier of the brand associated with this campaign.|
|campaignId|string|true|none|Alphanumeric identifier assigned by the registry for a campaign. This identifier is required by the NetNumber OSR SMS enabling process of 10DLC.|
|createDate|string|false|none|Unix timestamp when campaign was created.|
|status|string|false|none|Current campaign status. Possible values: ACTIVE, EXPIRED. A newly created campaign defaults to ACTIVE status. |
|usecase|string|true|none|Campaign usecase. Must be of defined valid types. Use `/10dlc/enum/usecase` operation to retrieve usecases available for given brand.|

```json
  },
```

```json
  "esim_installation_status": "released",
  "version": "4.3",
  "resources_with_in_progress_actions": [],
  "eid": null,
  "authorized_imeis": [
    "106516771852751",
    "534051870479563",
    "508821468377961"
  ],
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|Identifies the resource.|
|record_type|string|false|read-only|none|
|status|[SIMCardStatus](#schemasimcardstatus)|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of SIM card|
|iccid|string|false|read-only|The ICCID is the identifier of the specific SIM card/chip. Each SIM is internationally identified by its integrated circuit card identifier (ICCID). ICCIDs are stored in the SIM card's memory and are also engraved or printed on the SIM card body during a process called personalization.<br>|
|imsi|string|false|read-only|SIM cards are identified on their individual network operators by a unique International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI). <br/><br>Mobile network operators connect mobile phone calls and communicate with their market SIM cards using their IMSIs. The IMSI is stored in the Subscriber  Identity Module (SIM) inside the device and is sent by the device to the appropriate network. It is used to acquire the details of the device in the Home  Location Register (HLR) or the Visitor Location Register (VLR).<br>|
|msisdn|string|false|read-only|Mobile Station International Subscriber Directory Number (MSISDN) is a number used to identify a mobile phone number internationally. <br/><br>MSISDN is defined by the E.164 numbering plan. It includes a country code and a National Destination Code which identifies the subscriber's operator.<br>|
|sim_card_group_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The group SIMCardGroup identification. This attribute can be <code>null</code> when it's present in an associated resource.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Searchable tags associated with the SIM card|
|data_limit|object|false|read-only|The SIM card individual data limit configuration.|
|current_billing_period_consumed_data|object|false|read-only|The SIM card consumption so far in the current billing cycle.|
|actions_in_progress|boolean|false|read-only|Indicate whether the SIM card has any pending (in-progress) actions.|
|created_at|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was created.|
|updated_at|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was updated.|
|esim_installation_status|string \| null|false|read-only|The installation status of the eSIM. Only applicable for eSIM cards.|
|version|string|false|read-only|The version of the SIM card.|
|resources_with_in_progress_actions|[object]|false|read-only|List of resources with actions in progress.|
|eid|string \| null|false|read-only|The Embedded Identity Document (eID) for eSIM cards.|
|authorized_imeis|[string]|false|none|List of IMEIs authorized to use a given SIM card.|
|voice_enabled|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates whether voice services are enabled for the SIM card.|

|updated_at|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was updated.|

Use this field to modify sound effects, for example adjust the pitch.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|pitch|number(float)|false|none|Set the pitch directly, value should be > 0, default 1 (lower = lower tone)|

|octaves|number(float)|false|none|Adjust the pitch in octaves, values should be between -1 and 1, default 0|
|track|string|false|none|The track to which the sound modifications will be applied. Accepted values are `inbound` or `outbound`|

<h2 id="tocS_SpeakNode">SpeakNode</h2>


A standalone scripted-message step in a flow, as returned by the API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Node kind discriminator. Always `speak` for a speak node.|
|id|string|true|none|Caller-supplied unique identifier for this node within the flow.|
|name|string|false|none|Optional human-readable label, displayed in authoring UIs.|
|message|string|true|none|Message delivered to the user verbatim when the flow reaches this node. No LLM turn — the text is spoken/sent exactly as written. `{{variable}}` placeholders are interpolated from the conversation's dynamic variables; an unresolved placeholder renders as an empty string. After delivering, the flow routes via the node's outgoing `llm` / `expression` edges (commonly a single unconditional edge).|
|position|[NodePosition](#schemanodeposition)|false|none|Optional canvas coordinates used by authoring UIs to lay out the graph. Ignored by the runtime; round-trips so frontends can persist graph layout across reloads.|

<h2 id="tocS_SpeakNodeReq">SpeakNodeReq</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaspeaknodereq"></a>
<a id="schema_SpeakNodeReq"></a>
<a id="tocSspeaknodereq"></a>
<a id="tocsspeaknodereq"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "n_greeting",
  "message": "Thanks for calling, {{caller_name}}. Connecting you now.",
  "name": "Greeting",
  "position": {
    "x": 60,
    "y": 80
  },
  "type": "speak"
}
```

A standalone scripted-message step in a flow, as supplied by clients.

Unlike a prompt node, a speak node has no instructions or model — it isn't
an LLM turn. Reaching it delivers `message` to the user verbatim (with
`{{variable}}` interpolation), then routes via outgoing `llm` /
`expression` edges.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Node kind discriminator. Always `speak` for a speak node.|
|id|string|true|none|Caller-supplied unique identifier for this node within the flow.|
|name|string|false|none|Optional human-readable label, displayed in authoring UIs.|
|message|string|true|none|Message delivered to the user verbatim when the flow reaches this node. No LLM turn — the text is spoken/sent exactly as written. `{{variable}}` placeholders are interpolated from the conversation's dynamic variables; an unresolved placeholder renders as an empty string. After delivering, the flow routes via the node's outgoing `llm` / `expression` edges (commonly a single unconditional edge).|
|position|[NodePosition](#schemanodeposition)|false|none|Optional canvas coordinates used by authoring UIs to lay out the graph. Ignored by the runtime; round-trips so frontends can persist graph layout across reloads.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocsspeakrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "payload": "Say this on the call",
  "payload_type": "text",
  "service_level": "basic",
  "stop": "current",
  "voice": "female",
  "language": "arb",
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payload|string|true|none|The text or SSML to be converted into speech. There is a 3,000 character limit.|
|payload_type|string|false|none|The type of the provided payload. The payload can either be plain text, or Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML).|
|service_level|string|false|none|This parameter impacts speech quality, language options and payload types. When using `basic`, only the `en-US` language and payload type `text` are allowed.|
|stop|string|false|none|When specified, it stops the current audio being played. Specify `current` to stop the current audio being played, and to play the next file in the queue. Specify `all` to stop the current audio file being played and to also clear all audio files from the queue.|
|voice|string|true|none|Specifies the voice used in speech synthesis.<br><br>- Define voices using the format `<Provider>.<Model>.<VoiceId>`. Specifying only the provider will give default values for voice_id and model_id.<br><br> **Supported Providers:**<br>- **AWS:** Use `AWS.Polly.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna`). For neural voices, which provide more realistic, human-like speech, append `-Neural` to the `VoiceId` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna-Neural`). Check the [available voices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/available-voices.html) for compatibility.<br>- **Azure:** Use `Azure.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Azure.en-CA-ClaraNeural`, `Azure.en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural`, `Azure.en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural`). For a complete list of voices, go to [Azure Voice Gallery](https://speech.microsoft.com/portal/voicegallery). Use `voice_settings` to configure custom deployments, regions, or API keys.<br>- **ElevenLabs:** Use `ElevenLabs.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `ElevenLabs.eleven_multilingual_v2.21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM`). The `ModelId` part is optional. To use ElevenLabs, you must provide your ElevenLabs API key as an integration identifier secret in `"voice_settings": {"api_key_ref": "<secret_identifier>"}`. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) for details. Check [available voices](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/get-voices).<br>- **Telnyx:** Use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>` (e.g., `Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af`). Use `voice_settings` to configure voice_speed and other synthesis parameters. `Bayan` provides Arabic (multiple dialects) and English voices (e.g., `Telnyx.Bayan.Ahmed`, `Telnyx.Bayan.Amanda`). `Sukhan` provides Urdu voices (e.g., `Telnyx.Sukhan.urdu-professor`); `voice_speed` is not supported.<br>- **Minimax:** Use `Minimax.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Minimax.speech-02-hd.Wise_Woman`). Supported models: `speech-02-turbo`, `speech-02-hd`, `speech-2.6-turbo`, `speech-2.8-turbo`. Use `voice_settings` to configure speed, volume, pitch, and language_boost.<br>- **Resemble:** Use `Resemble.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Resemble.Turbo.Aaron_en-US`). Supported models: `Pro`, `Turbo`, `Urdu`. `<VoiceId>` is a stock voice name or the ID of a Resemble voice clone. Use `voice_settings` to configure precision, sample_rate, and format.<br>- **Inworld:** Use `Inworld.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Inworld.Mini.Loretta`, `Inworld.Max.Oliver`, `Inworld.TTS2.Loretta`). Supported models: `Mini`, `Max`, `TTS2`. Use `voice_settings` to configure `delivery_mode` (`STABLE`, `BALANCED`, `CREATIVE`), supported by `TTS2` only.<br>- **Fish Audio:** Use `FishAudio.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `FishAudio.s2.1-pro.<reference_id>`). Supported models: `s2.1-pro`, `s2-pro`, `s1`. `VoiceId` is a Fish Voice-Library reference ID.<br>- **Soniox:** Use `Soniox.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma`). Supported model: `tts-rt-v2`. Browse the catalog via the [Voices API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/text-to-speech-commands/list-available-voices). Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the text, for example `it`. SSML is not supported. Use `voice_settings` to configure `speed` (0.7 to 1.3) and `reduce_silence`.<br>- **xAI:** Use `xAI.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `xAI.eve`). Available voices: `eve`, `ara`, `rex`, `sal`, `leo`.<br>- **Humain:** Use `Humain.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Humain.sara-ar`). Available voices: `sara-en`, `abdulaziz-en`, `sara-ar`, `abdulaziz-ar`, `nourah-ar`, `abdullah-ar`. Native Arabic (Saudi dialect) and English voices only — no `ModelId` segment.<br><br>For service_level basic, you may define the gender of the speaker (male or female).|
|voice_settings|[ElevenLabsVoiceSettings](#schemaelevenlabsvoicesettings) \| [TelnyxVoiceSettings](#schematelnyxvoicesettings) \| [AWSVoiceSettings](#schemaawsvoicesettings) \| [MinimaxVoiceSettings](#schemaminimaxvoicesettings) \| [AzureVoiceSettings](#schemaazurevoicesettings) \| [ResembleVoiceSettings](#schemaresemblevoicesettings) \| [InworldVoiceSettings](#schemainworldvoicesettings) \| [XAIVoiceSettings](#schemaxaivoicesettings) \| [SonioxVoiceSettings](#schemasonioxvoicesettings) \| [AssemblyAIVoiceSettings](#schemaassemblyaivoicesettings)|false|none|The settings associated with the voice selected|
|language|string|false|none|The language you want spoken. This parameter is ignored when a `Polly.*` voice is specified.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|loop|[Loopcount](#schemaloopcount)|false|none|The number of times to play the audio file. Use `infinity` to loop indefinitely. Defaults to 1.|
|target_legs|string|false|none|Specifies which legs of the call should receive the spoken audio.|

<h2 id="tocS_SpeechmaticsTranscriptionLanguage">SpeechmaticsTranscriptionLanguage</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaspeechmaticstranscriptionlanguage"></a>
<a id="schema_SpeechmaticsTranscriptionLanguage"></a>
<a id="tocSspeechmaticstranscriptionlanguage"></a>
<a id="tocsspeechmaticstranscriptionlanguage"></a>

```json
"en"
```

Language to use for speech recognition. Accepted values depend on the selected `transcription_model`. `speechmatics/standard` supports: `en`, `ba`, `eu`, `gl`, `ga`, `mt`, `mn`, `sw`, `ug`, `cy`, `ar_en`, `cmn_en`, `en_ms`, `en_ta`, `tl`, `es-bilingual-en`, `cmn_en_ms_ta`. `speechmatics/linden-1` (preview) supports the same languages as Speechmatics Realtime: `ar`, `ar_en`, `ba`, `be`, `bg`, `bn`, `ca`, `cmn`, `cmn_en`, `cmn_en_ms_ta`, `cs`, `cy`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en`, `en_ms`, `en_ta`, `eo`, `es`, `es-bilingual-en`, `et`, `eu`, `fa`, `fi`, `fr`, `ga`, `gl`, `he`, `hi`, `hr`, `hu`, `ia`, `id`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `lt`, `lv`, `mn`, `mr`, `ms`, `mt`, `nl`, `no`, `pl`, `pt`, `ro`, `ru`, `sk`, `sl`, `sv`, `sw`, `ta`, `th`, `tl`, `tr`, `ug`, `uk`, `ur`, `vi`, `yue`, plus the spelling and script variants `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-AU`, `cmn-Hans`, and `cmn-Hant` (`en` alone uses the default spelling). A value outside the selected model's list is rejected. For `speechmatics/standard`, unset, blank, `auto`, `auto_beta`, or `multi` defaults to `en`; for `speechmatics/linden-1`, only an unset language defaults to `en`, and `auto`, `auto_beta`, or `multi` is rejected.

The spend limit, spend and block state of one product and period. The top-level fields describe the total limit of the account; API key limits are nested in `credential_limits`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|string|true|none|Identifies the type of the resource.|
|product|string|true|none|Product the entry applies to.|
|product_name|string|true|none|Display name of the product.|
|period|[SpendLimitPeriod](#schemaspendlimitperiod)|true|none|`daily` is the current UTC day; `monthly` is the current UTC calendar month.|
|period_start|string(date)|true|none|First UTC day of the current period.|
|period_end|string(date)|true|none|Exclusive end of the current period, a UTC date.|
|credential_id|string \| null|false|none|In write responses, the API key the write was about; `null` for the total limit. Always `null` in list entries, which describe the total limit.|
|limit|[SpendLimitLimit](#schemaspendlimitlimit)|true|none|The limit set on the account for the product and period, whoever set it. `null` when none is set.|
|effective_limit_usd|string \| null|true|none|The limit in USD that is enforced, as a decimal string. `null` means unlimited.|
|spend_usd|string \| null|true|none|Spend in USD so far in the period, as a decimal string. It can lag actual usage by about a minute. `null` when it could not be read.|
|spend_error|string \| null|true|none|Set when `spend_usd` is `null`.|
|blocked|boolean|true|none|The product is blocked for the whole account in this period (total limit). An API key's own block appears only in `credential_limits`. Always `false` in write responses; list the limits to read the block state.|
|block|[SpendLimitBlock](#schemaspendlimitblock)|true|none|The active block of the period. `null` when the period is not blocked.|
|credential_limits|[[SpendLimitCredentialLimit](#schemaspendlimitcredentiallimit)]|false|none|List responses only. One item per API key limit of the product and period, sorted by `credential_id`, plus every API key that is still blocked. `[]` when there are none.|
|evaluation|[SpendLimitEvaluation](#schemaspendlimitevaluation)|false|none|What a create, update or delete did to the period at once. Only present in write responses.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|period|daily|
|period|monthly|

The limit, spend and block state of one API key in the product and period.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|credential_id|string|true|none|Identifier of the API key as recorded on usage. Never the key's secret.|
|limit|[SpendLimitCredentialLimitValue](#schemaspendlimitcredentiallimitvalue)|true|none|The limit of one API key. It always has an amount. `null` for an API key that is still blocked after its limit was removed.|
|spend_usd|string \| null|true|none|Spend in USD in the period made with exactly this API key, as a decimal string. Usage without an API key identifier, or with another one, counts only toward the total. `null` when it could not be read.|
|spend_error|string \| null|true|none|Set when `spend_usd` is `null`.|
|exceeds_total|boolean|false|none|The API key's limit is above the period's total limit. Only a change by Telnyx support can cause it; the total limit still applies to the whole account. Lower the API key limit or raise the total.|
|blocked|boolean|true|none|This API key is blocked for the period.|
|block|[SpendLimitBlock](#schemaspendlimitblock)|true|none|The active block of the period. `null` when the period is not blocked.|


What a create, update or delete did to the period at once. Only present in write responses.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spend_usd|string \| null|true|none|Spend in USD used for the check, as a decimal string. `null` when the spend was not checked.|
|released|boolean|true|none|The change lifted a block of this period.|
|blocked_now|boolean|true|none|The change blocked the product: the spend was already above the new limit.|
|still_over_limit|boolean|true|none|A block of this period remains because the spend is still above the new limit.|
|still_blocked_other_period|boolean|true|none|The other period has an active block, so the product stays blocked whatever this period's result. For an API key write, the API key's limit in the other period.|
|account_blocked|boolean|false|none|API key writes only: the account itself remains blocked for the product under a total limit. Absent for total limit writes.|
|evaluation_deferred|boolean|true|none|The spend could not be checked now. The change is saved and applied within a few minutes.|
|note|string|false|none|Additional information about the result, when there is any.|

```json
  "sql": "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?",
  "params": [
    "alice"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sql|string|true|none|The SQL to run. Use positional `?` placeholders and supply the values in `params` rather than interpolating them into this string.|
|params|[string \| number \| boolean \| null]|false|none|Positional bind parameters, in placeholder order. Each value is a string, a number, a boolean, or null; booleans are cast to `1`/`0`. The count must match the number of `?` placeholders exactly — a mismatch is rejected with 422 rather than binding null for the ones you left out. (Not enforced for multi-statement scripts or named parameters, where the placeholder count is not the number bound.)|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|format|string|true|none|The audio file format used when storing the call recording. Can be either `mp3` or `wav`.|
|channels|string|true|none|When `dual`, final audio file will be stereo recorded with the first leg on channel A, and the rest on channel B.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|play_beep|boolean|false|none|If enabled, a beep sound will be played at the start of a recording.|
|max_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Defines the maximum length for the recording in seconds. The minimum value is 0. The maximum value is 14400. The default value is 0 (infinite)|
|timeout_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that call transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite)|
|recording_track|string|false|none|The audio track to be recorded. Can be either `both`, `inbound` or `outbound`. If only single track is specified (`inbound`, `outbound`), `channels` configuration is ignored and it will be recorded as mono (single channel).|
|trim|string|false|none|When set to `trim-silence`, silence will be removed from the beginning and end of the recording.|
|custom_file_name|string|false|none|The custom recording file name to be used instead of the default `call_leg_id`. Telnyx will still add a Unix timestamp suffix.|
|transcription|boolean|false|none|Enable post recording transcription. The default value is false.|
|transcription_engine|string|false|none|Engine to use for speech recognition. `A` - `Google`, `B` - `Telnyx`, `deepgram/nova-3` - `Deepgram Nova-3`. Note: `deepgram/nova-3` supports only `en` and `en-{Region}` languages.|
|transcription_language|[TranscriptionLanguage](#schematranscriptionlanguage)|false|none|Language code for transcription. Note: Not all languages are supported by all transcription engines (google, telnyx, deepgram). See engine-specific documentation for supported values.|
|transcription_profanity_filter|boolean|false|none|Enables profanity_filter. Applies to `google` engine only.|
|transcription_speaker_diarization|boolean|false|none|Enables speaker diarization. Applies to `google` engine only.|
|transcription_min_speaker_count|integer(int32)|false|none|Defines minimum number of speakers in the conversation. Applies to `google` engine only.|
|transcription_max_speaker_count|integer(int32)|false|none|Defines maximum number of speakers in the conversation. Applies to `google` engine only.|

<h2 id="tocS_StartSpeakingPlan">StartSpeakingPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastartspeakingplan"></a>
<a id="schema_StartSpeakingPlan"></a>
<a id="tocSstartspeakingplan"></a>
<a id="tocsstartspeakingplan"></a>

```json
{
  "wait_seconds": 0.4,
  "transcription_endpointing_plan": {
    "on_punctuation_seconds": 0.1,
    "on_no_punctuation_seconds": 1.5,
    "on_number_seconds": 0.5
  }
}
```

Controls when the assistant starts speaking after the user stops. These thresholds primarily apply to non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn detection is driven by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` instead.

Sending any `start_speaking_plan` object — an empty `{}` included (the stored config fills in field defaults) — engages per-turn transcript matching: on each turn the transcript tail is evaluated against the configured `transcription_endpointing_plan` tiers, and the wait is set to the matching tier's seconds. When the transcript ends without terminal punctuation or a number and `transcription_endpointing_plan` is set, its `on_no_punctuation_seconds` tier applies. Only when no tier matches (`transcription_endpointing_plan` unset or null) does the wait stay on `wait_seconds`. Setting `start_speaking_plan` to `null` (or omitting it) turns per-turn matching off entirely, and the assistant starts speaking as soon as silence is detected.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|wait_seconds|number(float)|false|none|Wait used when per-turn endpointing does not select a tier. While the plan is present this applies on every turn without a matching tier (including when `transcription_endpointing_plan` is unset); a matching tier replaces it for that turn, and a tier may be shorter or longer than this value.|
|transcription_endpointing_plan|[TranscriptionEndpointingPlan](#schematranscriptionendpointingplan) \| null|false|none|Omit (stay null) when unset: the per-turn wait stays on `wait_seconds`. Setting `null` on an update clears a previously configured plan.|

```json
    "analyze_sentiment": false,
    "partial_automated_agent_reply": false
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_url|string|false|none|The destination WebSocket address where the stream is going to be delivered.|
|stream_track|string|false|none|Specifies which track should be streamed.|
|stream_codec|[StreamCodec](#schemastreamcodec)|false|none|Specifies the codec to be used for the streamed audio. When set to 'default' or when transcoding is not possible, the codec from the call will be used.|
|stream_bidirectional_mode|[StreamBidirectionalMode](#schemastreambidirectionalmode)|false|none|Configures method of bidirectional streaming (mp3, rtp).|
|stream_bidirectional_codec|[StreamBidirectionalCodec](#schemastreambidirectionalcodec)|false|none|Indicates codec for bidirectional streaming RTP payloads. Used only with stream_bidirectional_mode=rtp. Case sensitive.|

Advisory: they steer the summary but never override or deny a profile's own facts, and they do not affect recall. Null or empty means none are set, and summaries use the neutral default. A change reaches each summary the next time it is regenerated.|

```json
  ],
```

```json
}
```

Every field is optional. A change queues a new provisioning run and returns the router with `status` `provisioning`. An empty object retries a `failed` router.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|A user specified name for the router.|
|advertised_routes|[string]|false|none|IPv4 subnets of the Network that the router advertises to the tailnet. Each entry is a canonical CIDR that the Network routes. Default, loopback, link-local, multicast, and Tailscale (`100.64.0.0/10`) ranges are rejected. So are ranges that overlap the router's own, `172.27.254.0/24` and `198.18.0.0/20`.|
|auth_key|string(password)|false|write-only|A replacement Tailscale auth key. Accepted only while the router has never enrolled, for example after a `failed` enrollment. Never returned.|

```json
  "time_limit_secs": 1800,
  "user_idle_timeout_secs": 10,
  "user_idle_reply_secs": 10,
  "fallback_destination": "string",
  "send_message_history_updates": true,
  "conversation_ended_full_history": false,
  "greeting_delay_ms": 0,
  "voicemail_detection": {
    "on_voicemail_detected": {
      "action": "stop_assistant",
      "voicemail_message": {
        "type": "prompt",
        "prompt": "string",
        "message": "string"
      }
    }
  },
  "disable_dtmf": false,
  "recording_settings": {
    "enabled": true,
    "channels": "dual",
    "format": "mp3",
    "stop_on_conversation_end": false
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default_texml_app_id|string|false|none|Default Texml App used for voice calls with your assistant. This will be created automatically on assistant creation.|
|supports_unauthenticated_web_calls|boolean|false|none|When enabled, allows users to interact with your AI assistant directly from your website without requiring authentication. This is required for FE widgets that work with assistants that have telephony enabled.|
|noise_suppression|string|false|none|The noise suppression engine to use. 'aicoustics' is STT-optimized and recommended for AI assistants (configure through noise_suppression_config). Use 'disabled' to turn off noise suppression.|
|noise_suppression_config|object|false|none|Configuration for noise suppression. Applicable fields depend on the engine: 'attenuation_limit' and 'mode' only when noise_suppression is 'deepfilternet'; 'family', 'size' and 'enhancement_level' only when noise_suppression is 'aicoustics'.|
|time_limit_secs|integer|false|none|Maximum duration in seconds for the AI assistant to participate on the call. When this limit is reached the assistant will be stopped. Stopping the assistant does not itself hang up the call, and what happens next depends on how the assistant is running. On Call Control (ai_assistant_start) the call leg stays connected and continues to be billed until it is hung up (for example with the Hangup call command) or until the call ends for another reason. On TeXML, the assistant's `<Connect><AIAssistant>` instruction ends; in the default TeXML setup for assistants no instructions follow it, so the call is hung up. Your application receives a call.conversation.ended webhook when the assistant stops. This limit does not apply to portions of a call without an active assistant (for instance, a call transferred to a human representative).|
|user_idle_timeout_secs|integer|false|none|Maximum duration in seconds of end user silence on the call. When this limit is reached the assistant will be stopped. Stopping the assistant does not itself hang up the call, and what happens next depends on how the assistant is running. On Call Control (ai_assistant_start) the call leg stays connected and continues to be billed until it is hung up (for example with the Hangup call command) or until the call ends for another reason. On TeXML, the assistant's `<Connect><AIAssistant>` instruction ends; in the default TeXML setup for assistants no instructions follow it, so the call is hung up. Your application receives a call.conversation.ended webhook when the assistant stops. This limit does not apply to portions of a call without an active assistant (for instance, a call transferred to a human representative).|
|user_idle_reply_secs|integer|false|none|Duration in seconds of end user silence before the assistant checks in on the user. When this limit is reached the assistant will prompt the user to respond. This is distinct from user_idle_timeout_secs which stops the assistant entirely.|
|fallback_destination|string|false|none|Destination number or SIP URI to transfer the caller to when the AI conversation ends abnormally, for example because of an assistant-side error, so the caller is not left in dead air. This only fires for abnormal ends: it does not fire when the conversation ends on purpose (the caller hung up, the assistant completed normally, the caller hung up after a relay handoff, or voicemail was detected), and it does not fire when the assistant already transferred or bridged the call.|
|send_message_history_updates|boolean|false|none|Whether the assistant sends a `call.ai_gather.message_history_updated` webhook with the full message history every time the conversation history changes. Leave unset to inherit the `send_message_history_updates` value from the `ai_assistant_start` or `gather_using_ai` command that started the conversation. Setting it here is authoritative: `true` turns the webhooks on even when the start command did not request them, and `false` turns them off even when it did. Messages exchanged during a private warm transfer acceptance phase are never included.|
|conversation_ended_full_history|boolean|false|none|When enabled, the `messages` array of the `call.conversation.ended` webhook contains the full conversation history in order: user and assistant turns, assistant tool calls (`tool_calls`), tool results (`role: tool` with `tool_call_id`), and informational `system` and `developer` entries. The assistant's instructions are never included. When disabled, `messages` contains only user and assistant text turns.|
|greeting_delay_ms|integer \| null|false|none|Milliseconds to wait after an inbound call is answered before the assistant starts and speaks its greeting. Increase it if the beginning of the greeting is cut off on some connections (for example, WebRTC calls). When unset (`null`), the platform default of 250 ms is used. Set to `0` to start without a delay. Maximum 2000.|
|voicemail_detection|object|false|none|Configuration for voicemail detection (AMD - Answering Machine Detection) on outgoing calls. These settings only apply if AMD is enabled on the Dial command. See [TeXML Dial documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/texml-rest-commands/initiate-an-outbound-call) for enabling AMD. Recommended settings: MachineDetection=Enable, AsyncAmd=true, DetectionMode=Premium.|
|disable_dtmf|boolean|false|none|Disable inbound DTMF for the entire call. Must be set to true if a 'pay' tool is configured anywhere on the assistant — on the main tool array or on any workflow node — enforced at write time.|
|recording_settings|object|false|none|Configuration for call recording format and channel settings.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|noise_suppression|aicoustics|
|noise_suppression|krisp|
|noise_suppression|deepfilternet|
|noise_suppression|disabled|

```json
}
```

Upload-based voice clone using the Telnyx Bayan model (Arabic and English). The clone is `active` on creation. Use it as voice `Telnyx.Bayan.<clone_id>`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|audio_file|string(binary)|true|none|Audio file to clone the voice from. Supported formats: WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A. Converted to 24 kHz mono WAV and trimmed to the first 10 seconds. For best quality, provide about 10 seconds of clean, single-speaker speech. Maximum size: 20MB.|
|name|string|true|none|Name for the voice clone.|
|language|string|false|none|Language of the reference audio: `ar` (Arabic) or `en` (English). Defaults to `ar`. Other values return `422`.|
|gender|string|true|none|Gender of the voice clone.|
|ref_text|string|true|none|Exact transcript of the reference audio. Required for Bayan: a missing, empty, or whitespace-only value returns `422` with `source.pointer` `/ref_text`. An inaccurate transcript can make synthesis with the clone truncated or garbled. Record a known script of about 10 seconds and pass it verbatim.|
|label|string|false|none|Optional custom label describing the voice style.|
|model_id|string|true|none|TTS model identifier. Must be `Bayan`.|
|provider|string|false|none|Voice synthesis provider. Defaults to `telnyx`.|

|Property|Value|

|language|ar|
|language|en|
|gender|male|
|gender|female|
|gender|neutral|
|model_id|Bayan|
|provider|telnyx|
|provider|Telnyx|

Campaign is generated by the 10DLC registry once the corresponding campaign request is approved. Each campaign is assigned a unique identifier - **campaignId**. Once a campaign is activated, limited information is published to the NetNumber OSR service for consumption by members of the ecosystem. When a campaign is suspended(reversible) or expired(non-reversible), campaign data is deleted from the OSR service. Most attributes of campaignare immutable, including **usecase**, **vertical**, **brandId** and **cspId**.

<h2 id="tocS_TelnyxProviderParams">TelnyxProviderParams</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematelnyxproviderparams"></a>
<a id="schema_TelnyxProviderParams"></a>
<a id="tocStelnyxproviderparams"></a>
<a id="tocstelnyxproviderparams"></a>

```json
{
  "voice_speed": 1,
  "response_format": "mp3",
  "sampling_rate": 24000,
  "volume": 1,
  "emotion": "neutral"
}
```

Telnyx provider-specific parameters. For the `Ultra` model, use `voice_speed`, `volume`, and `emotion`. `Bayan` and `Sukhan` don't use `temperature`, `volume`, or `emotion`. `Bayan` accepts `voice_speed` from 0.5 to 2.0; `Sukhan` doesn't support it. `Bayan` synthesizes at a native 16 kHz: `sampling_rate` `8000`, `22050`, or `24000` is resampled, needs `response_format: pcm`, and isn't available with `output_type: audio_id`. `Sukhan`'s `response_format` is restricted to `mp3` or `pcm` (no `wav`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice_speed|number(float)|false|none|Voice speed multiplier. Telnyx `Ultra` voices accept values from 0.6 to 1.5 — requests outside that range are rejected by the synthesis engine. `Bayan` accepts values from 0.5 to 2.0. `KokoroTTS` and `Qwen3TTS` accept the field but do not apply it. `Sukhan` doesn't support it.|
|response_format|string|false|none|Audio response format.|
|sampling_rate|integer|false|none|Audio sampling rate in Hz. `Bayan` ignores the default and synthesizes at its native 16 kHz unless `8000`, `22050`, or `24000` is set explicitly with `response_format: pcm`. Resampled rates aren't available with `output_type: audio_id`.|
|volume|number(float)|false|none|Volume level for the Ultra model. Telnyx `Ultra` voices accept values from 0.5 to 2.0 — requests outside that range are rejected by the synthesis engine. `KokoroTTS`, `Qwen3TTS`, `Bayan`, and `Sukhan` voices accept the field but do not apply it.|
|emotion|string|false|none|Emotion control for the Ultra model. Adjusts the emotional tone of the synthesized speech.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|emotion|neutral|
|emotion|happy|
|emotion|sad|
|emotion|angry|
|emotion|fearful|
|emotion|disgusted|
|emotion|surprised|

<h2 id="tocS_TestStatus">TestStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemateststatus"></a>
<a id="schema_TestStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSteststatus"></a>
<a id="tocsteststatus"></a>

```json
"pending"
```

Represents the lifecycle of a test:
  - 'pending': Test is waiting to be executed.
  - 'starting': Test execution is initializing.
  - 'running': Test is currently executing.
  - 'passed': Test completed successfully.
  - 'failed': Test executed but did not pass.
  - 'error': An error occurred during test execution.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`.|

|RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|[TexmlStatusCallbackMethod](#schematexmlstatuscallbackmethod)|false|none|HTTP method used to send status callbacks.|
|RecordingChannels|[TexmlRecordingChannels](#schematexmlrecordingchannels)|false|none|When `dual`, final audio file has the first leg on channel A, and the rest on channel B. `single` mixes both tracks into a single channel.|
|RecordingTrack|[RecordingTrack](#schemarecordingtrack)|false|none|The audio track to record for the call. The default is `both`.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematoolnode"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "position": {
    "x": 0,
    "y": 0
  },
  "shared_tool_id": "string",
  "tool": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "shared": true,
      "function": {
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "parameters": {}
      }
    }
  ],
  "type": "tool",
  "message": "One moment while I process your payment."
}
```

A standalone tool step in a conversation flow, as returned by the API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Caller-supplied unique identifier for this node within the flow.|
|name|string|false|none|Optional human-readable label, displayed in authoring UIs.|
|position|[NodePosition](#schemanodeposition)|false|none|Optional canvas coordinates used by authoring UIs to lay out the graph. Ignored by the runtime; round-trips so frontends can persist graph layout across reloads.|
|shared_tool_id|string|true|none|ID of the single shared (org-level) tool this node executes. When the flow reaches this node the tool runs as a deliberate step (no LLM turn); its outgoing `llm` / `expression` edges route the flow on the tool's outcome. Arguments are filled from the conversation's dynamic variables by name — a dynamic variable whose name matches one of the tool's parameters supplies that argument. Cross-validated against the org's shared tools on write.|
|tool|[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)|false|none|Full tool definition resolved from `shared_tool_id` server-side. Populated on responses so clients can render the node without a follow-up fetch. Ignored on input — set `shared_tool_id`.|
|type|string|false|none|Node kind discriminator. Always `tool` for a tool node.|
|message|string|false|none|Optional message delivered to the user verbatim immediately before the tool executes — an announcement such as 'One moment while I look that up.' No LLM turn and no customer turn: the message is spoken/sent, then the tool runs, in the same deterministic step. `{{variable}}` placeholders are interpolated from the conversation's dynamic variables (unresolved → empty string); the tool's own result is not yet available when the message is rendered. Omit for a silent tool step.|

<h2 id="tocS_ToolNodeReq">ToolNodeReq</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematoolnodereq"></a>
<a id="schema_ToolNodeReq"></a>
<a id="tocStoolnodereq"></a>
<a id="tocstoolnodereq"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "n_charge",
  "message": "One moment while I process your payment.",
  "name": "Charge card",
  "position": {
    "x": 300,
    "y": 200
  },
  "shared_tool_id": "tool-charge-card",
  "type": "tool"
}
```

A standalone tool step in a conversation flow, as supplied by clients.

Unlike a prompt node, a tool node has no instructions or model — it
isn't an LLM turn. Reaching it deterministically runs one shared tool
(arguments filled from matching dynamic variables by name), then routes
via outgoing `llm` / `expression` edges, with exactly one `default`
fallback edge required when the node has any outgoing edges (the
tool's outcome is readable as `telnyx_last_tool_status_code` in
`expression` conditions).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|Caller-supplied unique identifier for this node within the flow.|
|message|string|false|none|Optional message delivered to the user verbatim immediately before the tool executes — an announcement such as 'One moment while I look that up.' No LLM turn and no customer turn: the message is spoken/sent, then the tool runs, in the same deterministic step. `{{variable}}` placeholders are interpolated from the conversation's dynamic variables (unresolved → empty string); the tool's own result is not yet available when the message is rendered. Omit for a silent tool step.|
|name|string|false|none|Optional human-readable label, displayed in authoring UIs.|
|position|[NodePosition](#schemanodeposition)|false|none|Optional canvas coordinates used by authoring UIs to lay out the graph. Ignored by the runtime; round-trips so frontends can persist graph layout across reloads.|
|shared_tool_id|string|true|none|ID of the single shared (org-level) tool this node executes. When the flow reaches this node the tool runs as a deliberate step (no LLM turn); its outgoing `llm` / `expression` edges route the flow on the tool's outcome. Arguments are filled from the conversation's dynamic variables by name — a dynamic variable whose name matches one of the tool's parameters supplies that argument. Cross-validated against the org's shared tools on write.|
|type|string|false|none|Node kind discriminator. Always `tool` for a tool node.|

<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptionChallenger">TranscriptionChallenger</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematranscriptionchallenger"></a>
<a id="schema_TranscriptionChallenger"></a>
<a id="tocStranscriptionchallenger"></a>
<a id="tocstranscriptionchallenger"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "deepgram/nova-3",
  "language": "en",
  "rule": "best_turn"
}
```

A second speech-to-text model that transcribes alongside `transcription.model`, and the rule that decides which transcript the assistant uses.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|The language booster's model. It must be the same kind of model as `transcription.model`: both streaming (`deepgram/flux`, `deepgram/nova-3`, `deepgram/nova-2`, `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` or its legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming`, `xai/grok-stt`, `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `humain/realtime`, `reson8/turns`) or both non-streaming (`azure/fast`, `nvidia/parakeet-v3`, `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1`, `cohere/ar-stt`, `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2`, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, `telnyx/basira`). It can be the same model as `transcription.model` on a different `language`.|
|language|string \| null|false|none|The language this model transcribes. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the language of `transcription.model`. The request is rejected when this model doesn't support the language it would run. It is also rejected when it would run the same model on the same language as `transcription.model`.|
|settings|[TranscriptionSettingsConfig](#schematranscriptionsettingsconfig) \| null|false|none|Settings for the language booster, with the same fields and limits as `transcription.settings`. Fields that don't apply to this model's provider are dropped, and the provider's defaults fill in the rest. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the settings of `transcription.model` where they apply to this model.|
|rule|string|false|none|How the assistant picks the transcript it uses. The models are compared on how complete and confident their transcripts are, not on language, so the rules work best when both models understand the callers' language.<br><br>- `best_turn` (default): both models transcribe the whole call. Each turn uses the language booster's transcript only when it scores higher than the transcript of `transcription.model` (clearly higher with non-streaming models). With streaming models, `transcription.model` also decides when each turn ends. Available for every pair.<br>- `best_engine`: both models transcribe the first turns, then the call continues alone on the model whose transcripts scored higher. If neither clearly leads, `transcription.model` continues. Streaming models only.<br>- `merge_words`: both models transcribe each utterance and their words are merged, keeping Arabic and English spoken in the same sentence. Available only for `telnyx/basira` with `cohere/ar-stt`, in either order. The pair runs on the language that applies to `telnyx/basira` (its own, or that of `transcription.model`), which must be Arabic (`ar` or an `ar-` locale), `multi`, or `auto`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|model|deepgram/flux|
|model|deepgram/nova-3|
|model|deepgram/nova-2|
|model|azure/fast|
|model|assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro|
|model|assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro|
|model|assemblyai/universal-streaming|
|model|xai/grok-stt|
|model|soniox/stt-rt-v4|
|model|soniox/stt-rt-v5|
|model|nvidia/parakeet-v3|
|model|omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1|
|model|humain/realtime|
|model|reson8/turns|
|model|cohere/ar-stt|
|model|telnyx/basira|
|model|distil-whisper/distil-large-v2|
|model|openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo|
|rule|best_turn|
|rule|best_engine|

<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptionConfig">TranscriptionConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematranscriptionconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_TranscriptionConfig"></a>
<a id="tocStranscriptionconfig"></a>
<a id="tocstranscriptionconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "distil-whisper/distil-large-v2",
  "language": "string"
}
```

The settings associated with speech to text for the voice assistant. This is only relevant if the assistant uses a text-to-text language model. Any assistant using a model with native audio support (e.g. `fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_4`) will ignore this field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|false|none|The speech to text model to be used by the voice assistant. Supported models include:<br><br>- `deepgram/flux` (or `flux`) for live streaming turn-taking.<br>- `deepgram/nova-3` and `deepgram/nova-2` for live streaming transcription.<br>- `speechmatics/standard` and `speechmatics/enhanced` for live streaming transcription.<br>- `speechmatics/linden-1` (preview, vendor-hosted) for live streaming transcription; no auto-detect, so set `language` from Speechmatics' Realtime language list (defaults to `en`).<br>- `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` (AssemblyAI Universal-3.6 Pro) for live streaming transcription. The legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming` are still accepted and run the same Universal-3.6 Pro model.<br>- `xai/grok-stt` for live streaming transcription.<br>- `soniox/stt-rt-v4` for live streaming multilingual transcription with automatic language detection.<br>- `nvidia/parakeet-v3` for multilingual transcription with automatic language detection.<br>- `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1` for English-only medical transcription (Parakeet-based).<br>- `humain/realtime` for live streaming transcription with native Arabic and Arabic/English code-switching support.<br>- `reson8/turns` for live streaming turn-based transcription of 10 European languages with automatic language detection.<br>- `cohere/ar-stt` for non-streaming Arabic and English transcription.<br>- `azure/fast` and `azure/realtime`; Azure models require `region`, and unsupported regions require `api_key_ref`.<br>- `google/latest_long` for non-streaming multilingual transcription.<br>- `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2` for lower-latency English-only non-streaming transcription.<br>- `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` for multilingual non-streaming transcription with automatic language detection.|
|language|string|false|none|The language of the audio to be transcribed. If not set, or if set to `auto`, supported models will automatically detect the language. Supported and meaningful values depend on the selected transcription `model`. For `deepgram/flux`, supported values are: `auto` (Telnyx language detection controls the language hint), `multi` (no language hint), and language-specific hints `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, `hi`, `ru`, `pt`, `ja`, `it`, and `nl`. For `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `auto` omits the language hint and lets Soniox auto-detect; ISO 639-1 codes (e.g. `en`, `es`) bias detection toward that language. For `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` (and its legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming`), `auto` (or unset) enables native multilingual code-switching; language codes (`en`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `pt`, `it`, `tr`, `nl`, `sv`, `no`, `da`, `fi`, `hi`, `vi`, `ar`, `he`, `ja`, `zh`, `ur`, `ru`, `ko`, `ca`, `gl`, `ro`, `et`, `fa`, `yue`, `af`, `mr`, `zu`, `xh`, `nn`) bias the session to that language. For `humain/realtime`, supported values are `ar`, `en`, `codeswitch` (Arabic/English code-switching), and `auto` (resolves server-side to code-switching). Unlike other models, `humain/realtime` does not fall back to `auto` when `language` is omitted — omitting it applies `en` instead. For `reson8/turns`, supported values are `auto` (or unset) for automatic language detection, and the language codes `nl`, `en`, `fr`, `fy`, `de`, `it`, `pl`, `pt`, `es`, and `sv` to fix the transcription language. For `cohere/ar-stt`, supported values are `ar` and `en`; unlike other models, this model does not auto-detect and defaults to `ar` when `language` is omitted. For `speechmatics/linden-1`, there is no auto-detect; set a code from Speechmatics' Realtime language list (see `SpeechmaticsTranscriptionLanguage`); unset defaults to `en`, while an explicit `auto`, `auto_beta`, or `multi` is rejected (unlike `speechmatics/standard`, which defaults to `en`).|

<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptionEndpointingPlan">TranscriptionEndpointingPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematranscriptionendpointingplan"></a>
<a id="schema_TranscriptionEndpointingPlan"></a>
<a id="tocStranscriptionendpointingplan"></a>
<a id="tocstranscriptionendpointingplan"></a>

```json
{
  "on_punctuation_seconds": 0.1,
  "on_no_punctuation_seconds": 1.5,
  "on_number_seconds": 0.5
}
```

Endpointing thresholds used to decide when the user has finished speaking. Applies to non turn-taking transcription models. For `deepgram/flux`, use `transcription.settings.eot_threshold` / `eot_timeout_ms` / `eager_eot_threshold`. Evaluated per turn, on each caller transcript, only while `start_speaking_plan` is present: the tier whose suffix matches the transcript tail is applied (a transcript with no terminal punctuation or number falls through to `on_no_punctuation_seconds`); with no tiers configured (or a null nested plan), the per-turn wait stays on `start_speaking_plan.wait_seconds`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on_punctuation_seconds|number(float)|false|none|Seconds to wait after the transcript ends with punctuation.|
|on_no_punctuation_seconds|number(float)|false|none|Seconds to wait after the transcript ends without punctuation.|
|on_number_seconds|number(float)|false|none|Seconds to wait after the transcript ends with a number.|

Accepted values depend on the selected `transcription_model`. `speechmatics/standard` supports: `en`, `ba`, `eu`, `gl`, `ga`, `mt`, `mn`, `sw`, `ug`, `cy`, `ar_en`, `cmn_en`, `en_ms`, `en_ta`, `tl`, `es-bilingual-en`, `cmn_en_ms_ta`. `speechmatics/linden-1` (preview) supports the same languages as Speechmatics Realtime: `ar`, `ar_en`, `ba`, `be`, `bg`, `bn`, `ca`, `cmn`, `cmn_en`, `cmn_en_ms_ta`, `cs`, `cy`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en`, `en_ms`, `en_ta`, `eo`, `es`, `es-bilingual-en`, `et`, `eu`, `fa`, `fi`, `fr`, `ga`, `gl`, `he`, `hi`, `hr`, `hu`, `ia`, `id`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `lt`, `lv`, `mn`, `mr`, `ms`, `mt`, `nl`, `no`, `pl`, `pt`, `ro`, `ru`, `sk`, `sl`, `sv`, `sw`, `ta`, `th`, `tl`, `tr`, `ug`, `uk`, `ur`, `vi`, `yue`, plus the spelling and script variants `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-AU`, `cmn-Hans`, and `cmn-Hant` (`en` alone uses the default spelling). A value outside the selected model's list is rejected. A streaming speech-to-text model that takes over transcription when the model in use fails.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|The fallback model. It must be a streaming model other than `transcription.model` and the other fallbacks: `deepgram/flux`, `deepgram/nova-3`, `deepgram/nova-2`, `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` (or its legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming`), `xai/grok-stt`, `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `humain/realtime`, or `reson8/turns`.|
|language|string \| null|false|none|The language the fallback transcribes. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the language of `transcription.model`. The request is rejected when the fallback model doesn't support the language it would run.|
|settings|[TranscriptionSettingsConfig](#schematranscriptionsettingsconfig) \| null|false|none|Settings for the fallback, with the same fields and limits as `transcription.settings`. Fields that don't apply to this model's provider are dropped, and the provider's defaults fill in the rest. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the settings of `transcription.model` where they apply to this model.|
