<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptionSettings">TranscriptionSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematranscriptionsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_TranscriptionSettings"></a>
<a id="tocStranscriptionsettings"></a>
<a id="tocstranscriptionsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "deepgram/flux",
  "language": "string",
  "api_key_ref": "string",
  "region": "string",
  "settings": {
    "smart_format": true,
    "numerals": true,
    "eot_threshold": 0.8,
    "eot_timeout_ms": 5000,
    "eager_eot_threshold": 0.8,
    "keyterm": "string",
    "remove_disfluencies": false,
    "end_of_turn_confidence_threshold": 0,
    "prompt": "string",
    "min_turn_silence": 400,
    "max_turn_silence": 1280,
    "interim_results": false,
    "enable_endpoint_detection": false,
    "max_endpoint_delay_ms": 500,
    "context": "string",
    "language_hints": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "fallback_models": [
    {
      "model": "deepgram/nova-3",
      "language": "en"
    },
    {
      "model": "soniox/stt-rt-v5",
      "settings": {
        "context": "Telnyx,VoIP,SIP"
      }
    }
  ],
  "challenger": {
    "model": "deepgram/nova-3",
    "language": "en",
    "rule": "best_turn"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|false|none|The speech to text model to be used by the voice assistant. All Deepgram models are run on-premise.<br><br>- `deepgram/flux` is optimized for turn-taking with multilingual language hints.<br>- `deepgram/nova-3` is multilingual with automatic language detection.<br>- `deepgram/nova-2` is Deepgram's previous-generation multilingual model.<br>- `speechmatics/standard` is a Speechmatics model self-hosted by Telnyx; it supports a fixed set of language packs (including bilingual packs such as `ar_en`) and defaults to `en`.<br>- `speechmatics/linden-1` (preview) is a vendor-hosted streaming model with no auto-detect; set `language` from Speechmatics' Realtime language list (defaults to `en`).<br>- `azure/fast` is a multilingual Azure transcription model.<br>- `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` (AssemblyAI Universal-3.6 Pro) is a multilingual streaming model with configurable turn detection. The legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming` are still accepted and run the same model.<br>- `xai/grok-stt` is a multilingual Grok STT model.<br>- `soniox/stt-rt-v4` and `soniox/stt-rt-v5` are multilingual streaming models with automatic language detection, configurable endpointing, term biasing (`context`), and `language_hints`.<br>- `nvidia/parakeet-v3` is a multilingual transcription model with automatic language detection.<br>- `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1` is an English-only medical transcription model (Parakeet-based).<br>- `humain/realtime` is a streaming model with native Arabic and Arabic/English code-switching support.<br>- `reson8/turns` is a turn-based streaming model covering 10 European languages with automatic language detection.<br>- `cohere/ar-stt` is a non-streaming Arabic and English transcription model.<br>- `telnyx/basira` is a non-streaming Arabic transcription model.|
|language|string|false|none|The language of the audio to be transcribed. If not set, or if set to `auto`, supported models will automatically detect the language. For `deepgram/flux`, supported values are: `auto` (Telnyx language detection controls the language hint), `multi` (no language hint), and language-specific hints `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, `hi`, `ru`, `pt`, `ja`, `it`, and `nl`. For `soniox/stt-rt-v4` and `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `auto` omits the language hint and lets Soniox auto-detect; ISO 639-1 codes (e.g. `en`, `es`) bias detection toward that language; `settings.language_hints` can pin multiple languages at once instead. For `humain/realtime`, supported values are `ar`, `en`, `codeswitch` (Arabic/English code-switching), and `auto` (resolves server-side to code-switching). Unlike other models, `humain/realtime` does not fall back to `auto` when `language` is omitted — omitting it applies `en` instead. For `reson8/turns`, supported values are `auto` (or unset) for automatic language detection, and the language codes `nl`, `en`, `fr`, `fy`, `de`, `it`, `pl`, `pt`, `es`, and `sv` to fix the transcription language. For `cohere/ar-stt`, supported values are `ar` and `en`; unlike other models, this model does not auto-detect and defaults to `ar` when `language` is omitted. For `speechmatics/linden-1`, there is no auto-detect; set a code from Speechmatics' Realtime language list (67 language codes, including `es-bilingual-en` for Spanish and English bilingual, and the spelling and script variants `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-AU`, `cmn-Hans`, and `cmn-Hant`; `en` alone uses the default spelling); unset defaults to `en`, while an explicit `auto`, `auto_beta`, or `multi` is rejected with a 400.|
|api_key_ref|string|false|none|Integration secret identifier for the transcription provider API key. Currently used for Azure transcription regions that require a customer-provided API key.|
|region|string|false|none|Region on third party cloud providers (currently Azure) if using one of their models. Some regions require `api_key_ref`.|
|settings|[TranscriptionSettingsConfig](#schematranscriptionsettingsconfig)|false|none|none|
|fallback_models|[[TranscriptionFallbackModel](#schematranscriptionfallbackmodel)]|false|none|Up to 3 streaming models that take over transcription, in this order, when the model in use fails, at the start of a call or mid-call. `model` must be a streaming model too, and must support `language` alongside other models. On update, a list replaces the stored one: omit the field to keep the stored list, or send `null` or `[]` to remove it. When an update changes `model` or `language`, stored fallbacks that no longer fit are removed without an error. Can't be combined with `challenger`, the language booster; to replace a stored language booster, send `challenger: null` in the same request.|
|challenger|[TranscriptionChallenger](#schematranscriptionchallenger) \| null|false|none|The language booster: a second model that transcribes alongside `model`, and the rule that decides which transcript the assistant uses. Both models must be streaming, or both non-streaming, and, except with `merge_words`, `model` must support `language` alongside another model (for example, `cohere/ar-stt` supports only `ar` there). If the language booster can't run, the call runs on `model` alone; if either model fails mid-call, the call continues on the other. On update, omit the field to keep the stored language booster, or send `null` to remove it. When an update changes `model` or `language` and the stored language booster no longer fits, it is removed without an error. Can't be combined with `fallback_models`; to replace stored fallbacks, send `fallback_models: []` in the same request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|model|deepgram/flux|
|model|deepgram/nova-3|
|model|deepgram/nova-2|
|model|speechmatics/standard|
|model|speechmatics/linden-1|
|model|azure/fast|
|model|assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro|
|model|assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro|
|model|assemblyai/universal-streaming|
|model|xai/grok-stt|
|model|soniox/stt-rt-v4|
|model|soniox/stt-rt-v5|
|model|nvidia/parakeet-v3|
|model|omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1|
|model|humain/realtime|
|model|reson8/turns|
|model|cohere/ar-stt|
|model|telnyx/basira|
|model|distil-whisper/distil-large-v2|
|model|openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo|

<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptionSettingsConfig">TranscriptionSettingsConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematranscriptionsettingsconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_TranscriptionSettingsConfig"></a>
<a id="tocStranscriptionsettingsconfig"></a>
<a id="tocstranscriptionsettingsconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "smart_format": true,
  "numerals": true,
  "eot_threshold": 0.8,
  "eot_timeout_ms": 5000,
  "eager_eot_threshold": 0.8,
  "keyterm": "string",
  "remove_disfluencies": false,
  "end_of_turn_confidence_threshold": 0,
  "prompt": "string",
  "min_turn_silence": 400,
  "max_turn_silence": 1280,
  "interim_results": false,
  "enable_endpoint_detection": false,
  "max_endpoint_delay_ms": 500,
  "context": "string",
  "language_hints": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|smart_format|boolean|false|none|none|
|numerals|boolean|false|none|none|
|eot_threshold|number|false|none|Available only for deepgram/flux. Confidence required to trigger an end of turn. Higher values = more reliable turn detection but slightly increased latency.|
|eot_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|Available only for deepgram/flux. Maximum milliseconds of silence before forcing an end of turn, regardless of confidence.|
|eager_eot_threshold|number|false|none|Available only for deepgram/flux. Confidence threshold for eager end of turn detection. Must be lower than or equal to eot_threshold. Setting this equal to eot_threshold effectively disables eager end of turn.|
|keyterm|string|false|none|A comma-separated list of key terms to boost for recognition during transcription, used by Deepgram, Reson8, Speechmatics Linden 1 and AssemblyAI models. Helps improve accuracy for domain-specific terminology, proper nouns, or uncommon words. At most 1000 characters in total. For assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming), also at most 100 terms of up to 50 characters each. This field may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) using mustache syntax (e.g. `Telnyx,{{customer_name}},VoIP`). Variables are resolved at call time before the value is sent to the speech-to-text engine.|
|remove_disfluencies|boolean|false|none|Available only for speechmatics/linden-1. When true, filler words such as "um" and "uh" are removed from the transcript. Disfluency removal is supported only for `ar`, `cmn`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `he`, `hi`, `hu`, `it`, `ja`, `nl`, `pl`, `pt`, and `ru`, determined by the base language (so `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-AU`, `cmn-Hans`, and `cmn-Hant` are supported); for other languages, filler words remain in the transcript.|
|end_of_turn_confidence_threshold|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated and ignored. Accepted for backwards compatibility. AssemblyAI turn detection is configured with min_turn_silence and max_turn_silence.|
|prompt|string|false|none|Available only for assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming). Context about the conversation (domain, names, terms) to improve transcription; describe the content, do not give instructions. Leave empty unless needed. At most 1750 characters.|
|min_turn_silence|integer|false|none|Available only for assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming). Minimum duration of silence in milliseconds before a turn can end. Must be less than or equal to max_turn_silence.|
|max_turn_silence|integer|false|none|Available only for assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming). Maximum duration of silence in milliseconds before forcing an end of turn.|
|interim_results|boolean|false|none|Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. When true, Soniox streams interim (non-final) results in addition to finalized transcripts.|
|enable_endpoint_detection|boolean|false|none|Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. When true, Soniox emits end-of-utterance events at the cadence configured by `max_endpoint_delay_ms`.|
|max_endpoint_delay_ms|integer|false|none|Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. Maximum silence (in milliseconds) before Soniox emits an end-of-utterance event. Only honored when `enable_endpoint_detection` is true.|
|context|string|false|none|Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. A comma-separated list of terms to boost for recognition during transcription, for staff names, building names, or other domain-specific vocabulary. This field may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) using mustache syntax (e.g. `Telnyx,{{customer_name}},VoIP`). Variables are resolved at call time before the value is sent to Soniox.|
|language_hints|[string]|false|none|Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. A list of ISO 639-1 language codes (e.g. `["nl", "fr"]`) to pin recognition to multiple languages at once, overriding the single hint derived from `language`.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferCallRequest">TransferCallRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransfercallrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferCallRequest"></a>
<a id="tocStransfercallrequest"></a>
<a id="tocstransfercallrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "to": "+18005550100 or sip:username@sip.telnyx.com;secure=srtp",
  "from": "+18005550101",
  "from_display_name": "Company Name",
  "audio_url": "http://www.example.com/sounds/greeting.wav",
  "send_digits_on_answer": "wwww200",
  "timeout_secs": 60,
  "time_limit_secs": 60,
  "webhook_url": "https://www.example.com/server-b/",
  "webhook_url_method": "POST",
  "answering_machine_detection": "detect",
  "answering_machine_detection_config": {
    "total_analysis_time_millis": 5000,
    "after_greeting_silence_millis": 1000,
    "between_words_silence_millis": 1000,
    "greeting_duration_millis": 1000,
    "initial_silence_millis": 1000,
    "maximum_number_of_words": 1000,
    "maximum_word_length_millis": 2000,
    "silence_threshold": 512,
    "greeting_total_analysis_time_millis": 50000,
    "greeting_silence_duration_millis": 2000
  },
  "custom_headers": [
    {
      "name": "head_1",
      "value": "val_1"
    },
    {
      "name": "head_2",
      "value": "val_2"
    }
  ],
  "client_state": "aGF2ZSBhIG5pY2UgZGF5ID1d",
  "command_id": "891510ac-f3e4-11e8-af5b-de00688a4901",
  "early_media": true,
  "media_encryption": "SRTP",
  "sip_auth_username": "username",
  "sip_auth_password": "password",
  "sip_headers": [
    {
      "name": "User-to-User",
      "value": "value"
    }
  ],
  "sip_transport_protocol": "TLS"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|to|string|true|none|The DID or SIP URI to dial out to. For SIP URI destinations, append `;secure=true` or `;secure=srtp` to enable SRTP media encryption for that endpoint, or `;secure=dtls` to enable DTLS media encryption for that endpoint. If `media_encryption` is set to `SRTP` or `DTLS`, it takes precedence over any per-endpoint `secure` URI parameter. You may also append a comma followed by DTMF digits (e.g. `+18004247767,200`) to play those digits as DTMF once the transfer destination answers — equivalent to setting `send_digits_on_answer` separately. If both are present, the explicit `send_digits_on_answer` parameter takes precedence.|
|from|string|false|none|The `from` number to be used as the caller id presented to the destination (`to` number). The number should be in +E164 format. This attribute will default to the `to` number of the original call if omitted.|
|diversion|string|false|none|The `to` number of an active inbound call, in +E164 format. Telnyx checks whether there is currently an active inbound call where `to` matches this `diversion` value and `from` matches the `from` number supplied for this request. If such a call exists, the `from` number is treated as verified (since it is already on an active inbound call to you) and can be used as the caller id for this outbound call.|
|from_display_name|string|false|none|The `from_display_name` string to be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`to` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and -_~!.+ special characters. If ommited, the display name will be the same as the number in the `from` field.|
|privacy|string|false|none|Indicates the privacy level to be used for the call. When set to `id`, caller ID information (name and number) will be hidden from the called party. When set to `none` or omitted, caller ID will be shown normally.|
|audio_url|string|false|none|The URL of a file to be played back when the transfer destination answers before bridging the call. The URL can point to either a WAV or MP3 file. media_name and audio_url cannot be used together in one request.|
|send_digits_on_answer|string|false|none|DTMF digits to send automatically after the transfer destination answers. Useful for reaching an extension behind an IVR (e.g. `"200"` to dial extension 200 once the called party picks up). Allowed characters: `0-9`, `A-D`, `w` (0.5s pause), `W` (1s pause), `*`, `#`. Maximum 64 characters. When omitted, no automatic DTMF is sent. May also be supplied inline by appending `,<digits>` to `to` (e.g. `to=+18004247767,200`); if both forms are present, this explicit field takes precedence.|
|early_media|boolean|false|none|If set to false, early media will not be passed to the originating leg.|
|media_name|string|false|none|The media_name of a file to be played back when the transfer destination answers before bridging the call. The media_name must point to a file previously uploaded to api.telnyx.com/v2/media by the same user/organization. The file must either be a WAV or MP3 file.|
|timeout_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the call to be answered by the destination to which it is being transferred. If the timeout is reached before an answer is received, the call will hangup and a `call.hangup` webhook with a `hangup_cause` of `timeout` will be sent. Minimum value is 5 seconds. Maximum value is 600 seconds.|
|time_limit_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|Sets the maximum duration of a Call Control Leg in seconds. If the time limit is reached, the call will hangup and a `call.hangup` webhook with a `hangup_cause` of `time_limit` will be sent. For example, by setting a time limit of 120 seconds, a Call Leg will be automatically terminated two minutes after being answered. The default time limit is 14400 seconds or 4 hours and this is also the maximum allowed call length.|
|park_after_unbridge|string|false|none|Specifies behavior after the bridge ends (i.e. the opposite leg either hangs up or is transferred). If supplied with the value `self`, the current leg will be parked after unbridge. If not set, the default behavior is to hang up the leg.|
|answering_machine_detection|string|false|none|Enables Answering Machine Detection. When a call is answered, Telnyx runs real-time detection to determine if it was picked up by a human or a machine and sends an `call.machine.detection.ended` webhook with the analysis result. If 'greeting_end' or 'detect_words' is used and a 'machine' is detected, you will receive another 'call.machine.greeting.ended' webhook when the answering machine greeting ends with a beep or silence. If `detect_beep` is used, you will only receive 'call.machine.greeting.ended' if a beep is detected. If `answering_machine_detection` is set to `premium_ios_call_screening_detection`, Premium AMD runs with iOS Call Screening support: after an initial `machine` result, Telnyx listens for the iOS call-screening prompt to end or for an Apple Call Screening tone, sends `call.machine.premium.greeting.ended` with `result=prompt_ended` or `call.machine.premium.call_screening.detected` with `result=screening` respectively. When the Apple Call Screening tone is detected, Premium AMD is restarted on the screened call and a `call.machine.premium.detection.ended` webhook with the post-screening classification follows.|
|answering_machine_detection_config|object|false|none|Optional configuration parameters to modify 'answering_machine_detection' performance. Only `total_analysis_time_millis` and `greeting_duration_millis` parameters are applicable when `premium` is selected as answering_machine_detection. `prompt_end_timeout_millis` is additionally applicable when `premium_ios_call_screening_detection` is selected.|
|custom_headers|[[CustomSipHeader](#schemacustomsipheader)]|false|none|Custom headers to be added to the SIP INVITE.|
|client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|target_leg_client_state|string|false|none|Use this field to add state to every subsequent webhook for the new leg. It must be a valid Base-64 encoded string.|
|command_id|string|false|none|Use this field to avoid duplicate commands. Telnyx will ignore any command with the same `command_id` for the same `call_control_id`.|
|media_encryption|string|false|none|Defines whether media should be encrypted on the new call leg. For SIP URI destinations, media encryption can also be requested per endpoint with the `secure` URI parameter: `;secure=true` or `;secure=srtp` enables SRTP, and `;secure=dtls` enables DTLS. This parameter, when set to `SRTP` or `DTLS`, takes precedence over the per-endpoint `secure` value.|
|sip_auth_username|string|false|none|SIP Authentication username used for SIP challenges.|
|sip_auth_password|string|false|none|SIP Authentication password used for SIP challenges.|
|sip_headers|[[SipHeader](#schemasipheader)]|false|none|SIP headers to be added to the SIP INVITE. Currently only User-to-User header is supported.|
|sip_transport_protocol|string|false|none|Defines SIP transport protocol to be used on the call.|
|sound_modifications|[SoundModifications](#schemasoundmodifications)|false|none|Use this field to modify sound effects, for example adjust the pitch.|
|webhook_url|string|false|none|Use this field to override the URL for which Telnyx will send subsequent webhooks to for this call.|
|webhook_url_method|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `webhook_url`.|
|mute_dtmf|string|false|none|When enabled, DTMF tones are not passed to the call participant. The webhooks containing the DTMF information will be sent.|
|record|string|false|none|Start recording automatically after an event. Disabled by default.|
|record_channels|string|false|none|Defines which channel should be recorded ('single' or 'dual') when `record` is specified.|
|record_format|string|false|none|Defines the format of the recording ('wav' or 'mp3') when `record` is specified.|
|record_max_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Defines the maximum length for the recording in seconds when `record` is specified. The minimum value is 0. The maximum value is 43200. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_timeout_secs|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected when `record` is specified. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that call transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|record_track|string|false|none|The audio track to be recorded. Can be either `both`, `inbound` or `outbound`. If only single track is specified (`inbound`, `outbound`), `channels` configuration is ignored and it will be recorded as mono (single channel).|
|record_trim|string|false|none|When set to `trim-silence`, silence will be removed from the beginning and end of the recording.|
|record_custom_file_name|string|false|none|The custom recording file name to be used instead of the default `call_leg_id`. Telnyx will still add a Unix timestamp suffix.|
|sip_region|string|false|none|Defines the SIP region to be used for the call.|
|preferred_codecs|string|false|none|The list of comma-separated codecs in order of preference to be used during the call. The codecs supported are `G722`, `PCMU`, `PCMA`, `G729`, `OPUS`, `VP8`, `H264`, `AMR-WB`.|
|webhook_urls|object|false|none|A map of event types to arrays of webhook URLs. When an event of the specified type occurs, the webhook URLs associated with that event type will be called instead of `webhook_url`. Events not mapped here will use the default `webhook_url`.|
|webhook_urls_method|string|false|none|HTTP request method to invoke `webhook_urls`.|
|webhook_retries_policies|object|false|none|A map of event types to retry policies. Each retry policy contains an array of `retries_ms` specifying the delays between retry attempts in milliseconds. Maximum 5 retries, total delay cannot exceed 60 seconds.|
|route_to_mobile|boolean|false|none|When set to true, routes the call directly to the mobile device associated with the destination Telnyx Mobile number, bypassing Inbound Calls Interception configured in the Telnyx Portal under Mobile Numbers → select the number → Voice → Call Interception. Use this when transferring an intercepted call to the mobile device to prevent the call from being intercepted again. Defaults to false.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|Identifies the resource.|

|name|string|false|none|A user specified name for the tunnel.|
|status|string|false|read-only|`inactive` when no tunnel process is connected, and `healthy` when one or more are. `degraded` (Preview, not reported yet) when a process is connected but fails to reach its destinations.|

|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was created.|

A UAC (User Agent Client) Connection registers Telnyx to your PBX — the opposite of a standard SIP trunk, where the PBX registers to Telnyx. Use UAC when your PBX doesn’t support outbound SIP registration or you need Telnyx to maintain the registration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Identifies the type of resource.|
|record_type|string|false|none|Identifies the type of the resource.|
|active|boolean|false|none|Defaults to true|
|user_name|string|false|none|The user name to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 4-32 characters long and alphanumeric values only (no spaces or special characters). At least one of the first 5 characters must be a letter.|
|password|string|false|none|The password to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 8 to 128 characters long. For primary accounts created on or after September 8, 2026, this password is returned as `********`. The password is returned in full on create, and on update only when that update changed the password. Accounts created before September 8, 2026 are unaffected.|
|created_at|string|false|none|ISO-8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was created.|
|updated_at|string|false|none|ISO-8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was updated.|
|anchorsite_override|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|none|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|string|false|none|none|
|sip_uri_calling_preference|string|false|none|This feature enables inbound SIP URI calls to your Credential Auth Connection. If enabled for all (unrestricted) then anyone who calls the SIP URI <your-username>@telnyx.com will be connected to your Connection. You can also choose to allow only calls that are originated on any Connections under your account (internal).|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Defaults to false and returns the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|ios_push_credential_id|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|android_push_credential_id|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|inbound|[UacInbound](#schemauacinbound)|false|none|none|
|outbound|[UacOutbound](#schemauacoutbound)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|
|authentication|string|false|none|The authentication strategy used by this connection.|
|registration_status|string \| null|false|none|The most recently known SIP registration status for this UAC connection.|
|registration_status_updated_at|string \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the registration status was last updated.|
|fqdn|string|false|none|The Telnyx-managed FQDN generated for the UAC connection.|
|fqdns|[[Fqdn](#schemafqdn)]|false|none|FQDN records managed automatically by the UAC connection lifecycle.|
|fqdn_outbound_authentication|string|false|none|The fixed outbound authentication mode used by UAC FQDN records.|
|internal_uac_settings|[UacInternalSettings](#schemauacinternalsettings)|false|none|Internal Telnyx-side settings for a UAC connection.|
|external_uac_settings|[UacExternalSettings](#schemauacexternalsettings)|false|none|External SIP peer settings used by Telnyx when registering to your PBX and routing outbound calls.|

```json
{

  "proxy": "sip-pbx.acme.example",
  "auth_username": "auth8492",
  "from_user": "8492",
  "outbound_proxy": "outbound.sip-pbx.acme.example:5061",
  "expiration_sec": 600,
  "transport": "TLS",
  "user_agent": "Telnyx-Usage-Voice-Trunk/1.0"
}
```

External SIP peer settings used by Telnyx when registering to your PBX and routing outbound calls.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|string|false|none|The SIP username used to authenticate with the external SIP peer for registrations and outbound calls. Must start with a letter or number and contain only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.|
|password|string|false|none|The SIP password used for digest authentication with the external SIP peer. For primary accounts created on or after September 8, 2026, this password is returned as `********`. The password is returned in full on create, and on update only when that update changed the password. Accounts created before September 8, 2026 are unaffected.|
|proxy|string|false|none|The SIP proxy address of the external SIP peer used for registrations and outbound call routing.|
|auth_username|string \| null|false|none|The authentication username used in SIP digest authentication. If not set, the Username value will be used.|
|from_user|string \| null|false|none|The user portion of the SIP From header used in outbound requests. This controls the caller identity presented to the external SIP peer.|
|outbound_proxy|string \| null|false|none|An optional SIP proxy used to route outbound requests before reaching the external SIP peer.|
|expiration_sec|integer \| null|false|none|The registration interval, in seconds, indicating how often the system refreshes the SIP registration with the external SIP peer.|
|transport|string \| null|false|none|The transport protocol used for SIP signaling when communicating with the external SIP peer. One of UDP, TLS, or TCP.|
|user_agent|string \| null|false|none|Custom SIP User-Agent header value that Telnyx uses on outbound REGISTER and INVITE messages. Set to null to use Telnyx's default User-Agent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|transport|UDP|
|transport|TLS|
|transport|TCP|
|transport|null|

|codecs|[string]|false|none|Defines the list of codecs that Telnyx will send for inbound calls to a specific number on your portal account, in priority order. |default_routing_method|string|false|none|Default routing method to be used when a number is associated with the connection. Must be one of the routing method types or left blank, other values are not allowed.|

|generate_ringback_tone|boolean|false|none|Generate ringback tone through 183 session progress message with early media.|
|isup_headers_enabled|boolean|false|none|When set, inbound phone calls will receive ISUP parameters via SIP headers. (Only when available and only when using TCP or TLS transport.)|
|prack_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable PRACK messages as defined in RFC3262.|
|sip_compact_headers_enabled|boolean|false|none|Defaults to true.|

|timeout_2xx_secs|integer|false|none|Time(sec) before aborting if call is unanswered (min: 1, max: 600).|
|shaken_stir_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled the SIP Connection will receive the Identity header with Shaken/Stir data in the SIP INVITE message of inbound calls, even when using UDP transport.|
|simultaneous_ringing|string|false|none|When enabled, allows multiple devices to ring simultaneously on incoming calls.|
|sip_subdomain|string|false|none|The Telnyx-generated SIP subdomain for this UAC connection.|
|sip_subdomain_receive_settings|string|false|none|Controls which SIP URI callers may reach this connection.|

```json
{
  "call_parking_enabled": true,
  "ani_override": "always",
  "channel_limit": 10,
  "instant_ringback_enabled": true,
  "generate_ringback_tone": true,
  "localization": "US",
  "t38_reinvite_source": "customer",
  "outbound_voice_profile_id": "1293384261075731499"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_parking_enabled|boolean \| null|false|none|Forces all SIP calls originated on this connection to be "parked" instead of "bridged" to the destination specified on the URI. Parked calls will return ringback to the caller and will await for a Call Control command to define which action will be taken next.|
|ani_override|string|false|none|Set a phone number as the ani_override value to override caller id number on outbound calls.|
|ani_override_type|string|false|none|Specifies when we apply your ani_override setting. Only applies when ani_override is not blank.|
|channel_limit|integer|false|none|When set, this will limit the total number of outbound calls to phone numbers associated with this connection.|
|instant_ringback_enabled|boolean|false|none|When set, ringback will not wait for indication before sending ringback tone to calling party.|
|generate_ringback_tone|boolean|false|none|Generate ringback tone through 183 session progress message with early media.|
|localization|string|false|none|A 2-character country code specifying the country whose national dialing rules should be used. For example, if set to `US` then any US number can be dialed without preprending +1 to the number. When left blank, Telnyx will try US and GB dialing rules, in that order, by default.|
|t38_reinvite_source|string|false|none|This setting only affects connections with Fax-type Outbound Voice Profiles. The setting dictates whether or not Telnyx sends a t.38 reinvite.<br/><br/> By default, Telnyx will send the re-invite. If set to `customer`, the caller is expected to send the t.38 reinvite.|
|outbound_voice_profile_id|[connections_OutboundVoiceProfileId](#schemaconnections_outboundvoiceprofileid)|false|none|Identifies the associated outbound voice profile.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|ani_override_type|always|
|ani_override_type|normal|
|ani_override_type|emergency|
|t38_reinvite_source|telnyx|
|t38_reinvite_source|customer|
|t38_reinvite_source|disabled|
|t38_reinvite_source|passthru|
|t38_reinvite_source|caller-passthru|
|t38_reinvite_source|callee-passthru|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|model|string|false|none|ID of the model to use when `external_llm` is not set. You can use the [Get models API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/openai-chat/get-available-models-openai-compatible) to see available models. If `external_llm` is provided, the assistant uses `external_llm` instead of this field. If neither `model` nor `external_llm` is provided, Telnyx applies the default model.|
|instructions|string|false|none|System instructions for the assistant. These may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables)|
|tools|[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)|false|none|Deprecated for new integrations. Inline tool definitions available to the assistant. Prefer `tool_ids` to attach shared tools created with the AI Tools endpoints. On update, a sent `tools` array fully replaces the assistant's inline tools; omit the field to leave the inline tools unchanged. Each tool type except `function`, `webhook`, and `client_side_tool` allows at most one instance per assistant, counted across inline `tools` and shared `tool_ids` combined — sending a duplicate of such a type returns HTTP 400 with error code 10015. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; when updating, omit those tools from the `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead.|
|mcp_servers|[[AssistantMCPServer](#schemaassistantmcpserver)]|false|none|MCP servers attached to the assistant. Create MCP servers with `/ai/mcp_servers`, then reference them by `id` here.|
|a2a_agents|[[AssistantA2AAgent](#schemaassistanta2aagent)]|false|none|A2A agents this assistant can delegate to. Tools are not stored here: at the start of every conversation each agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises, named `a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`. The following limits are not enforced when the assistant is saved, and anything past them is dropped when the conversation starts: 64 agents per assistant, 64 skills per card, 128 derived tools per assistant, and a 6 second budget for all card fetches combined. An agent whose card cannot be fetched costs the assistant that capability for the conversation; it does not fail the call. Omit this field to leave the assistant's agents unchanged; send an empty array to remove them all.|

```json
  "name": "string",
```

```json
  "telnyx_conversation_channel": "phone_call",
  "destination": "string",
  "max_duration_seconds": 1,
  "test_suite": "string",

    {
      "name": "string",

    }
```

Request model for updating an existing assistant test.

All fields are optional, allowing partial updates of test configuration.
Only provided fields will be updated, others remain unchanged.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Updated name for the assistant test. Must be unique and descriptive.|
|description|string|false|none|Updated description of the test's purpose and evaluation criteria.|
|telnyx_conversation_channel|[TelnyxConversationChannel](#schematelnyxconversationchannel)|false|none|Updated communication channel for the test execution.|
|destination|string|false|none|Updated target destination for test conversations.|
|max_duration_seconds|integer|false|none|Updated maximum test duration in seconds.|
|test_suite|string|false|none|Updated test suite assignment for better organization.|
|instructions|string|false|none|Updated test scenario instructions and objectives.|
|rubric|[object]|false|none|Updated evaluation criteria for assessing assistant performance.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|active|boolean|false|none|Defaults to true|
|conversation_persistence|boolean|false|none|Whether conversation persistence is enabled for this connection. When enabled, calls handled by the connection are transcribed, stored, and indexed. Defaults to false.|
|user_name|string|false|none|The user name to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 4-32 characters long and alphanumeric values only (no spaces or special characters).|
|password|string|false|none|The password to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 8 to 128 characters long.|
|anchorsite_override|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|none|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|[ConnectionName](#schemaconnectionname)|false|none|A user-assigned name to help manage the connection.|
|sip_uri_calling_preference|string|false|none|This feature enables inbound SIP URI calls to your Credential Auth Connection. If enabled for all (unrestricted) then anyone who calls the SIP URI <your-username>@telnyx.com will be connected to your Connection. You can also choose to allow only calls that are originated on any Connections under your account (internal).|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; omitting this field preserves the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|ios_push_credential_id|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|android_push_credential_id|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|inbound|[CredentialInbound](#schemacredentialinbound)|false|none|none|
|outbound|[CredentialOutbound](#schemacredentialoutbound)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

#### Enumerated Values

<h2 id="tocS_UpdateDynamicVariablesTool">UpdateDynamicVariablesTool</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaupdatedynamicvariablestool"></a>
<a id="schema_UpdateDynamicVariablesTool"></a>
<a id="tocSupdatedynamicvariablestool"></a>
<a id="tocsupdatedynamicvariablestool"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "update_dynamic_variables",
  "shared": true,
  "update_dynamic_variables": {
    "name": "collect_details",
    "description": "Collect caller details into conversation variables.",
    "updatable_variables": [
      {
        "name": "customer_name",
        "type": "string",
        "description": "The caller's full name."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The update_dynamic_variables tool lets the assistant write values into the conversation's dynamic-variables context during the call. Updated variables are available to later `{{variable}}` interpolation (prompts, speak nodes, message templates) and to flow edge conditions. Declare each variable the assistant is allowed to set under `updatable_variables`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|shared|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this tool comes from the shared Tools Library. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. Read-only: set by the server, not accepted in requests. When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).|
|update_dynamic_variables|[UpdateDynamicVariablesToolParams](#schemaupdatedynamicvariablestoolparams)|true|none|Configuration for an update_dynamic_variables tool.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|update_dynamic_variables|

<a id="schemaupdatedynamicvariablestoolparams"></a>
<a id="schema_UpdateDynamicVariablesToolParams"></a>
<a id="tocSupdatedynamicvariablestoolparams"></a>
<a id="tocsupdatedynamicvariablestoolparams"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "collect_details",
  "description": "Collect caller details into conversation variables.",
  "updatable_variables": [
    {
      "name": "customer_name",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The caller's full name."
    }
  ]
}
```

Configuration for an update_dynamic_variables tool.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The function name surfaced to the LLM. Must match the OpenAI function-name pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` and be unique across the assistant's function, webhook, and client_side tools.|
|description|string|true|none|Description of the tool passed to the assistant, guiding when to call it and which variables to update.|
|updatable_variables|[object]|true|none|The dynamic variables the assistant is allowed to write. At least one is required.|

|text_body|string \| null|false|none|Liquid template text body.|

Setting `automatic` re-extracts immediately from the effective subject, HTML body, and text body and rejects a simultaneous non-null array. Setting `explicit` requires the exact non-null array, including valid `[]`. With the mode omitted, a non-null array selects explicit mode, null selects automatic mode, and omitting both fields preserves the current mode. Source-content changes re-extract only in automatic mode.|

|autoescape|boolean|false|none|Per-template HTML autoescaping setting.|
|variable_schema|object \| null|false|none|Structured variable requirements. Required variables cannot define defaults; invalid combinations return 422. Set to `null` to clear the schema.|

|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions.   }
```json
}
```

|config|[GenericPayConnectorConfig](#schemagenericpayconnectorconfig)|false|none|Configuration for a generic connector. A config update replaces the complete object, not individual keys. Unknown config keys are discarded. Authentication credentials must be nonblank strings when required by the selected auth_type.|

|type|generic|
|mode|test|
|mode|live|

Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|string|false|none|none|
|transport_protocol|string|false|none|One of UDP, TLS, or TCP. Applies only to connections with IP authentication or FQDN authentication.|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; omitting this field preserves the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|

|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|

|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|inbound|[InboundIp](#schemainboundip)|false|none|none|
|outbound|[OutboundIp](#schemaoutboundip)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|

```json
{
```

```json
  "active": false,

  "dtmf_type": "Inband",
  "first_command_timeout": true,
  "first_command_timeout_secs": 10,
  "voice_url": "https://example.com",
  "voice_fallback_url": "https://fallback.example.com",
  "call_cost_in_webhooks": false,
  "voice_method": "get",
  "status_callback": "https://example.com",
  "status_callback_method": "get",
  "tags": [
    "tag1",
    "tag2"
  ],
  "inbound": {
    "channel_limit": 10,
    "shaken_stir_enabled": true,
    "sip_subdomain": "example",
    "sip_subdomain_receive_settings": "only_my_connections"
  },
  "outbound": {
    "channel_limit": 10,
    "outbound_voice_profile_id": "1293384261075731499"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|friendly_name|[ApplicationName](#schemaapplicationname)|true|none|A user-assigned name to help manage the application.|
|active|[ConnectionActive](#schemaconnectionactive)|false|none|Specifies whether the connection can be used.|
|anchorsite_override|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|none|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|first_command_timeout|[FirstCommandTimeout](#schemafirstcommandtimeout)|false|none|Specifies whether calls to phone numbers associated with this connection should hangup after timing out.|
|first_command_timeout_secs|[FirstCommandTimeoutSecs](#schemafirstcommandtimeoutsecs)|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a dial command.|
|voice_url|string(uri)|true|none|URL to which Telnyx will deliver your XML Translator webhooks.|
|voice_fallback_url|string(uri)|false|none|URL to which Telnyx will deliver your XML Translator webhooks if we get an error response from your voice_url.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this TeXML Application.|
|voice_method|string|false|none|HTTP request method Telnyx will use to interact with your XML Translator webhooks. Either 'get' or 'post'.|
|status_callback|string(uri)|false|none|URL for Telnyx to send requests to containing information about call progress events.|
|status_callback_method|string|false|none|HTTP request method Telnyx should use when requesting the status_callback URL.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the Texml Application.|
|inbound|object|false|none|none|
|outbound|object|false|none|none|

Parameters that can be updated in a UAC connection. A UAC (User Agent Client) Connection registers Telnyx to your PBX — the opposite of a standard SIP trunk, where the PBX registers to Telnyx. Use UAC when your PBX doesn’t support outbound SIP registration or you need Telnyx to maintain the registration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|Defaults to true|
|user_name|string|false|none|The user name to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 4-32 characters long and alphanumeric values only (no spaces or special characters).|
|password|string|false|none|The password to be used as part of the credentials. Must be 8 to 128 characters long.|
|anchorsite_override|[AnchorsiteOverride](#schemaanchorsiteoverride)|false|none|`Latency` directs Telnyx to route media through the site with the lowest round-trip time to the user's connection. Telnyx calculates this time using ICMP ping messages. This can be disabled by specifying a site to handle all media.|
|connection_name|[ConnectionName](#schemaconnectionname)|false|none|A user-assigned name to help manage the connection.|
|sip_uri_calling_preference|string|false|none|This feature enables inbound SIP URI calls to your Credential Auth Connection. If enabled for all (unrestricted) then anyone who calls the SIP URI <your-username>@telnyx.com will be connected to your Connection. You can also choose to allow only calls that are originated on any Connections under your account (internal).|
|default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled|boolean|false|none|When enabled, Telnyx will generate comfort noise when you place the call on hold. If disabled, you will need to generate comfort noise or on hold music to avoid RTP timeout.|
|bridge_generate_comfort_noise_on_cn|boolean|false|none|Stores the connection preference for generating silent RTP toward the opposite call leg when comfort-noise packets (CN, payload type 13) are received during hold. Optional; omitting this field preserves the saved value. Only JSON true and false are accepted; null and non-boolean values are rejected. This preference is independent of default_on_hold_comfort_noise_enabled and does not modify that setting. This API provisions the preference; call-processing behavior is implemented separately.|
|dtmf_type|[DtmfType](#schemadtmftype)|false|none|Sets the type of DTMF digits sent from Telnyx to this Connection. Note that DTMF digits sent to Telnyx will be accepted in all formats.|
|encode_contact_header_enabled|boolean|false|none|Encode the SIP contact header sent by Telnyx to avoid issues for NAT or ALG scenarios.|
|encrypted_media|[EncryptedMedia](#schemaencryptedmedia)|false|none|Enable use of SRTP for encryption. Can only be set when the SIP signaling transport protocol is TLS.|
|onnet_t38_passthrough_enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable on-net T38 if you prefer the sender and receiver negotiating T38 directly if both are on the Telnyx network. If this is disabled, Telnyx will be able to use T38 on just one leg of the call depending on each leg's settings.|
|ios_push_credential_id|[ConnectionIosPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectioniospushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Ios|
|android_push_credential_id|[ConnectionAndroidPushCredentialId](#schemaconnectionandroidpushcredentialid)|false|none|The uuid of the push credential for Android|
|webhook_event_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_event_failover_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this connection will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails. Must include a scheme, such as 'https'.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1 or v2.|
|webhook_timeout_secs|integer \| null|false|none|Specifies how many seconds to wait before timing out a webhook.|
|call_cost_in_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Specifies if call cost webhooks should be sent for this connection.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the connection.|
|rtcp_settings|[ConnectionRtcpSettings](#schemaconnectionrtcpsettings)|false|none|none|
|inbound|[UacInboundRequest](#schemauacinboundrequest)|false|none|Inbound settings that can be supplied when creating or updating a UAC connection. The SIP subdomain fields returned in UAC connection responses are generated by Telnyx and are not accepted as request parameters.|
|outbound|[UacOutbound](#schemauacoutbound)|false|none|none|
|noise_suppression|[ConnectionNoiseSuppression](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppression)|false|none|Controls when noise suppression is applied to calls. When set to 'inbound', noise suppression is applied to incoming audio. When set to 'outbound', it's applied to outgoing audio. When set to 'both', it's applied in both directions. When set to 'disabled', noise suppression is turned off.|
|noise_suppression_details|[ConnectionNoiseSuppressionDetails](#schemaconnectionnoisesuppressiondetails)|false|none|Configuration options for noise suppression. These settings are stored regardless of the noise_suppression value, but only take effect when noise_suppression is not 'disabled'. If you disable noise suppression and later re-enable it, the previously configured settings will be used.|
|jitter_buffer|[ConnectionJitterBuffer](#schemaconnectionjitterbuffer)|false|none|Configuration options for Jitter Buffer. Enables Jitter Buffer for RTP streams of SIP Trunking calls. The feature is off unless enabled. You may define min and max values in msec for customized buffering behaviors. Larger values add latency but tolerate more jitter, while smaller values reduce latency but are more sensitive to jitter and reordering.|
|internal_uac_settings|[UacInternalSettings](#schemauacinternalsettings)|false|none|Internal Telnyx-side settings for a UAC connection.|
|external_uac_settings|[UacExternalSettings](#schemauacexternalsettings)|false|none|External SIP peer settings used by Telnyx when registering to your PBX and routing outbound calls.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

<h2 id="tocS_UrlShortenerSettings">UrlShortenerSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaurlshortenersettings"></a>
<a id="schema_UrlShortenerSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSurlshortenersettings"></a>
<a id="tocsurlshortenersettings"></a>

```json
{
  "domain": "example.ex",
  "prefix": "",
  "replace_blacklist_only": true,
  "send_webhooks": false
}
```

The URL shortener feature allows automatic replacement of URLs that were generated using
a public URL shortener service. Some examples include bit.do, bit.ly, goo.gl, ht.ly,
is.gd, ow.ly, rebrand.ly, t.co, tiny.cc, and tinyurl.com. Such URLs are replaced with
with links generated by Telnyx. The use of custom links can improve branding and message
deliverability.

To disable this feature, set the object field to `null`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|string|true|none|One of the domains provided by the Telnyx URL shortener service.<br>|
|prefix|string|false|none|Optional prefix that can be used to identify your brand, and will appear in the Telnyx generated URLs after the domain name.<br>|
|replace_blacklist_only|boolean|false|none|Use the link replacement tool only for links that are specifically blacklisted by Telnyx.<br>|
|send_webhooks|boolean|false|none|Receive webhooks for when your replaced links are clicked. Webhooks are sent to the webhooks on the messaging profile.<br>|

UserAddresses are generally used for shipping addresses, and failure to validate your shipping address will likely result in a failure to deliver SIM cards or other items ordered from Telnyx. Do not use this parameter unless you are sure that the address is correct even though it cannot be validated. If this is set to any value other than true, verification of the address will be attempted, and the user address will not be allowed if verification fails. If verification fails but suggested values are available that might make the address correct, they will be present in the response as well. If this value is set to true, then the verification will not be attempted. Defaults to false (verification will be performed).|

<h2 id="tocS_VisionTool">VisionTool</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavisiontool"></a>
<a id="schema_VisionTool"></a>
<a id="tocSvisiontool"></a>
<a id="tocsvisiontool"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "vision",
  "shared": true,
  "vision": {
    "max_frame_age_secs": 10
  }
}
```

(BETA) Lets the assistant look at recent image frames the client sent into the conversation (for example webcam or screen-share frames). Frames are sent with `conversation.item.create` and `item.buffer: true`; they never trigger a response on their own. The assistant decides when to look and which frames it needs. Requires a model that supports image input.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|shared|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this tool comes from the shared Tools Library. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. Read-only: set by the server, not accepted in requests. When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).|
|vision|[VisionToolParams](#schemavisiontoolparams)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|vision|

<h2 id="tocS_VoiceConfig">VoiceConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavoiceconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_VoiceConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSvoiceconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsvoiceconfig"></a>

```json
"Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af"
```

The voice to be used by the voice assistant. Currently we support ElevenLabs, Telnyx and AWS voices.

 **Supported Providers:**
- **AWS:** Use `AWS.Polly.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna`). For neural voices, which provide more realistic, human-like speech, append `-Neural` to the `VoiceId` (e.g., `AWS.Polly.Joanna-Neural`). Check the [available voices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/available-voices.html) for compatibility.
- **Azure:** Use `Azure.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Azure.en-CA-ClaraNeural`, `Azure.en-CA-LiamNeural`, `Azure.en-US-BrianMultilingualNeural`, `Azure.en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural`). For a complete list of voices, go to [Azure Voice Gallery](https://speech.microsoft.com/portal/voicegallery).
- **ElevenLabs:** Use `ElevenLabs.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `ElevenLabs.BaseModel.John`). The `ModelId` part is optional. To use ElevenLabs, you must provide your ElevenLabs API key as an integration secret under `"voice_settings": {"api_key_ref": "<secret_id>"}`. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api/secrets-manager/integration-secrets/create-integration-secret) for details. Check [available voices](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/get-voices).
 - **Telnyx:** Use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>`
- **Inworld:** Use `Inworld.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Inworld.Mini.Loretta`, `Inworld.Max.Oliver`, `Inworld.TTS2.Loretta`). Supported models: `Mini`, `Max`, `TTS2`.
- **Fish Audio:** Use `FishAudio.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `FishAudio.s2.1-pro.<reference_id>`). Supported models: `s2.1-pro`, `s2-pro`, `s1`. `VoiceId` is a Fish Voice-Library reference ID.
- **Soniox:** Use `Soniox.<ModelId>.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma`). Supported model: `tts-rt-v2`. Browse the catalog via the [Voices API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/text-to-speech-commands/list-available-voices). Every voice speaks all supported languages; set `language` to the two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the text, for example `it`. SSML is not supported. Use `voice_settings` to configure `speed` (0.7 to 1.3) and `reduce_silence`.
- **xAI:** Use `xAI.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `xAI.eve`). Available voices: `eve`, `ara`, `rex`, `sal`, `leo`.
- **Humain:** Use `Humain.<VoiceId>` (e.g., `Humain.sara-ar`). Available voices: `sara-en`, `abdulaziz-en`, `sara-ar`, `abdulaziz-ar`, `nourah-ar`, `abdullah-ar`. Native Arabic (Saudi dialect) and English voices only — no `ModelId` segment.

```json
  "name": "friendly-narrator",
  "text": "Hello, welcome to our service.",
  "prompt": "Speak in a warm, friendly tone",
  "language": "Auto",
  "provider": "telnyx"
}
```

Request body for creating a new voice design or adding a version to an existing one. Omit `voice_design_id` to create a new design; include it to add a new version.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Name for the voice design. Required when creating a new design (`voice_design_id` is not provided); ignored when adding a version. Cannot be a UUID.|
|voice_design_id|string(uuid)|false|none|ID of an existing voice design to add a new version to. When provided, a new version is created instead of a new design.|
|text|string|true|none|Sample text to synthesize for this voice design.|
|prompt|string|true|none|Natural language description of the voice style, e.g. 'Speak in a warm, friendly tone with a slight British accent'.|
|language|string|false|none|Language for synthesis. Supported values: Auto, Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian. Defaults to Auto.|
|temperature|number(float)|false|none|Sampling temperature controlling randomness. Higher values produce more varied output. Default: 0.9.|
|top_k|integer|false|none|Top-k sampling parameter — limits the token vocabulary considered at each step. Default: 50.|
|top_p|number(float)|false|none|Top-p (nucleus) sampling parameter — cumulative probability cutoff for token selection. Default: 1.0.|
|repetition_penalty|number(float)|false|none|Repetition penalty to reduce repeated patterns in generated audio. Default: 1.05.|
|max_new_tokens|integer|false|none|Maximum number of tokens to generate. Default: 2048.|
|provider|string|false|none|Voice synthesis provider. `telnyx` uses the Qwen3TTS model; `minimax` uses the Minimax speech models. Case-insensitive. Defaults to `telnyx`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|provider|telnyx|
|provider|minimax|
|provider|Telnyx|
|provider|Minimax|

A raw call report stats JSON payload. The schema is intentionally permissive because Voice SDK clients can add fields over time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|call_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Unique call identifier.|
|call_report_id|string|false|none|User-scoped storage grouping identifier derived from the authenticated user. This is not a unique per-call report identifier and may be shared by multiple calls for the same user.|
|user_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Authenticated user that owns the call report.|
|organization_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Organization associated with the stored call report when provided by the Voice SDK reporting path.|
|voice_sdk_id|string|false|none|Voice SDK instance identifier.|
|voice_sdk_session_id|string|false|none|Voice SDK session correlation identifier used to group stats segments for the same SDK session.|
|voice_sdk_id_decoded|object|false|none|Decoded Voice SDK identifier metadata emitted by voice-sdk-proxy when available.|
|user_agent|string|false|none|Voice SDK user agent string reported by the client. This is the preferred SDK/platform/version dimension when present.|
|version|string|false|none|Legacy SDK version value when the client reports one separately from the user agent.|
|telnyx_session_id|string|false|none|Telnyx RTC session identifier for correlating the report with Voice SDK signaling and media-session logs.|
|telnyx_leg_id|string|false|none|Telnyx call leg identifier for correlating the report with call-control, SIP, and media troubleshooting data.|
|summary|object|false|none|High-level call metadata.|
|stats|[VoiceSdkCallReportStats](#schemavoicesdkcallreportstats)|false|none|Raw stats payload emitted by the Voice SDK and stored without normalization. The exact shape can vary by SDK platform and version. Live responses commonly return an array of interval snapshots, but object-shaped stats payloads are also allowed for compatibility.|
|logs|[VoiceSdkCallReportLogs](#schemavoicesdkcallreportlogs)|false|none|Raw logs payload emitted by the Voice SDK and stored without normalization. Live responses commonly return an array of log entries, but object-shaped log payloads are also allowed for compatibility.|
|flushReason|object|false|none|Reason the SDK flushed this stats report segment, for example an intermediate socket-close flush.|
|segment|integer|false|none|Zero-based stats segment index when the SDK sends segmented or intermediate reports.|
|stored_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Time when the call report was stored.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Creation timestamp when present.|

Check the full list of [available voices](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/tts-stt/tts-available-voices) via our voices API.<br>To use ElevenLabs, you must reference your ElevenLabs API key as an integration secret under the `api_key_ref` field. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) for details. For Telnyx voices, use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>` (e.g. Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af_heart).<br>The voice portion of the identifier supports [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) using mustache syntax (e.g. `Telnyx.Ultra.{{voice_id}}`). The variable is resolved at call time from your dynamic variables webhook, allowing you to select the voice dynamically per call.|
|voice_speed|number|false|none|The speed of the voice in the range [0.6, 1.5]. 1.0 is the default speed. Larger numbers make the voice faster, smaller numbers make it slower. Applies to Telnyx `Ultra` voices; values outside this range are rejected by the synthesis engine.|
|api_key_ref|string|false|none|The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your ElevenLabs API key. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.|
|temperature|number|false|none|Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values create a broader emotional range; higher values produce more consistent, monotonous output. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|similarity_boost|number|false|none|Determines how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice when attempting to replicate it. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|use_speaker_boost|boolean|false|none|Amplifies similarity to the original speaker voice. Increases computational load and latency slightly. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|style|number|false|none|Determines the style exaggeration of the voice. Amplifies speaker style but consumes additional resources when set above 0. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|speed|number|false|none|Adjusts speech velocity. 1.0 is default speed; values less than 1.0 slow speech; values greater than 1.0 accelerate it. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|language_boost|string \| null|false|none|Enhances recognition for specific languages and dialects during MiniMax TTS synthesis. Default is null (no boost). Set to 'auto' for automatic language detection. Only applicable when using MiniMax voices.|
|expressive_mode|boolean|false|none|Enables emotionally expressive speech using SSML emotion tags. When enabled, the assistant uses audio tags like angry, excited, content, and sad to add emotional nuance. Only supported for Telnyx Ultra voices.|
|background_audio|object|false|none|Optional background audio to play on the call. Use a predefined media bed, or supply a looped MP3 URL. If a media URL is chosen in the portal, customers can preview it before saving.|
