```json
  },
  "preset_query_params": {
    "caller": "{{telnyx_end_user_target}}",
    "channel": "voice"
  },
  "async": false,
  "async_timeout_ms": 1,
  "store_fields_as_variables": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "value_path": "string"
    }
  ],
  "messages": [
    {
      "type": "request_start",
      "content": "Let me look that up for you."
    },
    {
      "type": "request_response_delayed",
      "content": "Still working on that.",
      "timing_ms": 5000
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the tool.|
|description|string|true|none|The description of the tool.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL of the external tool to be called. This URL is going to be used by the assistant. The URL can be templated like: `https://example.com/api/v1/{id}`, where `{id}` is a placeholder for a value that will be provided by the assistant if `path_parameters` are provided with the `id` attribute.|
|method|string|false|none|The HTTP method to be used when calling the external tool.|
|headers|[object]|false|none|The headers to be sent to the external tool.|
|body_parameters|object|false|none|The body parameters the webhook tool accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. These parameters will be passed to the webhook as the body of the request. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format|
|path_parameters|object|false|none|The path parameters the webhook tool accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. These parameters will be passed to the webhook as the path of the request if the URL contains a placeholder for a value. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format|
|query_parameters|object|false|none|The query parameters the webhook tool accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. These parameters will be passed to the webhook as the query of the request. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format|
|preset_body_fields|object|false|none|Body fields supplied by the assistant configuration rather than by the model. They are never advertised in the tool definition, so the LLM can neither see nor set them, and they take precedence over a `body_parameters` value of the same name. Values support mustache templating, so they can hold dynamic variables (`{{customer_id}}`) and integration secrets (`{{#integration_secret}}my-secret{{/integration_secret}}`). Not sent on `GET` requests, which carry no body.|
|preset_query_params|object|false|none|Query string parameters supplied by the assistant configuration rather than by the model. They are never advertised in the tool definition, so the LLM can neither see nor set them, and they take precedence over a `query_parameters` value of the same name. Values support mustache templating, so they can hold dynamic variables (`{{telnyx_end_user_target}}`) and integration secrets (`{{#integration_secret}}my-secret{{/integration_secret}}`). Unlike values templated directly into the `url`, these are percent-encoded, so a value such as `+15551234567` survives the round trip.|
|async|boolean|false|none|If async, the assistant will move forward without waiting for your server to respond.|
|async_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|Maximum time in milliseconds that the conversation worker waits for an async webhook response before returning "Submitted" to the LLM. If unset, the platform default (currently 300ms) is used.|
|store_fields_as_variables|[object]|false|none|A list of mappings that extract values from the webhook response and store them as dynamic variables. Each mapping specifies a dynamic variable name and a dot-notation path to the value in the response body.|
|messages|[object]|false|none|Filler messages spoken while a synchronous webhook request is in progress. `request_start` messages are spoken immediately when the request begins. `request_response_delayed` messages are spoken after `timing_ms` has elapsed only if the webhook response is still pending. Filler messages are not used for asynchronous webhooks.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|method|GET|
|method|POST|
|method|PUT|
|method|DELETE|
|method|PATCH|

<h2 id="tocS_WebsocketSettings">WebsocketSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawebsocketsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_WebsocketSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSwebsocketsettings"></a>
<a id="tocswebsocketsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "url": "string",
  "auth_ref": "string"
}
```

Streams conversation and telephony events to a WebSocket server you host, and accepts messages injected back into the conversation. Telnyx opens the connection as a client, once per conversation. Delivery is best effort throughout: while the connection is down events are dropped rather than queued, and no socket failure is ever allowed to affect the call. Beta feature.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Telnyx opens a WebSocket to `url` for each of this assistant's conversations. Defaults to `false`.|
|url|string|false|none|The `ws://` or `wss://` endpoint Telnyx connects to. Required when `enabled` is `true`. Must be externally reachable — localhost, private IP ranges and `.local` domains are rejected.|
|auth_ref|string|false|none|Integration secret identifier whose value Telnyx sends as an `Authorization: Bearer <value>` header on the upgrade request. Resolved on every connection attempt, so a rotated secret is picked up by the next reconnect.|

```json
  "imsi": "081932214823362973",

  "mobile_country_code": "310",
  "mobile_network_code": "410",
  "start_time": "2018-02-02T22:25:27.521Z",
  "stop_time": "2018-02-02T22:25:27.521Z",

```

This object represents a wireless connectivity session log that happened through a SIM card. It aids in finding out potential problems when the SIM is not able to attach properly.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|string|false|read-only|none|
|id|integer|false|read-only|Uniquely identifies the session.|
|sim_card_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The identification UUID of the related SIM card resource.|
|log_type|string|false|read-only|The type of the session, 'registration' being the initial authentication session and 'data' the actual data transfer sessions.|
|imsi|string|false|read-only|SIM cards are identified on their individual network operators by a unique International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI). <br/><br>Mobile network operators connect mobile phone calls and communicate with their market SIM cards using their IMSIs. The IMSI is stored in the Subscriber  Identity Module (SIM) inside the device and is sent by the device to the appropriate network. It is used to acquire the details of the device in the Home  Location Register (HLR) or the Visitor Location Register (VLR).<br>|
|imei|string|false|read-only|The International Mobile Equipment Identity (or IMEI) is a number, usually unique, that identifies the device currently being used connect to the network.|
|mobile_country_code|string|false|read-only|It's a three decimal digit that identifies a country.<br/><br/><br>This code is commonly seen joined with a Mobile Network Code (MNC) in a tuple that allows identifying a carrier known as PLMN (Public Land Mobile Network) code.|
|mobile_network_code|string|false|read-only|It's a two to three decimal digits that identify a network.<br/><br/><br> This code is commonly seen joined with a Mobile Country Code (MCC) in a tuple that allows identifying a carrier known as PLMN (Public Land Mobile Network) code.|
|start_time|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the session started.|
|stop_time|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the session ended.|
|created_at|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the record was created.|
|last_seen|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the last heartbeat to the device was successfully recorded.|
|apn|string|false|read-only|The Access Point Name (APN) identifies the packet data network that a mobile data user wants to communicate with.|
|ipv4|string|false|read-only|The SIM's address in the currently connected network. This IPv4 address is usually obtained dynamically, so it may vary according to the location or new connections.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_branded-calling_Error">branded-calling_Error</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabranded-calling_error"></a>
<a id="schema_branded-calling_Error"></a>
<a id="tocSbranded-calling_error"></a>
<a id="tocsbranded-calling_error"></a>

```json
{
  "code": "10005",
  "title": "Invalid parameters",
  "detail": "field required",
  "meta": {
    "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005",
    "pending_check_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "pending_check_codes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "pending_check_labels": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "source": {
    "pointer": "/body/legal_name",
    "parameter": "page[size]"
  }
}
```

A single entry in the canonical Telnyx error envelope. `code` is the stable Telnyx error catalog id; the human-readable explanation lives at `meta.url`. `detail` is a context-specific message; `source.pointer` (when present) names the offending field of the request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|true|none|Stable numeric Telnyx error catalog id. See `meta.url` for the full catalog entry.|
|title|string|true|none|Short human-readable category, e.g. `Bad Request`, `Duplicate resource`, `Not Found`, `Forbidden`. Treat as advisory only - the stable identifier is `code`.|
|detail|string|true|none|Context-specific message describing what went wrong on this particular request. May embed offending values; do not rely on it for programmatic matching - branch on `code`.|
|meta|object|true|none|Carries `url` linking to the Telnyx error catalog entry for this `code`. Useful for forwarding the user to documentation.|
|source|object|false|none|Optional pointer at the offending field of the request.|

<h2 id="tocS_branded-calling_Errors">branded-calling_Errors</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabranded-calling_errors"></a>
<a id="schema_branded-calling_Errors"></a>
<a id="tocSbranded-calling_errors"></a>
<a id="tocsbranded-calling_errors"></a>

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10005",
      "title": "Invalid parameters",
      "detail": "field required",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005",
        "pending_check_ids": [
          "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
        ],
        "pending_check_codes": [
          "string"
        ],
        "pending_check_labels": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/body/legal_name",
        "parameter": "page[size]"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Canonical Telnyx error envelope. Returned on every 4xx and 5xx response from this service. `errors` is non-empty; multiple entries indicate multiple distinct problems with the same request (e.g. one entry per invalid phone number on a bulk operation).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[branded-calling_Error](#schemabranded-calling_error)]|true|none|List of one or more error entries. Order is not significant.|

<h2 id="tocS_branded-calling_PaginationMeta">branded-calling_PaginationMeta</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabranded-calling_paginationmeta"></a>
<a id="schema_branded-calling_PaginationMeta"></a>
<a id="tocSbranded-calling_paginationmeta"></a>
<a id="tocsbranded-calling_paginationmeta"></a>

```json
{
  "total_pages": 3,
  "total_results": 42,
  "page_number": 1,
  "page_size": 20
}
```

JSON:API pagination metadata returned with every paginated list response. Page numbering is 1-based. `page_size` reports the number of items actually returned in `data` for this page; the requested size is taken from the `page[size]` query parameter.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_pages|integer|true|none|Total number of pages available given the current `page_size`.|
|total_results|integer|true|none|Total number of items across all pages (excludes soft-deleted rows).|
|page_number|integer|true|none|1-based index of this page. Echoes the `page[number]` query parameter (default `1`).|
|page_size|integer|true|none|Number of items returned in this page's `data` array. Capped at 250.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|From|string|true|none|The phone number of the party initiating the call. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|To|string|true|none|The phone number of the called party. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|AIAssistantId|string|true|none|The ID of the AI assistant to use for the call.|
|AIAssistantVersion|string|false|none|The version of the AI assistant to use.|
|AIAssistantDynamicVariables|object|false|none|Key-value map of dynamic variables to pass to the AI assistant.|
|CallerId|string|false|none|To be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`To` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and `-_~!.+` special characters. If omitted, the display name will be the same as the number in the `From` field.|
|StatusCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send status callback events for this AI call. When provided, this per-call value overrides the status callback URL configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|StatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The status callback events for which Telnyx should send a webhook for this AI call. Multiple events can be defined when separated by a space. Valid values: initiated, ringing, answered, completed, no-answer, busy, canceled, failed, analyzed. When provided, this per-call value overrides the status callback events configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|StatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `StatusCallback` and `StatusCallbacks` for this AI call. When provided, this per-call value overrides the status callback method configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|StatusCallbacks|[string]|false|none|Array of URL destinations for Telnyx to send status callback events for this AI call. When provided, these per-call values override the status callback URL configured on the TeXML application/connection.|
|CustomHeaders|[object]|false|none|Custom HTTP headers to be sent with the call. Each header should be an object with 'name' and 'value' properties.|
|ConversationCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send AI conversation callback events for this call. Events include `conversation_created` and `conversation_ended`.|
|ConversationCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `ConversationCallback` and `ConversationCallbacks`.|
|ConversationCallbacks|[string]|false|none|Array of URL destinations for AI conversation callback events for this call. Events include `conversation_created` and `conversation_ended`.|
|MachineDetection|string|false|none|Enables Answering Machine Detection.|
|DetectionMode|string|false|none|Allows you to choose between Regular, Premium, and PremiumCallScreening detections. See https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/voice/programmable-voice/answering-machine-detection|
|AsyncAmd|boolean|false|none|Select whether to perform answering machine detection in the background. By default execution is blocked until Answering Machine Detection is completed.|
|AsyncAmdStatusCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send AMD callback events to for the call.|
|AsyncAmdStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `AsyncAmdStatusCallback`.|
|MachineDetectionTimeout|integer|false|none|Maximum timeout threshold in milliseconds for overall detection.|
|MachineDetectionPromptEndTimeout|integer|false|none|Silence duration threshold after a call screening prompt before ending prompt detection, in milliseconds. Used when `DetectionMode` is `PremiumCallScreening`.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechThreshold|integer|false|none|Maximum threshold of a human greeting. If greeting longer than this value, considered machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold|integer|false|none|Silence duration threshold after a greeting message or voice for it be considered human. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSilenceTimeout|integer|false|none|If initial silence duration is greater than this value, consider it a machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|Passports|string|false|none|A string of passport identifiers to associate with the call.|
|TimeLimit|integer|false|none|The maximum duration of the call in seconds. The minimum value is 30 and the maximum value is 14400 (4 hours). Default is 14400 seconds.|
|Timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds to wait for the called party to answer the call before the call is canceled. The minimum value is 5 and the maximum value is 120. Default is 30 seconds.|
|Record|boolean|false|none|Whether to record the entire participant's call leg. Defaults to `false`.|
|RecordingChannels|string|false|none|The number of channels in the final recording. Defaults to `mono`.|
|RecordingStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the recording callbacks will be sent to.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `RecordingStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the recording's state that should generate a call to `RecordingStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`.|
|RecordingTimeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite).|
|RecordingTrack|string|false|none|The audio track to record for the call. The default is `both`.|
|Trim|string|false|none|Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the recording. Defaults to `trim-silence`.|
|SendRecordingUrl|[calls_SendRecordingUrl](#schemacalls_sendrecordingurl)|false|none|Whether to send RecordingUrl in webhooks.|
|PreferredCodecs|string|false|none|The list of comma-separated codecs to be offered on a call.|
|SipAuthUsername|string|false|none|The username to use for SIP authentication.|
|SipAuthPassword|string|false|none|The password to use for SIP authentication.|
|SipRegion|string|false|none|Defines the SIP region to be used for the call.|

|SuperviseCallSid|string|false|none|The call control ID of the existing call to supervise. When provided, the created leg will be added to the specified call in supervising mode. Status callbacks and action callbacks will NOT be sent for the supervising leg.|
|SupervisingRole|string|false|none|The supervising role for the new leg. Determines the audio behavior: barge (hear both sides), whisper (only hear supervisor), monitor (hear both sides but supervisor muted). Default: barge|
|Timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds to wait for the called party to answer the call before the call is canceled. The minimum value is 5 and the maximum value is 120. Default is 30 seconds.|
|TimeLimit|integer|false|none|The maximum duration of the call in seconds. The minimum value is 30 and the maximum value is 14400 (4 hours). Default is 14400 seconds.|
|Texml|string|false|none|TeXML to be used as instructions for the call. If provided, the call will execute these instructions instead of fetching from the Url.|

<h2 id="tocS_conference-participants_DialConferenceParticipantRequest">conference-participants_DialConferenceParticipantRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconference-participants_dialconferenceparticipantrequest"></a>

<a id="tocsconference-participants_dialconferenceparticipantrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "To": "+12065550100",
  "From": "+12065550200"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Beep|string|false|none|Whether to play a notification beep to the conference when the participant enters and exits.|
|StatusCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send status callback events to for the call.|
|StatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `StatusCallback`.|
|StatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the call's state that should generate a call to `StatusCallback`. Can be: `initiated`, `ringing`, `answered`, and `completed`. Separate multiple values with a space. The default value is `completed`.|
|To|string|false|none|The phone number of the called party. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|From|string|false|none|The phone number of the party that initiated the call. Phone numbers are formatted with a `+` and country code.|
|Timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that we should allow the phone to ring before assuming there is no answer. Can be an integer between 5 and 120, inclusive. The default value is 30.|
|Muted|boolean|false|none|Whether the participant should be muted.|
|StartConferenceOnEnter|boolean|false|none|Whether to start the conference when the participant enters. Defaults to `true`.|
|EndConferenceOnExit|boolean|false|none|Whether to end the conference when the participant leaves. Defaults to `false`.|
|Label|string|false|none|A unique label for the participant that will be added to the conference. The label can be used to reference the participant for updates via the TeXML REST API.|
|EarlyMedia|boolean|false|none|Whether participant shall be bridged to conference before the participant answers (from early media if available). Defaults to `false`.|
|ConferenceStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the conference callbacks will be sent to.|
|ConferenceStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `ConferenceStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|ConferenceStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the conference's state that should generate a call to `ConferenceStatusCallback`. Can be: `start`, `end`, `join` and `leave`. Separate multiple values with a space. By default no callbacks are sent.|
|WaitUrl|string|false|none|The URL to call for an audio file to play while the participant is waiting for the conference to start.|
|MaxParticipants|integer|false|none|The maximum number of participants in the conference. Can be a positive integer from 2 to 800. The default value is 250.|
|Coaching|boolean|false|none|Whether the participant is coaching another call. When `true`, `CallSidToCoach` has to be given.|
|CallSidToCoach|string|false|none|The SID of the participant who is being coached. The participant being coached is the only participant who can hear the participant who is coaching.|
|CallerId|string|false|none|To be used as the caller id name (SIP From Display Name) presented to the destination (`To` number). The string should have a maximum of 128 characters, containing only letters, numbers, spaces, and `-_~!.+` special characters. If ommited, the display name will be the same as the number in the `From` field.|
|TimeLimit|integer|false|none|The maximum duration of the call in seconds.|
|MachineDetection|string|false|none|Whether to detect if a human or an answering machine picked up the call. Use `Enable` if you would like to ne notified as soon as the called party is identified. Use `DetectMessageEnd`, if you would like to leave a message on an answering machine.|
|MachineDetectionTimeout|integer|false|none|How long answering machine detection should go on for before sending an `Unknown` result. Given in milliseconds.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechThreshold|integer|false|none|Maximum threshold of a human greeting. If greeting longer than this value, considered machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold|integer|false|none|Silence duration threshold after a greeting message or voice for it be considered human. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|MachineDetectionSilenceTimeout|integer|false|none|If initial silence duration is greater than this value, consider it a machine. Ignored when `premium` detection is used.|
|AmdStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the result of answering machine detection will be sent to.|
|AmdStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `AmdStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|ApplicationSid|string|false|none|The SID of the TeXML application that will handle the new participant's call. Required unless joining an existing conference by its ConferenceSid.|
|CancelPlaybackOnMachineDetection|boolean|false|none|Whether to cancel ongoing playback on `machine` detection. Defaults to `true`.|
|CancelPlaybackOnDetectMessageEnd|boolean|false|none|Whether to cancel ongoing playback on `greeting ended` detection. Defaults to `true`.|
|PreferredCodecs|string|false|none|The list of comma-separated codecs to be offered on a call.|
|Record|boolean|false|none|Whether to record the entire participant's call leg. Defaults to `false`.|
|RecordingChannels|string|false|none|The number of channels in the final recording. Defaults to `mono`.|
|RecordingStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the recording callbacks will be sent to.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `RecordingStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|RecordingStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the recording's state that should generate a call to `RecoridngStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`.|
|RecordingTrack|string|false|none|The audio track to record for the call. The default is `both`.|
|SipAuthPassword|string|false|none|The password to use for SIP authentication.|
|SipAuthUsername|string|false|none|The username to use for SIP authentication.|
|Trim|string|false|none|Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the recording. Defaults to `trim-silence`.|
|ConferenceRecord|string|false|none|Whether to record the conference the participant is joining. Defualts to `do-not-record`. The boolean values `true` and `false` are synonymous with `record-from-start` and `do-not-record` respectively.|
|ConferenceRecordingStatusCallback|string|false|none|The URL the conference recording callbacks will be sent to.|
|ConferenceRecordingStatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `ConferenceRecordingStatusCallback`. Defaults to `POST`.|
|ConferenceRecordingStatusCallbackEvent|string|false|none|The changes to the conference recording's state that should generate a call to `RecoridngStatusCallback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space. Defaults to `completed`. `failed` and `absent` are synonymous.|
|ConferenceRecordingTimeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that Telnyx will wait for the recording to be stopped if silence is detected. The timer only starts when the speech is detected. Please note that the transcription is used to detect silence and the related charge will be applied. The minimum value is 0. The default value is 0 (infinite)|
|ConferenceTrim|string|false|none|Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the conference recording. Defaults to `trim-silence`.|
|CustomHeaders|[object]|false|none|Custom HTTP headers to be sent with the call. Each header should be an object with 'name' and 'value' properties.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|version_id|string|false|none|Identifier for the assistant version returned by version-aware assistant endpoints.|
|version_created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when this assistant version was created.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|model|string|true|none|ID of the model to use when `external_llm` is not set. You can use the [Get models API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/openai-chat/get-available-models-openai-compatible) to see available models. If `external_llm` is provided, the assistant uses `external_llm` instead of this field. If neither `model` nor `external_llm` is provided, Telnyx applies the default model.|
|instructions|string|true|none|System instructions for the assistant. These may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables)|
|tools|[AssistantTools](#schemaassistanttools)|false|none|The assistant's tools. Responses merge the assistant's shared Tools Library tools into this array alongside inline tools, each flagged `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. On update, a sent `tools` array fully replaces the inline tools only — shared tools stay attached unless `tool_ids` changes. Each tool type except `function`, `webhook`, and `client_side_tool` allows at most one instance per assistant across both sources.|
|mcp_servers|[[AssistantMCPServer](#schemaassistantmcpserver)]|false|none|MCP servers attached to the assistant. Create MCP servers with `/ai/mcp_servers`, then reference them by `id` here.|
|a2a_agents|[[AssistantA2AAgent](#schemaassistanta2aagent)]|false|none|A2A agents this assistant can delegate to. Tools are not stored here: at the start of every conversation each agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises, named `a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`. The following limits are not enforced when the assistant is saved, and anything past them is dropped when the conversation starts: 64 agents per assistant, 64 skills per card, 128 derived tools per assistant, and a 6 second budget for all card fetches combined. An agent whose card cannot be fetched costs the assistant that capability for the conversation; it does not fail the call.|
|greeting|string|false|none|Text that the assistant will use to start the conversation. This may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables). Use an empty string to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. Use the special value `<assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message>` to have the assistant generate the greeting based on the system instructions.|
|llm_api_key_ref|string|false|none|This is only needed when using third-party inference providers selected by `model`. The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your LLM provider's API key. For bring-your-own endpoint authentication, use `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.|
|external_llm|[ExternalLLM](#schemaexternalllm)|false|none|none|
|fallback_config|[FallbackConfig](#schemafallbackconfig)|false|none|none|
|voice_settings|[inference-embedding_VoiceSettings](#schemainference-embedding_voicesettings)|false|none|none|
|avatar_settings|[AvatarSettings](#schemaavatarsettings) \| null|false|none|**Beta:** Saved avatar configuration for supported realtime browser conversations. `null` means that no avatar is configured.|
|transcription|[TranscriptionSettings](#schematranscriptionsettings)|false|none|none|
|telephony_settings|[TelephonySettings](#schematelephonysettings)|false|none|none|
|messaging_settings|[MessagingSettings](#schemamessagingsettings)|false|none|none|
|enabled_features|[[EnabledFeatures](#schemaenabledfeatures)]|false|none|none|
|insight_settings|[InsightSettings](#schemainsightsettings)|false|none|none|
|privacy_settings|[PrivacySettings](#schemaprivacysettings)|false|none|none|
|dynamic_variables_webhook_url|string|false|none|If `dynamic_variables_webhook_url` is set, Telnyx sends a POST request to this URL at the start of the conversation to resolve dynamic variables. **Gotcha:** the webhook response must wrap variables under a top-level `dynamic_variables` object, e.g. `{"dynamic_variables": {"customer_name": "Jane"}}`. Returning a flat object will be ignored and variables will fall back to their defaults. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) for the full request/response format and timeout behavior.|
|dynamic_variables_webhook_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|Timeout in milliseconds for the dynamic variables webhook. Must be between 1 and 10000 ms. If the webhook does not respond within this timeout, the call proceeds with default values. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables).|
|dynamic_variables|object|false|none|Map of dynamic variables and their values|
|import_metadata|[ImportMetadata](#schemaimportmetadata)|false|none|none|
|widget_settings|[WidgetSettings](#schemawidgetsettings)|false|none|Configuration settings for the assistant's web widget.|
|interruption_settings|[inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings](#schemainference-embedding_interruptionsettings)|false|none|Settings for interruptions and how the assistant decides the user has finished speaking. These timings are most relevant when using non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn behavior is controlled by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` (`eot_threshold`, `eot_timeout_ms`, `eager_eot_threshold`).|
|integrations|[[AssistantIntegration](#schemaassistantintegration)]|false|none|Connected integrations attached to the assistant. The catalog of available integrations is at `/ai/integrations`; the user's connected integrations are at `/ai/integrations/connections`. Each item references a catalog integration by `integration_id`.|
|observability_settings|[Observability](#schemaobservability)|false|none|none|
|version_name|string|false|none|Human-readable name for the assistant version.|
|related_mission_ids|[string]|false|none|IDs of missions related to this assistant.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags associated with the assistant. Tags can also be managed with the assistant tag endpoints.|
|post_conversation_settings|[PostConversationSettings](#schemapostconversationsettings)|false|none|Configuration for post-conversation processing. When enabled, the assistant receives one additional LLM turn after the conversation ends, allowing it to execute final tool calls such as sending a summary or updating a record via webhook or function tools. Integration and MCP server tools are not available post-conversation; call-control tools (e.g. hangup, transfer) are also unavailable. Beta feature.|
|delegation_settings|[DelegationSettings](#schemadelegationsettings)|false|none|Splits the conversation between a frontend model that talks to the caller and a backend model that does the work. On the GPT-Live route the frontend model cannot call tools at all — when it needs something done it raises a delegation and waits. On the chat completion route the frontend keeps a single `delegate` tool that returns immediately, so the conversation carries on while the backend works. Either way the backend's answer is spoken as commentary or kept as silent context, depending on `speak_results`. Beta feature.|
|websocket_settings|[WebsocketSettings](#schemawebsocketsettings)|false|none|Streams conversation and telephony events to a WebSocket server you host, and accepts messages injected back into the conversation. Telnyx opens the connection as a client, once per conversation. Delivery is best effort throughout: while the connection is down events are dropped rather than queued, and no socket failure is ever allowed to affect the call. Beta feature.|
|conversation_flow|[ConversationFlow](#schemaconversationflow)|false|none|Conversation flow as returned by the API.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|enabled_features|telephony|
|enabled_features|messaging|

Read-only: set by the server, not accepted in requests. When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).|

<h2 id="tocS_inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings">inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainference-embedding_interruptionsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_inference-embedding_InterruptionSettings"></a>
<a id="tocSinference-embedding_interruptionsettings"></a>
<a id="tocsinference-embedding_interruptionsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "enable": true,
  "disable_greeting_interruption": true,
  "start_speaking_plan": {
    "wait_seconds": 0.4,
    "transcription_endpointing_plan": {
      "on_punctuation_seconds": 0.1,
      "on_no_punctuation_seconds": 1.5,
      "on_number_seconds": 0.5
    }
  },
  "interrupt_prediction_threshold": 0
}
```

Settings for interruptions and how the assistant decides the user has finished speaking. These timings are most relevant when using non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn behavior is controlled by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` (`eot_threshold`, `eot_timeout_ms`, `eager_eot_threshold`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enable|boolean|false|none|Whether users can interrupt the assistant while it is speaking.|
|disable_greeting_interruption|boolean|false|none|When true, disables user interruptions while the assistant greeting is playing.|
|start_speaking_plan|[StartSpeakingPlan](#schemastartspeakingplan) \| null|false|none|Presence of this object (even `{}`) enables per-turn transcript endpointing while it is set; setting it to `null` clears the plan and disables per-turn matching entirely. Omitting it from an update leaves the existing plan in place (updates are validated against the merged configuration).|
|interrupt_prediction_threshold|number \| null|false|none|Interrupt-prediction sensitivity, from 0.0 to 1.0. Set to null or 0.0 to disable interrupt prediction.|

```json
{
```

```json
  "voice_speed": 1,

  "temperature": 0.5,

  "use_speaker_boost": true,
  "style": 0,
  "speed": 1,
  "language": null,
  "language_boost": null,
  "expressive_mode": false,
  "background_audio": {

  },

    "value": "typing",
    "volume": 0.5
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|voice|string|true|none|The voice to be used by the voice assistant. Check the full list of [available voices](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/tts-stt/tts-available-voices) via our voices API.<br>To use ElevenLabs, you must reference your ElevenLabs API key as an integration secret under the `api_key_ref` field. See [integration secrets documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) for details. For Telnyx voices, use `Telnyx.<model_id>.<voice_id>` (e.g. Telnyx.KokoroTTS.af_heart). For Soniox voices, use `Soniox.tts-rt-v2.<voice_id>` (e.g. Soniox.tts-rt-v2.Emma); every Soniox voice speaks all supported languages.<br>The voice portion of the identifier supports [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) using mustache syntax (e.g. `Telnyx.Ultra.{{voice_id}}`). The variable is resolved at call time from your dynamic variables webhook, allowing you to select the voice dynamically per call.|
|voice_speed|number|false|none|The speed of the voice in the range [0.6, 1.5]. 1.0 is the default speed. Larger numbers make the voice faster, smaller numbers make it slower. Applies to Telnyx `Ultra` voices; values outside this range are rejected by the synthesis engine. Soniox voices support a speed range of 0.7 to 1.3.|
|api_key_ref|string|false|none|The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your ElevenLabs API key. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.|
|temperature|number|false|none|Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values create a broader emotional range; higher values produce more consistent, monotonous output. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|similarity_boost|number|false|none|Determines how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice when attempting to replicate it. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|use_speaker_boost|boolean|false|none|Amplifies similarity to the original speaker voice. Increases computational load and latency slightly. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|style|number|false|none|Determines the style exaggeration of the voice. Amplifies speaker style but consumes additional resources when set above 0. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|speed|number|false|none|Adjusts speech velocity. 1.0 is default speed; values less than 1.0 slow speech; values greater than 1.0 accelerate it. Only applicable when using ElevenLabs.|
|language|string \| null|false|none|Two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the language the voice speaks, for example `es`. Only applicable to Soniox and AssemblyAI voices, which speak every language of their model. AssemblyAI accepts `en`, `es`, `de`, `fr`, `it`, and `pt`. When unset, the voice speaks English.|
|language_boost|string \| null|false|none|Enhances recognition for specific languages and dialects during MiniMax TTS synthesis. Default is null (no boost). Set to 'auto' for automatic language detection. Only applicable when using MiniMax voices.|
|expressive_mode|boolean|false|none|Enables emotionally expressive speech using SSML emotion tags. When enabled, the assistant uses audio tags like angry, excited, content, and sad to add emotional nuance. Only supported for Telnyx Ultra voices.|
|background_audio|object|false|none|Optional background audio to play on the call. Use a predefined media bed, or supply a looped MP3 URL. If a media URL is chosen in the portal, customers can preview it before saving.|
|tool_call_audio|object \| null|false|none|Optional sound played to the caller while the assistant runs a tool (for example a webhook or MCP tool). It replaces the background audio until the tool responds, then the background audio resumes. Defaults to null, which plays no sound; send `null` on update to clear it. Not played in conference calls.|

Applies when `webhook.async` is false.|

|IncludeMetadataCustomHeaders|boolean|false|none|When set, custom parameters will be added as metadata (recording.session.ExtensionParameters). Otherwise, they’ll be added to sip headers.|
|Secure|boolean|false|none|Controls whether to encrypt media sent to your SRS using SRTP and TLS. When set you need to configure SRS port in your connector to 5061.|
|SessionTimeoutSecs|integer|false|none|Sets `Session-Expires` header to the INVITE. A reinvite is sent every half the value set. Usefull for session keep alive. Minimum value is 90, set to 0 to disable.|
|SipTransport|string|false|none|Specifies SIP transport protocol.|
|StatusCallback|string|false|none|URL destination for Telnyx to send status callback events to for the siprec session.|
|StatusCallbackMethod|string|false|none|HTTP request type used for `StatusCallback`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|record_type|string|false|read-only|Identifies the type of the resource.|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|Identifies the type of resource.|
|name|string|false|none|A user friendly name for the messaging profile.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the messaging profile is enabled or not.|
|webhook_url|string \| null(url)|false|none|The URL where webhooks related to this messaging profile will be sent.|
|webhook_failover_url|string \| null(url)|false|none|The failover URL where webhooks related to this messaging profile will be sent if sending to the primary URL fails.|
|webhook_api_version|string|false|none|Determines which webhook format will be used, Telnyx API v1, v2, or a legacy 2010-04-01 format.|
|whitelisted_destinations|[string]|false|none|Destinations to which the messaging profile is allowed to send. The elements in the list must be valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes. If set to `["*"]`, all destinations will be allowed.<br><br>This field is required if the messaging profile doesn't have it defined yet.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was created.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was updated.|
|v1_secret|string|false|none|Secret used to authenticate with v1 endpoints.|
|number_pool_settings|[NumberPoolSettings](#schemanumberpoolsettings)|false|none|Number Pool allows you to send messages from a pool of numbers of different types, assigning<br>weights to each type. The pool consists of all the long code and toll free numbers<br>assigned to the messaging profile.<br><br>To disable this feature, set the object field to `null`.<br>|
|url_shortener_settings|[UrlShortenerSettings](#schemaurlshortenersettings)|false|none|The URL shortener feature allows automatic replacement of URLs that were generated using<br>a public URL shortener service. Some examples include bit.do, bit.ly, goo.gl, ht.ly,<br>is.gd, ow.ly, rebrand.ly, t.co, tiny.cc, and tinyurl.com. Such URLs are replaced with<br>with links generated by Telnyx. The use of custom links can improve branding and message<br>deliverability.<br><br>To disable this feature, set the object field to `null`.<br>|
|mm7_metadata|[MM7Metadata](#schemamm7metadata)|false|none|MM7 settings for inbound messages|
|alpha_sender|string \| null|false|none|The alphanumeric sender ID to use when sending to destinations that require an alphanumeric sender ID.|
|daily_spend_limit|string|false|none|The maximum amount of money (in USD) that can be spent by this profile before midnight UTC.|
|daily_spend_limit_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to enforce the value configured by `daily_spend_limit`.|
|mms_fall_back_to_sms|boolean|false|none|enables SMS fallback for MMS messages.|
|mms_transcoding|boolean|false|none|enables automated resizing of MMS media.|
|mobile_only|boolean|false|none|Send messages only to mobile phone numbers.|
|smart_encoding|boolean|false|none|Enables automatic character encoding optimization for SMS messages. When enabled, the system automatically selects the most efficient encoding (GSM-7 or UCS-2) based on message content to maximize character limits and minimize costs.|
|features|[MessagingProfileFeatures](#schemamessagingprofilefeatures)|false|none|Telnyx product features the messaging customer can enable on the messaging profile. Keys map to individual feature flags; unknown keys are accepted and preserved for forward compatibility with rolling deployments.|
|ai_assistant_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the AI assistant associated with this messaging profile.|
|redaction_enabled|boolean|false|none|Set to true to enable message content redaction on this profile, or false to disable it. Ignored if the organization is not on the redaction allowlist. See the [Message Redaction guide](/docs/messaging/messages/message-redaction) for what is redacted.|
|redaction_level|integer|false|none|The redaction level to apply when redaction is enabled. 1: redact message records and reporting only. 2 (default): also redact inbound webhook payloads. See the [Message Redaction guide](/docs/messaging/messages/message-redaction).|

|webhook_api_version|1|
|webhook_api_version|2|
|webhook_api_version|2010-04-01|

The body of a tollfree verification request

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|businessName|string|true|none|Name of the business; there are no specific formatting requirements|
|corporateWebsite|string|true|none|A URL, including the scheme, pointing to the corporate website|
|businessAddr1|string|true|none|Line 1 of the business address|
|businessAddr2|string|false|none|Line 2 of the business address|
|businessCity|string|true|none|The city of the business address; the first letter should be capitalized|
|businessState|string|true|none|The full name of the state (not the 2 letter code) of the business address; the first letter should be capitalized|
|businessZip|string|true|none|The ZIP code of the business address|
|businessContactFirstName|string|true|none|First name of the business contact; there are no specific requirements on formatting|
|businessContactLastName|string|true|none|Last name of the business contact; there are no specific requirements on formatting|
|businessContactEmail|string|true|none|The email address of the business contact|
|businessContactPhone|string|true|none|The phone number of the business contact in E.164 format|
|messageVolume|object|true|none|Estimated monthly volume of messages from the given phone numbers|
|phoneNumbers|[[TFPhoneNumber](#schematfphonenumber)]|true|none|The phone numbers to request the verification of|
|useCase|object|true|none|Machine-readable use-case for the phone numbers|
|useCaseSummary|string|true|none|Human-readable summary of the desired use-case|
|productionMessageContent|string|true|none|An example of a message that will be sent from the given phone numbers|
|optInWorkflow|string|true|none|Human-readable description of how end users will opt into receiving messages from the given phone numbers|
|optInWorkflowImageURLs|[[Url](#schemaurl)]|true|none|Images showing the opt-in workflow|
|additionalInformation|string|true|none|Any additional information|
|isvReseller|string \| null|false|none|ISV name|
|webhookUrl|string|false|none|URL that should receive webhooks relating to this verification request|
|businessRegistrationNumber|string \| null|false|none|Official business registration number (e.g., Employer Identification Number (EIN) in the U.S.). Required from January 2026.|
|businessRegistrationType|string \| null|false|none|Type of business registration being provided. Required from January 2026.|
|businessRegistrationCountry|string \| null|false|none|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the issuing business authority. Must be exactly 2 letters. Automatically converted to uppercase. Required from January 2026.|
|doingBusinessAs|string \| null|false|none|Doing Business As (DBA) name if different from legal name|
|entityType|[messaging_toll_free_verification_EntityType](#schemamessaging_toll_free_verification_entitytype) \| null|false|none|Business entity classification. Must be one of the 5 valid enum values.|
|optInConfirmationResponse|string \| null|false|none|Message sent to users confirming their opt-in to receive messages|
|helpMessageResponse|string \| null|false|none|The message returned when users text 'HELP'|
|privacyPolicyURL|string \| null|false|none|URL pointing to the business's privacy policy. Plain string, no URL format validation.|
|termsAndConditionURL|string \| null|false|none|URL pointing to the business's terms and conditions. Plain string, no URL format validation.|
|ageGatedContent|boolean|false|none|Indicates if messaging content requires age gating (e.g., 18+). Defaults to false if not provided.|
|optInKeywords|string \| null|false|none|Keywords used to collect and process consumer opt-ins|
|campaignVerifyAuthorizationToken|string \| null|false|none|Campaign Verify Authorization Token required for Political use case submissions starting February 17, 2026. This token is validated by Zipwhip and must be provided for all Political use case verifications after the deadline.|

<h2 id="tocS_number-reputation_Error">number-reputation_Error</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanumber-reputation_error"></a>
<a id="schema_number-reputation_Error"></a>
<a id="tocSnumber-reputation_error"></a>
<a id="tocsnumber-reputation_error"></a>

```json
{
  "code": "10005",
  "title": "Invalid parameters",
  "detail": "field required",
  "meta": {
    "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005",
    "pending_check_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "pending_check_codes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "pending_check_labels": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "source": {
    "pointer": "/body/legal_name",
    "parameter": "page[size]"
  }
}
```

A single entry in the canonical Telnyx error envelope. `code` is the stable Telnyx error catalog id; the human-readable explanation lives at `meta.url`. `detail` is a context-specific message; `source.pointer` (when present) names the offending field of the request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|true|none|Stable numeric Telnyx error catalog id. See `meta.url` for the full catalog entry.|
|title|string|true|none|Short human-readable category, e.g. `Bad Request`, `Duplicate resource`, `Not Found`, `Forbidden`. Treat as advisory only - the stable identifier is `code`.|
|detail|string|true|none|Context-specific message describing what went wrong on this particular request. May embed offending values; do not rely on it for programmatic matching - branch on `code`.|
|meta|object|true|none|Carries `url` linking to the Telnyx error catalog entry for this `code`. Useful for forwarding the user to documentation.|
|source|object|false|none|Optional pointer at the offending field of the request.|

<h2 id="tocS_number-reputation_Errors">number-reputation_Errors</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanumber-reputation_errors"></a>
<a id="schema_number-reputation_Errors"></a>
<a id="tocSnumber-reputation_errors"></a>
<a id="tocsnumber-reputation_errors"></a>

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "10005",
      "title": "Invalid parameters",
      "detail": "field required",
      "meta": {
        "url": "https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/overview/errors/10005",
        "pending_check_ids": [
          "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
        ],
        "pending_check_codes": [
          "string"
        ],
        "pending_check_labels": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "source": {
        "pointer": "/body/legal_name",
        "parameter": "page[size]"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Canonical Telnyx error envelope. Returned on every 4xx and 5xx response from this service. `errors` is non-empty; multiple entries indicate multiple distinct problems with the same request (e.g. one entry per invalid phone number on a bulk operation).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[number-reputation_Error](#schemanumber-reputation_error)]|true|none|List of one or more error entries. Order is not significant.|

<h2 id="tocS_number-reputation_PaginationMeta">number-reputation_PaginationMeta</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanumber-reputation_paginationmeta"></a>
<a id="schema_number-reputation_PaginationMeta"></a>
<a id="tocSnumber-reputation_paginationmeta"></a>
<a id="tocsnumber-reputation_paginationmeta"></a>

```json
{
  "total_pages": 3,
  "total_results": 42,
  "page_number": 1,
  "page_size": 20
}
```

JSON:API pagination metadata returned with every paginated list response. Page numbering is 1-based. `page_size` reports the number of items actually returned in `data` for this page; the requested size is taken from the `page[size]` query parameter.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_pages|integer|true|none|Total number of pages available given the current `page_size`.|
|total_results|integer|true|none|Total number of items across all pages (excludes soft-deleted rows).|
|page_number|integer|true|none|1-based index of this page. Echoes the `page[number]` query parameter (default `1`).|
|page_size|integer|true|none|Number of items returned in this page's `data` array. Capped at 250.|

|caller_id_name_enabled|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates whether caller ID is enabled for this number.|
|call_recording_enabled|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates whether call recording is enabled for this number.|
|t38_fax_gateway_enabled|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates whether T38 Fax Gateway for inbound calls to this number.|
|purchased_at|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was purchased.|
|created_at|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was created.|
|phone_number_type|string|false|read-only|The phone number's type.<br>Note: For numbers purchased prior to July 2023 or when fetching a number's details immediately after a purchase completes, the legacy values `tollfree`, `shortcode` or `longcode` may be returned instead.|
|updated_at|string|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the resource was updated.|
|hd_voice_enabled|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates whether HD voice is enabled for this number.|
|inbound_call_screening|string|false|none|The inbound_call_screening setting is a phone number configuration option variable that allows users to configure their settings to block or flag fraudulent calls. It can be set to disabled, reject_calls, or flag_calls. This feature has an additional per-number monthly cost associated with it.|
|activated_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date indicating when the phone number was first activated (transitioned from purchase-pending or port-pending to active). Will be null for numbers that have not yet been activated, or for legacy numbers activated before this field was tracked.|

<h2 id="tocS_skip_address_verification">skip_address_verification</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaskip_address_verification"></a>
<a id="schema_skip_address_verification"></a>
<a id="tocSskip_address_verification"></a>
<a id="tocsskip_address_verification"></a>

```json
false
```

An optional boolean value specifying if verification of the address should be skipped or not. UserAddresses are generally used for shipping addresses, and failure to validate your shipping address will likely result in a failure to deliver SIM cards or other items ordered from Telnyx. Do not use this parameter unless you are sure that the address is correct even though it cannot be validated. If this is set to any value other than true, verification of the address will be attempted, and the user address will not be allowed if verification fails. If verification fails but suggested values are available that might make the address correct, they will be present in the response as well. If this value is set to true, then the verification will not be attempted. Defaults to false (verification will be performed).

Available Speechmatics models. `speechmatics/linden-1` is a preview, vendor-hosted model that accepts only 16 kHz raw audio: set `input_format` to `linear16` or `linear32` and `sample_rate` to `16000`. `mp3`, `wav`, and other sample rates are not supported for this model.

|skip_address_verification|[skip_address_verification](#schemaskip_address_verification)|false|none|An optional boolean value specifying if verification of the address should be skipped or not. UserAddresses are generally used for shipping addresses, and failure to validate your shipping address will likely result in a failure to deliver SIM cards or other items ordered from Telnyx. Do not use this parameter unless you are sure that the address is correct even though it cannot be validated. If this is set to any value other than true, verification of the address will be attempted, and the user address will not be allowed if verification fails. If verification fails but suggested values are available that might make the address correct, they will be present in the response as well. If this value is set to true, then the verification will not be attempted. Defaults to false (verification will be performed).|

<h2 id="tocS_validate_address">validate_address</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavalidate_address"></a>
<a id="schema_validate_address"></a>
<a id="tocSvalidate_address"></a>
<a id="tocsvalidate_address"></a>

```json
true
```

Indicates whether or not the address should be validated for emergency use upon creation or not. This should be left with the default value of `true` unless you have used the `/addresses/actions/validate` endpoint to validate the address separately prior to creation. If an address is not validated for emergency use upon creation and it is not valid, it will not be able to be used for emergency services. In an address record, this flag indicates whether emergency validation was performed at creation: `true` means the record passed emergency validation before it was created; `false` means validation was skipped during this creation request, and the address may have been validated separately. This flag is not a current validity status; emergency use still requires a valid address.

This object represents a SIM card action. It allows tracking the current status of an operation that impacts the SIM card.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|action_type|string|false|read-only|The operation type. It can be one of the following: <br/><br><ul><br> <li><code>enable</code> - move the SIM card to the <code>enabled</code> status</li><br> <li><code>enable_standby_sim_card</code> - move a SIM card previously on the <code>standby</code> status to the <code>enabled</code> status after it consumes data.</li><br> <li><code>disable</code> - move the SIM card to the <code>disabled</code> status</li><br> <li><code>set_standby</code> - move the SIM card to the <code>standby</code> status</li><br> <li><code>enable_voice</code> - enable voice calling on the SIM card</li><br> <li><code>disable_voice</code> - disable voice calling on the SIM card</li><br> </ul>|
|status|object|false|none|none|
|settings|object \| null|false|read-only|A JSON object representation of the action params.|
|created_at|[wireless_CreatedAt_c5290d5308](#schemawireless_createdat_c5290d5308)|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was created.|
|updated_at|[wireless_UpdatedAt_c5290d5308](#schemawireless_updatedat_c5290d5308)|false|read-only|ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was updated.|
